qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the statute of limitations and statute of repose for civil actions arising from child sexual abuse. Authorizes victims of child sexual abuse to file civil actions for damages at any time. Revives previously time-barred claims retroactively unless the alleged victim is deceased when the action commences. Caps noneconomic damages for revived claims at $1,500,000 against a single defendant. Limits sexual abuse liability for the State, local governments, and county boards of education to $890,000 per claimant. Authorizes an interlocutory appeal if a circuit court denies a motion to dismiss challenging claim revival constitutionality.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Education; Maryland Insurance Commissioner; Maryland State Treasurer's Office
qa_results.stakeholders: Victims and survivors of child sexual abuse, alleged perpetrators, the State of Maryland, local governments, county boards of education, and liability insurers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Reimbursable fund expenditures for the State Treasurer's Office increase by $70,700 in FY 2024 and $96,096 by FY 2028 to hire a claims adjuster. Indeterminate expenditure increases for the State Insurance Trust Fund and affected State agencies due to higher litigation costs, claims payments, and insurance premiums. Indeterminate expenditure increases for local governments and county boards of education for litigation, claims, and liability insurance coverage.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Treasurer's Office administers the State Insurance Trust Fund (SITF) and handles claims under the Maryland Tort Claims Act (MTCA). The bill revives time-barred child sexual abuse claims and increases the State's liability limit under MTCA to $890,000, creating direct financial and workload impacts on the Treasurer's Office, including the need for additional claims adjusters.

The bill eliminates the statute of limitations and statute of repose for child sexual abuse civil actions retroactively, permitting an influx of revived litigation in Maryland circuit courts and authorizing interlocutory appeals on certain motions to dismiss.

The bill amends the Education Article (§ 4-105) to require the State Board of Education to establish updated standards for county school boards' comprehensive liability insurance policies, increasing the required minimum coverage for sexual abuse claims to $890,000.

The Office of the Attorney General represents the State and its agencies in civil litigation, and will be tasked with defending State entities against revived and prospective tort claims filed under the expanded MTCA provisions.

Under the amended Education Article (§ 4-105(c)), the State Insurance Commissioner must adopt rules and regulations and review and approve the terms and conditions of county boards of education that elect to self-insure individually up to the updated $890,000 coverage requirement.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a subtraction modification under the Maryland income tax for qualifying union dues paid during the taxable year. Applies to dues allowed as a deduction under Internal Revenue Code Section 162 before 2018. Permits the subtraction regardless of the two-percent limitation imposed under Internal Revenue Code Section 67. Caps the allowable subtraction modification at $250 for any taxable year. Takes effect July 1, 2023, and applies to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2022.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland taxpayers who pay union dues and labor union members
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by $9.88 million in FY 2024, growing to $11.56 million by FY 2028 due to subtraction claims. State general fund expenditures increase by $50,000 in FY 2024 only for one-time Comptroller tax system modifications. Local income tax revenues decrease by $6.45 million in FY 2024 and $7.54 million by FY 2028.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland administers the state's income tax system. The bill creates a new income tax subtraction modification for union dues, directly requiring the Comptroller to update tax forms and systems, resulting in an estimated $50,000 administrative expenditure in FY 2024.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the purpose of the Maryland State Police Gun Center to track, screen, and vet firearms surrendered under final protective orders. Requires the Center to create and maintain a statewide database tracking surrendered firearms. Mandates each law enforcement agency to report information on firearms surrendered under final protective orders in its jurisdiction. Requires reported details to include the number and type of firearms and demographic information of individuals surrendering them. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of State Police; Maryland State Police Gun Center
qa_results.stakeholders: State and local law enforcement agencies, and individuals subject to final protective orders who surrender firearms
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local expenditures can be handled with existing budgeted resources; revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Maryland State Police and its Gun Center with expanding operations to create and maintain a statewide database to track, screen, and vet firearms surrendered under final protective orders.

Final protective orders under which firearms are ordered to be surrendered are issued and administered through the Maryland Judicial Branch, which coordinates protective order records across jurisdictions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the prohibition against prosecuting an individual for rape or a sexual offense committed against their legal spouse. Eliminates statutory requirements regarding separation agreements, living apart, or decrees of limited divorce to prosecute spousal sexual offenses. Allows prosecution for first-degree rape, second-degree rape, third-degree sexual offense, and fourth-degree sexual offense regardless of marital status. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: Victims of spousal rape and sexual offenses; married individuals subject to prosecution for sexual crimes against their spouse
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in State general fund expenditures and local incarceration expenditures resulting from the expanded application of existing penalties; State and local revenues are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands criminal liability by repealing the spousal defense for rape and sexual offenses, potentially increasing the caseload of indigent defendants requiring legal representation by OPD.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands prosecution and incarceration penalties for certain sexual offenses, resulting in an expected increase in commitments to State correctional facilities operated by DPSCS.
The bill allows criminal prosecution of spousal sexual offenses previously barred under law, impacting the volume and proceedings of criminal cases in the State court system.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of General Services to establish standards for State buildings to conserve energy and minimize adverse impacts on birds. Requires the Department to update the standards every five years while considering occupants' physical and mental health. Excludes public school construction, nonprofit capital grant projects, and public work contracts under $500,000. Requires shielding and minimizing building lighting from midnight to dawn during specified spring and fall periods. Requires the Maryland Green Building Council to include the standards in the Maryland High Performance Green Building Program.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of General Services; Maryland Green Building Council; Secretary of General Services
qa_results.stakeholders: State agencies and departments occupying or acquiring State buildings; architects and contractors designing or constructing State buildings; State building occupants
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate effect on State construction and maintenance costs across all funds, though utility costs may decrease over time. Revenues and local governments are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DGS is the primary agency tasked with implementing the bill, including establishing and updating bird-safe and energy-conserving standards for State buildings every five years, reducing lighting in existing State facilities, and adopting regulations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Green Building Council (MGBC) is explicitly mandated under the bill to incorporate the newly established standards into the requirements for the Maryland High Performance Green Building Program for State buildings.

MDOT owns and operates a significant inventory of State buildings that are not managed by DGS, making its future capital construction, substantial alterations, and lighting operations subject to the bill's standards.

USM owns and maintains a substantial portion of State-owned facilities independent of DGS management, and its capital construction and building renovations exceeding statutory funding thresholds will be impacted by the new standards.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Transportation and Maryland Transit Administration to evaluate equity in State transportation plans, goals, and reports. Expands the advisory committee on State transportation goals to include labor and civil rights representatives. Requires transit equity analyses, cost-benefit analyses, and community outreach before proposing major transit service changes. Prohibits implementing major service changes causing disparate impacts or disproportionate burdens unless substantial justification necessitates the change. Requires similar equity analyses and public reports before reducing or cancelling eligible capital expansion projects in the construction program.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation; Maryland Transit Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Transit riders in Maryland, including racial minority, low-income, disabled, transit-reliant, senior, and limited English proficiency riders, as well as transit contractors.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund expenditures increase by $602,600 in FY 2025 to cover 3 new permanent staff positions, consultant support, and required transit equity and cost-benefit analyses, with ongoing costs reflecting inflation. State revenues are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill, including considering transportation equity in the Maryland Transportation Plan, evaluating performance indicators for racial/disability/low-income disparities, collaborating on transit equity and cost-benefit analyses, and staffing the expanded planning processes.

MTA is directly responsible for developing transit equity analysis policies, conducting transit equity and cost-benefit analyses prior to major service changes or capital project cancellations, conducting community outreach, publishing evaluations, and hiring additional staff and consultants.
The Maryland Department of Planning holds a designated statutory seat on the advisory committee that advises MDOT on State transportation goals, benchmarks, and equity indicators.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the composition, meeting requirements, and advisory scope of the advisory committee on State transportation goals, benchmarks, and indicators to include equity metrics and additional stakeholder representatives.
The Governor is responsible for appointing members and the chair to the advisory committee advising MDOT and receives the annual report on the attainment of State transportation goals and benchmarks.

The members of the Board of Public Works are mandated recipients of the transit equity analysis, cost-benefit analysis, and community outreach reports before major transit service changes or capital expansion project cancellations.

The Attorney General is a mandated statutory recipient of the final transit equity analysis and impact reports compiled by the MTA for major service changes or capital project reductions/cancellations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Mandates membership in the Correctional Officers' Retirement System for Talbot County detention center officers if the county becomes a participating unit. Grants qualifying officers eligibility and creditable service in the retirement system for prior employment with Talbot County. Terminates their membership and rights to any benefits in the Employees' Pension System upon transfer. Exempts the transfer of creditable service from standard statutory member contribution repayment requirements. Directs that existing statutory procedures govern the transfer and crediting of plan assets.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Retirement Agency; Talbot County
qa_results.stakeholders: Talbot County local detention center officers and Talbot County government
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. If Talbot County elects to participate, county pension liabilities increase by $918,300, resulting in an ongoing annual increase of $94,000 in employer pension contributions for 25 years. Local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates the transfer of Talbot County detention center officers from the Employees' Pension System to the Correctional Officers' Retirement System if the county elects to participate, requiring the Maryland State Retirement Agency to administer the membership changes, calculate service credits, and manage the transfer of assets and liabilities.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of the Environment to adopt regulations by December 31, 2026, establishing additional private well water testing standards. Directs the department, subject to available funding, to utilize an online portal providing public access to well testing information. Requires contracts for real property sales with private wells to include water quality testing as a condition of sale. Authorizes a purchaser to waive the water quality testing requirement in writing. Requires State-certified laboratories to submit well water testing results to the department within five business days. Mandates that the department study long-term funding options for groundwater monitoring and report by December 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment; Department of Information Technology; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: buyers and sellers of real property with private or domestic water supply wells, State-certified water testing laboratories, residential tenants and landlords, and local health departments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $186,800 in FY 2025 and reach $250,700 by FY 2029 to fund three staff positions at the Maryland Department of the Environment. If funded, online portal development could cost approximately $3.4 million over two years. Potential indeterminate impact on local health departments and MDH Laboratories Administration depending on testing standards developed.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary agency responsible for administering the Act, including establishing private well water quality testing regulations, managing the online testing portal, receiving water testing data, conducting a groundwater funding study, and submitting required reports.
The bill statutorily requires MDE to consult with the Department of Information Technology regarding the planning, development, and utilization of the private well water quality online portal.

The bill mandates continuous information sharing between MDE and MDH regarding well water quality data. Additionally, the fiscal note highlights potential operational and staffing impacts on MDH's Laboratories Administration to conduct additional water quality testing.
MDE is required to submit a report of its findings and recommendations regarding long-term funding options for groundwater monitoring and analysis directly to the Governor by December 1, 2025.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Transit-Oriented Development Capital Grant and Revolving Loan Fund to finance local transit-oriented development projects. Authorizes the Maryland Department of Transportation to provide grants and loans for design plans, infrastructure, and gap funding. Expands the definition of transit-oriented development to include properties adjacent to planned or existing transit corridors. Transfers transit-oriented development designation authority from the Secretary of Transportation to the Smart Growth Subcabinet. Requires the Governor to include an annual budget appropriation ensuring a fund balance of at least $5,000,000. Directs the Secretary of Transportation to submit an annual progress report to the General Assembly by November 30.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation; Smart Growth Subcabinet; Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: county and municipal governments; transit commuters; commercial and residential developers partnering on transit-oriented development projects; low-income and minority transit riders
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures increase by $5.0 million annually beginning in FY 2024 (mandated beginning in FY 2025) to maintain the required fund balance, with matching special fund revenues and expenditures. Transportation Trust Fund expenditures increase by $258,249 in FY 2024 for MDOT administrative staff and start-up IT consultant costs, with ongoing operational costs in future years. Local revenues and expenditures increase to the extent local jurisdictions receive grants or revolving loans.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT is the primary agency responsible for administering the Transit-Oriented Development Capital Grant and Revolving Loan Fund, publishing scoring standards, providing financial assistance to local jurisdictions, and submitting the annual report to the General Assembly.
DHCD is statutorily required to collaborate with MDOT to support recipients of awards from the fund by providing technical services for studies, plans, and code changes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Smart Growth Subcabinet is given statutory responsibility to designate transit-oriented developments (TODs) and establish eligibility requirements and objective scoring standards for financial assistance applications under the fund.
DBM is responsible for state budget preparation and execution, and the bill establishes a mandated annual state budget appropriation of at least $5,000,000 to capitalize the new fund.
The bill mandates that the Governor include an appropriation sufficient to ensure a fund balance of at least $5,000,000 at the start of each fiscal year in the annual budget bill.
The State Treasurer is statutorily designated to hold the new special, nonlapsing fund separately and invest its moneys.
The Comptroller is statutorily required to account for the newly established Transit-Oriented Development Capital Grant and Revolving Loan Fund and its interest earnings.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a victim of an act that would constitute a state hate crime violation to file a civil action. Permits the court to issue an injunction to prevent or restrain the prohibited act. Authorizes awards for economic damages, specified noneconomic damages, and reasonable attorney's fees and court costs. Excludes distress or anguish caused solely by property repair or replacement from recoverable noneconomic damages. Permits the court to award damages up to three times the amount of actual damages. Applies prospectively only to causes of action arising on or after October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: District Court of Maryland; Circuit Courts
qa_results.stakeholders: victims of hate crimes and individuals sued for committing hate crime violations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Any increase in District Court or circuit court proceedings can be handled using existing judicial resources. State and local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a civil cause of action allowing victims of hate crimes to bring civil lawsuits in Maryland courts for injunctive relief and damages (including treble actual damages and attorney's fees), directly impacting District Court and circuit court caseloads and judicial administration.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the authority of a court to decree a limited divorce. Alters the statutory grounds required to obtain an absolute divorce. Establishes a six-month separation and irreconcilable differences as grounds for absolute divorce. Repeals prior grounds including adultery, desertion, criminal conviction, insanity, and cruelty of treatment. Deems parties living under the same roof as separated if they pursue separate lives.
qa_results.responsible_party: Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals seeking a divorce or legal separation in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Judiciary increase by $18,000 in FY 2024 only for computer programming changes. Operations and finances of the Judiciary and circuit court workloads are not otherwise materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the legal grounds and processes for granting divorces in Maryland circuit courts by repealing limited divorce and altering absolute divorce requirements. The Judiciary/Administrative Office of the Courts incurs a direct fiscal and operational impact to update court forms and case management programming.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires each public school to provide Title IX information to students, faculty, staff, and parents. Mandates disclosure of the individual who serves as the Title IX coordinator for the school. Requires schools to explain the process in place for filing a sexual misconduct complaint. Directs schools to detail available support measures for individuals filing complaints and how to access them. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland public schools
qa_results.stakeholders: Public school students, faculty, staff, and parents in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Local school systems can provide the required information using existing resources, resulting in no material impact on local expenditures or revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) oversees the state's public primary and secondary education system and sets educational standards and policies. MSDE provides policy guidance and oversight to ensure local public schools comply with Title IX regulations and state education requirements.

As a state agency operating public schools for deaf and hard-of-hearing students, the Maryland School for the Deaf is directly subject to the bill's requirement to provide Title IX coordinator, complaint process, and support measures information to students, faculty, staff, and parents.

An independent unit within MSDE, the Center supports comprehensive school safety, supportive learning environments, and reporting systems for safety and misconduct concerns across public schools in Maryland.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the Maryland statutory forms for personal financial powers of attorney and limited powers of attorney. Authorizes agents to perform acts necessary to enable principals to qualify for governmental benefits or programs. Adds provisions granting agents general authority over tangible personal property, trust and estate matters, and disclaimers. Expands optional specific powers regarding gifts, joint accounts, beneficiary designations, and appointing successor agents. Incorporates warnings regarding asset risks for principals and specifies fiduciary duties of loyalty for agents.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; Register of Wills
qa_results.stakeholders: principals executing powers of attorney, designated agents and coagents, beneficiaries, and third parties relying on power of attorney documents
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends statutory power of attorney forms to include specific authority for agents to perform acts, transfer assets, or create special needs trusts to enable a principal to qualify for government benefit programs, specifically including Medicaid, which is administered by the Maryland Department of Health.

The bill modifies statutory power of attorney forms that govern agent authority over trust and estate matters, demanding custody of wills, and making elective share elections subject to the Estates and Trusts Article, which intersect with estate administration overseen by the Registers of Wills.

The statutory power of attorney forms contain provisions concerning court litigation, guardian of the person and property nominations, and statutory elective share elections, which impact judicial branch proceedings supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the State Board of Examiners of Psychologists to issue electronic licenses and registrations to qualifying applicants. Requires the Board, upon specific request, to mail a paper verification of licensure or registration to the applicant. Repeals requirements for the Board to include specific details, signatures, and its seal on licenses and registrations. Requires the Board to send renewal notices by electronic means at least 90 days before expiration. Directs the Board to send renewal notices by first-class mail if electronic transmissions fail or upon specific request.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Examiners of Psychologists
qa_results.stakeholders: licensed psychologists, registered psychology associates, and applicants for psychology licensure or registration in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal effect, as the operational changes are procedural in nature and do not materially affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Examiners of Psychologists operates within the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) as a health occupations licensing board. MDH regulates health care professionals, and this bill directly alters the board's statutory licensing, registration, and renewal notification procedures.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires holders of tax sale certificates to include email addresses in pre-foreclosure notices sent to interested parties. Authorizes owners, mortgagees, mortgage servicers, and deed of trust beneficiaries of owner-occupied residential property to request payoff amounts. Excludes owner-occupied residential property in Baltimore City from this specific payoff request process. Limits the payoff amount to expenses incurred before the certificate holder received the request. Deems the provided payoff amount valid for 30 days after the certificate holder provides it.
qa_results.responsible_party: County Tax Collectors; Municipal Tax Collectors
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners of owner-occupied residential property sold at tax sales, mortgage lenders and servicers, deed of trust beneficiaries, and holders of tax sale certificates of sale outside Baltimore City
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State finances, and local government finances are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the statutory requirements and prerequisites that must be satisfied before a certificate holder can file a complaint to foreclose the right of redemption in Maryland circuit courts. As the administrative support body for the Judicial Branch, the Administrative Office of the Courts oversees court operations and case processing where these foreclosure actions are filed.

The bill impacts owner-occupied residential property retention and foreclosure prevention by establishing procedures for obtaining payoff redemption amounts. While the department has no direct administrative duties under the bill, it monitors residential property tax sale policies and programs related to homeownership preservation and foreclosure mitigation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters relocation plan requirements when closing a mobile home park with more than 10 sites. Increases mandatory relocation assistance to 12 months of rent instead of 10 months. Conditions community purchase offers on filing an affidavit limiting lot rent increases and preserving park use. Requires community owners to notify homeowners and provide them an opportunity to purchase the property instead. Authorizes homeowners organizations to make purchase offers backed by 75% of member residents. Imposes $10,000 civil liability on community owners or purchasers who violate statutory requirements.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Manufactured home owners, mobile home park residents, manufactured housing community owners, and prospective purchasers of manufactured housing communities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local government operations and finances are not anticipated to be materially affected. The Department of Housing and Community Development and local housing agencies can receive notices and maintain web listings with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) with receiving notices of conditionally accepted offers to sell manufactured housing communities and requires the department to maintain a public list on its website of organizations and county housing agencies that can assist homeowners with financing.

The bill creates civil liability provisions allowing homeowners organizations to seek $10,000 in statutory damages against community owners or purchasers for specific violations, which could result in civil actions handled by the state court system.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the qualifications required for an individual to obtain a license as a psychologist. Expands the definition of a doctoral degree in psychology to include programs with recognized regional accreditation. Establishes a second licensure pathway for individuals who earn a postdoctoral respecialization certificate. Requires the respecialization program to include at least 1,750 hours in a supervised internship. Requires completing at least 1,500 hours of advanced training or psychology associate service. Mandates at least two years of board-approved professional, supervised experience in psychology.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Examiners of Psychologists
qa_results.stakeholders: Applicants for psychologist licensure, including doctoral-level psychologists with nonclinical psychology degrees seeking clinical licensure
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the licensure requirements and qualifications overseen by the State Board of Examiners of Psychologists, which operates as a health occupations licensing board under the Maryland Department of Health.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the membership requirements and geographic composition of the State Board of On-Site Wastewater Professionals. Reduces the required number of on-site wastewater professional members on the Board from six to five. Clarifies that inspection license requirements and penalties apply only to inspections conducted for property transfers. Directs property transfer inspection license application fees into the On-Site Wastewater Professionals Fund. Redirects administrative penalties for property transfer inspection violations to the Maryland Clean Water Fund.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment; State Board of On-Site Wastewater Professionals
qa_results.stakeholders: On-site wastewater professionals, property transfer septic inspectors, and consumers purchasing or selling real property with on-site sewage disposal systems
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No net impact on State finances, but results in a minimal shift in special fund administrative penalty revenue from the Bay Restoration Fund to the Maryland Clean Water Fund in fiscal years 2023 through 2025. No direct material impact on local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) is the primary implementing agency for the bill. It is responsible for issuing on-site wastewater property transfer inspection licenses, setting fees, collecting administrative penalties, and directing revenues into the Maryland Clean Water Fund and the On-Site Wastewater Professionals Fund.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the membership composition, geographic representation requirements, and licensing prerequisites for the State Board of On-Site Wastewater Professionals.

The bill modifies the statutory qualifications and geographic distribution criteria for the six board members appointed by the Governor to the State Board of On-Site Wastewater Professionals, which directly impacts the vetting and recruitment process overseen by the Office of Appointments.

qa_results.bill_summary: Places the Maryland Food System Resiliency Council in the Office of Resilience within the Maryland Department of Emergency Management. Requires the Maryland Department of Emergency Management to provide staff for the Council. Adds one representative of the seafood industry, appointed by the Secretary of Emergency Management, to the Council. Authorizes the Council to elect an annual cochair from among any of its members. Transfers Council appointment and administrative authorities from the Director to the Secretary of Emergency Management.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Emergency Management; Office of Resilience; Maryland Food System Resiliency Council
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland seafood industry, local food council organizations, Maryland farmers, food businesses, and state food security agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal effect. The Department of Legislative Services determined the bill creates no new council duties or additional expenditures because the Maryland Department of Emergency Management already provides staff for the Council.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 32 establishes that the Maryland Food System Resiliency Council is housed within the Office of Resilience in MDEM. The Secretary of Emergency Management cochairs the council, appoints numerous members, and MDEM is charged with providing staffing for the council.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the statutory placement, membership composition, and cochair election process of the Maryland Food System Resiliency Council.
The Secretary of Agriculture (or designee) is designated in statute as a member and co-vice chair of the Maryland Food System Resiliency Council.
The Secretary of Human Services (or designee) is designated in statute as a member and co-vice chair of the Maryland Food System Resiliency Council.

The Dean of the University of Maryland College of Agriculture and Natural Resources serves as a co-vice chair of the council. The bill also alters staffing provisions by removing the statutory requirement for the college to co-staff the council.
The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) serves as an ex officio member of the Maryland Food System Resiliency Council.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Executive Director of MARBIDCO (or designee) serves as a designated statutory member of the council.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires residential landlords in jurisdictions requiring rental licenses to plead and prove licensure status when filing repossession actions. Mandates that landlords state with supporting facts whether the property is licensed, exempt, or unlicensed for specified reasons. Excludes repossession actions for breach of lease involving clear and imminent danger from the initial pleading mandate. Requires landlords to demonstrate licensure compliance, exemption, or permitted unlicensed status at trial by a preponderance of the evidence. Authorizes landlords to provide electronic proof of licensure. Directs the court to grant one postponement if a party seeks additional evidence regarding licensure.
qa_results.responsible_party: District Court of Maryland; Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: residential landlords and residential tenants in Maryland jurisdictions that require rental licensing
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Judiciary can implement form revisions and computer programming changes with existing budgeted resources. No material effect on State or local government revenues or expenditures is anticipated.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 36 directly affects District Court proceedings for residential repossession actions by requiring landlords to plead licensure compliance using a form prescribed by the Judiciary, prove compliance by a preponderance of the evidence, and requiring the court to grant a postponement under certain conditions. The Administrative Office of the Courts must revise court forms and update judicial case management systems.

The Office of the Attorney General, particularly through its Consumer Protection Division, enforces state consumer protection and tenant rights laws regarding residential leases and unlicensed rental properties. While not assigned direct procedural duties under the bill, it monitors and investigates unlawful landlord repossession practices.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits a person from making telephone solicitations using automated dialing systems or recorded messages without prior express written consent. Restricts telephone solicitations to the hours between 8:00 a.m. and 8:00 p.m. in the called party's time zone. Limits solicitations to no more than three times per 24-hour period on the same subject matter. Prohibits deliberately concealing caller identification information or altering caller voice to defraud or confuse the called party. Establishes violations as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices subject to enforcement under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: telephone solicitors and telephone subscribers receiving telephone solicitations in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material impact on State or local finances or operations; minimal complaint processing costs for the Office of the Attorney General are expected to be absorbed within existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Violations of the bill's telephone solicitation provisions are designated as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which is investigated and enforced by the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General.

The bill provides an exemption for certain noncommercial telephone solicitations by nonprofits, conditioning that exemption on the organization being registered with the Secretary of State under Title 6 of the Business Regulation Article.

The bill defines telephone solicitations by cross-referencing Section 8-205 of the Public Utilities Article and specifies that it does not preclude the applicability of related Public Utilities Article provisions and Public Service Commission oversight.

Violations of the Maryland Consumer Protection Act may result in civil actions or misdemeanor criminal charges adjudicated in the state court system administered by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts up to $500 in a debtor's account held by a depository institution from execution without debtor election. Caps the cumulative value of cash and property exempted under this provision and election-based exemptions at $6,000. Requires writs of garnishment to instruct garnishees to garnish only amounts exceeding the exempted $500. Requires depository institutions receiving a writ of garnishment to answer stating whether debtor funds exceed $500. Authorizes depository institutions to determine how to apply the $500 exemption across multiple accounts. Shields depository institutions acting in good faith reliance on writ instructions from liability to judgment creditors.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: judgment debtors, judgment creditors, and depository institutions (including banks, credit unions, trust companies, savings banks, and savings and loan associations)
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local revenues and expenditures are not materially affected. State and local debt collection practices rarely involve bank account garnishment, and any resulting revenue changes are anticipated to be negligible.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies court garnishment procedures by requiring writs of garnishment issued by Maryland courts to instruct depository institutions to exempt up to $500 in deposit accounts without debtor election. The Administrative Office of the Courts must update court forms, processes, and case management systems to reflect these statutory changes.

DBM houses the Central Collection Unit (CCU), the state's primary delinquent debt collector. The bill impacts state collections by automatically exempting the first $500 in debtor bank accounts from garnishment or execution, though the fiscal note anticipates minimal impact given CCU's collection practices.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires each county to establish a uniform process to claim surplus balances following tax sale foreclosures. Prohibits the claim process from requiring a court order unless a dispute arises regarding payment. Requires county tax collectors to notify prior property owners of record within 90 days after delivering a deed. Specifies the notice must detail the surplus balance amount and the county process for claiming it.
qa_results.responsible_party: County Governments; County Tax Collectors
qa_results.stakeholders: Prior property owners of record whose properties are sold at tax sale foreclosure, tax sale purchasers, and county tax offices
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State finances. Local government finances are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill impacts judicial branch operations by specifying that a county's process for claiming surplus tax sale proceeds may not require a court order unless there is an active dispute regarding payment, thereby potentially reducing routine filings and petitions in circuit courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the Collaborative Care Pilot Program and its associated reporting requirement. Removes the June 30, 2024 termination date for the program's original enabling statutes. Requires the Maryland Department of Health to implement and reimburse Collaborative Care Model services statewide. Covers somatic and behavioral health integration in primary care settings serving Maryland Medical Assistance Program recipients. Clarifies that primary care providers may still refer patients to specialty behavioral health care providers.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland Medical Assistance Program recipients, primary care practices, and behavioral health care providers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Medicaid expenditures increase by up to $15.7 million (61% federal funds, 39% general funds) in FY 2024 and $20.9 million annually beginning in FY 2025. Federal fund revenues increase correspondingly by $9.6 million in FY 2024 and $12.8 million annually thereafter. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly requires the Maryland Department of Health to implement and provide Medicaid reimbursement for somatic and behavioral health services provided under the Collaborative Care Model statewide in primary care settings, resulting in significant programmatic and fiscal impacts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Codifies the Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council as an instrumentality of the State. Requires the Council to work with Centers for Independent Living to submit, monitor, implement, and evaluate the State Plan. Directs the Governor to appoint Council members considering diversity and statewide geographic representation. Requires the Council to employ an executive director and authorizes the Council to hire staff. Designates the Attorney General as the legal advisor to the Council. Exempts the Council from State and local taxes and specified State procurement and personnel laws.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council; Office of the Attorney General; Governor
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals with disabilities in Maryland, Centers for Independent Living, and members and staff of the Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures and federal fund revenues may increase beginning in fiscal 2024 if additional legal staff is needed for the Office of the Attorney General, though exact costs cannot be reliably determined. No material effect on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly designates the Attorney General as the legal advisor to the Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council, and the fiscal note indicates a potential fiscal impact from additional staffing needed to advise the council.

MSDE houses the Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS), which serves as the Designated State Entity under the federal Rehabilitation Act and State Plan for Independent Living, and is tasked with auditing the council's books and records.
The bill requires the Governor to appoint members to the council in compliance with federal guidelines and diversity criteria, as well as granting the authority to remove members for cause.

As the principal agency coordinating statewide policies and programs for individuals with disabilities, the department's mission directly intersects with the council's oversight of independent living programs and centers.
The office assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and managing the appointment process for members of the newly codified council.
The bill explicitly subjects members and employees of the Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council to the Maryland Public Ethics Law administered by the commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the statutory requirement that county tax collectors sell property with delinquent taxes within two years. Repeals the mandate that the Calvert County tax collector sell delinquent property after one year. Requires collectors to sell property with delinquent taxes at the time required by local law. Provides that failure to sell within that time does not affect the validity of taxes or sales. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: County tax collectors; local governing bodies
qa_results.stakeholders: Property owners with delinquent property taxes, local governments, and tax sale purchasers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Annuity Bond Fund revenues and local government revenues may be delayed beginning in fiscal 2024 if local governments allow longer periods before holding tax sales. Specific revenue figures cannot be reliably estimated. Expenditures are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill may cause a delay in Annuity Bond Fund (ABF) revenues from state property taxes if local governments extend the time before conducting tax sales. The ABF is used to pay debt service on the State's general obligation bonds, which are overseen and managed by the State Treasurer's Office.

The Administrative Office of the Courts provided information on the bill, as tax sales and subsequent proceedings to foreclose the right of redemption involve filings and adjudications within the Maryland Judiciary's Circuit Courts.

The Board of Public Works is responsible for setting the annual State property tax rate to support the Annuity Bond Fund for debt service payments on general obligation bonds, the timing of which may be marginally affected by delayed property tax collections.

qa_results.bill_summary: Subjects the State Ethics Commission to enhanced transparency requirements under the Open Meetings Act. Requires the Commission to post open meeting agendas and voting materials online at least 48 hours in advance. Mandates that the Commission provide live video streaming of each open session. Requires the Commission to maintain approved meeting minutes online for at least five years. Requires archived video recordings to remain available online for at least one year. Directs the Department of Information Technology to provide technical staff, support, and livestreaming equipment.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Ethics Commission; Department of Information Technology
qa_results.stakeholders: State Ethics Commission and members of the public seeking access to State Ethics Commission open meetings
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $10,000 in FY 2024 only for the State Ethics Commission to reimburse the Department of Information Technology for video streaming equipment and support services. Reimbursable revenues and expenditures for the Department of Information Technology increase commensurately in FY 2024. No local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly applies enhanced Open Meetings Act requirements to the State Ethics Commission, requiring it to livestream open meetings, post advance agendas and materials, and maintain video and minutes archives online, with an associated $10,000 fiscal expenditure in FY 2024.
The bill statutorily mandates that the Department of Information Technology provide the technical staff, support, and equipment necessary to livestream open meetings of the State Ethics Commission.
The Office of the Attorney General provides legal guidance on the Open Meetings Act and houses/staffs the Open Meetings Law Compliance Board, which handles complaints arising under the Act.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits local jurisdictions from imposing unreasonable limitations or land use restrictions on utility-designated pollinator areas. Applies the protection when an area meets a federal conservation agreement or statutory pollinator-friendly maintenance standards. Excludes utility property located on or below a trail overlap, a park overlap, or active farmland. Authorizes local land use restrictions that pertain to safe energy delivery or human health and safety. Requires participating public service companies to mow designated pollinator areas only within specified seasonal windows. Limits mowing of these pollinator areas to not more than once every other year.
qa_results.responsible_party: Public Service Commission; local governments
qa_results.stakeholders: Public service companies maintaining utility-designated pollinator areas, local governments and zoning authorities, and native pollinator and wildlife populations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes standards and protections for utility-designated pollinator areas and vegetation management performed by public service companies, which are regulated by the Public Service Commission pursuant to statewide service quality, reliability, and vegetation management standards.

The bill references plant listings maintained by the Department of Agriculture to define native plants and explicitly preserves existing State and local weed control laws under Title 9, Subtitle 4 of the Agriculture Article.

qa_results.bill_summary: Renames the Certified Local Farm Enterprise Program to be the Certified Local Farm and Fish Program. Expands the State's 20% food procurement goal to include food from certified Chesapeake invasive species providers. Defines certified Chesapeake invasive species as high-priority finfish harvested from the Chesapeake Bay or its tributaries. Requires each State unit to structure food procurement procedures to try to achieve the combined 20% goal. Directs the Department of Agriculture to maintain a public directory and submit an annual consolidated implementation report.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture; Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
qa_results.stakeholders: State procurement units, licensed seafood dealers and watermen providing Chesapeake invasive species, and certified local farms
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State revenues or expenditures. The Maryland Department of Agriculture can implement program expansion and reporting requirements using existing budgeted resources, with minimal expected impact on agency food procurement costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Agriculture houses the Office for the Certified Local Farm and Fish Program and is responsible for administering the program, certifying providers, adopting regulations, maintaining the provider directory, and submitting annual consolidated reports.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MARBIDCO administers the Certified Local Farm and Fish Food Aggregation Grant Fund and receives mandated general fund appropriations to provide grants and near-equity investments supporting aggregation sites and program participation.
The Board of Public Works receives annual reports regarding procurement goal waivers, must approve agency reporting guidelines, and submits waiver records annually to the General Assembly.
The bill explicitly applies Title 14, Subtitle 7 procurement goals and requirements for food purchasing to the University System of Maryland.
The bill explicitly applies Title 14, Subtitle 7 procurement goals and requirements for food purchasing to Morgan State University.
The bill explicitly applies Title 14, Subtitle 7 procurement goals and requirements for food purchasing to St. Mary's College of Maryland.
The bill amends the Education Article regarding the definition of 'local' agricultural products for the Maryland Farm-to-School Meal Grant Pilot Program overseen by MSDE.
The criteria for certified Chesapeake invasive species rely on DNR's Maryland Aquatic Nuisance Species Management Plan and seafood dealer licensing under the Natural Resources Article.
As the state's central procurement authority, DGS manages state procurement standards and contracts that must adhere to the expanded food procurement goals.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the service charge a circuit court clerk may impose for a dishonored check from $10 to $30. Authorizes the District Court to impose a $30 service charge for returned checks in motor vehicle, criminal, or civil cases. Applies when a check is returned for insufficient funds, a closed account, or a nonexistent account. Specifies that this service charge is in addition to any other penalty prescribed by law. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Judiciary; Circuit Courts; District Court of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals who issue dishonored checks to pay circuit court charges or District Court fines and costs
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues increase by a minimum of $7,600 in fiscal 2024 and by a minimum of $10,100 annually thereafter due to higher service charges collected. Central Collection Unit special fund revenues may increase minimally. No material effect on State expenditures or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the judicial branch by authorizing clerks of the circuit courts and the District Court to increase the service charge assessed on dishonored checks from $10 to $30, resulting in increased general fund revenues collected by the courts.

DBM houses the Central Collection Unit (CCU), which has a $30 minimum debt threshold. Increasing the fee to $30 enables the courts to refer delinquent check fees to CCU for collection, potentially generating minimal special fund fee revenues.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Transportation to recommend and implement context-driven pedestrian and bicycle safety design elements. Applies this requirement during any construction, improvement, postconstruction, preservation, or maintenance project. Aligns these design elements with Federal Highway Administration Proven Safety Countermeasures. Mandates incremental, near-term safety improvements for approved pedestrian or bicycle projects projected to exceed 12 months. Requires implementation of these near-term improvements as soon as practicable. Maintains each project's priority ranking throughout implementation.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation
qa_results.stakeholders: Pedestrians and bicyclists using Maryland roadways, and highway contractors working on state transportation projects
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal redirection of Maryland Department of Transportation capital program funding beginning as early as fiscal 2023 to implement incremental safety improvements. No impact on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT is the primary department responsible for implementing the bill's requirements, specifically mandating that the Department implement incremental, near-term pedestrian and bicycle safety improvements whenever an approved safety project takes longer than 12 months.

As the modal agency within MDOT responsible for roadway planning, construction, and pedestrian/bicycle safety improvements across Maryland highways, SHA is directly responsible for carrying out the design and installation of the required near-term safety countermeasures.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the definition of charitable contribution under Maryland law regulating charitable organizations. Excludes certain donated property intended for free redistribution from the charitable contribution definition. Excludes discounts on or authorized use of services, materials, equipment, or facilities from the definition. Authorizes the Secretary of State to accept alternative documentation instead of an independent audit or review. Restricts this alternative option to qualifying charitable organizations that primarily solicit in-kind contributions.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Secretary of State
qa_results.stakeholders: Charitable organizations operating or soliciting in Maryland and donors of in-kind property or discounted services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential increase in Maryland Secretary of State operational expenditures if additional staff are required to process waiver requests; revenues are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 72 directly impacts the Secretary of State, which is the agency responsible for registering and overseeing charitable organizations in Maryland. The bill alters definitions regarding charitable contributions and authorizes the Secretary of State to review and accept alternative documentation in place of required audits or reviews for charitable registrations.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Secretary of State on regulatory matters and assists in enforcing state laws related to charitable organizations and consumer protection.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires each county board of education to adopt, implement, and publish guidelines reducing allergen exposure risks before the 2024–2025 school year. Requires the Maryland State Department of Education and the Maryland Department of Health jointly to update school health guidelines by August 1, 2023. Directs each public school to develop a system to disclose served foods and their major food allergens in advance. Mandates that school principals monitor and implement local board guidelines for attending students with identified anaphylactic allergies. Prohibits requiring schools to dispose of certain pre-2023 food products lacking sesame labels before January 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Maryland Department of Health; county boards of education
qa_results.stakeholders: public school students with anaphylactic food allergies, parents and guardians, public school educators and staff, and county boards of education
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State or local revenues. The Maryland State Department of Education, the Maryland Department of Health, and local boards of education can implement the bill's guideline updates and disclosure requirements with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 78 specifically requires the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), jointly with the Maryland Department of Health, to update the Maryland State School Health Services guidelines regarding anaphylactic food allergies and major food allergens, and oversees public school implementation.

HB 78 mandates that the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) jointly update the Maryland State School Health Services guidelines for anaphylaxis with MSDE. Additionally, local health departments and school health professionals under MDH's sphere have operational roles in school health services.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires a tax collector to attempt contact with a tax sale certificate holder by phone and email. Triggers this requirement when the certificate holder fails to respond to an expense request for redemption. Applies to requests from the property owner, current mortgagee, assignee, mortgage servicer, or deed of trust beneficial interest holder. Authorizes the collector to redeem property without a satisfaction letter if the holder fails to respond within five business days.
qa_results.responsible_party: Local Tax Collectors
qa_results.stakeholders: Property owners whose property is sold at tax sale, mortgage lenders and mortgage servicers, holders of a beneficial interest in a deed of trust, and tax sale certificate holders
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State finances and is not anticipated to materially affect local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill impacts procedures surrounding property tax sales and the redemption process, which directly intersect with judicial actions to foreclose the right of redemption filed in the circuit courts. The Administrative Office of the Courts was consulted regarding court operations and proceedings related to these foreclosure actions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Comptroller to disclose specified tax information to the Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Board and its authorized contractors. Limits disclosures strictly to administering the Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Program and Trust. Permits disclosure of business identification numbers, names, addresses, and contact details received from State tax filings. Prohibits the disclosure of individual tax information and any information protected under federal law. Specifies that the Comptroller need not validate the tax information prior to disclosure. Requires recipients to use the information solely for purposes authorized by the Comptroller.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland; Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Board
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Board, its authorized contractors, and Maryland business entities subject to retirement savings program requirements
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The Comptroller's Office can handle the expanded disclosure authorization with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly authorizes the Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Board, which administers the MarylandSaves program, and its contractors to receive specific business tax information from the Comptroller to administer the program.

The bill amends Maryland tax disclosure statutes to authorize the Comptroller to disclose designated business entity tax information to the Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Board under specified conditions and safeguards.

The State Treasurer's Office works closely with state savings initiatives and provided analysis regarding how accessing this tax information streamlines business registration and tracking for the program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the governing body of a county or municipality to regulate invasive bamboo by ordinance. Permits local ordinances to prohibit selling or planting invasive bamboo. Permits ordinances to prohibit growing invasive bamboo without proper upkeep and containment measures, including barriers or trenches. Authorizes local governing bodies to enforce ordinances by requiring mitigation of damages caused by invasive bamboo. Authorizes local governments to establish civil fines for violations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governing bodies of counties and municipalities
qa_results.stakeholders: Property owners growing invasive bamboo, plant retailers and nurseries, landscaping businesses, and neighboring property owners
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. County and municipal governments can implement regulations using existing resources, with a potential indeterminate increase in local fine revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Agriculture oversees the regulation and classification of invasive plant species (Tier 1 and Tier 2) and regulates plant nurseries and commercial sales statewide, which relates closely to local ordinances restricting the sale and planting of invasive bamboo.

The Department of Natural Resources manages invasive species impacts on Maryland natural habitats and public lands, maintains the statewide list of native plants, and served as an information source for the legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes that ground leases and amendments are not registered until posted on the online state registry. Prohibits unregistered ground lease holders from collecting or attempting to collect ground rent, late fees, interest, or collection costs. Authorizes leasehold tenants to submit affidavits alleging unlawful collection to the State Department of Assessments and Taxation. Requires the Department to notify leaseholders, review responses, and issue decisions on alleged violations. Authorizes either party to file a circuit court action within 45 days of a final administrative decision. Requires the Department to void relevant ground lease registrations upon finding a violation or under court order.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: ground lease holders and leasehold tenants in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Department of Assessments and Taxation and Judiciary operations can be handled with existing budgeted resources. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a right of action authorizing ground lease holders or leasehold tenants to file a de novo appeal in circuit court following a decision by the State Department of Assessments and Taxation, requiring the courts to adjudicate these cases and issue orders regarding ground lease registrations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals a prohibition against leasehold tenants submitting redemption documentation and payments earlier than 90 days after website posting. Applies to tenants seeking to redeem or extinguish residential ground rents through the State Department of Assessments and Taxation. Authorizes the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City to submit required materials early for abandoned or distressed properties. Requires the Department to issue a certificate after notice has remained posted online for at least 90 days. Conditions certificate issuance on receipt of all required documentation, fees, redemption amounts, and past due ground rent.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: leasehold tenants of residential ground leases, ground lease holders, and the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Likely generates operational efficiencies for the State Department of Assessments and Taxation but is not anticipated to materially affect State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Administrative Office of the Courts is identified as an information source in the fiscal note. The underlying statutory provisions governing ground rent redemption and extinguishment involve the circuit courts for interpleader actions and valuation disputes, although the bill's procedural timing changes primarily streamline the process before the State Department of Assessments and Taxation without imposing a significant operational impact on the courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters mandatory property insurance requirements maintained by a condominium council of unit owners. Limits mandatory council property insurance coverage to common elements for detached condominium units. Maintains required council coverage on common elements and units for attached or multifamily dwelling units. Requires owners of residential, detached units to carry homeowners insurance on the entire unit. Restricts insurance proceeds disbursements for damaged units to condominiums with attached or multifamily units.
qa_results.responsible_party: Council of Unit Owners
qa_results.stakeholders: Condominium councils of unit owners, owners of detached condominium units, owners of attached or multifamily condominium units, and property insurers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters mandatory property insurance coverage requirements for condominium associations and establishes a statutory requirement for owners of detached condominium units to carry homeowners insurance, directly impacting the types and terms of property and casualty insurance policies regulated by the Maryland Insurance Administration.

The Secretary of State is the primary state entity responsible for the registration and oversight of condominium regimes in Maryland, which are directly governed by the condominium provisions modified by this bill.

The Administrative Office of the Courts provided information for the fiscal analysis and oversees the judicial branch, which adjudicates property dispute claims and disputes arising under the Maryland Condominium Act.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes pet protection procedures during evictions and real property repossession actions. Requires the Maryland Department of Agriculture to publish a pet care eviction fact sheet by October 1, 2023. Requires landlords knowing a tenant has a pet to provide the fact sheet link at lease execution. Requires the Maryland Judiciary to include the fact sheet link with specified warrants. Mandates that executing officials inspect for pets and contact shelters if occupants are absent. Prohibits leaving a removed pet on public property or a public right-of-way.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture; Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: Residential tenants with pets, residential landlords, property owners, sheriffs, constables, animal shelters, and animal rescue organizations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact; the Maryland Department of Agriculture and the Maryland Judiciary can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the Department of Agriculture develop, publish on its website, and regularly update a fact sheet providing information on how a person may care for and protect pets in the event of an eviction or loss of possession of real property.

The bill requires the Maryland Judiciary to include a link to the Department of Agriculture's pet protection fact sheet on warrants issued for failure to pay rent, breach of lease, tenant holding over, and wrongful detainer actions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the chief executive officer of a municipality to provide notice of a proposed charter amendment through an alternative delivery method. Allows publishing a fair summary in a newspaper at least once and delivering a copy to every municipal residence. Permits delivery by hand, mail, or inclusion in a printed newsletter or regular municipal publication. Requires the municipality to maintain delivery records under its records retention schedule and make them publicly available. Extends the required posting duration for petition-initiated charter amendments from four weeks to at least 40 days before a referendum.
qa_results.responsible_party: Chief executive officer of each Maryland municipality; Maryland municipal governments
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents of Maryland municipalities and municipal officials
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Municipal expenditures and revenues are not materially affected.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to establish an Express Lane Eligibility Program by January 1, 2025. It enrolls individuals in the Maryland Medical Assistance Program and Maryland Children's Health Program based on SNAP eligibility. Prohibits the department from considering any other income or eligibility requirements. Requires the department to apply for federal Section 1115 waivers if needed to maximize eligible residents. Authorizes the department to implement express lane eligibility for renewals before initial enrollments. Requires the Workgroup on Low-Income Utility Assistance to submit a final report by January 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Workgroup on Low-Income Utility Assistance
qa_results.stakeholders: Low-income individuals and children receiving Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program benefits who are eligible for Medicaid or the Maryland Children's Health Program; low-income utility customers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate impact on Maryland Department of Health revenues and expenditures to implement the Express Lane Eligibility Program, though new costs are subject to a 61% federal matching rate. The Workgroup on Low-Income Utility Assistance can complete its final report using existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 111 directly mandates the Maryland Department of Health to establish an Express Lane Eligibility Program by January 1, 2025, to enroll individuals into Medicaid and the Maryland Children's Health Program based on SNAP eligibility determinations, including applying for any necessary federal § 1115 waivers.

DHS administers the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), whose eligibility findings serve as the foundation for the Express Lane Eligibility Program, requiring DHS to enter into data use agreements with MDH. Additionally, DHS staffs the Workgroup on Low-Income Utility Assistance, whose final reporting deadline is extended under the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the statutory reporting requirement for the Workgroup on Low-Income Utility Assistance, requiring it to submit a final report of study, findings, and recommendations by January 1, 2024.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes an Ocean City promoter’s license in Worcester County. Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners for Worcester County to issue the license to a for-profit organization. Allows the licensee to sell and serve beer, wine, and liquor at entertainment events on specified town-owned premises. Requires event premises to be within Ocean City and designated and approved in writing by the Ocean City Police Department. Authorizes the board to adopt regulations restricting annual licenses and establishing health and safety standards. Sets the promoter's license fee at $5,000 per entertainment event.
qa_results.responsible_party: Worcester County Board of License Commissioners; Ocean City Police Department
qa_results.stakeholders: for-profit entertainment event promoters in Ocean City, the Town of Ocean City, and the Worcester County government
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Worcester County revenues increase by approximately $25,000 in fiscal 2024 from an estimated five licenses issued at $5,000 per event. Additional local enforcement activity can be absorbed within existing county resources. No state fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the alcohol industry and administers state alcohol and sales taxes. While this bill specifically authorizes the local Worcester County Board of License Commissioners to issue promoter licenses for events in Ocean City with no direct state fiscal impact, it relates generally to the regulation of alcoholic beverage sales in the state.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits requiring leasehold tenants of unregistered ground leases to hold more than 3 years of ground rent in escrow. Requires ground lease holders to mail possession notices, installment bills, and transfer notices by first-class and certified mail. Prohibits ground lease holders from requiring leasehold tenants to reimburse costs incurred in providing required notices and bills. Requires the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to develop and publish mandatory forms for notices and bills. Requires transferees of ground leases to notify the department and tenants within 30 days of a transfer.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
