qa_results.stakeholders: Ground lease holders, ground lease transferees, and leasehold tenants in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The State Department of Assessments and Taxation can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources, resulting in no material impact on State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes strict pre-filing notice, billing, and documentation requirements for ground lease holders seeking to file civil actions for possession in Maryland courts, directly impacting civil case filings and procedures administered by the judicial branch.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires mental health treatment plans in health care facilities to include a long-range discharge goal and estimated length of stay. Requires direct-care facility staff to reassess treatment plans every 15 days initially and every 60 days thereafter. Requires facilities to offer patients opportunities to authorize family members or other individuals to participate in treatment meetings. Authorizes patients or authorized individuals to request reviews of treatment plans and file grievances through the Resident Grievance System. Authorizes appeals of grievance reconsiderations to the Maryland Department of Health's Healthcare System Chief Medical Officer. Requires the Department to submit an annual report to the General Assembly on the Resident Grievance System starting in 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals admitted to mental health facilities, their family members and designated representatives, facility treatment staff, and health care providers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate increase in general fund expenditures for additional Maryland Department of Health staff to manage reviews, reconsiderations, and appeals, as well as potential costs for providing treatment outside State facilities. Specific dollar figures are unavailable. Revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) directly oversees State mental health facilities, administers the Resident Grievance System, is tasked with adopting regulations for the new appeals process to its Healthcare System's Chief Medical Officer, and must submit an annual report to the General Assembly on grievances received.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes certain plug-in electric drive vehicles with permits to use high-occupancy vehicle lanes regardless of passenger occupancy. Applies only to plug-in electric drive vehicles capable of maximum speeds of at least 65 miles per hour. Requires the Motor Vehicle Administration to charge a permit fee not exceeding $20. Authorizes the Motor Vehicle Administration to limit permit quantities upon recommendation of the State Highway Administration. Requires both administrations jointly to report annually by January 1 on the permit program's traffic effects. Terminates the authorization on September 30, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration; State Highway Administration; Department of State Police
qa_results.stakeholders: owners and drivers of plug-in electric drive vehicles capable of at least 65 miles per hour; Maryland motorists using high-occupancy vehicle lanes
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund revenues increase through fiscal 2026 from permit fees capped at $20 (potentially up to $380,000 for roughly 19,000 projected permits). Transportation Trust Fund expenditures increase minimally through fiscal 2026 by up to $26,220 to purchase decals.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MVA is the primary implementing agency tasked with issuing the plug-in electric vehicle HOV permits, collecting permit fees of up to $20, procuring decals, consulting on permit design, and submitting an annual report jointly with SHA.

SHA designates HOV lanes, may consult on permit design, provides recommendations to MVA to limit permit issuance to avoid operational degradation of HOV lanes, and co-authors the annual report to the Governor and General Assembly.
MDOT is the parent department of both MVA and SHA; the bill directly impacts the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) through permit fee revenues and decal expenditures.
The Department of State Police is authorized to consult with MVA and SHA regarding the design of the HOV permit and enforces traffic regulations on state highways.
The Governor's Office receives the required annual report submitted jointly by MVA and SHA evaluating the effect of the permits on HOV lane operations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals numerous statutory reporting mandates identified as obsolete, duplicative, or unnecessary across multiple state agencies. Modifies submission deadlines and reporting frequencies for specified annual reports submitted to the General Assembly and the Governor. Transfers primary reporting responsibilities for certain programs between designated state departments. Requires the Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center to publish graphic data dashboards on higher education experiences. Consolidates individual state agency telework reporting under the Department of Budget and Management.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Budget and Management; Department of Human Services; Department of the Environment; Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Higher Education Commission; Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center; Alcohol and Tobacco Commission; Comptroller; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; Maryland Technology Development Corporation
qa_results.stakeholders: State agencies, commissions, boards, and institutions of higher education subject to statutory reporting requirements; the General Assembly; the Governor
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State or local finances. Certain State agencies may experience operational efficiencies from the repeal, rescheduling, or consolidation of mandated reports.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Centralizes the annual state employee telework reporting requirement under DBM rather than having every individual state department or unit submit separate reports.
Modifies multiple statutory reporting deadlines and requirements regarding climate change status, solid waste diversion, and Bay Restoration Fund projects.
Transfers primary responsibility for collecting and submitting reports on state-funded home visiting programs to MDH and repeals obsolete health-related reports.
Repeals several obsolete and unnecessary annual reporting requirements to the Joint Committee on Pensions concerning rehired retirees.
Modifies annual reporting requirements for the Community College Promise Scholarship program and repeals obsolete reporting mandates related to Complete College America.
Reduces reporting frequency from quarterly to biannually and repeals a duplicative annual reporting requirement regarding the Maryland Technology Incubator Program.
Repeals unnecessary annual reporting requirements concerning service of process on nonresident drivers and organ donor designations on driver's licenses.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Removes the requirement to collect and report inmates' places of birth and repeals an obsolete annual report on the P.R.O.T.E.C.T. program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Transfers home visiting program reporting oversight to the Department of Health and repeals annual reporting requirements under the P.R.O.T.E.C.T. program.

Repeals several obsolete and unnecessary mandated reports for USM entities, including the Board of Regents report on business entities, the UMCEED report, the UMBC internship report, and the UMD School of Nursing Wellmobile report.
Repeals a duplicative statutory requirement for the Board to submit an annual report on the state procurement system.
Adjusts annual reporting deadlines regarding licensed beer manufacturer production and sales to December 1.
Alters the reporting frequency regarding minority business enterprise participation under the Energy Efficient Homes Construction Loan Program from semiannual to annual.
Formally designates DHS as the primary reporting entity for the annual report on the progress of implementing the outcomes evaluation system.
Shifts annual reporting deadlines to the Governor and General Assembly from October 1 to December 1 to accommodate CPA certification schedules.
Modifies data dashboard and reporting requirements concerning dually enrolled high school students, foster care recipients, and homeless youth in higher education.
Modifies the deadline for a joint annual report with MDE regarding wastewater treatment upgrades and requires precinct boundary descriptions to be received electronically.
Repeals an unnecessary reporting mandate regarding consumer complaints and protections related to Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) services.
Repeals an obsolete statutory reporting requirement regarding corporate headquarters loan and grant compliance under the Economic Development Opportunities Program Account.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Repeals an unnecessary and obsolete reporting requirement concerning employee demographic data for video lottery facility licensees in Baltimore City.
Repeals the requirement for an independent certified public accountant to submit annual audit reports of the Commission to the Department of Legislative Services.
Alters the reporting schedule of the Frederick County LYNX High School evaluation report submitted to the State Board of Education from annual to every odd-numbered year.
Repeals an underutilized annual reporting mandate regarding alternative financing mechanisms used for public school construction projects.
Requires the State Administrator of Elections to transmit precinct boundary descriptions and maps to state entities electronically rather than by physical documentation.
Modifies the annual reporting deadline for the Governor's report to the General Assembly regarding Cigarette Restitution Fund program expenditures.
Modifies the reporting frequency and establishes a specific deadline for the solid waste and recycling study conducted in coordination with MDE.
Repeals an obsolete annual reporting requirement under the P.R.O.T.E.C.T. program.
Repeals an obsolete annual reporting requirement under the P.R.O.T.E.C.T. program.
Adjusts the applicable multi-year reporting period for specified 9-1-1 personnel and transition updates submitted by the Maryland 9-1-1 Board.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits the District Court from ordering an individual to appear for an examination to enforce a small claims judgment. Prohibits the court from ordering an individual to answer interrogatories in aid of judgment execution. Limits post-judgment discovery methods available to creditors seeking to collect on small claims judgments. These statutory changes take effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: District Court of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Judgment debtors and judgment creditors in District Court small claims actions, including small businesses seeking debt collection
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on state or local finances. District Court operational adjustments, such as updating forms, brochures, and webpages, can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters procedures in the District Court by prohibiting judges from ordering individuals to appear for examinations or answer interrogatories in aid of enforcement of money judgments resulting from small claims actions. The Administrative Office of the Courts must implement these operational changes and update District Court forms, brochures, and webpages.

qa_results.bill_summary: Converts enhanced underinsured motorist coverage from an opt-in option to an opt-out default for private passenger motor vehicle liability insurance. Requires insurers to provide enhanced coverage on new policies issued on or after July 1, 2024, unless affirmatively waived in writing. Prohibits a waiver from taking effect unless the insurer first provides written notice of the coverage's nature, benefit, and cost. Requires waivers to be executed on a form required by the Insurance Commissioner. Directs the Maryland Insurance Administration to study the conversion's impact and submit reports by December 2026 and December 2028.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Private passenger motor vehicle liability insurers and policyholders purchasing or renewing private passenger motor vehicle liability insurance in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration in FY 2024 from the $125 rate and form filing fee. Potential minimal increase in State general fund revenues from the 2% insurance premium tax due to higher overall premiums. The Maryland Insurance Administration can conduct the study and complete required reports using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIA is the primary regulatory agency tasked with implementing the bill. It is responsible for prescribing the required waiver and offer forms, reviewing rate and form filings from insurers, and conducting a multi-year study with interim and final reports on the impact of moving EUIM coverage to an opt-out default.

MAIF issues private passenger motor vehicle liability policies as the insurer of last resort in Maryland, is subject to the statutory insurance requirements regarding underinsured motorist coverage, and is explicitly referenced in the bill's provisions regarding order of recovery priority.

The Maryland Insurance Administration is required to submit an interim report by December 31, 2026, and a final report by December 31, 2028, to the Governor detailing the findings and recommendations of the EUIM study.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the criminal prohibition against unnatural or perverted sexual practices. Replaces statutory references to unnatural or perverted sexual practices with any other sexual conduct that is a crime. Retains prior convictions as qualifying offenses for human trafficking victims seeking to vacate judgments. Prohibits expungement of prior convictions committed without consent, with minors under age 16, or involving incapacitated individuals. Maintains Tier III sex offender registration requirements for prior offenses committed with force or threat of force. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Judiciary; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals previously charged or convicted under prior unnatural or perverted sexual practice statutes, human trafficking victims, criminal justice entities, and sex offender registry officials
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals a criminal offense and modifies statutory provisions regarding criminal proceedings, motions to vacate judgments for human trafficking victims, and court record expungement petitions, directly impacting judicial administration and case tracking.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department oversees state correctional facilities, community supervision, criminal history records, and sex offender registration requirements, which are modified under the bill's Tier III sex offender provisions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The office represents indigent defendants charged with crimes, files motions to vacate convictions for human trafficking survivors, and assists clients with petitions for expungement affected by the repeal.

As the primary state law enforcement agency and repository for central criminal records, MSP is responsible for adjusting enforcement practices and complying with expungement orders for police records.

The bill amends the definition of sexual molestation and exploitation under Family Law and child welfare provisions governing Child in Need of Assistance (CINA) and protective services administered by local social services departments.
The State Archives was consulted regarding the bill due to its role in maintaining permanent court and government records subject to statutory expungement provisions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters qualifications for a journeyman license to provide heating, ventilation, air-conditioning, and refrigeration services. Increases the required duration an applicant must hold an apprentice license from three years to four years. Raises the required training hours under a licensed contractor from at least 1,875 hours to 6,000 hours. Maintains the requirement that an applicant pass an examination administered by the Board.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Heating, Ventilation, Air-Conditioning, and Refrigeration Contractors; Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Heating, ventilation, air-conditioning, and refrigeration (HVACR) apprentices seeking journeyman licenses, licensed HVACR contractors, and businesses training apprentices
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund licensing revenues may be delayed if applicants spend more time in training before applying, but State finances and operations are not materially affected. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor directly regulates HVACR licensing through the State Board of Heating, Ventilation, Air-Conditioning, and Refrigeration Contractors, and oversees the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Program within its Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning. The bill alters statutory training hours and experience requirements for obtaining an HVACR journeyman license.

qa_results.bill_summary: Limits the amount the Secretary of Labor may deduct from future weekly benefits to recover nonfraud overpayments. Authorizes deductions of up to 50% of the weekly benefit amount from future weekly benefits payable. Restricts the deduction to up to 25% if the weekly benefit amount is $100 or less. Maintains existing alternative collection methods, including civil suits, assessments, and debt collection under State or federal law. Takes effect April 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Unemployment insurance claimants who received nonfraud benefit overpayments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Labor can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources, incurring a one-time administrative programming cost of $16,400 in fiscal 2024 funded by existing or additional federal funds. Nonbudgeted Unemployment Insurance Trust Fund expenditures increase and revenues increase as alternative recovery methods are used; the net impact on the trust fund is unknown but expected to be negative. Local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor's Division of Unemployment Insurance directly administers the State's unemployment insurance program. The bill restricts the Secretary of Labor's ability to recover non-fraud overpayments by capping weekly benefit deductions, requires the Secretary to adopt implementing regulations, and impacts the Unemployment Insurance Trust Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Renames the Commission on LGBTQ Affairs in the Governor's Office of Community Initiatives to the Commission on LGBTQIA+ Affairs. Expands the Commission's membership from 15 to 21 members appointed by the Governor with Senate advice and consent. Establishes staggered four-year terms for Commission members expiring in 2024, 2025, and 2026. Broadens appointment criteria to reflect additional forms of diversity including age, disability, and socioeconomic status. Directs the Commission to assess challenges, study best practices, and collect State agency data regarding LGBTQIA+ communities.
qa_results.responsible_party: Commission on LGBTQIA+ Affairs; Governor's Office of Community Initiatives
qa_results.stakeholders: LGBTQIA+ individuals and communities in Maryland, and members of the Commission on LGBTQIA+ Affairs
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures for expense reimbursements for additional commission members can be absorbed with existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Commission on LGBTQIA+ Affairs is explicitly housed as a unit within the Governor's Office of Community Initiatives, which provides administrative support and oversight to the commission.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the composition, member qualifications, terms, and duties of the Commission on LGBTQIA+ Affairs, an executive commission.

The bill increases the number of Commission members from 15 to 21, sets new qualification criteria, and establishes staggered terms, directly impacting the Office of Appointments' duties to recruit and vet gubernatorial appointees.
The Governor is responsible for appointing the 21 members of the Commission with the advice and consent of the Senate, and holds the authority to remove members for cause.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires individuals whose inactive real estate licenses expire to satisfy initial licensing qualifications to obtain a new license. Applies when a real estate broker, associate broker, or salesperson fails to reactivate within three years. Mandates compliance with statutory application, examination, and prelicensing education requirements under state law. Retains existing reactivation procedures for inactive licensees who apply before the three-year expiration period ends. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Real Estate Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed real estate brokers, associate real estate brokers, and real estate salespersons holding inactive licenses
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not materially affected, as the Maryland Real Estate Commission can implement procedural changes using existing budgeted resources. Local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Real Estate Commission is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor's Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing. The department oversees professional licensing standards and will implement the procedural requirements for real estate brokers seeking licensure after inactive status expiration.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts certain applicants for a change of resident agent from public hearing requirements in Howard County. Applies to license holders seeking to become resident agents for their existing alcoholic beverages license. Requires that the applicant previously appeared and received approval at a nonviolation hearing for the same license. Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners to hold a hearing if it determines good cause exists. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Howard County
qa_results.stakeholders: alcoholic beverages license holders in Howard County seeking to become resident agents
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State finances or local revenues. Howard County expenditures decrease by up to approximately $14,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2024 due to reduced hearing costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry. While this legislation amends the Alcoholic Beverages Article, it specifically alters hearing notice and public hearing requirements administered by the Howard County Board of License Commissioners with no state-level regulatory or fiscal impact.

qa_results.bill_summary: Designates the Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning to approve electrician apprenticeship programs. Replaces inactive licensing status with uninsured status throughout the Maryland Electricians Act. Prohibits contracting for electrical services unless covered by specified general liability and property damage insurance. Authorizes an uninsured master electrician to provide electrical services only as a journeyperson electrician in certain counties. Requires the State Board of Electricians to specify on each license whether the holder meets insurance requirements.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Electricians; Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning
qa_results.stakeholders: licensed master electricians, journeyperson electricians, apprentice electricians, electrical inspectors, and electrical services businesses
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State revenues. The State Board of Electricians can implement the bill's administrative changes with existing resources. There is no material impact on local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor directly oversees professional licensing—including the State Board of Electricians—and houses the Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning (DWDAL), which is designated under the bill as the approving entity for electrician apprenticeship programs and continuing education.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes that adaptive reuse of existing buildings to develop affordable multifamily housing is an eligible loan use. Applies to any Department of Housing and Community Development program awarding loans for affordable multifamily housing development. Specifies that more specific program laws or regulations govern when they establish distinct adaptive reuse rules. Requires the Department to notify covered loan applicants that adaptive reuse is an eligible use of loan proceeds. Exempts loan applications under Department programs that do not focus on housing from the notice requirement.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: applicants for Department of Housing and Community Development housing loans, affordable housing developers, and individuals in need of affordable multifamily housing
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material impact on State or local operations or finances. The Department of Housing and Community Development already finances adaptive reuse projects and can notify loan applicants using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs loan programs administered by the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD), clarifying that adaptive reuse of existing buildings for affordable multifamily housing is an eligible use of loan proceeds and requiring DHCD to notify loan applicants of this eligibility.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires residential landlords to notify tenants in writing in advance of rent increases. Establishes advance notification timelines ranging from 7 to 90 days based on the length of the tenancy. Prohibits lease provisions requiring tenants to accept electronic delivery of rent increase notices. Prohibits landlords from conditioning lease application acceptance on electing electronic delivery. Requires local jurisdictions enacting rent increase limits to report bill details and multifamily rental building permit data to the General Assembly.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland General Assembly; local jurisdictions (counties and municipalities)
qa_results.stakeholders: residential tenants, residential landlords, and county and municipal governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State or local operations or finances, with minimal impact on small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Judiciary adjudicates landlord-tenant disputes and eviction proceedings, which may involve enforcement or defenses related to statutory lease requirements and rent increase notice periods.
The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division enforces state consumer protection and fair housing laws, which encompass residential lease provisions and landlord-tenant practices.
The Department of Housing and Community Development monitors state housing policy, multifamily rental housing conditions, and regulations affecting residential rental communities.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands eligibility for grants under the Urban Agriculture Grant Program to agricultural producers, nonprofit organizations, and institutions of higher education. Broadens the definition of urban agricultural producer to include producers in any census-delineated urban area or municipal corporation. Requires the Governor to appropriate at least $100,000 annually to the Fund for fiscal years 2025 through 2029. Establishes the Urban Agriculture Advisory Committee to recommend grant guidelines, policies, and practices. Requires the committee to report annually to the Governor and designated legislative committees by December 30.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture
qa_results.stakeholders: Urban agricultural producers, nonprofit organizations, and institutions of higher education in urban areas across Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $100,000 annually from fiscal 2025 through 2029 under a mandated appropriation. Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Urban Agriculture Grant Fund increase correspondingly. Local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDA is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the Urban Agriculture Grant Program, managing the Urban Agriculture Grant Fund, providing staff support to the Urban Agriculture Advisory Committee, and determining applicant qualifications.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MARBIDCO is statutorily designated to appoint one member to the newly established Urban Agriculture Advisory Committee.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally establishes the Urban Agriculture Advisory Committee to advise on program guidelines, policies, and practices and to submit an annual report to the Governor and General Assembly.
DBM oversees the state budget and will be responsible for incorporating the bill's mandated annual appropriation of at least $100,000 for fiscal years 2025 through 2029.

The Governor is mandated to include an appropriation of at least $100,000 annually in the state budget for FY 2025 through 2029, and the Governor receives an annual report from the Urban Agriculture Advisory Committee.
The State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold the Urban Agriculture Grant Fund as a separate, nonlapsing special fund.
The Comptroller is statutorily responsible for accounting for the Urban Agriculture Grant Fund.
Public institutions of higher education within USM are made eligible to apply for and receive grant funding and provide farmer training and technical assistance under the expanded program.
As a public institution of higher education, MSU is eligible to qualify for grant funds to provide agricultural training and technical assistance under the program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the voting rights of the student member of the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners. Requires the student member to be an enrolled high school junior or senior. Requires middle and high school students in the Baltimore City Public School System to elect the student member. Authorizes the student member to vote on budgets, school boundaries, and student disciplinary matters. Prohibits the student member from voting on personnel and collective bargaining decisions. Establishes a task force to study board compensation and adding a second student member.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners; Office of the Mayor of Baltimore City; Task Force to Study Compensation and Student Members of the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Middle and high school students in the Baltimore City Public School System, the student member, and members of the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal and absorbable impact on State expenditures for task force travel reimbursements. Baltimore City Public Schools and the Baltimore City Mayor's Office can implement the bill using existing resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill statutorily creates the Task Force to Study Compensation and Student Members of the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners to examine board member compensation, evaluate adding a second student member, and submit recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly.

The Maryland State Department of Education exercises statewide oversight and leadership of Maryland's 24 local school systems, and the bill amends the state Education Article regarding the governance, composition, and voting powers of the Baltimore City local school board.

The Task Force to Study Compensation and Student Members of the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners is required by statute to report its findings and recommendations directly to the Governor by April 1, 2024.

qa_results.bill_summary: Allows an individual who resides anywhere in Maryland to satisfy residency requirements for an alcoholic beverages license in Howard County. Extends this statewide residency qualification to applicants applying on behalf of partnerships, corporations, clubs, and limited liability companies. Alters petition of support provisions to verify Maryland residency instead of county residency. Removes requirements that continuing care retirement community license applicants be Howard County registered voters and taxpayers. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Howard County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license applicants and license holders in Howard County, including partnerships, corporations, clubs, limited liability companies, and Maryland residents seeking county licenses
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The bill is not anticipated to materially affect Howard County finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the alcohol industry in the state and prescribes statewide alcoholic beverages application forms referenced under Article - Alcoholic Beverages § 4-108. However, because the bill specifically alters local residency requirements for alcoholic beverages license applicants in Howard County, the direct impact on the Comptroller is minimal with no state fiscal effect.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits the Northeast Maryland Waste Disposal Authority from issuing bonds beginning June 1, 2023. Requires the Department of Legislative Services to evaluate the Authority and submit draft merger legislation by December 1, 2024. Directs the Maryland Environmental Service to review the Authority's contracts and employees by December 1, 2024. Requires the Maryland Environmental Service to temporarily assume the Authority's functions, employees, and contracts during any merger. Mandates that any entity assuming the Authority's operations establish a system to maintain stakeholder engagement.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Legislative Services; Maryland Environmental Service; Northeast Maryland Waste Disposal Authority
qa_results.stakeholders: Member jurisdictions of the Northeast Maryland Waste Disposal Authority (Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Carroll, Frederick, Harford, Howard, and Montgomery counties and Baltimore City), employees of the Northeast Maryland Waste Disposal Authority, and entities contracting with the Authority
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Nonbudgeted expenditures and matching revenues increase by $100,000 in FY 2024 for the Maryland Environmental Service to conduct the required review. Potential indeterminate increase in general fund expenditures for the Department of Legislative Services in FY 2024 and FY 2025. Potential increase in local expenditures for member jurisdictions via Authority membership fees to cover study costs. Significant potential nonbudgeted expenditure and revenue impacts may occur in FY 2026 or later if the Maryland Environmental Service temporarily assumes Authority functions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 161 directly mandates that the Maryland Environmental Service review the functions, employees, and contracts of the Northeast Maryland Waste Disposal Authority (NMWDA) and report to the General Assembly by December 1, 2024. MES is also required to temporarily assume all functions, employees, and active contracts of NMWDA during any merger, incurring estimated nonbudgeted expenditures of $100,000 in FY 2024.

The bill explicitly requires the evaluation of NMWDA to assess the impact that discontinuing the authority would have on the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS) and the pensions of NMWDA employees.
MDE regulates solid waste management and recycling under the Maryland Recycling Act, which is evaluated under the bill. MDE also served as an information source for the bill's fiscal and policy note.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires membership in the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System for permanent full-time Crisfield police officers if the department participates. Grants transferred officers eligibility and creditable service for their prior employment with the Crisfield Police Department. Terminates their membership and benefit rights in the Employees' Pension System upon joining the system. Exempts the service credit transfer from standard statutory contribution repayment requirements. Directs the transfer of assets and crediting of contributions under existing statutory procedures.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Retirement Agency; Crisfield Police Department
qa_results.stakeholders: permanent full-time local law enforcement officers of the Crisfield Police Department and the City of Crisfield
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Contingent on the City of Crisfield electing to join the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System as a participating governmental unit, local employer pension contributions increase by approximately $120,700 annually and pension liabilities increase by $1.0 million. No effect on local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System, including the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System (LEOPS) and the Employees' Pension System (EPS). The bill directly impacts their administration by governing the membership, service credit transfer, and asset crediting for eligible Crisfield Police Department officers transferring into LEOPS.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the statutory definition of a crime of violence to include sexual abuse of a minor under specified conditions. Applies this classification when an offender is at least 21 years old and the victim is under 16. Requires lifetime sexual offender supervision for adults convicted of child sexual abuse against victims under age 13. Mandates lifetime sexual offender supervision when an offender at least 21 years old abuses a victim under 16. Extends lifetime supervision mandates to adults convicted of specified second-degree sexual offenses occurring before October 1, 2017. Applies all changes prospectively to convictions occurring on or after October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; Division of Parole and Probation
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals convicted of sexual abuse of a minor or second-degree sexual offenses; victims of child sexual abuse; sex offender supervision agents
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in state general fund expenditures beginning in future years due to expanded incarceration and lifetime sexual offender supervision requirements. State revenues and local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS and its Division of Parole and Probation are directly responsible for conducting lifetime sexual offender supervision, managing incarceration and diminution credits for crimes of violence, and adopting regulations to administer the supervision requirements.

The Judiciary and sentencing courts are tasked with imposing the required lifetime supervision conditions at sentencing, reviewing presentence investigations, and adjudicating petitions for discharge from supervision.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD represents indigent defendants facing criminal prosecution, sentencing enhancements, and lifetime supervision requirements expanded under the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of Housing and Community Development to procure or provide energy efficiency and conservation programs for low-income electricity customers. Sets annual incremental gross energy savings targets of 0.53% in 2024, 0.72% in 2025, and 1% in 2026. Mandates approved contractors pay at least 150% of the State minimum wage and provide specified employee benefits. Establishes the Green and Healthy Task Force to coordinate housing resources for low-income communities. Directs the Department and task force to plan energy efficiency retrofits for all low-income households by 2031. Requires a disparity study evaluating remedial measures for minority- and women-owned businesses by December 31, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development; Public Service Commission; Maryland Department of Transportation; Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs
qa_results.stakeholders: Low-income residential electricity customers and tenants; affordable housing owners and managers; electric companies; weatherization and energy efficiency contractors; minority-, women-, and veteran-owned businesses
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures for the Department of Housing and Community Development increase by an estimated $39.8 million in FY 2024, rising to $214.2 million by FY 2028 to meet statutory savings targets. These costs are funded by special fund revenues from EmPOWER Maryland surcharges collected on utility bills, ultimately increasing electricity rates for customers. Local housing authorities and weatherization agencies receive increased program and grant funds.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHCD is the primary implementing agency under the bill, responsible for procuring and providing energy efficiency and conservation programs, achieving incremental gross energy savings targets, submitting triennial plans and biannual updates to the PSC, and staffing and chairing the newly established Green and Healthy Task Force.

PSC oversees the EmPOWER Maryland program, reviews and approves DHCD's triennial energy savings plans, establishes procedures for implementation, and reports annually to the General Assembly on low-income energy efficiency programs.

MEA is consulted on PSC's annual report, required to apply for all available federal funding to implement the bill, and serves as a designated member on the Green and Healthy Task Force, with potential special fund expenditure impacts.

As the State's designated MBE certification agency under the Board of Public Works, MDOT is tasked alongside GOSBA with conducting a disparity study regarding energy efficiency and conservation services by December 31, 2025.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOSBA is mandated, in conjunction with the State's certification agency (MDOT), to initiate and submit a disparity study on minority- and women-owned businesses in the energy efficiency and conservation sector.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill statutorily creates the Green and Healthy Task Force to meet quarterly for three years to coordinate resources and develop policy recommendations for healthy, energy-efficient housing for low-income households.
DHCD is required to coordinate directly with DBM to identify additional funding sources to support whole-home energy efficiency and safety upgrade program expansions.
The Secretary of Human Services (or a designee) is designated by statute as a formal voting member of the Green and Healthy Task Force.
A representative from the Office of People's Counsel is designated to serve as a member of the Green and Healthy Task Force.
OAG must be consulted by MDOT and GOSBA during the execution of the required disparity study on energy efficiency contracting.
The Secretary of Health is designated as an official recipient of the annual findings and recommendations reported by the Green and Healthy Task Force.
The Secretary of the Environment is designated as an official recipient of the annual findings and recommendations reported by the Green and Healthy Task Force.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the State Board of Physicians to approve licensed athletic trainers to perform dry needling as a specialized task. Requires applicants to complete at least 80 hours of approved continuing education instruction. Mandates at least 40 hours of didactic coursework and 40 hours of practical, hands-on instruction. Requires hands-on training under the guidance of a licensed practitioner with at least five years of dry needling experience. Subjects athletic trainers who perform dry needling without Board approval to disciplinary action.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Physicians
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed athletic trainers and patients receiving athletic training services in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by $31,893 in fiscal 2024 and $6,400 in fiscal 2025 for a part-time contractual analyst and one-time licensing software modifications. Special fund revenues may increase if the Board establishes an approval fee. No local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Maryland Board of Physicians, a licensing board within the Department of Health, by requiring it to establish an approval process, verify training requirements, handle specialized applications, and enforce disciplinary standards for licensed athletic trainers performing dry needling.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires an assistant State’s Attorney with knowledge of a case to meet with a victim of sexually assaultive behavior. The requirement also permits meeting with a representative designated by the victim. The meeting must take place within 20 days after receiving a request from the victim. The obligation applies when prosecutors decide not to file charges or dismiss charges against an alleged suspect. The assistant State’s Attorney must explain the justification for not filing charges or for dismissing charges. Participants may conduct the meeting in person, by telephone, or by other mutually agreed means.
qa_results.responsible_party: Offices of the State's Attorney
qa_results.stakeholders: victims of sexually assaultive behavior, designated victim representatives, and assistant State's Attorneys
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not materially affected. Local State's Attorneys' offices can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. Local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy (GOCPP) serves as Maryland's primary coordinating body for public safety and oversees statewide victim services policies and funding. The bill expands crime victims' rights by requiring prosecutors to meet with victims of sexually assaultive behavior when charges are dropped or declined.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the student member of the Baltimore County Board of Education to vote on capital and operating budget matters. Requires each student member to complete budget training within two months of election to vote on budgetary matters. Requires a workgroup of board members and school executive leadership to develop a draft budget training curriculum. Mandates submission of the draft curriculum to the county board for review by December 31, 2023. Requires the training to focus on budget processes and be facilitated by the Division of Business Services.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore County Board of Education; Baltimore County Public School System
qa_results.stakeholders: Student members of the Baltimore County Board of Education and Baltimore County public school students
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. Baltimore County Public Schools and the Baltimore County Board of Education can develop and implement the training curriculum using existing local resources, with no impact on local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education oversees the state's public education system and local school boards. While the bill specifically governs voting rights and budget training requirements for the student member of the Baltimore County Board of Education with no direct state fiscal impact, it relates to the statutory framework and governance of a local school system under the Education Article.

qa_results.bill_summary: Designates Maryland Rye or Maryland Rye Whiskey as the official State spirit. Adds the designation to the list of official State symbols in the General Provisions Article. Renumbers existing statutory sections within the subtitle to accommodate the addition. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Archives
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland distillers, rye farmers, and spirits producers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Archives maintains official state records, state symbols, and the Maryland Manual On-Line, and served as the informational source regarding official State symbols for this legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the deadline to file a Maryland estate tax return solely to elect deceased spousal unused exclusion portability. Replaces the former two-year deadline with the time period prescribed under federal estate tax law. Requires the Comptroller to adopt regulations ensuring the State and federal election deadlines are identical. Applies retroactively to affect decedents dying on or after January 1, 2019. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Surviving spouses and personal representatives or executors of decedents' estates electing estate tax exclusion portability
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential general fund revenue decrease beginning in FY 2024 due to increased use of the deceased spousal unused exclusion election. Administrative costs for the Comptroller's Office to update forms and adopt regulations will be absorbed with existing budgeted resources. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Comptroller with administering the Maryland estate tax return deadlines for the deceased spousal unused exclusion (DSUE) portability election, updating tax forms and instructions, and adopting regulations to align the state filing period with federal standards.

The Register of Wills administers probate estates and collects inheritance taxes; the statute references the registers' role in certifying inheritance tax paid to the Comptroller in relation to amended estate tax returns, and the agency was consulted for the bill's fiscal analysis.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters eligibility for and the amount of the Maryland income tax subtraction modification for adopting a child. Sets the subtraction modification at $12,000 for adopting a child with a special need. Sets the subtraction modification at $10,000 for adopting a child without a special need. Requires adoptions to occur through a private, nonprofit, licensed adoption agency or a public child welfare agency. Repeals prior limits based on whether the child is a State resident at adoption. Applies to all taxable years beginning after December 31, 2022.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland taxpayers adopting a child; adoptive parents; adopted children with or without special needs; private, nonprofit, licensed adoption agencies; public child welfare agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by an estimated $91,000 annually beginning in FY 2024. State general fund expenditures increase by $43,000 in FY 2024 only for one-time tax system alterations by the Comptroller's Office. Local income tax revenues decrease by an estimated $54,000 annually beginning in FY 2024.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is responsible for collecting state income taxes and administering tax modifications. The bill alters the personal income tax subtraction modification for adoption expenses, requiring one-time computer system changes that will cost the Comptroller's Office $43,000 in FY 2024.

The Department of Human Services oversees Maryland's foster care and public adoption services, including public child welfare agencies and determining whether a child has special needs under the relevant federal Social Security Act standards cited in the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a county or municipality to execute and record a restrictive covenant modification for property within its boundaries. Applies to recorded covenants or restrictions that unlawfully restrict ownership based on race, religious belief, or national origin. Requires the county or municipality to provide written notice by first-class mail to all property owners. Mandates that this notice be sent at least 30 days before executing and recording the modification. Allows a property owner to decline the modification by notifying the local government within 30 days after notice. Excludes unlawfully restrictive covenants in declarations, general schemes, or development plans of homeowners associations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Counties and Municipalities; Clerks of the Circuit Court; County Attorneys; Administrative Office of the Courts
qa_results.stakeholders: Property owners whose deeds or chains of title contain unlawfully restrictive covenants; Maryland counties and municipalities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State operations or finances. Local government expenditures and operational impacts are anticipated to be minimal and absorbable within existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill interacts directly with the land recording processes of the Circuit Court Clerks, and the restrictive covenant modifications must be accompanied by an intake sheet on a form provided and maintained by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes employees of specified State higher education institutions and the Maryland Department of Transportation to initiate grievances for wage reporting failures. Allows exclusive representatives of covered employees to initiate these grievance procedures. Requires decision makers in grievance proceedings to award statutory damages when wages are improperly withheld. Mandates that employee grievance procedures for these entities provide redress and damages for wage reporting violations. Requires grievances to be initiated within 20 days after the failure to pay, or within six months if undiscovered. Caps damages at three times the amount of wage due that an appointing authority failed to report.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation; University System of Maryland; Morgan State University; St. Mary's College of Maryland; Baltimore City Community College
qa_results.stakeholders: Employees and exclusive representatives of the Maryland Department of Transportation, University System of Maryland, Morgan State University, St. Mary's College of Maryland, and Baltimore City Community College
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate, but anticipated to be minimal, increase in Transportation Trust Fund and higher education expenditures for potential grievance filings and damage payments. Reimbursable expenditures and revenues for the Office of Administrative Hearings increase to the extent additional grievance cases are referred and adjudicated.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly amends the Transportation Article (§ 2-103.4) requiring MDOT to update its regulations and human resources management grievance procedures to include redress and damages for wage and payroll reporting violations.

The bill amends the Education Article (§ 13-201 and § 13-203) governing USM employee grievances, expanding grievance definitions to include wage withholding violations and mandating that decision-makers award damages.
The bill amends the Education Article (§ 14-302) to require decision-makers in grievance procedures at Morgan State University to award damages for wage withholding violations.

The bill amends the Education Article (§ 14-408) requiring the personnel system and grievance procedures of St. Mary's College of Maryland to provide redress and damage awards for wage payment violations.

The bill affects grievance appeal procedures that are referred to the Office of Administrative Hearings for adjudication, resulting in an increase in reimbursable expenditures and revenues per case heard.

As the state's principal personnel agency managing state employee systems and policies, DBM oversees general State Personnel Management System grievance frameworks and provided estimates on grievance hearing costs.
The Central Payroll Bureau operates under the Comptroller of Maryland, receiving reported payroll information and processing missing wages and damages following resolved grievances.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the State Board of Education to identify methods to find and eliminate corporal punishment of students statewide. Prohibits the Board from issuing certificates of approval to noncollegiate educational institutions lacking corporal punishment prohibition policies. Excludes institutions operated by bona fide church organizations from the certificate of approval requirement. Requires regulations for family child care homes and large family child care homes to prohibit corporal punishment. Mandates that child care center licensing and operating regulations prohibit corporal punishment to discipline a child.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Education; Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Noncollegiate educational institutions, family child care homes, large family child care homes, child care centers, and enrolled children and students
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Education and the Maryland State Department of Education can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources, with no effect on revenues or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 185 directly tasks the State Board of Education and the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) with updating statewide plans to eliminate corporal punishment, conditioning certificates of approval for nonpublic educational institutions on corporal punishment prohibitions, and adopting regulations prohibiting physical discipline in registered and licensed child care facilities.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Governor’s Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services to help support victim services programs statewide. Authorizes the office to award grants to public or private nonprofit organizations operating victim services programs. Requires the Governor to include an annual budget appropriation that, with prior-year federal funds, totals $60,000,000. Prohibits requiring programs to match state funds and prohibits using awarded funds for capital projects. Requires the Executive Director to submit an annual report to the General Assembly by December 31.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Victims of crime, crime victim services programs, and public or private nonprofit organizations providing victim services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Establishes a mandated aggregate appropriation of $60.0 million combining federal VOCA funds and State funds beginning in FY 2025. General fund expenditures are not anticipated to be affected assuming federal VOCA grants and current State funding levels remain steady. Local government revenues and expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy (identified in the bill as the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services) is the primary administering agency responsible for supporting victim services programs, awarding grants, coordinating with federal VOCA funds, consulting stakeholder groups, and submitting an annual report to the General Assembly.

The bill places a statutory mandate on the Governor to include an appropriation in the annual state budget bill that, in combination with federal VOCA awards from the prior year, totals $60.0 million for crime victim services programs.

As the principal agency responsible for formulating and executing the state budget, the Department of Budget and Management must incorporate and oversee the statutory mandated appropriation totaling $60.0 million in aggregate funding.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the Wildlife Advisory Commission from nine to 10 members appointed by the Governor. Requires the Governor to appoint an academic researcher with expertise in wildlife biology, conservation, management, or ecology. Mandates commission representation from the farming, hunting, wildlife preservation, and passive wildlife recreation communities. Establishes a four-year term for the new academic member beginning July 1, 2024. Prohibits altering the terms of commission members serving as of October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor; Department of Natural Resources; Wildlife Advisory Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Wildlife Advisory Commission members, academic researchers in wildlife sciences, farmers, hunters, wildlife preservation advocates, and passive wildlife recreationists
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Wildlife Advisory Commission is established within the Department of Natural Resources to advise on wildlife management, conservation, and recreational use policies.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the statutory size, qualifications, terms, and stakeholder representation requirements of the Wildlife Advisory Commission.
The Governor is tasked with soliciting nominations and appointing the additional member who meets specific academic researcher criteria, as well as maintaining stakeholder balance on the commission.

The Office of Appointments vets and manages nominations and candidate selections for state boards and commissions on behalf of the Governor to fulfill the bill's new statutory appointment requirements.

qa_results.bill_summary: Clarifies language governing automatic expungement of records for specified offenses with qualifying dispositions. Applies provisions to specified civil cannabis offenses and crimes other than non-appearance transportation violations. Requires expungement three years after disposition if charges result only in acquittal, dismissal, not guilty, or nolle prosequi. Mandates courts notify the Central Repository, relevant law enforcement agencies, and the defendant of the expungement date. Requires courts to notify eligible defendants of their right to expungement alongside a tort claim waiver form.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals charged with specified civil cannabis offenses or crimes other than non-appearance transportation violations whose charges result in favorable dispositions
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact, as the bill clarifies existing statutory language without modifying government operations or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 189 directly impacts court processes by clarifying which court records are subject to automatic expungement and modifying the statutory notice requirements that the courts must send to defendants, the Central Repository, and law enforcement.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS houses the Criminal Justice Information System (CJIS) Central Repository, which receives notices of disposition from the courts and is responsible for expunging state criminal history records according to the clarified statutory criteria.
As the primary statewide law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police maintains arrest and charging records that are subject to the automatic expungement provisions clarified under this bill.
The bill explicitly clarifies provisions concerning crimes and violations under the Transportation Article and the circumstances where an individual is or is not required to appear.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits persons from making or accepting campaign contributions or donations using any currency other than United States currency. Prohibits campaign finance entities from making monetary expenditures using any currency other than United States currency. Authorizes the State Administrator of Elections to investigate potential violations and issue subpoenas for testimony and records. Authorizes the State Board of Elections to impose civil penalties or refer violations to the State Prosecutor. Expands the tax law definition of financial institution to include regulated virtual currency money transmitters. Authorizes the Comptroller to request tax enforcement information and assistance from virtual currency money transmitters.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Administrator of Elections; Maryland State Board of Elections; Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: campaign finance entities, political donors, entities making independent expenditures or electioneering communications, and regulated virtual currency money transmitters
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate potential increase in general fund revenues beginning in FY 2024 from tax liens satisfied through virtual currency accounts, and potential indeterminate increase in Fair Campaign Financing Fund revenues from civil and criminal penalties. Enforcement activities can be handled using existing agency resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill assigns direct regulatory and enforcement authority to the State Administrator of Elections and the State Board of Elections to investigate campaign finance violations involving non-U.S. currency, issue subpoenas, hold hearings, impose civil penalties, and adopt regulations.

The bill amends the Tax - General Article to authorize the Comptroller to request information and assistance from virtual currency money transmitters and direct them to seize or attach property subject to tax liens to enforce state tax laws.

The bill authorizes the State Board of Elections to refer potential willful and knowing criminal violations of campaign finance currency prohibitions to the State Prosecutor for investigation and prosecution.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a court to defer entering a conviction and grant probation before judgment when a defendant pleads not guilty. Requires the State's consent, written consent from the defendant, and a finding serving public welfare. Mandates that the agreement provide the defendant admits no guilt and waives trial and appeal rights. Requires the court to find facts justifying guilt beyond a reasonable doubt while expressly withholding a finding of guilt. Authorizes the court to find guilt and impose the maximum statutory penalty if the probation terms are violated. Treats the resulting disposition as probation before judgment for all other purposes under State law.
qa_results.responsible_party: Judiciary; Administrative Office of the Courts; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Criminal defendants pleading not guilty, State's Attorneys, District Court and Circuit Court judges
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $33,400 in FY 2024 only for Judiciary computer programming changes. Local finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Administrative Office of the Courts (AOC) is explicitly amended in statutory text regarding notification and records of approved treatment programs, and the Judiciary incurs a direct fiscal impact of $33,400 in FY 2024 for computer and case management programming changes to implement the new probation agreement procedures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Office of the Public Defender represents indigent criminal defendants who will directly utilize and negotiate these new not-guilty probation before judgment agreements to avoid federal immigration and collateral consequences.

The bill amends provisions in the Health - General Article governing the Maryland Department of Health's responsibility to approve, monitor, and report alcoholism and substance abuse education and treatment programs utilized as probation conditions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services oversees the Division of Parole and Probation, which is responsible for supervising individuals placed on probation before judgment and monitoring compliance with court-ordered conditions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Appropriates funds for the operating and capital expenses of Maryland State government for fiscal 2024. Funds public education, healthcare programs, transportation infrastructure, environmental initiatives, and public safety operations statewide. Authorizes cost-of-living adjustments, salary increments, and benefit enhancements for qualifying State employees. Provides state aid to local governments, including disparity grants and public school funding formulas. Allocates dedicated resources to the Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund and the State Reserve Fund. Enacts deficiency appropriations across multiple State agencies to address budgetary needs for fiscal 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Budget and Management; Comptroller of Maryland; State Treasurer's Office
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland State agencies, state employees, public school students and teachers, Medicaid recipients, local governments, and Maryland taxpayers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Establishes total net appropriations of approximately $63.1 billion for fiscal 2024 across general, special, and federal funds. Enacts fiscal 2023 deficiency appropriations exceeding $2.4 billion to address agency shortfalls, leave payouts, inflationary utility costs, and programmatic caseload adjustments. Distributes billions in state formula aid and grants to county governments, Baltimore City, and local school systems.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 200 is the State Operating Budget bill for Fiscal Year 2024, providing direct operating appropriations, deficiency appropriations, and position authorizations for the Executive Department - Governor (Program D10A01.01).
The bill specifies the statutory flat-rate salary and compensation for the Lieutenant Governor within the Executive Department salary schedule.

The bill provides full FY 2024 appropriations for the Office of the Comptroller (Program E00A), mandates a specific study on fines, penalties, and interest rates, and directs statewide accounting and IT operations.

The bill appropriates operational and capital funding for Treasury Management, bond sale expenses, and the State Insurance Trust Fund, and provides appropriations to implement the transition of Maryland 529 under the Treasurer's Office.
The bill provides comprehensive operating and deficiency appropriations across all divisions of the Office of the Attorney General (Program C81C) and establishes executive salary levels.
The bill provides FY 2024 appropriations for the Department of Aging (Program D26A), including community services, senior centers, and grants to eliminate waitlists in the Senior Care program.
The bill provides operating, capital, and deficiency funding across MDA programs (Program L00A), including animal health, resource conservation, pest management, and marketing.
DBM is the primary administrative agency overseeing state fiscal operations, position allocations, statewide compensation, budget execution, and reporting requirements throughout the Act.

The bill provides annual appropriations for the Department of Commerce (Program T00), funding economic development programs, tax credit reserves, the Maryland State Arts Council, and tourism promotion.

The bill appropriates general, special, and federal funds for the Department of Disabilities (Program D12A), including Telecommunications Access of Maryland and the Developmental Disabilities Council.

The bill funds MSDE (Program R00A) including the foundation program, Blueprint for Maryland's Future formulas, nonpublic school programs, and early childhood programs, and imposes significant legislative reporting conditions.
The bill appropriates state and federal funding for MDEM operations and the Maryland 911 Board (Program D52A), including disaster relief and emergency management operations.
The bill appropriates operating and capital funding for MDE (Program U00A), including water quality revolving funds, clean air and materials administration, and bay restoration programs.

The bill provides operating and capital appropriations for DGS (Program H00), covering facilities management, capitol police security, procurement, real estate, and capital PAYGO miscellaneous grants.
The bill provides major state and federal appropriations for MDH (Program M00), funding Medicaid, behavioral health administration, developmental disabilities, state hospitals, and regulatory boards.
The bill appropriates operating, capital, and federal grant funds to DHCD (Program S00A), including neighborhood revitalization, rental housing programs, and statewide broadband deployment.

The bill provides operating appropriations to DHS (Program N00) for social services administration, foster care maintenance payments, child welfare services, and family investment assistance payments.
The bill provides operational appropriations for DoIT (Program F50) and funds the Major Information Technology Development Project Fund (MITDPF) across state agencies.
The bill provides appropriations for DJS (Program V00) across departmental support, community operations, detention facilities, and the juvenile services educational program.
The bill appropriates operational funds for MD Labor (Program P00), including unemployment insurance, occupational licensing, workforce development, and the newly established Division of Paid Leave.
The bill provides funding for DNR (Program K00), covering the Maryland Park Service, Natural Resources Police, Program Open Space capital programs, and Chesapeake and coastal services.
The bill appropriates funds for MDP (Program D40W), including planning data, the State Clearinghouse, museum services, and the Maryland Historic Revitalization Tax Credit.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill provides extensive appropriations for DPSCS (Program Q00), covering correctional facilities, parole and probation, pretrial detention, and correctional training commissions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes and finances the operational budget for DSCI (Program I00A), providing funding for the Service Year Option Program and the transfer of the Maryland Corps Program.
The bill contains the complete Consolidated Transportation Program appropriations and debt limits for MDOT (Program J00) across all modal administrations and WMATA commitments.
The bill provides operating and deficiency appropriations for Veterans Affairs (Program D55P), including the Charlotte Hall Veterans Home, state veteran cemeteries, and outreach services.
The bill establishes executive salary scales for the Adjutant General and appropriates funds for Military Department operations and maintenance (Program D50H).
The bill provides extensive funding for MHEC (Program R62I), including community college aid formulas, Sellinger formula grants, and various state student financial aid programs.
The bill appropriates funding for the Department of State Police (Program W00A), covering field operations, criminal investigations, vehicle replacements, and the State Fire Marshal.
The bill provides operating appropriations for the Office of the Secretary of State (Program D16A06.01), including charitable organization regulation and Sister States program funding.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill provides consolidated appropriations and staffing support for various executive boards and commissions under program code D15A05.
The bill provides a direct operating appropriation for the Governor's Grants Office under Program D15A05.22.
The bill funds the Children's Cabinet Interagency Fund (Program D21A02.02) and mandates reporting on children and youth services and out-of-home placements.
