The bill appropriates general, special, and federal funds for GOCI (Program D15A05.05) and handles the reallocation of service programs to the Department of Service and Civic Innovation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill appropriates state and federal funds for GOCPP (Program D21A), allocating millions in local law enforcement grants, Victims of Crime Act grants, and violence prevention initiatives.
The bill details the transfer of personnel and positions for the Governor's Office of Performance Improvement from DBM to the Governor's Office.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill provides a direct general fund appropriation for the Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs under Program D15A05.03.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill provides a direct general fund appropriation for the Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing under Program D11A04.01.
The bill directly appropriates funds for the Governor's Workforce Development Board under MD Labor Program P00A01.09.
The bill funds the Judicial Branch and specifically appropriates over $120 million to the Administrative Office of the Courts (Program C00A00.06).

The bill appropriates operational and contingent funds for BPW (Program D05E01), funds judgments against the State, and authorizes BPW actions regarding state position ceilings and contingency allocations.
The bill includes operating and capital appropriations for the Canal Place Preservation and Development Authority under Program D90U00.01 and D90U00.02.
The bill includes a specific $11,500,000 grant appropriation to the Chesapeake Bay Trust within BPW Miscellaneous Grants (D05E01.10).
The bill provides general and federal fund operating appropriations and new position additions for MCCR under Program D27L00.01.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Health Care Alternative Dispute Resolution Office
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill provides an annual operating appropriation for HCADRO under Program D15A05.07.
The bill appropriates special funds exceeding $150 million to HSCRC under Program M00R01.02 to support hospital rate regulation and health financing programs.
The bill provides direct general, special, and federal fund appropriations for the administration of the Historic St. Mary's City Commission under Program D17B01.51.
The bill includes deficiency funding for the State's IWIF account and mandates general ledger debit/credit control accounting procedures for IWIF payments under Section 33.
The bill appropriates operational and major capital funding for public school construction and school safety grants under Program R00A07.
The bill transfers positions and provides dedicated grant funding to the Sister States program within the Office of the Secretary of State.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters state budget appropriations, revenue distributions, and statutory mandates to finance state and local government operations. Reduces the required Medicaid Deficit Assessment for hospitals to $244,825,000 for fiscal year 2024 only. Eliminates the required fiscal year 2024 surplus appropriation to the Revenue Stabilization Account. Extends the Bainbridge Development Corporation land transfer deadline to the Department of Natural Resources to June 1, 2025. Reduces the fiscal year 2023 appropriation for the Department of Human Services Assistance Payments Program by $7,500,000. qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Department_of Human Services; Maryland Energy Administration; Department of Natural Resources; State Department of Assessments and Taxation; University of Maryland Medical System
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland hospitals, public assistance recipients, Washington Gas customers, Baltimore County library users, Bainbridge Development Corporation, and patients of University of Maryland Capital Region Medical Center
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: In FY 2023, State general fund expenditures decrease by $0.2 million. In FY 2024, special fund revenues decrease by $50.0 million, special fund expenditures decrease by $40.8 million, and general fund expenditures increase by $49.5 million, reflecting hospital assessment reductions and contingent fund swaps. No local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary fiscal and budget agency for the State, DBM oversees state spending, manages the budget, and prepares the Budget Reconciliation and Financing Act (BRFA) to balance the state operating budget and implement budget-related statutory changes.

The bill explicitly alters the budgeted Medicaid Deficit Assessment for fiscal year 2024, lowering it by $50 million, and tasks MDH alongside HSCRC to adopt policies preserving the State's Medicare waiver.

HSCRC regulates hospital revenues and is directed alongside MDH to adopt policies regarding hospital assessment and remittance revenue and to reduce the Medicaid Deficit Assessment while preserving the Medicare waiver.

The bill extends the statutory deadline by which the Bainbridge Development Corporation must transfer 120 to 150 acres of the Bainbridge Naval Training Center site to DNR for a state park.
The bill authorizes the transfer of unexpended capital grant appropriations budgeted under DGS (Miscellaneous Grants - Capital Appropriation H00H01.03) to Baltimore County library projects.

The bill repeals the requirement to repay the Local Reserve Account (administered by the Comptroller for local income tax reserves) over 15 years for refunds of recalculated homeowners' property tax credits.

The elimination of the fiscal 2024 Revenue Stabilization Account transfer results in $500 million being redirected to the Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund, directly impacting long-term public education funding overseen by MSDE.
The bill is an Administration bill establishing budget reconciliation provisions, altering mandated executive budget appropriations and authorizing executive budget amendments.
The bill details surplus formula allocations under State Finance and Procurement § 7-311, including statutory funding for the Maryland Equity Investment Fund administered by TEDCO.

The bill references statutory distributions of state general fund surplus allocations under State Finance and Procurement § 7-311 directed to the accumulation funds of the State Retirement and Pension System.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters eligibility requirements for Montessori schools and programs participating in State prekindergarten programs. Requires Montessori classroom teachers to hold a bachelor’s degree in any field and an approved Montessori credential. Recognizes credentials from Association Montessori Internationale, American Montessori Society, or Montessori Accreditation Council for Teacher Education accredited programs. Establishes a student-to-classroom personnel ratio of 10 to 1 for students under age 5. Sets a maximum class size of 20 students when all students are under age 5. Permits a ratio of 14 to 1 and 28 students when some are at least 5.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Montessori schools and programs, prekindergarten teachers and staff, and enrolled prekindergarten students and their families
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact, as altering eligibility requirements is not anticipated to materially affect State funding under the Prekindergarten Expansion Grant program or the publicly funded full-day prekindergarten program.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) oversees early childhood education, approves prekindergarten providers, and administers the Prekindergarten Expansion Grant Program, which is directly altered by the bill to accommodate Montessori credentials and ratios.

qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland corporations, close corporations, nonstock corporations, limited liability companies, real estate investment trusts, closed-end statutory trusts, and their stockholders and members

The State Board of Elections oversees election administration in Maryland, and the bill codifies that the seven elected members of the Baltimore County Board of Education are elected at general elections in gubernatorial election years.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly establishes a temporary, independent advisory body—the Commission on Public Health—along with multiple thematic workgroups to assess and recommend systemic reforms to the State's public health delivery.

The bill requires a faculty member from a public health program at a historically Black college or university to be appointed as a member and co-chair of the commission. Academic institutions represented by co-chairs must provide staff support for the commission, which may impact Morgan State University's expenditures as identified in the fiscal note.

The bill mandates that representatives from State academic institutions with expertise in public health systems serve on and co-chair the commission, requiring the represented institutions to provide staff support to the commission and potentially increasing higher education expenditures.
The Governor is responsible for appointing numerous members to the Commission, designating co-chairs, and receiving the Commission's interim and final reports on public health reform.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments to the newly created Commission on Public Health, including local health officers, academic experts, and public members.
The bill specifically directs the Commission on Public Health to consult with the Maryland Health Care Commission as appropriate and necessary in performing its duties.

The bill specifically directs the Commission on Public Health to consult with the Health Services Cost Review Commission as appropriate and necessary in conducting its assessments and formulating recommendations.

The bill mandates that the Commission consult with the Department of General Services, particularly as recommendations are formulated concerning state procurement and oversight of contractors.
The bill explicitly requires the Commission on Public Health to consult with the Maryland Department of Disabilities in performing its duties and assessments.

qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. St. Mary's County can produce and submit the required report using existing resources, resulting in no local revenue or expenditure impact.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the definition of a person in a position of authority under the fourth-degree sexual offense statute. Prohibits qualifying school workers and volunteers from engaging in sexual acts, sexual contact, or vaginal intercourse with enrolled students. Authorizes sentences under this statute to run consecutive to or concurrent with sentences for related crimes.

qa_results.stakeholders: minors attending schools or youth programs; employees and volunteers at schools, child care facilities, sports, camps, and youth-serving programs

The bill alters criminal penalties and definitions under fourth-degree sexual offenses, impacting District and Circuit Court caseloads, trial proceedings, and fine collection.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of the Environment to adopt regulations establishing requirements for selling new zero-emission medium- and heavy-duty vehicles. Incorporates California's Advanced Clean Trucks regulations by reference, taking effect starting with model year 2027. Directs the department to submit a needs assessment and deployment plan to the General Assembly by December 1, 2024. Authorizes the department to delay implementation by model years if assessment criteria demonstrate it is not feasible. Alters the Medium-Duty and Heavy-Duty Zero-Emission Vehicle Grant Program to cover up to 75% of incremental equipment costs. Mandates an annual $10,000,000 appropriation from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund for grants from fiscal 2024 through 2027.

qa_results.stakeholders: commercial and industrial vehicle fleet owners, medium- and heavy-duty vehicle manufacturers and dealers, local governments, and entities operating in overburdened or underserved communities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $474,200 in FY 2024 for staffing and contractual costs, with ongoing operational costs in future years. Strategic Energy Investment Fund expenditures increase by $5.25 million in FY 2024 and $5.0 million annually from FY 2025 through FY 2027 for vehicle and equipment grants. Local governments face indeterminate expenditure changes when replacing municipal fleet vehicles, potentially offset by higher grant amounts.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary implementing agency responsible for promulgating regulations incorporating California's Advanced Clean Trucks regulations, preparing the zero-emission needs assessment and deployment plan, and determining any potential delays in implementation.

MDOT is explicitly named as a consulting agency required to collaborate with MDE on developing the needs assessment and deployment plan and determining whether to delay implementation of the regulations.

DGS oversees state-owned facilities and fleet management and is statutorily required to consult with MDE on the needs assessment and deployment plan, particularly regarding transitioning the State vehicle fleet to zero-emission vehicles.
PSC is statutorily required to consult with MDE on the needs assessment and deployment plan, specifically assessing electric grid capacity, transmission, distribution demands, and feasibility.
The bill mandates that the Governor include an appropriation of at least $10 million from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund in the annual budget bill for fiscal years 2024 through 2027.
DBM oversees the development of the state budget and must incorporate the bill's mandated annual appropriations from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the definition of neglect within statutory provisions governing child in need of assistance proceedings. Excludes cannabis use by any parent or individual with care, custody, or supervision of a child from constituting neglect. Authorizes a finding of neglect if cannabis use harms or places the child's health or welfare at substantial risk. Permits a neglect finding if cannabis use causes mental injury or substantial risk of mental injury. Takes effect July 1, 2023.

qa_results.stakeholders: Parents and caretakers who use cannabis, and children involved in Child in Need of Assistance proceedings
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the State Board of Chiropractic Examiners to discipline an applicant or licensee for failing to comply with any Board order. qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Comptroller, upon request of the State Tax Sale Ombudsman, to provide telephone numbers of homeowners that were included on tax returns filed with the Comptroller's Office. agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill addresses special death benefits for the surviving spouse of a correctional officer who died in the line of duty while employed at a state correctional facility under the department.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly transfers both the Baltimore City Young Readers Program and the Young Readers Matching Grant Program to the Maryland State Library Agency, requiring the State Librarian to administer the programs and the State Library Board to report biennially to the General Assembly.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy

qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in state general fund revenues beginning in FY 2024 due to reduced administrative costs for paper filings. State expenditures and local government finances are not affected.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Baltimore County Board of License Commissioners to issue a Class B–ECF/DS beer, wine, and liquor license for Towson University. Creates potential operational impacts for the Judiciary and local circuit courts due to requirements to hold hearings on the next business day following the execution of an ex parte warrant. Specific figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 267 creates the Maryland Child Abduction Prevention Act, enacting new judicial procedures, evidentiary standards, abduction prevention orders, and ex parte warrants for physical custody of children in custody proceedings. The fiscal note explicitly notes an operational impact on the Judiciary to handle expedited next-business-day hearings following the execution of an ex parte warrant.

The bill authorizes courts to issue ex parte warrants directing law enforcement officers to immediately take physical custody of a child and authorizes law enforcement to enter private property or make forcible entry under exigent circumstances to locate and recover the child.

As the state's primary agency for child welfare and family stability, DHS often intersects with child custody proceedings involving allegations of child abuse, neglect, and domestic violence, which are key risk factors evaluated under this Act. DHS was also consulted as an information source for the bill's fiscal and policy note.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Governor to include a $12,000,000 appropriation to the 9-8-8 Trust Fund in the fiscal 2025 budget bill. Supports maintaining 9-8-8 as the universal telephone number for suicide prevention and mental health crises. Directs funding toward crisis call centers, mobile crisis teams, and crisis stabilization centers. Authorizes the Maryland Department of Health to administer the nonlapsing special fund. Specifies that the Act takes effect July 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Office of the Governor
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals experiencing behavioral health crises, operators of crisis call centers, mobile crisis teams, crisis stabilization centers, and acute behavioral health care providers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures and special fund revenues increase by $12.0 million in FY 2025 due to the mandated appropriation. Special fund expenditures increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in FY 2025 to support crisis response services and MDH personnel costs ($94,023 in FY 2025 for one administrator). Local revenues and expenditures may increase significantly for jurisdictions providing behavioral health crisis response services.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health administers the 9-8-8 Trust Fund and is responsible for implementing the statewide behavioral health crisis hotline, awarding funding for crisis response services, and managing personnel supported by the fund.
The bill legally mandates that the Governor include a $12.0 million appropriation to the 9-8-8 Trust Fund in the fiscal year 2025 annual budget bill.

As the principal agency responsible for preparing and supervising the executive state budget, the Department of Budget and Management must implement the $12.0 million mandated appropriation for fiscal year 2025.
The State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold the 9-8-8 Trust Fund separately and invest the money in the fund.
The Comptroller of Maryland is statutorily required to account for the 9-8-8 Trust Fund.
The 9-8-8 Trust Fund is statutorily subject to audit by the Office of Legislative Audits.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters educational and experience requirements for licensure as an environmental health specialist. Reduces required science semester credit hours for baccalaureate degree applicants from 60 to 30. Replaces statutory laboratory course requirements with laboratory coursework required under Board regulations. Repeals an alternative licensing pathway requiring 24 months of in-training experience. Expands disciplinary grounds to include misfeasance and malfeasance committed while performing specialist duties. Repeals statutory reexamination application and fee mandates.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Environmental Health Specialists
qa_results.stakeholders: applicants for environmental health specialist licensure and licensed environmental health specialists in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State or local governmental finances, as the bill's changes are largely technical in nature.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Environmental Health Specialists is a health occupations licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Health, which regulates environmental health specialists and oversees licensure, examination, and disciplinary requirements.

The Department of the Environment employs and collaborates extensively with environmental health specialists across environmental protection and public health programs, and was consulted as an information source for the legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Provides per-resident funding of $19.10 for county public library systems for fiscal year 2027 and each subsequent fiscal year. Continues the minimum library program funding allocation for operating and capital expenses. Requires the State and participating counties to share the capital and operating costs of the minimum library program. Maintains the State share at approximately 40 percent and county funding at approximately 60 percent statewide.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Budget and Management
qa_results.stakeholders: county public library systems, county governments, Baltimore City, and county public library employees
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State or local fiscal impact because the bill codifies existing funding levels for local library systems established under prior legislation.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Library Agency is the primary state entity responsible for providing funding, leadership, and coordination to Maryland's 24 public library systems, which are the direct subjects of the statutory library aid funding formula in this bill.
The Department of Budget and Management develops and oversees the state budget, which incorporates the state share of mandated funding formulas for local library systems.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts Montgomery County Class B-BWL clubhouse or lodge license holders from a retail license limitation on micro-breweries. The exemption applies when the license holder is issued a Class 7 micro-brewery license. General law restricts micro-brewery licensees from holding a financial interest in more than one separate retail license. Class B-BWL licenses are issued for Montgomery County Revenue Authority multiuse facilities accommodating golf courses. The act takes effect July 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Montgomery County Board of License Commissioners; Alcohol and Tobacco Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Montgomery County Class B–BWL (clubhouse/lodge) license holders, including the Montgomery County Revenue Authority, and Class 7 micro-brewery operators
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State operations or finances and is not anticipated to materially affect Montgomery County operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry and oversees statutory provisions related to alcoholic beverages and manufacturer licenses referenced in the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes clinical nurse specialists to prescribe drugs and durable medical equipment under State Board of Nursing regulations. Defines clinical nurse specialists and practice as a clinical nurse specialist under the Health Occupations Article. Permits clinical nurse specialists to order diagnostic and laboratory tests, home health care, and hospice care. Designates clinical nurse specialists as authorized prescribers under the Maryland Pharmacy Act. Authorizes licensed physicians to prepare and dispense prescriptions written by advanced practice registered nurses in their office.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Nursing
qa_results.stakeholders: clinical nurse specialists, advanced practice registered nurses, licensed physicians, and patients receiving complex care
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No substantive impact on State or local governmental operations or finances. The Maryland Board of Nursing can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health oversees the State Board of Nursing, which is tasked with certifying clinical nurse specialists, regulating their expanded scope of practice, and adopting regulations governing their authority to prescribe drugs and durable medical equipment.

qa_results.bill_summary: Reestablishes authority for the Prescription Drug Affordability Board to draft an action plan for setting upper payment limits. Applies the process to prescription drug products determined to have led or will lead to affordability challenges. Requires approval of the plan by the Legislative Policy Committee or both the Governor and the Attorney General. Authorizes payment limits on drugs purchased or paid through State and local entities, employee plans, or Medicaid. Prohibits applying upper payment limits to drugs on the federal Food and Drug Administration drug shortage list. Requires a report by December 1, 2026, on expanding payment limits to all purchases statewide.
qa_results.responsible_party: Prescription Drug Affordability Board
qa_results.stakeholders: State and local government entities, public employee health benefit plans, the Maryland Medical Assistance Program, prescription drug manufacturers, and health care payors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures and local government health care expenditures decrease to the extent that upper payment limits are implemented and reduce prescription drug costs. State and local revenues are not affected. Specific savings figures are indeterminate.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes upper payment limits for prescription drugs purchased or paid for by the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) and state hospitals, both of which are administered and operated by the Maryland Department of Health.

If the Legislative Policy Committee does not approve the Prescription Drug Affordability Board's plan of action, the plan must be submitted to the Governor and the Attorney General for joint approval before upper payment limits may be set.
The Attorney General is given joint statutory authority with the Governor to approve the plan of action for setting upper payment limits if the Legislative Policy Committee does not approve it.

As the agency administering the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, DBM is directly impacted because upper payment limits apply to prescription drugs paid for through State health benefit plans.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly applies upper payment limits to prescription drugs purchased or paid for by State correctional facilities operated by DPSCS.
Upper payment limits apply to prescription drug products purchased or paid for by health clinics at State institutions of higher education.

The agency regulates commercial health benefit plans in Maryland and provided information for the bill's fiscal note regarding the application and impact of drug payment limits on health benefit plans.
Decisions by the Board regarding upper payment limits may be contested and appealed under the Administrative Procedure Act, which involves the administrative hearings framework.

The bill provides that any person aggrieved by a final decision of the Board regarding an upper payment limit may petition for judicial review in the State courts under the Administrative Procedure Act.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Medical Assistance Program, beginning January 1, 2024, to cover medically necessary gender-affirming treatment in a nondiscriminatory manner. Prohibits the Program from excluding treatments as cosmetic services or establishing categorical exclusions for particular gender-affirming procedures. Prohibits issuing an adverse benefit determination unless an experienced provider reviews and confirms the determination's appropriateness. Requires Medicaid managed care organizations to submit annual reports identifying contracted providers offering gender-affirming care who consent to inclusion. Mandates that the Maryland Department of Health publish an annual geographic access report on its website beginning January 1, 2025. Requires the Department and managed care organizations to include participating gender-affirming treatment providers in their provider directories.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland Medical Assistance Program recipients seeking gender-affirming care (including transgender, nonbinary, intersex, two-spirit, and other gender diverse individuals), Medicaid managed care organizations, and health care providers offering gender-affirming treatment
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Medicaid expenditures increase by an indeterminate but likely significant amount beginning in fiscal 2024, with federal matching fund revenues increasing accordingly. No effect on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health directly administers the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), which is required by this bill to cover medically necessary gender-affirming care, establish review standards for adverse benefit determinations, compile annual geographic access reports, and maintain updated provider directories.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires owners and operators of certain grocery stores and restaurants to place and maintain an automated external defibrillator. Exempts grocery stores that have an annual gross income of $10,000,000 or less. Exempts restaurants with seating under 100 individuals or annual gross income of $1,000,000 or less, excluding off-premises sales. Excludes covered grocery stores and restaurants from the Public Access Automated External Defibrillator Program but requires MIEMSS registration. Grants civil liability immunity to grocery stores, restaurants, and individuals rendering aid in good faith without compensation. Requires the Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems to adopt regulations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners and operators of grocery stores and restaurants; customers and employees of grocery stores and restaurants; individuals experiencing sudden cardiac arrest
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures from the Maryland Emergency Medical System Operations Fund increase by at least $41,371 in FY 2024 for MIEMSS to employ a part-time administrator and oversee registration. Annual operating costs range between $46,000 and $53,100 from FY 2025 through FY 2028. State revenues are not affected. Local health department expenditures may increase minimally if required to conduct AED inspections.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS is the primary regulatory and administrative agency tasked with implementing the AED program for qualifying grocery stores and restaurants. The agency must jointly adopt regulations with MDH, maintain the registration system, provide maintenance/recall notices, and complete two evaluation reports for the General Assembly, resulting in direct fiscal impacts on the Maryland Emergency Medical System Operations Fund.

MDH is statutorily required to jointly adopt regulations with MIEMSS establishing guidelines for AED periodic inspections, annual maintenance, and assistance to facility owners. Additionally, local health departments under MDH oversight may inspect or monitor AED requirements during food service and grocery inspections.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Forestry Education Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund administered by the Maryland Forestry Foundation. Directs the Fund to support forestry education, outreach, sustainability programs, and grants for testing innovative best management practices. Allocates resources to forest landowners, district forestry boards, local governments, and businesses. Requires the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $250,000 to the Fund in fiscal 2025 and 2026. Exempts the Fund from general fund interest accrual and credits interest earnings directly to the Fund.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Forestry Foundation; State Treasurer; Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland forest landowners, district forestry boards, local governments, and forestry businesses
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $250,000 annually in FY 2025 and FY 2026 due to the mandated appropriation. Special fund revenues and expenditures increase correspondingly as funds are received and disbursed. Local government grant revenues and expenditures likely increase in FY 2025 and FY 2026.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill is codified under the Natural Resources Article and directly impacts forestry in Maryland, providing resources and education to district forestry boards established under the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) and supporting programs aligned with DNR's Forest Service mission.
The bill explicitly tasks the State Treasurer with holding the Maryland Forestry Education Fund separately and investing its moneys in the same manner as other State funds.
The bill statutorily requires the Comptroller to account for the newly established Maryland Forestry Education Fund.
The bill mandates an annual general fund appropriation of $250,000 for fiscal years 2025 and 2026, which impacts state budget formulation and fiscal planning managed by DBM.
The bill mandates that the Governor include a $250,000 appropriation in the annual budget bill for fiscal years 2025 and 2026 for the Maryland Forestry Education Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the Maryland Dent-Care Program to include licensed dental hygienists. Sets loan assistance grants of at least $50,000 annually for dentists and up to $10,000 for dental hygienists. Requires the Maryland Department of Health to annually evaluate Medicaid reimbursement rates for dental services. Directs the department to create plain language dental health materials and distribute them to dental practices. Requires the State Board of Dental Examiners to maintain a searchable directory of mobile and portable dental providers. Mandates studies on provider participation, community health worker reimbursement, and opening dental practices in underserved areas.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Higher Education Commission; State Board of Dental Examiners
qa_results.stakeholders: Dentists, dental hygienists, Maryland Medical Assistance Program recipients, and mobile or portable dental service providers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $186,400 in FY 2024 ($136,400 general funds, $50,000 federal funds) and $20,000 in FY 2025 ($10,000 general funds, $10,000 federal funds) for contractual studies, educational materials, and system updates. Federal fund revenues increase by $50,000 in FY 2024 and $10,000 in FY 2025 from Medicaid matching funds. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) is the primary implementing agency. The bill tasks MDH with evaluating Medicaid dental reimbursement rates, assisting with the Maryland Dent-Care Program via the Office of Oral Health, developing and distributing plain language dental health materials, conducting studies on dental provider participation and community health worker reimbursement, and overseeing the State Board of Dental Examiners' new reporting and directory requirements for mobile/portable dental providers.

The Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC), through its Office of Student Financial Assistance, administers the Maryland Dent-Care Program. The bill alters program eligibility to include dental hygienists and establishes statutory grant award parameters, requiring updates to MHEC's Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS).

The Higher Education Commission administers the Maryland Dent-Care Program through its Office of Student Financial Assistance, which must update program systems and grant amounts to accommodate dental hygienists and revised award amounts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates the establishment of a stakeholder workgroup to study the creation of a grant or no-interest loan program for dental providers in underserved areas and report findings and recommendations to the General Assembly by December 1, 2024.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters educational requirements for licensing clinical alcohol and drug counselors and graduate alcohol and drug counselors. Requires qualifying master's or doctoral degrees to be in a professional counseling field instead of health and human services. Permits qualifying degrees from accredited institutions rather than specifying regionally accredited institutions. Repeals the alternative educational pathway for clinical alcohol and drug counselor licensure. Removes specific statutory coursework credit-hour requirements to practice as a licensed graduate alcohol and drug counselor.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Professional Counselors
qa_results.stakeholders: applicants for licensure as clinical alcohol and drug counselors and licensed graduate alcohol and drug counselors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The procedural changes to educational qualifications do not affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health houses and oversees the State Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists, which regulates and administers licenses for clinical and graduate alcohol and drug counselors impacted by this bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts certain family child care homes, large family child care homes, and child care centers from State registration and licensing requirements. Applies to providers that serve only dependent children of military personnel. Requires providers to be on a military base or federal property, or certified by defense authorities. Authorizes the U.S. Department of Defense, the U.S. Coast Guard, or their agents to approve children served. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Military personnel and their dependent children, and operators of military-associated family child care homes, large family child care homes, and child care centers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact. Qualifying child care providers that are small businesses may benefit from the elimination of duplicative State and federal licensing and registration requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) regulates and licenses child care centers, family child care homes, and large family child care homes across the state. This bill directly amends the Education Article to exempt qualifying military-affiliated child care providers from MSDE licensing and registration requirements.

The Adjutant General heads the Maryland Military Department, which was consulted on the legislation. The bill establishes exemptions for child care providers operating on military installations or certified by military branches serving dependents of military personnel.

The department is tasked with advocating for and supporting active-duty service members, military personnel, and their families, who are the direct beneficiaries of the military child care facilities addressed by the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits criminal prosecution of a minor for qualifying offenses committed as a direct result of being a trafficking victim. Requires law enforcement officers to notify a regional navigator and child welfare agency upon detaining a suspected child victim. Prohibits detaining a suspected child trafficking victim in a juvenile detention facility for a qualifying offense. Requires juvenile courts to stay proceedings and dismiss charges upon determining the offense resulted directly from trafficking. Adds unauthorized use of a motor vehicle and prostitution solicitation to offenses eligible for vacated judgments.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Human Services; Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: Minors who are victims of sex trafficking or human trafficking, law enforcement officers, and individuals seeking to vacate qualifying convictions
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local operations and finances are not materially affected; any workload changes can be absorbed with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters juvenile and criminal court procedures, requiring courts to stay proceedings, schedule hearings within specified timelines, refer children to regional navigators, determine victim status, dismiss certain charges, and adjudicate motions to vacate judgments.
Law enforcement and courts are required to notify DHS and report suspected victims to local child welfare agencies, which may also receive custody of youth when return to parents/guardians is unsafe.

The bill explicitly prohibits law enforcement from detaining a suspected child victim of human or sex trafficking in a juvenile detention facility for qualifying offenses, directly affecting DJS intake and detention facilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD attorneys represent juveniles and indigent individuals charged with qualifying offenses and will utilize the safe harbor protections to file motions staying proceedings, dismissing charges, or vacating prior judgments.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, MSP troopers must adhere to altered mandatory procedures when detaining children suspected of being human trafficking victims, including regional navigator notification and child welfare placement protocols.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP oversees statewide victim services funding, juvenile justice policy, and public safety initiatives, making the implementation of human trafficking safe harbor provisions directly relevant to its coordination role.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The expansion of qualifying offenses eligible for motions to vacate judgments under Criminal Procedure § 8-302 impacts adult criminal records and correctional or supervision caseloads managed by DPSCS.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Rare Disease Advisory Council to study matters relating to individuals with rare diseases. Requires the Maryland Department of Health to provide staff for the council. Directs the council to survey the needs of rare disease patients, caregivers, and health care providers. Mandates policy recommendations regarding healthcare coverage, diagnostics, timely treatment, and provider educational resources. Requires an annual activities and recommendations report to the Governor and General Assembly beginning December 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Rare Disease Advisory Council
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals diagnosed with rare diseases, caregivers of rare disease patients, health care providers treating rare diseases, and health insurance carriers in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not materially affected as the Maryland Department of Health can staff the council using existing budgeted resources. Potential indeterminate increase in federal fund revenues and expenditures if the council secures federal grants. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill adds the Rare Disease Advisory Council under the Health - General Article and requires the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) to provide staff support for the council. Furthermore, the Secretary of Health, representatives from Maryland Medicaid, and the Office of Minority Health and Health Disparities serve on the council.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The legislation formally establishes a new, ongoing state advisory body—the Rare Disease Advisory Council—charged with studying and formulating policy recommendations regarding individuals living with rare diseases in Maryland.

The Maryland Insurance Commissioner must designate a representative from the Maryland Insurance Administration to serve on the advisory council, which is tasked with researching insurance utilization management procedures and coverage of prescription drugs for rare diseases.

The Governor is responsible for appointing 14 members of the advisory council, designating the initial council chair, and receiving the council's annual reports on rare disease findings and recommendations.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting, managing applications, and facilitating the appointment of 14 diverse stakeholders and experts to the newly created council.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes an applicant or State employee to file a written complaint alleging employer harassment with the principal unit head. Requires harassment complaints to be filed within two years after the alleged violation occurred. Increases the deadline to file complaints alleging prohibited personnel actions from 30 days to one year. Starts the one-year period when the complainant first knew or reasonably should have known of the violation. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Heads of principal units of State government; Maryland Department of Budget and Management
qa_results.stakeholders: State Executive Branch employees, applicants for employment in Executive Branch agencies, and Executive Branch employers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures across all funds may increase beginning in fiscal 2024 to investigate and manage additional complaints, but the exact cost cannot be reliably estimated. Local governments and revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the State's central personnel agency, DBM oversees Executive Branch personnel policies, rules, and equal employment opportunity complaint processes. The bill directly impacts the administration of state employee complaints regarding prohibited personnel actions and workplace harassment.

MCCR investigates and enforces Maryland's anti-discrimination laws, including workplace harassment under § 20-606 of the State Government Article. The bill specifically references these violations and alters the complaint processes and timelines available to state employees.
OAH adjudicates contested administrative cases, including state personnel and employment grievances that proceed through the appeals process following agency decisions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes an individual income tax checkoff for voluntary contributions to the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund. Requires the Comptroller to include the checkoff on individual income tax return forms. Requires the Comptroller to describe the purposes of the Fund within income tax return packages. Directs the Comptroller to deduct administrative costs and distribute remaining proceeds to the Fund. Applies to all taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland; Maryland Department of Veterans Affairs
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland individual income taxpayers, Maryland veterans and their families, and public and private programs supporting veterans
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No fiscal impact in FY 2024 or FY 2025. In FY 2026, general fund expenditures increase by $150,598 ($79,000 for one-time Comptroller tax system modifications and $71,598 for one Department of Veterans Affairs grants specialist), with ongoing department personnel costs of $90,500 in FY 2027 and $95,300 in FY 2028. Maryland Veterans Trust Fund nonbudgeted revenues increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in FY 2026, while revenues to other income tax checkoffs may potentially decrease. Local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is directly responsible for implementing the bill by modifying the individual income tax return form and tax packages to include the checkoff, collecting contributions, deducting administrative costs, and distributing net proceeds to the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund, requiring $79,000 in FY 2026 for tax system changes.

The department (formerly the Maryland Department of Veterans Affairs) houses and staffs the Maryland Veterans Trust, which maintains the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund. Increased checkoff revenues will directly support the fund's grants and require an additional grants specialist position starting in FY 2026.
The bill explicitly requires the Comptroller to account to the State Treasurer for checkoff contribution moneys collected and deposited.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of Agriculture to study the use of perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances in pesticides in Maryland. Mandates consultation with the Department of the Environment, the Maryland Department of Health, and the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency. Directs the study to analyze health and environmental impacts and identify pesticide testing methods. Requires updates on federal testing method certifications and state and federal regulatory efforts. Mandates reporting findings and recommendations to the Governor and designated legislative committees by November 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture; Maryland Department of the Environment; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: pesticide manufacturers, pesticide distributors, agricultural producers, and public health and environmental advocates
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The Maryland Department of Agriculture and consulting agencies can complete the study and report using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Agriculture is the primary implementing agency directed to conduct the study on the use of PFAS in pesticides and report its findings and recommendations.

The bill statutorily requires the Department of Agriculture to consult with the Maryland Department of the Environment in studying the environmental impacts, testing methods, and regulation of PFAS in pesticides.
The bill statutorily requires the Department of Agriculture to consult with the Maryland Department of Health to analyze the health impacts associated with PFAS in pesticides.
The Governor's Office is a designated recipient of the final study report and recommendations submitted by the Department of Agriculture.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the statutory definition of student data within the Maryland Longitudinal Data System. Adds student disability data by specific disability category to the system's inventory. Maintains the general statutory exclusion of medical and health records from student data. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center; Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: students with disabilities in Maryland public schools, education policymakers, and academic researchers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected because the Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center and the Maryland State Department of Education can incorporate and transfer the data using existing resources. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the statutory definition of student data collected, analyzed, and maintained by the Maryland Longitudinal Data System (MLDS) Center to include student disability data by specific disability category.
The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) collects student disability data by category and must coordinate with the MLDS Center to provide and transfer this data for inclusion in the system.

As the principal state agency coordinating services and policy for residents with disabilities, including education and youth transitioning to adulthood, the department has an interest in longitudinal data tracking outcomes for students with disabilities.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Cigarette Restitution Fund to include a separate account for electronic smoking device enforcement payments. Captures payments from any judgment, settlement, penalty, offer of compromise, or other enforcement action. Limits account distributions to supplementing General Fund appropriations for programs reducing tobacco product use under age 21. Mandates that all distributions remain consistent with any other provision of State law. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Department of Budget and Management
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals under age 21; manufacturers and retailers of electronic smoking devices; tobacco use prevention and cessation program providers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No significant net effect on overall State finances, but redirects future spending. Settlement and enforcement revenues related to electronic smoking devices (such as Maryland's anticipated $13.0 million share from the JUUL Labs settlement) will be deposited into a separate account to supplement General Fund appropriations for youth tobacco prevention programs rather than following standard statutory distributions. Any administrative costs are handled using existing budgeted resources. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH administers the State's tobacco use prevention, cessation, and public health programs. It is directly impacted as funds from the new separate account will supplement appropriations for its programs targeting youth tobacco reduction, likely increasing program funding and staffing needs.

The OAG investigates, prosecutes, and enters into settlements regarding electronic smoking device manufacturers' sales and marketing practices (such as the JUUL Labs settlement), which generate the revenues credited to this separate account.

DBM is responsible for state budget preparation and execution, including supervising how Cigarette Restitution Fund revenues are allocated and ensuring compliance with the statutory distribution requirements for the new separate account.

The bill impacts executive budgeting requirements, and statute requires the Governor to develop key goals and performance indicators for funded activities and submit an annual report to the General Assembly on fund expenditures and outcomes.

As the state's chief financial officer and accounting agency, the Comptroller maintains the state's accounting records and manages fund and account structures, including establishing and maintaining the separate account within the Cigarette Restitution Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to expand access to and reimburse specified wraparound and intensive in-home services. Directs the Behavioral Health Administration to fund 100 case management slots for youth at risk of out-of-home placement. Mandates budget appropriations of $150,000 in fiscal 2025, $250,000 in 2026, and $350,000 thereafter for customized youth goods and services. Requires the Department to reimburse at least one pilot program utilizing value-based purchasing for case management services. Directs the Department to submit annual enrollment reports and review eligibility criteria and provider reimbursement rates.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Behavioral Health Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Children and youth with intensive behavioral health needs, children at risk of out-of-home placement, their families, and behavioral health care providers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $3,496,500 in FY 2024 for three new positions, consultant contracts, and additional case management slots. Indeterminate additional expenditures and matching federal revenues will occur for service reimbursements. Mandated general fund appropriations provide $150,000 in FY 2025, $250,000 in FY 2026, and $350,000 annually beginning in FY 2027 for customized goods and services.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH and its Behavioral Health Administration are directly responsible for implementing the bill, including providing reimbursements for wraparound and in-home services, funding 100 case management slots, establishing a value-based purchasing pilot, and conducting required stakeholder reviews and annual reports.

The bill establishes a statutory mandate requiring the Governor to include specific funding allocations in the annual operating budget bill beginning in FY 2025 ($150,000 in FY 2025, $250,000 in FY 2026, and $350,000 annually thereafter) for customized goods and services.
DBM is the principal agency responsible for state budget preparation and execution, and it must incorporate and manage the bill's mandated annual operating budget appropriations starting in FY 2025.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Office of Home Energy Programs to enroll qualifying households in any fuel and utility assistance program. Covers households containing an individual eligible for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program or Temporary Assistance for Needy Families. Covers households containing an individual eligible for Supplemental Security Income or means-tested Veterans Affairs benefits. Expands electric universal service program eligibility to all customers with incomes at or below 200% of the federal poverty level. Takes effect January 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of Home Energy Programs; Department of Human Services; Public Service Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Low-income households, electric utility customers with household incomes up to 200% of the federal poverty level, and recipients of SNAP, TANF, SSI, or means-tested Veterans Affairs benefits
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Department of Human Services special fund expenditures increase by at least $15,024,000 in FY 2024 and by $30,048,000 annually thereafter for bill payment assistance and auto-enrollment in the Electric Universal Service Program. No effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP), a unit within DHS, with enrolling eligible households receiving SNAP, TANF, SSI, or means-tested Veterans Affairs benefits into fuel and utility assistance programs. The bill also has a significant fiscal impact on DHS special fund expenditures of at least $15 million in FY 2024 and $30 million annually thereafter.

The bill amends the Public Utilities Article governing the Electric Universal Service Program (EUSP), which the Public Service Commission is statutorily required to establish, expanding customer income eligibility up to 200% of the federal poverty level.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners to establish an expedited licensing process for out-of-state veterinary practitioners. Authorizes the Board to license animal control facilities to administer rabies vaccines. Requires the Secretary of Health to allow veterinary technicians and clinical staff at animal facilities to administer rabies vaccines. Restricts these rabies vaccinations to animals under the custody or control of the shelter or facility. Mandates training verification and identification of the administering individual on the rabies certificate. Requires the Board to report on the expedited process status and funding needs by December 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Out-of-state veterinary practitioners, veterinary technicians and clinical staff at animal shelters and animal control facilities, animal shelters, and animal control facilities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $25,000 in FY 2024 only to update the SBVME licensing portal. Special fund revenues may increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in FY 2024 from application and license fees. Local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners (SBVME) is housed within the Department of Agriculture. The bill requires SBVME to establish an expedited licensing process for out-of-state veterinarians, expands the board's licensing authority for animal control facilities regarding rabies vaccines, incurs IT portal modification expenses, and requires reporting to the General Assembly.

The bill amends the Health - General Article to require the Secretary of Health to allow registered veterinary technicians and clinical staff at animal shelters or animal control facilities to administer rabies vaccines under certain conditions, and requires consultation on regulations with the Department of Agriculture.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes prompt payment and invoicing standards for State grant agreements with 501(c) nonprofit organizations. Sets a State policy to pay proper invoices within 37 days of receipt or due date. Requires grant-making entities to review invoices within five business days and report defects within two business days. Directs the Comptroller to disburse payment within five business days after receiving an approved invoice. Assesses a 9% annual interest penalty starting on the 38th day on qualifying late payments. Mandates payment of accrued interest from an agency's operating budget rather than grant appropriations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland; State grant-making entities
qa_results.stakeholders: 501(c) nonprofit organizations receiving State grants; State grant-making agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general and special fund expenditures may increase by up to $8,100 in FY 2023 and up to $97,100 annually thereafter to pay interest on late grant disbursements. No effect on State revenues or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is statutory responsible for issuing payments within five business days once a proper invoice is submitted by a grant-making entity and coordinates the state's accounting and payment processing under the bill.

MDH administers a very high volume of operating grants to nonprofit health organizations and is specifically highlighted in the fiscal note as being substantially impacted by invoice turnaround deadlines, interest liability, and potential staffing needs.

DNR awards a significant volume of grants to nonprofits and is specifically cited in the fiscal note regarding the operational and fiscal impact of adhering to the strict invoice review and prompt payment timelines.

The Governor's Grants Office assists state agencies with grant management practices, training, and compliance, making the new statewide prompt payment rules for grants directly relevant to its advisory and coordination mission.
DBM oversees executive agency operating budgets, from which any 9% interest penalties incurred by grant-making agencies for late payments must be paid.
MDOT is explicitly noted in the fiscal note regarding how prompt payment timelines interact with agency-specific grant reporting and performance milestones required before payments can be dispersed.
MSDE awards and manages substantial grant funding to educational and community nonprofit entities that will be subject to the 37-day prompt payment timetable and interest penalty provisions.

DHCD regularly administers operational grants to nonprofit community development and housing organizations, making its invoice processing subject to the new review schedule and potential late interest liabilities.
DHS contracts and provides grant funding to numerous nonprofit social service providers across Maryland, directly subjecting its grant administration workflow to the bill's prompt payment rules.
The bill explicitly carves out and exempts grants funded from general fund capital appropriations made to the Board of Public Works.
Commerce provides state financial assistance and economic development grants to nonprofit organizations that will be governed by the bill's prompt payment mandates.

qa_results.bill_summary: Modifies the process for identifying and reimbursing hospital patients who paid out-of-pocket costs and qualified for free care. Requires implementation of Option 3 from the Health Services Cost Review Commission's December 2022 refund process report. Directs State agencies to share tax and public assistance benefits data as de facto evidence of patient eligibility. Requires each hospital to reimburse participating State agencies for the costs incurred in implementing the refund process. Authorizes civil fines up to $50,000 per violation and classifies hospital violations as unfair trade practices.
qa_results.responsible_party: Health Services Cost Review Commission; Office of the Comptroller; Maryland Department of Health; Department of Human Services; Maryland State Department of Education; Health Education and Advocacy Unit in the Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Hospital patients who paid more than $25 out of pocket for hospital care between 2017 and 2021 while eligible for free care; hospitals in Maryland; local education agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase in FY 2024 and FY 2025 for affected agencies to conduct data matching and patient assistance, including approximately $28,000 annually for the Comptroller's Office. State revenues increase correspondingly because hospitals must reimburse State entities for all implementation costs, resulting in generally no net effect on State finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HSCRC is the primary regulatory body charged with developing, modifying, and overseeing the hospital financial assistance refund process, coordinating with other agencies, calculating hospital cost reimbursements to state entities, reporting to the General Assembly, and levying civil penalties up to $50,000 per violation.

The Health Education and Advocacy Unit (HEAU) within the Office of the Attorney General is specifically tasked with assisting patients in obtaining refunds, requesting and receiving patient data, and receiving cost reimbursement from hospitals. In addition, violations of the Act are enforceable by the OAG as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act.

The Comptroller's Office is required to match hospital patient data with state tax records to identify patients with incomes at or below 200% of the federal poverty level, share confidential tax information as authorized, and receive reimbursement from hospitals for incurred costs.

The Maryland Department of Health is required to coordinate with HSCRC, match patient data against public health assistance program enrollment data (such as WIC), share information with hospitals and state entities, and receive cost reimbursement from hospitals.

The Department of Human Services coordinates in developing the refund process, matches patient records against benefit programs including SNAP and the State energy assistance program for presumptive eligibility, shares relevant data, and receives reimbursement from hospitals for expenses incurred.

The Maryland State Department of Education is added as a coordinating entity to match patient information against enrollment data for the free and reduced-cost meal program, disclose necessary data, report to HSCRC, and obtain reimbursement from hospitals for operational costs.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date of the Maryland Lynching Truth and Reconciliation Commission to June 30, 2026. Delays the required submission date for the Commission's final report to December 1, 2025. Requires the Commission to deliver its final findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly. Continues the statutory operations and authority of the Commission for an additional two years.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Lynching Truth and Reconciliation Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Families and communities affected by racially motivated lynchings in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on state revenues. The Commission can continue operations with existing resources through its extended termination date.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly extends the operational sunset date and final reporting deadline for the Maryland Lynching Truth and Reconciliation Commission.

Bowie State University, a member institution of the University System of Maryland, provides primary staffing and administrative support for the Commission, and this operational commitment is extended under the bill.
The Office of the Attorney General is statutorily required to provide dedicated staff to assist the Commission and exercise subpoena authority on its behalf throughout its extended duration.
The Commission is mandated to submit its final report of findings and restorative justice recommendations directly to the Governor by December 1, 2025.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the membership of the Advisory Board of the Alcohol Beverage Services of Montgomery County. Authorizes the Director of Alcohol Beverage Services to designate an alternate representative to the board. Permits the Director of the Montgomery County Department of Police to send a designee. Maintains the existing seats for the Board of License Commissioners Chair and five appointed county residents.
qa_results.responsible_party: Advisory Board of the Alcohol Beverage Services of Montgomery County; Montgomery County Alcohol Beverage Services; Montgomery County Department of Police
qa_results.stakeholders: Advisory Board of the Alcohol Beverage Services of Montgomery County, Montgomery County Alcohol Beverage Services leadership, and Montgomery County Department of Police leadership
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. The bill is not anticipated to materially affect Montgomery County operations or finances.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the termination date for funding the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund. Requires the Comptroller to distribute $250,000 annually from abandoned property funds to the fund. Distributes fund grants equally to the University of Maryland School of Law and University of Baltimore School of Law. Distributes one-third of the grant funds to the Maryland Volunteer Lawyers Service. Supports legal clinics that assist low-income Maryland residents with tax disputes.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Low-income Maryland residents facing tax disputes, University of Maryland School of Law, University of Baltimore School of Law, and Maryland Volunteer Lawyers Service
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by $250,000 annually beginning in FY 2024 due to the permanent distribution from the Unclaimed Property Fund to the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund (TCLIM). In FY 2024, TCLIM special fund revenues and expenditures increase by $250,000, and higher education revenues and expenditures increase by $166,700. Starting in FY 2025, general fund expenditures are assumed to decrease by $250,000 annually, resulting in no net state fiscal effect. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller administers both the unclaimed/abandoned property funds and the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund, and is responsible for making the permanent $250,000 annual distribution to the Fund.

Two constituent institutions (the University of Maryland School of Law and the University of Baltimore School of Law) each receive a mandatory one-third distribution of grant funds to operate tax clinics for low-income residents.
The State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund separately and invest its moneys.
The bill permanently diverts $250,000 annually from General Fund revenues and directly impacts state budget formulations and assumptions regarding appropriations.
The statute specifically references the Governor's discretionary authority to include an annual budget appropriation to the Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters public hearing requirements for the Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission when filling school board vacancies. Requires at least one public meeting in the councilmanic district or at administrative offices for single vacancies. Mandates website publication of live video streams and complete unedited archived recordings of each public meeting. Authorizes the Commission to retain and reactivate candidate applications for up to two years with applicant consent. Sets 14-day deadlines for requesting and receiving consent to reactivate an application after a new vacancy occurs.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission; Baltimore County Public Schools
qa_results.stakeholders: applicants and nominees for the Baltimore County Board of Education, Baltimore County Public Schools, and Baltimore County residents
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Baltimore County can implement the bill's requirements using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor is responsible for appointing members to the Baltimore County Board of Education from the list of nominees submitted by the Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission, whose vacancy and nomination procedures are modified by the bill.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting, managing, and processing appointments to state and local boards, including gubernatorial appointments to the Baltimore County Board of Education.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the termination date on the Maryland School for the Blind's eligibility for Public School Construction Program funding. Maintains the school's eligibility for state capital improvement and construction funding beyond fiscal 2028. Directs the Interagency Commission on School Construction to adopt regulations for funding projects at the school. Applies statutory requirements governing construction and capital improvement projects funded for county boards of education. Takes effect June 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Interagency Commission on School Construction
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland School for the Blind; local school systems
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on total State revenues or expenditures, as Public School Construction Program funding is determined annually through the capital budget process. Beginning in fiscal 2029, Public School Construction Program funds awarded to the Maryland School for the Blind may decrease funding available for local school systems.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Interagency Commission on School Construction (IAC) with adopting regulations for school construction and capital improvements at the Maryland School for the Blind, and permanently extends the school's eligibility for funding administered by the IAC under the Public School Construction Program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Governor annually to proclaim March 9 as 6888th Central Postal Directory Battalion Day. Recognizes the wartime service of the women of the 6888th Central Postal Directory Battalion during World War II. Renumbers existing statutory sections within the General Provisions Article to codify the commemoration. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: women veterans, families and descendants of the 6888th Central Postal Directory Battalion, and the general public
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State or local expenditures or revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Governor annually proclaim March 9 as 6888th Central Postal Directory Battalion Day.

As the primary state department dedicated to recognizing and supporting military veterans and their history, the department has an interest in and may participate in commemorations honoring the World War II service of the 6888th Central Postal Directory Battalion.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the threshold for indemnity mortgage transactions exempt from recordation tax from $3,000,000 to less than $15,000,000. Applies the exemption to mortgages securing repayment of a loan or series of qualifying loans. Requires county tax collectors or circuit court clerks to submit an annual report starting July 1, 2025. Directs reports to the Senate Budget and Taxation Committee and House Ways and Means Committee. Requires reports to detail exempt mortgage counts, secured debt amounts, and forgone recordation tax revenue. Takes effect July 1, 2024, applying to instruments of writing recorded on or after that date.
qa_results.responsible_party: Clerks of the Circuit Court; County Tax Collectors
qa_results.stakeholders: Commercial borrowers, loan guarantors, commercial lenders, and Maryland counties and Baltimore City
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential significant decrease in local recordation tax revenues beginning in fiscal 2025.
