qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Natural Resources Article to authorize the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) to permit Sunday hunting for game birds and mammals in Worcester County on private and designated public lands, as well as alters the archery hunting safety zone in the county.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits a person from setting on fire or burning oriented strand board for fire-fighting training purposes. Excludes the manufacture, sale, use, or distribution of oriented strand board for purposes outside fire-fighting training. Establishes an administrative penalty not exceeding $500 for a first violation. Subjects a violator to a civil penalty not exceeding $1,000 for a second or subsequent violation. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: fire departments, public and private fire-fighting training academies, and emergency personnel conducting fire training
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $57,100 in FY 2024 for MDE enforcement and outreach staffing, continuing through FY 2026. Local government expenditures may increase to dispose of existing oriented strand board and purchase alternative training materials.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill adds a new subtitle to the Environment Article and assigns regulatory oversight to the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE). MDE incurs a direct fiscal impact to hire a contractual environmental compliance specialist to conduct outreach, investigate complaints, and enforce the prohibition against burning oriented strand board in fire-fighting training.

The Maryland State Police (which includes the Office of the State Fire Marshal) oversees fire safety and fire service regulations, and was evaluated as an entity that conducts or oversees fire-fighting training, though it reported no current use of oriented strand board.

The agency conducts specialized aircraft rescue and fire-fighting training at state-owned airports (BWI and Martin State) and was evaluated for potential operational impacts or material replacements under the bill.
DNR's Maryland Forest Service conducts wildfire suppression and wildland fire-fighting training, making it subject to review regarding the materials used in fire training operations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the initial designation period of a Regional Institution Strategic Enterprise (RISE) zone from 5 years to 10 years. Authorizes the Secretary of Commerce to approve up to four RISE zones in Baltimore City. Extends the termination date of the RISE Zone Program and associated benefits to January 1, 2030. Includes RISE zones in the statutory definition of Maryland Economic Development Corporation infrastructure financing obligations. Authorizes political subdivisions to pledge local tax revenues to secure debt service on those obligations. Requires the Department of Commerce to study program effectiveness and report recommendations by December 15, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Commerce; Maryland Economic Development Corporation
qa_results.stakeholders: businesses located in RISE zones, qualified higher education institutions, regional higher education centers, and local governments including Baltimore City
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected through FY 2028, but extending the program may increase rental assistance matching grant expenditures in FY 2029 and FY 2030. MEDCO nonbudgeted revenues and expenditures may increase beginning in FY 2024. Local property tax revenues may decrease beginning in FY 2025 due to extensions of legacy property tax credits, while local expenditures and matching revenues for rental assistance and infrastructure obligations may increase.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Commerce administers the RISE Zone Program. The bill extends the program's sunset date, lengthens zone designations from 5 to 10 years, increases the number of allowable zones in Baltimore City, and mandates that the Department conduct a study on program effectiveness and report to the General Assembly.

The bill amends statutory provisions regarding MEDCO obligations to explicitly include infrastructure improvements located in or supporting a RISE zone and authorizes political subdivisions to pledge special fund and tax revenues to secure MEDCO obligations, directly impacting MEDCO's financing activities and operations.

The bill extends the termination date for the RISE Zone Program and its authorized tax credits and benefits through January 1, 2030, impacting tax incentives administered and collected by the Comptroller's Office.

Public four-year higher education institutions within USM serve as qualified institutions anchoring RISE zones, can sponsor rental assistance programs for businesses in the zones, and are key stakeholders consulted in Commerce's mandated study.

As a public research university located in Baltimore City, Morgan State qualifies as an institutional anchor for RISE zones and could be directly impacted by the bill's increase in the cap on allowable RISE zones in Baltimore City from three to four.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires certain public senior higher education institutions, in consultation with students, to develop and implement a reproductive health services plan. Sets a deadline of August 1, 2024, for plan implementation and mandates annual updates. Requires plans to provide or refer students to comprehensive contraception, sexually transmitted infection treatment, and abortion care. Mandates 24-hour access to over-the-counter contraception on campus through health centers, retail establishments, or vending machines. Authorizes the University of Baltimore to provide over-the-counter contraception in lieu of developing a plan. Requires the Maryland Department of Health to assist institutions upon request.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; University System of Maryland; Morgan State University; St. Mary's College of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Students enrolled at public senior higher education institutions in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Higher education expenditures increase for some institutions, particularly for one-time setup costs in fiscal 2024, which may be offset by student fees. The Maryland Department of Health can likely provide required assistance using existing budgeted resources. Specific dollar figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that constituent institutions of the University System of Maryland develop, implement, and annually update a reproductive health services plan, or in the case of the University of Baltimore, provide 24-hour access to over-the-counter contraception.

Morgan State University is explicitly designated as a public senior higher education institution required to develop, implement, and annually update a comprehensive reproductive health services plan for students.

St. Mary's College of Maryland is explicitly designated as a public senior higher education institution required to develop, implement, and annually update a comprehensive reproductive health services plan for students.

The Maryland Department of Health is statutorily required to provide technical assistance and clinical guidance upon request to public senior higher education institutions developing their reproductive health services plans.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of Veterans Affairs to bury an eligible spouse or dependent of a veteran without charge. Mandates that the Department provide a grave liner at no cost for an eligible spouse or dependent. Prohibits the Department from charging for opening and closing the plot for an eligible spouse or dependent. Defines eligible spouses and dependents based on federal national veterans' cemetery eligibility standards. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Veterans Affairs
qa_results.stakeholders: Eligible spouses and dependents of qualifying military veterans seeking burial in Maryland State veterans' cemeteries
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: MDVA special fund revenues decrease, likely by a significant amount, beginning in FY 2024 due to eliminated interment fees and grave liner charges. General fund expenditures increase accordingly to backfill the lost fee revenue and maintain the Cemetery Program, illustratively estimated at $1.24 million annually.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Department of Veterans Affairs (now Department of Veterans & Military Families) bury eligible spouses and dependents of veterans in State veterans' cemeteries at no charge and provide grave liners at no cost, which eliminates fee revenue and directly impacts the operations and funding of its Cemetery Program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes that prior convictions for drunk or drugged driving constitute prior convictions when calculating subsequent vessel operating penalties. Treats prior convictions for operating a vessel while under the influence or impaired as prior convictions for driving offenses. Applies enhanced penalties to repeat driving offenders previously convicted of grossly negligent manslaughter by vehicle or vessel. Counts equivalent violations committed in other states or under federal law as prior convictions. Imposes misdemeanor penalties of up to 10 years imprisonment, a $10,000 fine, or both for specified repeat violations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Judiciary; Department of Natural Resources; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals convicted of driving or operating a vessel while under the influence of alcohol, impaired by alcohol or drugs, or convicted of grossly negligent manslaughter by vehicle or vessel
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in State general fund revenues from District Court fines and potential minimal increase in State correctional expenditures due to longer sentences. Potential minimal increase in local revenues from circuit court fines and potential minimal decrease in local incarceration expenditures as individuals shift to State facilities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Natural Resources Article (§ 8-738) concerning the operation of vessels while under the influence or impaired, which is enforced and administered by the Department of Natural Resources and its Natural Resources Police.

The bill amends § 21-902 of the Transportation Article governing penalties for driving under the influence or impaired by alcohol or drugs, establishing cross-applicability with vessel operating convictions.

As the modal administration within MDOT responsible for driver records, driver licensing, and traffic safety compliance, the MVA tracks vehicle convictions and sanctions related to § 21-902 violations.

The Judiciary (District and Circuit courts) adjudicates motor vehicle and vessel impairment offenses, determines subsequent offender status based on prior convictions, and imposes enhanced statutory penalties and fines.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Attorneys with the Office of the Public Defender represent indigent clients charged with criminal driving or boating offenses who face enhanced criminal subsequent-offender penalties and longer potential terms of imprisonment.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS manages State correctional facilities, which may experience a minimal fiscal impact and increased commitment lengths if defendants receive higher terms of incarceration under subsequent offender provisions.
As the primary state law enforcement agency enforcing motor vehicle laws and impaired driving statutes, MSP investigates and charges individuals under § 21-902 of the Transportation Article.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Task Force to Study Nonpublic Student Bus Transportation. Requires the Maryland State Department of Education to chair and provide staff for the Task Force. Directs the Task Force to collect data from local school boards regarding nonpublic student busing programs. Mandates evaluation of traffic congestion, fiscal impacts, and nonpublic busing models adopted by other states. Requires the Task Force to report findings and recommendations to specified legislative committees by December 15, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Task Force to Study Nonpublic Student Bus Transportation
qa_results.stakeholders: nonpublic school students and administrators, local boards of education, school bus drivers, and county departments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expense reimbursements and staffing costs for the Maryland State Department of Education can be absorbed with existing budgeted resources. Local school boards and county governments can provide required information using existing budgeted resources. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) to provide staff for the Task Force to Study Nonpublic Student Bus Transportation. Additionally, the Director of the Office of Pupil Transportation and Emergency Management within MSDE chairs the task force, another MSDE director serves as a member, and MSDE is responsible for designating several other members.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new temporary body, the Task Force to Study Nonpublic Student Bus Transportation, to examine nonpublic student busing programs, evaluate potential policies and programs, and submit findings and recommendations to the General Assembly.
The Secretary of Transportation, or the Secretary's designee, is named as a member of the Task Force to Study Nonpublic Student Bus Transportation.

The task force is required to consult with the Comptroller when evaluating the impact on State revenues and expenditures of potential credits against the State income tax for student bus transportation expenses or other financial support.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes school vehicles in Anne Arundel County to operate for up to 15 years instead of 12 years. Requires vehicles operating past 12 years to meet applicable school bus and motor vehicle safety standards. Mandates compliance with a preventive maintenance plan approved by state authorities. Requires an inspection at the end of the twelfth year and at least two inspections each year thereafter. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration; Department of State Police; Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Anne Arundel County Public Schools, school vehicle contractors, bus drivers, and public school students in Anne Arundel County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State finances or Anne Arundel County Public School System finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Education Article regarding the operational life of school vehicles in Anne Arundel County and affects oversight and waiver policies administered under the State Superintendent of Schools and the Maryland State Department of Education.

The bill directly involves the Motor Vehicle Administration, which inspects school vehicles operating beyond standard limits and approves preventive maintenance plans and structural repair certifications pursuant to Section 7-804 of the Education Article.

The Automotive Safety Enforcement Division of the Department of State Police is statutorily tasked under Section 7-804 with jointly approving preventive maintenance plans for extended-use school vehicles.
The Department of Transportation oversees the Motor Vehicle Administration and general vehicle safety regulations and school bus standards in Maryland.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits the State Department of Education from altering the Child Care Scholarship Program in effect January 1, 2023. Prohibits increasing copayment levels, reducing reimbursement rates, reducing income eligibility requirements, or implementing enrollment freezes. Authorizes these alterations if the department notifies four specified General Assembly committees. Prohibits implementing notified alterations until the completion of the immediately following regular legislative session. Authorizes alterations during the fiscal year if the Board of Public Works approves program budget reductions.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Board of Public Works
qa_results.stakeholders: Low-income families participating in or eligible for the Child Care Scholarship Program and participating child care providers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal impact in fiscal 2024. Future-year general fund expenditure impacts are indeterminate, but restricting the Maryland State Department of Education's ability to freeze enrollment, raise copayments, or reduce subsidy rates and eligibility may significantly limit cost-saving measures when federal funds expire. No effect on local finances or state revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE administers the Child Care Scholarship Program. The bill directly restricts MSDE from increasing copayment levels, lowering reimbursement rates, lowering income eligibility thresholds, or implementing enrollment freezes without submitting advance legislative notification or receiving Board of Public Works budget reduction approval.

The bill explicitly establishes that if the Board of Public Works approves budget reductions for the program under § 7-213 of the State Finance and Procurement Article, MSDE may make alterations (such as rate cuts, copay increases, eligibility reductions, or freezes) at any time during that fiscal year.

DBM oversees statewide budget execution, long-term fiscal planning, and the formulation of § 7-213 budget reduction proposals submitted to the Board of Public Works. The bill restricts fiscal flexibility and could significantly impact general fund expenditures in future fiscal years.

The bill reenacts provisions governing the program's payment process, under which the Comptroller is statutory tasked with disbursing payments to child care providers within 5 days of receiving notice from MSDE.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the statutory provisions establishing and governing the Rural Health Collaborative Pilot. Requires the Governor to include an annual budget appropriation beginning in fiscal year 2024. Directs the mandated funding to support operations of the Mid Shore Health Improvement Coalition. Eliminates statutory procedures and governance structures for establishing rural health complexes. Supports regional health collaboration across Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne’s, and Talbot counties.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Office of the Governor
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents, healthcare providers, and local health departments in Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne’s, and Talbot counties, and the Mid Shore Health Improvement Coalition
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures of $150,000 annually are maintained beyond fiscal 2023 but shift from the Rural Health Collaborative Pilot to the Mid Shore Health Improvement Coalition. State revenues are unaffected. Local revenues and expenditures shift accordingly from the Kent County Health Department to the regional coalition.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals the Rural Health Collaborative Pilot, which was established as an independent unit within the Department of Health, and mandates funding for the Mid Shore Health Improvement Coalition to address regional public health priorities.
The bill statutorily mandates that the Governor include an annual appropriation in the State budget starting in fiscal year 2024 to fund the operations of the Mid Shore Health Improvement Coalition.
As the principal agency responsible for preparing and supervising the annual State budget, DBM must incorporate and administer the statutory mandated general fund appropriation of $150,000 annually.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Board of Public Works to allow the public to electronically submit comments on meeting agenda items. Applies this requirement to board meetings held on or after October 1, 2024. Directs the board to include submitted comments in meeting packets and post them online. Mandates the retention of public comments online through the board's website. Excludes discussion items not subject to open meetings requirements from public comment. Requires the board to employ at least one additional staff position beyond fiscal 2023 authorized levels.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Public Works
qa_results.stakeholders: Members of the public participating in Board of Public Works proceedings, and Board of Public Works staff and members.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $227,400 in FY 2024 to hire one computer operator manager and develop an online public comment web portal, and by $92,200 in FY 2025 for ongoing personnel and operating expenses. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Board of Public Works establish an electronic public comment submission process for its agenda items, include comments in meeting packets, post and retain them online, and hire an additional staff member to carry out these requirements.

As noted in the fiscal note, the Department of Information Technology provides IT services to the Board of Public Works on a fee-for-service basis and is anticipated to administer the new web portal required to receive, post, and store public comments.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of Human Services to automatically restore public assistance benefits lost due to theft. Requires the department to decide, restore stolen benefits, and issue a replacement card within 10 days. Prohibits the department from requiring a police report as a condition of benefit restoration. Authorizes households to request an administrative hearing within 90 days to dispute restoration decisions. Authorizes the department to restore benefits lost to theft between January 1, 2021, and October 1, 2022. Requires the State to give procurement preference to electronic benefit distribution vendors offering identity fraud protections.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Human Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) cardholders, recipients of public assistance benefits, and electronic benefits distribution vendors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by up to $1.9 million in FY 2023, $6.2 million in FY 2024, and $4.2 million annually thereafter for benefit restorations. Federal fund revenues offset SNAP benefit reimbursements through FY 2025. Local law enforcement agencies can handle reporting consultation duties using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHS is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) programs, investigating benefit theft, automatically restoring stolen benefits, issuing new cards, enhancing EBT security features, and submitting an annual report to the General Assembly.

As the State's central procurement authority, DGS is impacted by the bill's procurement preferences for EBT distribution and administration vendors and must establish procurement templates, guidelines, and training for DHS solicitations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Greenspace Equity Program and Advisory Board within the Department of Natural Resources. Authorizes grants to eligible land trusts, nongovernmental organizations, counties, and municipalities for community greenspace projects. Targets projects located in or adjacent to overburdened communities and underserved communities. Redirects Program Open Space funds up to $5,000,000 in fiscal 2025, rising to $10,000,000 annually by fiscal 2027. Requires recommended grant applications to undergo State Clearinghouse review and receive Board of Public Works approval.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources; Board of Public Works; Greenspace Equity Advisory Board; Maryland Department of Planning
qa_results.stakeholders: residents of overburdened communities and underserved communities, land trusts, nongovernmental organizations, and county and municipal governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $101,000 in FY 2024 and $365,700 in FY 2025 for agency administration. Special fund allocations under Program Open Space of up to $5.0 million in FY 2025, $7.0 million in FY 2026, and $10.0 million annually thereafter are redirected to grants, causing no net change to special fund expenditures. Local revenues and expenditures may increase beginning in FY 2025 to the extent local governments receive grants.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes and requires the Department of Natural Resources to administer the Greenspace Equity Program, provide staff for the Greenspace Equity Advisory Board, develop grant applications and regulations, and award grants funded through redirected Program Open Space funds.
Each grant application recommended for an award under the Greenspace Equity Program is statutorily subject to final review and approval by the Board of Public Works.

Grant applications recommended for award must be submitted to the Maryland State Clearinghouse for Intergovernmental Assistance (housed within MDP) for review and comment. Additionally, the Secretary of Planning must approve any proposed conversion of land acquired under the program to another use.
The Secretary of Budget and Management must provide prior written approval before any land acquired through the program can be converted from outdoor public recreation or open space to any other use.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Greenspace Equity Advisory Board as an advisory body to consult with and advise the Department of Natural Resources on program implementation and grant application review.
The Governor is tasked with appointing multiple members to the newly created Greenspace Equity Advisory Board and designating the chair of the board.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in the recruitment, vetting, and processing of gubernatorial appointees to the newly established Greenspace Equity Advisory Board.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Developmental Disabilities Council as an independent unit of State government. Requires the Council to operate and receive funding under the federal Developmental Disabilities Assistance and Bill of Rights Act. Mandates that the Council develop, implement, and annually evaluate a five-year strategic plan. Requires the Governor to appoint members, with at least 60% representing individuals with developmental disabilities and families. Prohibits State entities from interfering with Council advocacy, budget, personnel, or plan implementation.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Developmental Disabilities Council; Governor
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals with developmental disabilities, their parents, guardians, and immediate relatives, and disability service providers in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact beyond minimal, absorbable operational costs for the Maryland Department of Aging. The Council is an existing entity fully funded under federal law.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Disabilities (or a designee) is designated by statute as a member of the Maryland Developmental Disabilities Council, and the Council's advocacy directly aligns with the Department's core mission.

The bill mandates three representatives from units within the Department of Health to serve on the Council: the Deputy Secretary of the Developmental Disabilities Administration, a representative of the Prevention and Health Promotion Administration, and a representative of the Maryland Medical Assistance Program.
The bill establishes that the Secretary of Aging (or a designee) will serve as a member of the Council, adding MDoA representation where it previously was not included.
The State Superintendent of Schools and the Assistant State Superintendent of the Division of Rehabilitation Services (both within MSDE) are mandated members of the Council.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill codifies into State law the Maryland Developmental Disabilities Council to advise government leadership, evaluate State plans, and conduct advocacy and capacity-building activities.
The Governor appoints all members of the Council, and the Council is tasked with advising the Governor on policies and programs affecting individuals with developmental disabilities.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments to the Council to meet specific statutory composition requirements.

qa_results.bill_summary: Subjects elevator units installed in privately owned single-family residential dwellings on or after October 1, 2023, to registration and inspection requirements. Requires owners or lessees to register the unit at least 60 days before planned completion and placement in service. Requires the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to conduct a final acceptance inspection before the elevator enters service. Prohibits the Commissioner from disclosing unit registration information to the public. Requires the Commissioner to delete the registration upon completion of the final acceptance inspection. Exempts these residential elevator units from statutory reregistration requirements.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Commissioner of Labor and Industry
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners and lessees of privately owned single-family residential dwellings with newly installed elevators, elevator contractors and mechanics, and state elevator inspectors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures for the Maryland Department of Labor increase by $171,900 in FY 2024 to hire two elevator inspectors, increasing to $235,500 by FY 2028. State special fund revenues to the Elevator Safety Review Board Fund increase by $109,700 in FY 2024 and approximately $146,300 annually thereafter from inspection fees. Local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor's Commissioner of Labor and Industry administers elevator safety laws and oversees the Elevator Safety Inspection Unit. The bill directly requires the Commissioner to handle registrations, conduct final acceptance inspections for newly installed residential elevators, and hire additional safety inspectors, resulting in notable fiscal impacts on department expenditures and revenues.

The Maryland Department of Labor's Elevator Safety Inspection Unit is funded through an annual appropriation from the Workers' Compensation Commission. Consequently, the addition of new elevator inspection staff and related operating costs impacts the commission's funding stream and could theoretically influence employer assessment rates.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires each county or municipal corporation to define by law who is a law enforcement officer or rescue worker. Expands eligibility for local property tax credits granted on qualifying dwellings. Covers officers or rescue workers domiciled in Maryland within five years before being adjudged disabled or dying. Authorizes the credit for eligible surviving spouses and cohabitants meeting the five-year domicile standard. Takes effect June 1, 2023, and applies to taxable years beginning after June 30, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City; governing body of each county or municipal corporation
qa_results.stakeholders: disabled law enforcement officers, disabled rescue workers, surviving spouses, cohabitants, and county and municipal governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential decrease in local property tax revenues beginning in FY 2024 to the extent local credits are authorized and additional taxpayers qualify. The specific revenue decrease cannot be reliably estimated. Local expenditures and State finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board hears appeals and resolves disputes regarding property valuations, tax exemptions, and property tax credits. Clarifications and expansions to eligibility criteria for local property tax credits may occasionally lead to administrative appeals brought before the local boards.

The Maryland Tax Court serves as the highest administrative body for reviewing property tax disputes and appeals arising from decisions of local taxing authorities and Property Tax Assessment Appeals Boards, including determinations regarding property tax credit eligibility.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the State Board of Elections to publish municipal election results immediately on its website upon submission. Mandates organizing the published results by election year and the name of the municipality. Requires municipalities to submit certified election results to the State Board within 30 days after certification. Requires vote totals for each office or question reported separately by voting method, if applicable. Includes in-person early voting, mail-in voting or vote-by-mail, provisional voting, and in-person election day voting. Mandates reporting candidate party affiliation if the municipality conducts partisan elections.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland municipalities, municipal election officials, municipal candidates, and municipal voters
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local government finances are not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 509 directly requires the Maryland State Board of Elections to publish municipal election results submitted by municipalities on its website, organized by election year and municipality.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Labor to enforce prevailing wage requirements for contractors on investor-owned utility underground infrastructure projects. Specifies that prevailing wage rates are determined solely by the Commissioner of Labor and Industry. Requires covered contractors and subcontractors to request wage determinations from the Department by October 1, 2023. Directs the Commissioner to determine initial wage rates by hand survey by December 1, 2023, if no rates apply. Requires the Commissioner to waive civil penalties for noncompliant contractors who achieve compliance by March 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Commissioner of Labor and Industry
qa_results.stakeholders: Investor-owned gas and electric companies, contractors and subcontractors performing underground utility work and related traffic control, and utility construction workers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not materially affected because the Maryland Department of Labor can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. Assuming general compliance by contractors and subcontractors, State revenues are not materially affected. There is no direct local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Department of Labor and the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to enforce prevailing wage requirements on underground utility infrastructure projects, issue wage determinations, provide guidance to contractors, and conduct wage surveys if needed.

The bill amends the Public Utilities Article concerning investor-owned gas and electric utilities regulated by the Public Service Commission, clarifying that prevailing wage enforcement rests with the Department of Labor rather than the Commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the annual deadline for the Maryland Department of Agriculture to submit a report on antimicrobial drug use. Moves the reporting date to the General Assembly from February 1 to July 1 each year. Retains the February 1 deadline for licensed veterinarians to submit drug records and animal accounting to the department. Governs reported data on medically important antimicrobial drugs administered to cattle, swine, and poultry.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture
qa_results.stakeholders: licensed veterinarians who prescribe antimicrobial drugs for food-producing animals, and owners and operators of cattle, swine, and poultry farm operations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The reporting date change is procedural in nature and does not directly affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 516 directly alters the statutory annual deadline from February 1 to July 1 for the Maryland Department of Agriculture to submit its report to the General Assembly regarding the use of medically important antimicrobial drugs in cattle, swine, and poultry.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes an art establishment beer and wine license in the City of Annapolis. Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners to issue the license to qualifying nonprofit organizations. Restricts eligibility to nonprofits primarily engaged in art display, art instruction, or live performances. Prohibits licenses for organizations that sell mass-produced art or lack a dedicated artistic corporate purpose. Authorizes license holders to sell or serve beer and wine at retail for on-premises consumption. Sets the annual license fee at $1,000 and prohibits transferring the license to another location.
qa_results.responsible_party: City of Annapolis Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: nonprofit art organizations in the City of Annapolis
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. City of Annapolis revenues decrease to the extent that the new annual art establishment licenses replace multiple single-use event licenses. City of Annapolis expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland oversees the regulation of the alcohol industry in the state. While HB 520 specifically authorizes the local City of Annapolis Board of License Commissioners to issue art establishment beer and wine licenses with no direct state fiscal impact, it relates to the state's broader alcoholic beverages statutory framework under the Comptroller's general regulatory domain.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Camden Yards Football Sports Facility Supplemental Financing Fund and the Camden Yards Baseball Sports Facility Supplemental Financing Fund within the Maryland Stadium Authority. Establishes the Bus Rapid Transit Fund within the Maryland Department of Transportation to provide grants to eligible local grantees. Alters the required annual distributions of State Lottery Fund proceeds across stadium financing funds and bus rapid transit grants. Expands the Maryland Stadium Authority membership from 9 to 11 members, adding appointments by the Governor and the Prince George's County Executive. Alters the boundary definition for the Prince George's County Blue Line Corridor and specifies that corridor facilities do not include sports facilities. Requires Montgomery County to receive at least $20,000,000 annually in bus rapid transit grants when eligible and multiple grantees qualify.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Stadium Authority; Maryland Department of Transportation; Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Montgomery County; Prince George's County; Maryland Stadium Authority; Baltimore sports franchises; local governments operating or developing bus rapid transit systems
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State General Fund revenues increase by $14.2 million in FY 2024 due to modified lottery distribution triggers, while Maryland Department of Transportation special fund revenues and expenditures decrease correspondingly by $14.2 million. Local revenues and expenditures for Montgomery County decrease by $14.2 million in FY 2024, with potential reallocation of transit grant funding among local governments in FY 2025 and later.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 524 directly impacts MSA by expanding its board membership and establishing two new nonlapsing funds—the Camden Yards Football Sports Facility Supplemental Financing Fund and the Camden Yards Baseball Sports Facility Supplemental Financing Fund—which MSA is tasked with administering to manage debt service and facility expenses.

The bill creates the Bus Rapid Transit Fund within MDOT, tasks the department with administering the fund, and modifies statutory formulas and eligibility criteria for MDOT's distribution of bus rapid transit system grants.

The Comptroller is responsible for accounting for the newly established funds and adjusting monthly distributions from the State Lottery Fund to the stadium facilities funds and the Bus Rapid Transit Fund.

The State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold the newly established Camden Yards sports facility supplemental financing funds and the Bus Rapid Transit Fund separately and invest their moneys in the same manner as other State funds.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters statutory distributions of State Lottery Fund proceeds and requires agency regulations to apportion lottery money in accordance with the amended statutory schedule.
The bill expands the Maryland Stadium Authority membership, increasing the number of members appointed by the Governor from six to seven.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting and vetting candidates for state boards and commissions, including the newly added gubernatorial seat on the Maryland Stadium Authority.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Outdoor Preschool License Pilot Program in the Maryland State Department of Education. Requires the department to license outdoor, nature-based early learning and child care programs. Directs the department to select between five and 10 participating programs for the initial school year. Mandates the adoption of licensing regulations governing health, safety, and operating standards in outdoor classrooms. Requires the department to submit interim implementation reports and a final findings report by December 1, 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Outdoor, nature-based early learning and child care providers, licensed child care centers, registered family child care homes, enrolled preschool children, and their families
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland State Department of Education can implement the pilot program and comply with reporting requirements using existing resources. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly establishes the Outdoor Preschool License Pilot Program within the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), requiring the department to administer the program, adopt regulations, select participating programs, convene an advisory group, and submit progress reports.
The bill references programs licensed as camps by the Maryland Department of Health, establishing priority selection for these entities to participate in the pilot program.
The Maryland State Department of Education is required to submit interim and final implementation and evaluation reports on the pilot program directly to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Transfers all child support enforcement functions and personnel from the St. Mary's County State's Attorney's Office to the Child Support Administration. Requires the Department of Budget and Management to create State positions for transferred personnel within the Department of Human Services. Grants transferred employees credit for county employment toward State seniority, leave accumulation, and layoff rights without reducing compensation. Requires St. Mary's County to pay transferred employees any salary compensation due upon termination of county employment. Directs the transfer of county employer pension contributions and interest from the municipal pool to the State pool.
qa_results.responsible_party: Child Support Administration; Department of Human Services; Department of Budget and Management; Office of the Attorney General; Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System
qa_results.stakeholders: Employees of the Child Support Unit of the Office of the State's Attorney for St. Mary's County, child support recipients and obligors in St. Mary's County, and St. Mary's County government
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $236,300 in FY 2024 (and $251,900 to $289,300 annually thereafter) to absorb operating costs and personnel, while federal fund expenditures increase by $38,400 in FY 2024. State general fund revenues decrease by $24,200 in FY 2024 and $32,300 annually from the loss of the county administrative fee. St. Mary's County expenditures decrease by an estimated $249,200 in FY 2024 and at least $332,300 annually thereafter.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly transfers the functions, duties, and personnel of the Child Support Unit of the Office of the State's Attorney for St. Mary's County to the Child Support Administration within the Department of Human Services, resulting in notable operational and expenditure impacts.

The bill explicitly mandates the Department of Budget and Management to create and establish new State Position Identification Numbers (PINs) allocated to the Department of Human Services for the transferred employees.

The bill authorizes the Office of the Attorney General to appoint legal personnel (an Assistant State's Attorney) transitioning from county service to continue providing child support legal services as a State employee.

The bill requires employer contributions and interest for transferred employees to be shifted from the municipal pool to the State pool within the State Employees' Pension System, requiring actuarial valuation oversight designated by the system's Board of Trustees.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the State Retirement and Pension System to transfer eligible members' service credit to the Correctional Officers' Retirement System. Authorizes affected individuals to elect not to transfer service credit on or before June 1, 2024. Makes certain transferred members eligible to receive retirement creditable service for unused sick leave accrued in prior systems. Extends unused sick leave credit adjustments to specified Department of Juvenile Services positions transferred on or after July 1, 2022. Requires earlier transfer of service credit if an eligible individual applies to retire before June 30, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System; State Retirement Agency
qa_results.stakeholders: Current members of the Correctional Officers' Retirement System transferred from the Employees' Retirement System or Employees' Pension System, including specified Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services and Department of Juvenile Services personnel.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State pension liabilities and contributions increase minimally across all funds beginning in fiscal 2025, but a precise estimate is not feasible. There is no effect on local revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency (SRA) administers the State Retirement and Pension System and is directly responsible for executing the transfer of service credit from ERS/EPS to CORS, providing the opt-out election forms to members, and recalculating creditable service for unused sick leave.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly affects DPSCS employees transferred into CORS under prior enactments (including case management specialists, parole and probation agents, and maintenance officers) regarding the transfer of their pension service credit.

The bill directly impacts DJS staff (including detention officers, resident advisors, case management specialists, and group life managers) concerning the transfer of their pension service credit and eligibility for unused sick leave credits.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the distribution of video lottery terminal local impact grants within Baltimore City for fiscal years 2024 through 2032. Increases the portion dedicated to capital projects consistent with the Park Heights Master Plan from 75% to 85%. Reduces the share dedicated to other specified Baltimore City neighborhoods surrounding Pimlico Race Course from 25% to 15%. Requires Senate advice and consent for ten Pimlico Community Development Authority members appointed by the Mayor of Baltimore City. Repeals the requirement that the Mayor consult with General Assembly members representing legislative districts 40 and 41.
qa_results.responsible_party: Mayor of Baltimore City; Pimlico Community Development Authority; Senate of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: residents, business owners, and community service providers in the Park Heights Corridor and surrounding Baltimore City neighborhoods near Pimlico Race Course
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Total annual local impact grants distributed to Baltimore City remain unchanged, but the bill reallocates grant funding within the city. Funding for Park Heights Master Plan projects increases by $363,500 in FY 2024 (growing to $424,200 by FY 2028), with an equal reduction in funding for other specified nearby Baltimore City neighborhoods.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the membership appointment process for the Pimlico Community Development Authority by requiring the advice and consent of the Senate for certain mayoral appointments. It also alters the formula for video lottery terminal local impact grants that the Authority oversees and advises on for neighborhood revitalization.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency regulates commercial gaming and video lottery terminal operations in Maryland, which generate the local impact grant revenues distributed under this legislation.
The Comptroller receives statutorily required reports from the Legislative Policy Committee regarding the continuation of video lottery terminal fund distributions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires local boards of elections to begin processing absentee ballots eight business days before early voting. Mandates sending absentee ballots at least 43 days before an election to voters requesting them early. Establishes procedures allowing voters to cure missing signatures on absentee ballot envelopes up to ten days post-election. Directs election boards receiving multiple ballots from one voter to count only the first legally sufficient ballot. Requires the State Board of Elections to report precinct results including early, absentee, and provisional votes. Moves Maryland's 2024 statewide and Baltimore City municipal primary elections to the second Tuesday in May.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Elections; local boards of elections
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland registered voters, absentee and provisional ballot voters, candidates in the 2024 primary election, and local election officials
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $84,100 in FY 2024 and ongoing amounts exceeding $100,000 annually thereafter for an IT programmer and related system costs. Local board of elections expenditures increase beginning in FY 2024 due to additional personnel for early canvassing, flash drives, scanners, and shared contractual software costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 535 directly governs Maryland election administration by altering absentee ballot issuance timelines, canvassing procedures, ballot signature curing processes, and election result reporting requirements. The State Board of Elections is required to adopt regulations, oversee local election board implementation, manage waiver requests, update reporting formats, and hire additional IT personnel and acquire technology solutions to implement ballot curing systems.

qa_results.bill_summary: Excludes retroactive lump sum salary payments from the definition of earnable compensation in the State Retirement and Pension System. Applies this exclusion retroactively to July 1, 2022, while exempting qualifying Maryland Department of Transportation payments. Requires the Board of Trustees to pay accumulated contributions of a deceased nonvested former member to their beneficiary or estate. Specifies twenty-one appointed State agency heads, commissioners, and officials who vest immediately upon taking office.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System; State Retirement Agency
qa_results.stakeholders: Nonvested former members of the State Retirement and Pension System, beneficiaries and estates of deceased members, specified appointed State agency heads and officials, and State employees receiving retroactive lump sum salary payments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State revenues and no local fiscal impact. The bill has no discernible effect on State pension liabilities or contribution rates because the vesting provisions clarify existing law, payment of deceased nonvested members' contributions codifies current practice, and earnable compensation exclusions produce at most a negligible liability reduction.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the administrator of the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS), SRA is the primary implementing agency responsible for executing the definition of earnable compensation, disbursing accumulated contributions of deceased nonvested members, and administering immediate vesting provisions.

The bill explicitly carves out retroactive salary increase lump-sum payments made by the Maryland Department of Transportation between July 1, 2022, and June 30, 2023, from the retroactive exclusion from earnable compensation.
The bill explicitly codifies immediate vesting rights in the State Retirement and Pension System for the Adjutant General upon taking office.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly codifies immediate vesting rights in the State Retirement and Pension System for the Executive Director of the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services (now GOCPP) upon taking office.
The bill explicitly codifies immediate vesting rights in the State Retirement and Pension System for the Director of the Office of Homeland Security upon taking office.
The bill explicitly codifies immediate vesting rights in the State Retirement and Pension System for the Director of the Office of Performance Improvement upon taking office.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly codifies immediate vesting rights in the State Retirement and Pension System for the Special Secretary of the Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs upon taking office.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly codifies immediate vesting rights in the State Retirement and Pension System for the Director of the Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing upon taking office.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Health Care Alternative Dispute Resolution Office
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly codifies immediate vesting rights in the State Retirement and Pension System for the Director of the Health Care Alternative Dispute Resolution Office upon taking office.
The bill explicitly codifies immediate vesting rights in the State Retirement and Pension System for the Director of the Maryland Energy Administration upon taking office.
The bill explicitly codifies immediate vesting rights in the State Retirement and Pension System for the Insurance Commissioner upon taking office.
The bill explicitly codifies immediate vesting rights in the State Retirement and Pension System for the State Archivist upon taking office.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Board of Contract Appeals
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly codifies immediate vesting rights in the State Retirement and Pension System for the Chair of the State Board of Contract Appeals upon taking office.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly codifies immediate vesting rights in the State Retirement and Pension System for the Director of the State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency upon taking office.
The bill explicitly codifies immediate vesting rights in the State Retirement and Pension System for the Chief Administrative Law Judge of the Office of Administrative Hearings upon taking office.
The bill explicitly codifies immediate vesting rights in the State Retirement and Pension System for the State Prosecutor upon taking office.
The bill explicitly codifies immediate vesting rights in the State Retirement and Pension System for the Chair of the Public Service Commission upon taking office.
The bill explicitly codifies immediate vesting rights in the State Retirement and Pension System for the Chair of the Workers' Compensation Commission upon taking office.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the general State small procurement spending threshold from $50,000 to $100,000. Raises the small procurement ceiling for specified revenue-generating service contracts from $50,000 to $100,000. Doubles the small procurement limit to $200,000 for Department of General Services and Maryland Department of Transportation construction contracts. Increases the threshold to $200,000 for Department of Natural Resources capital projects or maintenance contracts. Raises the spending ceiling to $100,000 for State Retirement Agency independent medical evaluation and testimony expenses.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of General Services; Maryland Department of Transportation; Department of Natural Resources; State Retirement Agency; Board of Public Works
qa_results.stakeholders: State procurement agencies and contractors, vendors, and small businesses bidding on State contracts
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State finances, though State agencies may experience administrative efficiencies by using small procurement methods for higher-value purchases. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly increases the small procurement dollar threshold for construction contracts sought by the Department of General Services from $100,000 to $200,000, and as the state's central procurement authority, DGS is directly affected by changes to state small procurement thresholds.
The bill explicitly alters the small procurement definition to raise the maximum contract value for construction procurements sought by the Department of Transportation from $100,000 to $200,000.
The bill explicitly increases the small procurement threshold for contracts sought by the Department of Natural Resources for capital projects or maintenance from $100,000 to $200,000.

The bill explicitly doubles the small procurement threshold from $50,000 to $100,000 for expenditures by the State Retirement Agency regarding independent medical evaluations and related physician hearing testimony.

The Board of Public Works oversees state procurement and is statutory tasked under this section with reviewing labor and material costs every three years to recommend adjustments to small procurement thresholds to the General Assembly.

qa_results.bill_summary: Permanently extends and expands the refundable Maryland earned income tax credit and State child tax credit. Maintains the refundable earned income credit at 45% of the federal credit for eligible residents. Eliminates the $530 cap on the 100% refundable earned income credit for individuals without qualifying children. Expands child tax credit eligibility to resident taxpayers with federal adjusted gross income of $15,000 or less. Includes all qualifying dependents under age six and repeals the credit reduction for federal child tax credits claimed.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Low-to-moderate-income Maryland resident taxpayers, low-income workers without qualifying children, and low-income parents or guardians of dependents under age 6 or dependents under age 17 with disabilities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by $172.3 million in FY 2024, increasing to $186.5 million by FY 2028. General fund expenditures increase by $36,533 in FY 2024 and approximately $60,000 to $70,000 annually thereafter for one revenue examiner in the Comptroller's Office. Local income tax revenues decrease by an estimated $6.1 million in FY 2024 and similar amounts annually thereafter, while Montgomery County expenditures for its local supplement program may increase.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for tax administration and collection. The bill alters the State earned income tax credit and child tax credit, requiring the Comptroller's Office to adjust tax forms, validate claims, and hire additional personnel to process the anticipated increase in credit claims.
This is an Administration bill ('By Request - Administration') championed as a key executive policy initiative (Family Prosperity Act of 2023) to support low-income families and combat poverty.

The bill results in a significant reduction in State general fund revenues exceeding $170 million annually, which directly affects the State budget development, revenue estimates, and long-term fiscal planning managed by DBM.

The office is tasked with coordinating efforts to promote child well-being and reduce child poverty in Maryland, which aligns directly with the bill's permanent expansion of the child tax credit and earned income tax credit for low-income families.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Community Investment Venture Fund as an instrumentality of the State using public and private funds. Authorizes the Commissioner of Financial Regulation to provide an initial equity investment of up to $2,500,000. Authorizes the Commissioner to use up to $250,000 from the regulatory fund for startup and administrative expenses. Authorizes eligible banking institutions and credit unions to request assessment offset credits for branches in low- to moderate-income tracts. Authorizes the Commissioner to match qualifying institutional investments in the venture fund through June 30, 2028.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation
qa_results.stakeholders: State-chartered banking institutions, credit unions, and businesses located in low- to moderate-income census tracts
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures from the Banking Institution and Credit Union Regulation Fund increase by $2,838,500 in fiscal 2024 for initial capital investment, administrative setup costs, and matching expenditures. Special fund revenues decrease by $171,000 in fiscal 2024 and by $310,000 in fiscal 2028 due to assessment offset credits claimed by eligible depository institutions. Local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor. The Commissioner is the primary official tasked with establishing and governing the Maryland Community Investment Venture Fund, authorizing investments, administering assessment offset credits, and regulating banking institutions and credit unions.

The State Treasurer acts as the custodian of the Banking Institution and Credit Union Regulation Fund, receiving and depositing revenues and managing the fund from which initial capital and administrative expenditures for the new venture fund are drawn.

The Department of Budget and Management oversees state budget processes, including budget amendment procedures under § 7-209 of the State Finance and Procurement Article applicable to expenditures from the special fund.
This is an Administration priority bill ('Access to Banking Act') sponsored by request of the Governor to improve capital access and banking services in low- to moderate-income communities.

qa_results.bill_summary: Modifies clean transportation and energy programs administered by the Maryland Energy Administration. Extends the Electric Vehicle Recharging Equipment Rebate Program through fiscal year 2026. Increases the annual rebate cap to $2,500,000 and raises maximum rebate amounts for individuals and businesses. Alters the Medium-Duty and Heavy-Duty Zero-Emission Vehicle Grant Program to cover up to 75% of incremental costs. Limits vehicle grants to commercial or industrial uses and requires preference for overburdened or underserved communities. Raises the administrative expense cap for the Strategic Energy Investment Fund to $7,500,000.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Energy Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Purchasers and installers of electric vehicle recharging equipment, commercial and industrial fleet operators, local governments, and residents of overburdened or underserved communities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund increase by $7.75 million in FY 2024, $7.5 million annually in FY 2025 and FY 2026, $5.0 million in FY 2027, and an indeterminate amount in FY 2028. Revenues are unaffected. Local governments may benefit from increased grant and rebate availability.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MEA is the primary administering agency for the Electric Vehicle Recharging Equipment Rebate Program, the Medium-Duty and Heavy-Duty Zero-Emission Vehicle Grant Program, and the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF), which are all amended by this bill.
DBM oversees the development of the executive budget, including monitoring statutory mandated appropriations from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund and reviewing SEIF budget amendments.
The legislation was introduced as an Administration bill and modifies requirements governing the Governor's annual budget bill appropriations from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund.

The bill references statutory definitions under the Environment Article for overburdened and underserved communities to prioritize grants and rebates, and impacts programs funded by carbon allowance proceeds under the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative (RGGI).
The bill alters the authorized uses of Alternative Compliance Payments (ACPs) paid by electricity suppliers under Maryland's Renewable Energy Portfolio Standard, which is regulated by the PSC.

The bill reenacts provisions governing the distribution of RGGI proceeds within the Strategic Energy Investment Fund, which includes designated allocations to DHS for the Electric Universal Service Program and electricity assistance.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Office of Statewide Broadband to study incentives for expanding broadband infrastructure to unserved and underserved communities. Directs the study to evaluate regulatory and financial incentives for broadband service providers. Requires the Office to examine how other states encourage private investment in broadband networks. Directs the Office to identify ways to deploy federal broadband infrastructure grants effectively. Mandates reporting findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly by January 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of Statewide Broadband; Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: broadband service providers and Maryland residents in unserved or underserved communities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures for the Department of Housing and Community Development can likely be handled with existing budgeted resources, though general fund expenditures could potentially increase by a limited amount in FY 2024 if contractual consulting costs cannot be absorbed. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 551 specifically tasks the Office of Statewide Broadband, which is housed within the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD), with conducting a comprehensive study on incentives for expanding broadband infrastructure and submitting findings and recommendations.

The bill was introduced as an Administration initiative and requires the Office of Statewide Broadband to submit its final report, findings, and recommendations directly to the Governor by January 1, 2024.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Build Our Future Grant Pilot Program and Fund in the Department of Commerce. Authorizes the department to award up to $2,000,000 per fiscal year for innovation infrastructure projects in eligible technology sectors. Permits grants to private companies, nonprofit entities, local governments, and colleges and universities in the State. Requires matching funds of at least 200% for grants up to $1,000,000 and 400% for larger grants. Caps awards to colleges and universities at 50% of the fund's annual appropriation. Terminates the program and abrogates the act on June 30, 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Commerce
qa_results.stakeholders: Private companies, nonprofit entities, local governments, and colleges and universities in Maryland pursuing innovation infrastructure projects
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $10.0 million annually from FY 2024 through FY 2027 to capitalize the fund. Special fund revenues and expenditures increase correspondingly for grants and administrative costs. Local government and higher education revenues and expenditures increase to the extent they receive grants and provide required matching funds.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Department of Commerce as the primary administering agency for the newly created Build Our Future Grant Pilot Program and the Build Our Future Grant Fund, including awarding grants, adopting regulations, and submitting program evaluation reports.

Constituent institutions of the University System of Maryland are directly eligible to receive grant funding (up to 50% of total fund appropriations) for technology infrastructure projects and must provide matching funds.
As a public university in Maryland, Morgan State University is eligible to receive grants under the program for qualifying technology and innovation infrastructure projects.
As a public higher education institution in the State, Saint Mary's College of Maryland is an eligible applicant for grant funding for eligible technology infrastructure initiatives.
The bill requires the State Treasurer to hold the newly created Build Our Future Grant Fund separately and invest its moneys, with interest credited directly to the fund.
The bill explicitly mandates the Comptroller to account for the newly established Build Our Future Grant Fund.
DBM is responsible for supervising state budget execution and fiscal planning associated with the bill's annual $10 million general fund appropriation into the special fund.
The legislation is an Administration bill, and the Department of Commerce must report to the Governor by July 1, 2026, regarding the program's projects and economic impact.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the Maryland income tax subtraction modification for eligible military retirement income. Repeals the prior age-based distinction that restricted subtraction amounts by age. Sets the subtraction at the first $25,000 of military retirement income for tax year 2023. Increases the subtraction to the first $40,000 of military retirement income starting in tax year 2024. Covers retirement and death benefits from active, reserve, Maryland National Guard, and specified commissioned corps service.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Military retirees and beneficiaries of military death benefits in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by $11.2 million in FY 2024, growing to $13.1 million in FY 2028 due to increased subtraction modifications. Local income tax revenues decrease by $7.3 million in FY 2024 and by $8.6 million by FY 2028. State and local expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the primary tax administrator responsible for collecting state income taxes and implementing income tax subtraction modifications, forms, and reporting rules affected by this bill.

The Department is the state's lead agency advocating for and serving veterans and military retirees, who are the direct beneficiaries of the increased income tax subtraction for military retirement pay.
The bill causes a notable reduction in State General Fund revenues (over $11 million annually), directly impacting state revenue estimates and executive budget planning overseen by DBM.
Service in the Maryland National Guard is explicitly enumerated in the bill as qualifying military service for the military retirement income tax subtraction modification.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the number of resident judges of the Circuit Court for Baltimore County from 20 to 21. Adds one new circuit court judgeship to address critical judicial resource needs. Provides support for associated judicial staff, including a courtroom clerk and a law clerk. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; Circuit Court for Baltimore County
qa_results.stakeholders: Baltimore County Circuit Court judges and court staff; litigants in Baltimore County; Baltimore County government
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $365,916 in fiscal 2024 and by $486,000 in fiscal 2025 for one additional judge, a courtroom clerk, and a law clerk. Baltimore County expenditures increase beginning in fiscal 2024 to fund an administrative assistant and related operating costs. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates an additional circuit court judgeship in Baltimore County. The Administrative Office of the Courts provides operational, financial, and technological support to the Maryland Judiciary, and the bill has a direct state fiscal impact on the Judiciary's budget for the new judge, associated staff, and operating costs.
The Governor is responsible for appointing judges to newly created circuit court positions.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor by recruiting, vetting, and processing candidates to fill judicial vacancies and new judicial seats.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a comprehensive regulatory, licensing, and taxation framework for adult-use and medical cannabis in Maryland. Renames the Alcohol and Tobacco Commission to the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission. Creates the Maryland Cannabis Administration as an independent unit of State government to regulate cannabis businesses. Imposes a 9% sales and use tax on retail sales of adult-use cannabis beginning in fiscal 2024. Establishes the Office of Social Equity and the Social Equity Partnership Grant Program to support qualifying applicants. Distributes cannabis tax revenues among dedicated special funds, counties, municipalities, and the General Fund.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Cannabis Administration; Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission; Comptroller of Maryland; Department of Commerce; Maryland Economic Development Corporation; Department of General Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Adult-use cannabis consumers, qualifying medical cannabis patients and caregivers, cannabis business license applicants, medical cannabis growers, processors, and dispensaries, social equity applicants, and local governments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State sales and use tax revenues from adult-use cannabis generate an estimated $36.0 million in FY 2024, rising to $146.6 million by FY 2027. Special fund revenues from fees and tax distributions increase by $67.95 million in FY 2024. Net General Fund revenues increase by $18.0 million in FY 2024. State expenditures increase for administration operations and grant programs, including an annual $5.0 million mandated appropriation beginning in FY 2025. Local government revenues increase through a 5% direct tax share and distributions from the Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 556 creates the Maryland Cannabis Administration as an independent unit of State government and the successor to the Maryland Medical Cannabis Commission, tasked with the comprehensive licensing, regulation, and enforcement of medical and adult-use cannabis in Maryland.

Administers and collects the 9% adult-use cannabis sales and use tax, distributes the revenues to mandated special funds and local jurisdictions, and accounts for and administers the Cannabis Regulation and Enforcement Fund and Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund.

Administers the expanded Cannabis Business Assistance Fund providing grants and loans to small, minority-owned, and women-owned cannabis businesses, and establishes and operates the new Capital Access Program to stimulate financing for social equity licensees.

Transfers medical cannabis regulatory oversight and personnel out of MDH, administers the Cannabis Public Health Fund, and is authorized to explore an MOU with the Cannabis Administration to co-locate testing at state health laboratories.

Required to conduct a study identifying potential incubator space locations across four specified regions, and to acquire, construct, or refurbish at least one facility for use as a cannabis incubator space.

Responsible for appointing the Director of the Maryland Cannabis Administration, the Executive Director of the Office of Social Equity, and members of the Advisory Board on Medical and Adult-Use Cannabis, as well as authorizing budget transfers.
