agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Consulted on disparity studies, licensing lottery remedial measures, and the establishment of MBE participation goals and procurement procedures for cannabis businesses.
Takes ownership of incubator space facilities acquired and constructed by MEDCO upon completion and is tasked with contracting with nonprofit organizations to operate them.
Consults on determining communities most impacted by disproportionate cannabis enforcement, reviews disparity studies, and advises on constitutional requirements for MBE remedial measures.

Holds and invests moneys for several newly created or recodified nonlapsing special funds, including the Cannabis Regulation and Enforcement Fund, Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund, and Compassionate Use Fund.
Adjudicates contested licensing decisions, denials, and enforcement/disciplinary proceedings delegated to it by the Cannabis Administration.
Statutorily mandated to audit the Cannabis Regulation and Enforcement Fund, Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund, and Medical Cannabis Compassionate Use Fund.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Its Criminal Justice Information System Central Repository is required to process state and national criminal history background checks for cannabis agent applicants and business owners.
As the State's designated MBE certification agency, MDOT is consulted on disparity studies and remedial measures; MVA credentials are used for age verification at dispensaries.
Authorized to enter into an MOU with the Cannabis Administration to co-locate cannabis testing operations at an existing state agricultural laboratory.
Impacted by the transfer and conversion of dozens of contractual and merit positions to the Maryland Cannabis Administration and associated state personnel/budget oversight.
Affected by provisions governing the application of state insurance regulation, prohibiting state liability or adverse action against insurers providing services to legal cannabis businesses.
Maintains the 10-year cannabis possession charge records used to identify 'disproportionately impacted areas' for social equity licensing and county CRRF allocations.
Oversees the State's MBE certification designations referenced in disparity study review requirements and procurement exemptions.
Eligible to receive grants from the Cannabis Business Assistance Fund for cannabis-related training programs, business incubators, and bona fide research projects.
The Secretary of State Police serves as an ex officio nonvoting member of the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission, which coordinates on cannabis public health and enforcement.
Referenced regarding existing standards for designated school personnel administering medical cannabis to qualified students, and zoning distance protections for schools.

Establishes that an applicant satisfies residency requirements by residing in Maryland when filing the application. Maintains license validity only as long as at least one applicant remains a Maryland resident. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Carroll County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license applicants and holders in Carroll County, including partnerships, corporations, clubs, and limited liability companies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. The bill is not anticipated to materially affect Carroll County operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry and prescribes standard alcoholic beverage application forms referenced in Title 4 of the Alcoholic Beverages Article, though this bill specifically modifies local licensing residency rules in Carroll County with no direct state fiscal impact.

qa_results.bill_summary: Modifies seating requirements for certain beer, wine, and liquor licenses in Carroll County. Permits up to 15 seats at bars or counters to count toward the required 50-seat minimum capacity. Applies the modified seating standard to hotels and restaurants holding or seeking a Class B license. Applies the standard to restaurants holding or seeking a Class BR license. Extends the seating modification to clubs holding or seeking a Class C license.
qa_results.responsible_party: Carroll County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Hotels, restaurants, and clubs holding or seeking Class B, Class BR, or Class C alcoholic beverages licenses in Carroll County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. The bill is not anticipated to materially affect Carroll County finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller regulates the alcohol industry in Maryland. Although this legislation specifically affects local seating capacity rules for alcoholic beverage licenses administered in Carroll County and has no state fiscal impact, it relates to the state's alcoholic beverages statutory framework.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the 40-day calendar year limit for Class C multiple event entertainment licenses in Carroll County. Establishes an annual fee of $2,000 for a multiple event license for 41 or more events per year. Applies to licenses issued to a Carroll County fire department or an arts center on West Main Street in Westminster. Retains existing fee tiers ranging from $125 to $500 for up to 40 events per year. Prohibits an eligible entity from receiving more than one multiple event license in a calendar year.
qa_results.responsible_party: Carroll County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Carroll County fire departments and arts centers on West Main Street in Westminster
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State finances. Carroll County local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcoholic beverage industry. Although this legislation specifically affects local licensing administered by the Carroll County Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal impact, the Comptroller maintains broad regulatory oversight over alcohol administration in the state.

qa_results.bill_summary: Grants urban renewal authority to the Town of Mount Airy in Carroll County and Frederick County. Authorizes the municipality to acquire real property within urban renewal areas by purchase, lease, gift, or eminent domain. Requires the town legislative body to adopt a resolution defining slum or blighted areas before initiating a project. Authorizes the town to issue general obligation bonds and tax-exempt revenue bonds to finance urban renewal activities. Permits the town to establish a separate public body or agency to exercise specified urban renewal powers. Allows the municipality to levy taxes and assessments and sell or lease acquired property to private or public entities.
qa_results.responsible_party: Town of Mount Airy
qa_results.stakeholders: Property owners, businesses, and residents within designated urban renewal areas in the Town of Mount Airy, private redevelopers, and town taxpayers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No direct State effect, though a minimal increase in State and local tax revenues may occur if redevelopment expands the property assessable base. Town of Mount Airy expenditures may increase for property acquisition, legal fees, and project execution if the authority is used, potentially offset by bond issuances or subsequent property sales. Exact figures are unavailable because costs depend on future municipal actions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill grants the Town of Mount Airy urban renewal and eminent domain powers, authorizing the town to obtain court orders for property entry and conduct condemnation proceedings through the circuit courts, which are supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

The bill requires urban renewal plans to conform to municipal master plans and involves local land use and redevelopment planning, which relates to the Maryland Department of Planning's role in guiding land use planning and sustainable growth across the state.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a holder of a Class 9 limited distillery license to obtain a Class 8 liquor wholesaler’s license. Permits the license holder to distribute not more than 27,500 gallons of its own liquor annually. Restricts eligibility to license holders that produce not more than 100,000 gallons of liquor annually in aggregate. Allows the wholesaler license holder to sell liquor to authorized retail license holders and permit holders. Sets an annual license fee of $100 for the Class 8 license.
qa_results.responsible_party: Alcohol and Tobacco Commission; Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Class 9 limited distillery license holders, licensed liquor wholesalers, and authorized alcoholic beverage retailers in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues increase minimally, estimated at up to $1,800 in FY 2024 and $780 annually thereafter from license, application, and renewal fees if all six eligible limited distilleries participate. The Alcohol and Tobacco Commission can implement and monitor the licenses using existing budgeted resources. Local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly tasks the Comptroller with reviewing and approving applications for additional warehousing, sale, and delivery locations for Class 8 liquor wholesaler license holders, and collecting associated fees. Additionally, the Comptroller regulates the alcohol industry and collects related state revenues.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Attorney General to direct the formation of an Opioid Restitution Fund Advisory Council committee under certain agreements. Requires the Maryland Department of Health to allow entities to choose their preferred formulation or dosage of overdose reversal drugs. Subjects this choice of drug formulation and dosage to the limitations of the State budget. Applies Opioid Restitution Fund appropriation rules to all opioid-related judgments and settlements involving the State and political subdivisions. Directs the Secretary of Health to administer grant distributions to political subdivisions under those agreements.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Office of the Attorney General; Opioid Restitution Fund Advisory Council
qa_results.stakeholders: Entities participating in the Overdose Response Program, individuals experiencing or at risk of opioid overdose, and Maryland political subdivisions receiving Opioid Restitution Fund distributions
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Maryland Department of Health may increase minimally to purchase higher-cost formulations or dosages of FDA-approved opioid overdose reversal drugs requested by entities, subject to budget limits. Advisory council committee requirements and fund processing can be implemented within existing budgeted resources. Local revenues and expenditures are not directly affected beyond the distribution of settlement funds pursuant to agreements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary agency responsible for administering the Overdose Response Program, purchasing and distributing FDA-approved opioid overdose reversal drugs, and allowing participating entities to choose drug formulation and dosage. Additionally, the Secretary of Health is tasked with administering the grant program for distributing Opioid Restitution Fund monies to local subdivisions.

The bill explicitly authorizes the Attorney General to direct the formation of committees within the Opioid Restitution Fund Advisory Council pursuant to court/administrative orders or settlement agreements, establish procedures for those committees, and identify controlling versions of opioid-related settlement agreements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters statutory governance, committee formation rules, and operational procedures for the Opioid Restitution Fund Advisory Council, an executive advisory body.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Access to Mental Health Advisory Committee within the Maryland Higher Education Commission. Requires institutions of higher education with committee members to provide staff support on a rotating basis. Directs the committee to study higher education mental health policies, challenges, and service delivery models. Mandates recommendations on reducing costs and expanding access through telemedicine, hotlines, and specialized counseling. Requires the committee to meet six times per year and submit an annual findings report starting December 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Access to Mental Health Advisory Committee; Maryland Higher Education Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Higher education students, campus mental health counselors and clinical staff, and Maryland public and nonpublic institutions of higher education
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in higher education expenditures for public four-year institutions, Baltimore City Community College, and local community colleges to staff the committee on a rotating basis. Expense reimbursements for members are minimal and absorbable within existing budgeted resources. Revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Access to Mental Health Advisory Committee within the Maryland Higher Education Commission, and the Secretary of Higher Education serves on the committee and appoints licensed clinical social worker members.

The bill establishes the Access to Mental Health Advisory Committee within the Maryland Higher Education Commission, and the Secretary of Higher Education serves on the committee and appoints licensed clinical social worker members.

The Chancellor of USM (or designee) is a designated member of the committee and appoints four committee members. USM institutions are also required to assist with staffing the committee on a rotating basis.
The President of Morgan State University (or designee) is designated as a committee member, and the university participates in staffing the committee on a rotating basis.
The President of St. Mary's College of Maryland (or designee) is a designated committee member, and the college participates in staffing the committee on a rotating basis.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new permanent statutory advisory body, the Access to Mental Health Advisory Committee, to study and report on mental health services in Maryland higher education institutions.
The committee is statutorily required to submit an annual report of its findings and recommendations to the Governor by December 1 each year.

qa_results.bill_summary: Redefines creditable service for State retiree health benefit eligibility to include service in the Executive, Legislative, or Judicial Branch. Includes periods of enrollment in the State Retirement and Pension System or the Optional Retirement Program. Allows Optional Retirement Program retirees to count State service enrolled under the State Retirement and Pension System. Permits qualifying retirees to combine service credit across systems to meet health benefit and subsidy requirements. Takes effect June 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Budget and Management; State Retirement Agency
qa_results.stakeholders: State employees and retirees with service credit divided between the State Retirement and Pension System and the Optional Retirement Program, as well as their surviving spouses and dependent children
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in State liabilities for Other Post Employment Benefits (OPEB) beyond the five-year fiscal window, with no immediate direct effect on State expenditures under pay-as-you-go funding and no effect on revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Budget and Management (DBM) is responsible for administering the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program and determining retiree eligibility and state subsidies for health benefits.

The Maryland State Retirement Agency (SRA) administers the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS) and manages records of creditable service and retirement allowances needed to verify eligibility under the bill.

USM employs individuals who participate in the Optional Retirement Program (ORP) under Title 30, and their employees transitioning between SRPS and ORP are impacted by the redefined creditable service calculations for retiree health benefits.

qa_results.bill_summary: Permanently extends the State income tax credit for eligible food donations by qualified farms. Increases the tax credit value to 100% of the wholesale value of eligible food donations and certified organic produce. Maintains the maximum credit of $5,000 per qualified farm, which the Secretary of Agriculture may increase by $5,000. Limits the total tax credit certificates issued under the program to $100,000 per fiscal year. Expresses legislative intent for the Department of Agriculture to continue funding marketing and transportation assistance for donations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture; Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Qualified farm businesses in Maryland donating fresh food products and certified organic produce, and certified tax credit certificate administrators
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by up to $100,000 annually beginning in FY 2025, with an indeterminate decrease in FY 2024. Transportation Trust Fund revenues, Higher Education Investment Fund revenues, and local highway user revenues decrease minimally to the extent credits are claimed against the corporate income tax. Expenditures are unaffected as the Maryland Department of Agriculture can administer the program with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Agriculture is the primary agency responsible for administering the food donation tax credit program, which includes calculating product values, certifying tax credit certificate administrators, adopting regulations in consultation with the Comptroller, marketing the program, and submitting annual reports.

The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for administering the state income tax credit, receiving copies of issued tax credit certificates, and collaborating with the Department of Agriculture on program regulations, certificate forms, and annual reporting.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Green Purchasing Committee to establish specifications for purchasing compost, mulch, soil amendments, and aggregate. Directs the committee to publish and maintain these specifications online for State agencies. Covers products produced from recycled or organic materials such as municipal solid waste and yard waste. Requires each unit of State government purchasing these materials to include the specifications in procurements. Applies this requirement only when qualifying products are readily available, competitively priced, and of satisfactory quality.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Green Purchasing Committee
qa_results.stakeholders: State agencies purchasing landscaping and aggregate materials, vendors and producers of recycled or organic soil and aggregate products, and local governments managing municipal solid waste
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State administrative costs can be absorbed with existing resources, but overall procurement cost impacts cannot be reliably estimated due to uncertain product pricing and availability. Potential minimal increase in local government revenues if State purchases of municipal solid waste increase.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DGS is the primary procurement agency for state commodities and facilities management, explicitly referenced in the bill regarding state property composting goals. Furthermore, DGS provides administrative staff support to and chairs the Maryland Green Purchasing Committee, which is tasked with establishing and publishing the required procurement specifications.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland Green Purchasing Committee—a statutory state committee—to establish, publish, and maintain online specifications for purchasing compost, mulch, soil amendments, and aggregate made from recycled or organic materials.

MDOT oversees major capital and maintenance projects across the state that require extensive procurement of aggregate, crushed stone, sand, and soil amendments, making the bill's procurement specifications directly applicable to its contracting operations.

As the agency responsible for maintaining thousands of lane miles of highways and roadside land, SHA is one of the state's largest purchasers of aggregate, mulch, and soil amendments for roadwork, erosion control, and landscaping.

DNR manages over 500,000 acres of public lands and state parks where compost and soil amendments are utilized, and the fiscal note highlights specific agency concerns regarding contaminant risks in solid waste and organic materials applied to state lands.

MDE regulates solid waste management, food waste diversion, sludge, and dredged material beneficial reuse, which form the source materials for the compost and aggregate specifications governed by this bill.

MES operates composting, recycling, dredged material containment, and solid waste facilities across the state, making it directly connected to the supply and production of recycled soil amendments and aggregates purchased by state units.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners to exchange a specified Class B-D-7 license for a Class A-7 license. Permits this exchange for premises on the odd side of the 4000 block of Frederick Avenue. Repeals the geographic restriction barring Class A-7 licenses in the 43rd legislative district. Expands the definition of a marketplace to include establishments expected to open within 24 months of license issuance. Authorizes a marketplace license holder to sell beer, wine, and liquor for off-premises consumption.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City
qa_results.stakeholders: Class B-D-7 alcoholic beverages license holders on the 4000 block of Frederick Avenue, marketplace license holders in the 41st legislative district, and retail alcoholic beverages establishments in Baltimore City
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. Baltimore City finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the state agency responsible for regulating the alcohol industry and collecting alcohol-related taxes. While the bill specifically governs local retail licenses administered by the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners and has no state fiscal impact, it relates to the broader regulatory domain of alcoholic beverages.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits courts from assessing costs on a person or governmental unit for recording and indexing a restitution order. Applies the cost exemption to an order of restitution issued by any court in the State. Expands existing protections beyond only the court that originally entered the restitution judgment. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Judiciary (Administrative Office of the Courts)
qa_results.stakeholders: Crime victims, governmental units, and other persons or entities owed restitution
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal decrease in State fee revenues, with no material effect on State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs court operations by prohibiting state courts from assessing recording and indexing fees on victims or governmental units for restitution orders issued by any court in Maryland.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The office coordinates victim services and crime prevention policy across the state, which encompasses victim restitution policies, and served as an information source on this legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation in the Maryland Department of Transportation. Repeals the $500,000 annual grant cap under the Maryland Senior Rides Program. Repeals the $400,000 annual funding cap for the Job Access and Reverse Commute Program. Requires the Governor to provide funding for the Job Access and Reverse Commute Program in the State budget. Requires the committee to devise a 5-year health and human services transportation plan. Mandates an annual report from the committee to the Governor and General Assembly by September 1.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation; Maryland Transit Administration; State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation
qa_results.stakeholders: Transportation-disadvantaged Maryland residents including seniors, individuals with disabilities, reverse commute workers, and health and human services transportation providers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund expenditures increase by $180,000 in FY 2024 and by $80,000 annually thereafter to hire consultants assisting the new coordinating committee. State revenues are unaffected. Repealing funding limits for the Maryland Senior Rides Program and the Job Access and Reverse Commute Program creates no mandated funding increase, leaving any additional spending discretionary.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT is required to chair and staff the newly established State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation and incurs direct fiscal impacts for consultant support under the Transportation Trust Fund.
MTA administers the Maryland Senior Rides Program and the Job Access and Reverse Commute Program, both of which have their statutory annual funding caps repealed by this bill.
The Secretary of Aging (or designee) is designated as a member of the State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation, which addresses transit needs for seniors.

The Secretary of Disabilities (or designee) is designated as a member of the State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation, which is tasked with examining transit needs for individuals with disabilities.
The Secretary of Health (or designee) is named as a member of the State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation to coordinate healthcare access and transportation.
The Secretary of Human Services (or designee) serves on the State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation to assist transportation-disadvantaged populations.
The Secretary of Housing and Community Development (or designee) is appointed as a statutory member of the State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation.
The Secretary of Labor (or designee) serves on the Coordinating Committee, aligning with efforts to connect transportation-disadvantaged individuals with employment and training.
The Secretary of Planning (or designee) is designated as a member of the State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation.
The Secretary of Veterans Affairs/Veterans and Military Families (or designee) is named as a member of the State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Director of the Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing (or designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Coordinating Committee.
The Executive Board Chair of the Rural Maryland Council (or designee) is designated as a member of the Coordinating Committee to represent rural transportation needs.
The Governor is required to provide funding for the Job Access and Reverse Commute Program in the annual budget, receives annual reports from the Committee, and appoints additional members.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally establishes a new permanent interagency coordinating body: the State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes certain retirees of three State retirement systems to convert an optional retirement allowance to an unreduced basic allowance. Applies to State Police Retirement System, Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System, and Judges' Retirement System retirees. Requires the retiree to have retired on or before December 31, 2012, and named a same-sex designated beneficiary. Requires the retiree to have married that beneficiary on or after January 1, 2013, without divorcing before July 1, 2023. Requires eligible retirees or surviving beneficiaries to submit application documents on or before December 31, 2023. Directs the Board of Trustees to pay retroactive lump-sum adjustments with 4% annual compound interest.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System; State Retirement Agency
qa_results.stakeholders: Retirees of the State Police Retirement System, Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System, and Judges' Retirement System who retired on or before December 31, 2012, and their same-sex spouses
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal effect on State pension assets and unfunded liabilities due to the small number of eligible participants, resulting in no discernible effect on State or local pension contribution rates. No effect on State or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the State Retirement Agency and the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System, requiring the agency to administer and process benefit conversion applications, recalculate retirement and survivor allowances, and issue retroactive lump-sum adjustment payments for eligible retirees and beneficiaries in the SPRS, LEOPS, and JRS.

The bill directly modifies retirement and surviving spouse benefits for retirees of the State Police Retirement System (SPRS), which specifically covers former Maryland State Police officers, though the system is administered by the State Retirement Agency.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits housing discrimination against an individual with a disability who has, obtains, or retains a service dog or guide dog. Authorizes an individual to retain a former service dog or guide dog as a pet for its life after retirement. Exempts qualifying individuals from lease provisions prohibiting dogs and bars landlords from charging additional rent or fees. Holds the individual liable for any damage done to the premises by the service dog or former service dog. Excludes from the definition of service dog animals meant to deter crime or provide only emotional support or companionship.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Commission on Civil Rights
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals with disabilities who have, obtain, or retain service dogs or guide dogs; housing providers, residential property sellers, and landlords
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Commission on Civil Rights is the primary enforcement agency responsible for investigating and resolving complaints of discriminatory housing practices under Title 20 of the State Government Article.
The Office of Administrative Hearings conducts administrative hearings for contested housing discrimination claims referred by the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights.
The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the circuit courts, where individuals alleging housing discrimination under these provisions may file civil actions.
The Maryland Department of Disabilities coordinates state policies and initiatives to advance accessible housing and protect the rights of individuals with disabilities.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date of the State Board of Nursing to July 1, 2025. Transfers temporary authority over Board infrastructure operations and staff employment to the Secretary of Health through June 30, 2025. Prohibits using the Board of Nursing Fund for infrastructure operations during that period. Terminates the terms of Board members in office across two staggered dates in 2023. Authorizes applicants who fail the licensing exam once within 120 days of application to practice while pending. Requires the Board to hire an external consultant to evaluate operations and create an action plan.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Nursing; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: registered nurses, licensed practical nurses, applicants for nursing licensure, and members of the State Board of Nursing
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase from fiscal 2023 through fiscal 2025 to cover Board infrastructure operations, including $8.0 million allocated in the fiscal 2024 budget. Special fund expenditures from the Board of Nursing Fund correspondingly decrease for infrastructure but increase by at least $150,000 to hire an external consultant. No local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Nursing is a health occupations board within the Department of Health. The bill extends the Board's termination date, temporarily transfers authority over the Board's infrastructure operations to the Secretary of Health, authorizes the Secretary to employ staff and set compensation, and directs millions in general fund expenditures to MDH for these operations.

The Secretary of Budget and Management is statutorily required to consult with the Secretary of Health to determine the board positions for which compensation may be set independently, and DBM is mandated to partner in developing the comprehensive action plan addressing Board staffing and infrastructure needs.
The bill mandates that the Board's independent action plan be developed in partnership with DoIT to address immediate infrastructure and operational technology needs.

The bill terminates the terms of all 14 existing Board of Nursing members on staggered dates, requiring gubernatorial appointment and reappointment actions, and requires the Board to submit specified reports directly to the Governor.

Because the terms of all 14 current Board members end on an expedited, staggered schedule under the bill, the Office of Appointments will be responsible for processing, vetting, and administering the appointments and reappointments to the Board.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires each area agency on aging to develop a long-term care and dementia care navigation program. Tasks programs with providing cognitive screening, caregiver support, and referrals to long-term care and chronic disease services. Requires the Maryland Department of Aging to oversee and train program staff and collect interaction data. Mandates an annual report on program services submitted to state officials and published online by October 1. Mandates an annual state appropriation of $2,400,000 beginning in fiscal year 2025 to fund statewide management and local programs.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Aging; Area Agencies on Aging
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals experiencing cognitive changes or symptoms of dementia, family caregivers, and area agencies on aging
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $79,733 in FY 2024 for personnel and operating expenses. General fund expenditures increase by $2,400,000 annually beginning in FY 2025 due to a mandated appropriation. Local area agencies on aging that are units of local government see matching increases in revenues and expenditures beginning in FY 2025.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Aging is the primary implementing agency for the bill. It is required to oversee and train navigation program staff, disseminate best practices, collect interaction data, distribute $2.4 million in annual mandated funding proportionally to Area Agencies on Aging, and submit an annual report on program outcomes.

The bill mandates an annual general fund appropriation of $2,400,000 starting in fiscal year 2025, which directly impacts state budget planning and execution overseen by the Department of Budget and Management.

The bill statutorily requires the Governor to include a $2,400,000 appropriation in the annual budget bill beginning in fiscal year 2025 and requires the Department of Aging to submit an annual report on navigation services directly to the Governor.

The work of the navigation programs must be guided by recommendations from the Virginia I. Jones Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias Council (established under the Health - General Article), and the programs must establish relationships with health care providers and make referrals to chronic disease services.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends deadlines for the Workgroup on Black, Latino, Asian American Pacific Islander, and Other Underrepresented Behavioral Health Professionals. Requires the Workgroup to report findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by July 1, 2024. Extends the Workgroup's termination date to June 30, 2025. Directs the Workgroup to study shortages and recommend incentives to increase underrepresented behavioral health professionals. Maintains joint staffing support from the University System of Maryland and the Maryland Department of Health.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; University System of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Black, Latino, Asian American Pacific Islander, and other underrepresented behavioral health professionals and students; patients in underserved communities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal and absorbable increase in State expenditures within existing budgeted resources for the University System of Maryland and the Maryland Department of Health for staffing and workgroup travel reimbursements. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health jointly staffs the Workgroup with the University System of Maryland, and the Secretary of Health designates the chair and appoints several members to the Workgroup.

The University System of Maryland jointly provides staff for the Workgroup, and the presidents of three constituent USM institutions (Bowie State University, Coppin State University, and University of Maryland Eastern Shore) serve as members.
The President of Morgan State University, or the President's designee, is designated by statute as a member of the Workgroup.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly extends the reporting and termination deadlines for a state-established advisory workgroup examining diversity within behavioral health professions.
The Workgroup is statutorily required to submit its findings and recommendations directly to the Governor by the extended reporting deadline.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Industry 4.0 Technology Grant Program in the Department of Commerce. Authorizes competitive grants between $25,000 and $500,000 to qualifying small and medium-sized enterprise manufacturers. Requires grant recipients to provide matching funds under a sliding scale formula based on employee count. Directs the Department to reserve at least 20% of annual grant funds for manufacturers employing 50 or fewer employees. Mandates an annual state budget appropriation of $1,000,000 to the program fund for fiscal years 2025 through 2028.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Commerce
qa_results.stakeholders: Small and medium-sized enterprise manufacturers in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures increase by $1,123,176 in FY 2025 and approximately $1.1 million annually from FY 2026 through FY 2028 to fund grants and department administrative costs. Special fund revenues and expenditures increase by $1.0 million annually from FY 2025 through FY 2028 as mandated appropriations are received and awarded as grants. Local finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly establishes the Industry 4.0 Technology Grant Program and the Industry 4.0 Technology Grant Fund within the Department of Commerce, tasking the department with program administration, regulation adoption, application evaluation, and grant distribution.

The bill authorizes the Department of Commerce to enter into a memorandum of understanding with a State-chartered corporation under Title 10 to administer the program, and the fiscal note explicitly identifies TEDCO as a potential administrator.

The bill allows Commerce to partner via MOU with a State-chartered corporation under Title 10 to administer the grant program, with MEDCO specifically identified in the fiscal note as an eligible entity.
The bill mandates that the Governor include an annual appropriation of $1,000,000 to the Industry 4.0 Technology Grant Fund in the state budget bill for fiscal years 2025 through 2028.

DBM oversees the state budget execution and development, which must incorporate the statutorily mandated $1.0 million annual appropriation to the Fund from fiscal 2025 through 2028 along with associated administrative costs.
The bill statutorily requires the State Treasurer to hold the newly established special fund separately and to invest the fund's moneys.
The bill statutorily requires the Comptroller to account for the newly established Industry 4.0 Technology Grant Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the Appraisal Gap From Historic Redlining Financial Assistance Program within the Department of Housing and Community Development. Expands allowable financial assistance to include loans, grants, interest reductions, prepayments, assurances, guarantees, and credit enhancements. Permits developers to apply for financial assistance when a qualified project is proposed rather than completed. Repeals statutory limits on the amount of financial assistance DHCD may provide. Adds infrastructure and other expenses determined by the Secretary to eligible construction expenses. Requires qualified projects receiving financial assistance to comply with local development and land use plans.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Affordable housing developers and homebuyers in low-income census tracts and sustainable communities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State operations or finances because funding for the program has not been budgeted since its enactment. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 625 alters the Appraisal Gap From Historic Redlining Financial Assistance Program, which is administered by the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD). The bill expands the types of financial assistance DHCD may provide, alters application timelines, requires DHCD to develop regulations for the application process and distribution of assistance, and authorizes the Secretary of Housing and Community Development to determine eligible construction expenses.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Human–Relevant Research Fund under the administration of the Maryland Technology Development Corporation. Requires the Corporation to establish a grant and loan program promoting human–relevant alternatives to animal testing. Requires Maryland research facilities that submit federal APHIS Form 7023 to pay an annual contribution to the Department of Health. Sets annual contribution tiers between $5,000 and $75,000 based on the total number of animals reported. Subjects research facilities that fail to pay the required contribution to a civil penalty up to $1,000 per day.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Technology Development Corporation; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Research facilities in Maryland conducting animal testing or research; public and private entities researching human-relevant animal testing alternatives; public higher education institutions; Community College of Baltimore County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Human-Relevant Research Fund increase by up to $915,000 annually beginning in FY 2024. State higher education expenditures increase by $120,000 annually across four public universities to pay mandatory contributions. Local expenditures increase by $5,000 annually for the Community College of Baltimore County.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: TEDCO is the primary implementing agency tasked with administering the newly established Human-Relevant Research Fund, creating and operating the grant and loan program, contracting with an independent review board, adopting regulations, and reporting annually.

The Maryland Department of Health is responsible for collecting the mandatory annual contributions from animal testing research facilities based on federal APHIS Form 7023 filings, assessing civil penalties for failure to pay, and transferring collected funds to TEDCO.

Four USM member institutions (University of Maryland, College Park; University of Maryland, Baltimore; Towson University; and Frostburg State University) conduct animal research subject to the bill and are directly impacted by paying an estimated combined $120,000 annually in required contributions.
The State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold the Human-Relevant Research Fund separately as a special, nonlapsing fund and invest fund monies, with interest credited to the Fund.
The Comptroller is statutorily designated to account for the Human-Relevant Research Fund.

The Governor's Office receives the required annual progress report regarding research funded by the program and has discretionary authority to include an appropriation to the Fund in the annual state budget.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands eligibility for the Edward T. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program to include certain surviving spouses of service members. Authorizes surviving spouses to apply if the service member died from military service after December 7, 1941. Authorizes surviving spouses to apply if the service member suffered a service-connected 100% permanent disability. Authorizes surviving spouses to apply if the member was declared a prisoner of war or missing in action. Requires applicants to be Maryland residents at application or at the disabling or fatal event.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Surviving spouses of deceased, disabled, or POW/MIA U.S. armed forces members; eligible Maryland postsecondary institutions
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures and special fund revenues and expenditures increase by an estimated $7,700 per award annually, but the total fiscal impact cannot be reliably determined because the number of new recipients is unknown.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC is the primary state agency responsible for overseeing and administering the Edward T. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program, updating program regulations, and allocating scholarship funds to postsecondary institutions for eligible recipients.
As the state's postsecondary coordinating body, it oversees financial aid administration including the Edward T. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program and allocates funds to participating institutions.

USM constituent institutions verify eligibility and award Conroy scholarships to enrolled students; additionally, the statutory cap on scholarship award amounts is directly benchmarked to the highest resident undergraduate tuition and mandatory fees within USM.
As an eligible public four-year university, Morgan State processes applications, verifies eligibility, and disburses scholarship awards to qualifying students under the expanded eligibility rules.

The department advocates for and provides outreach to military families and surviving dependents regarding available state educational assistance benefits, including expanded eligibility for surviving spouses under this program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a utility account holder who is a victim of abuse to terminate future liability under a utility contract. Requires a covered utility to allow termination upon written notice by first-class mail or hand delivery. Requires the notice to include an eligible protective order, peace order, or qualified third-party report. Limits the terminating account holder's liability to charges incurred through the billing cycle when notice is submitted. Requires the utility to allow the account holder to open a new account regardless of past arrearages.
qa_results.responsible_party: Public Service Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Utility account holders who are victims of abuse, and utilities including electric companies, electricity suppliers, gas companies, gas suppliers, sewage disposal companies, and water companies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Public Service Commission and local utilities can implement the bill's requirements with existing budgeted resources, resulting in no material impact on State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary regulatory body overseeing electric, gas, water, and sewage disposal companies in Maryland, which are directly subject to the utility account termination and customer protection mandates established by the bill.

The Office of the People's Counsel advocates on behalf of residential utility consumers regarding utility service practices, consumer rights, and billing protections, aligning directly with the bill's protections for abuse victims holding utility accounts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy coordinates victim services and public safety policy across Maryland and provided information for the evaluation of this bill regarding protections for domestic violence and abuse survivors.

qa_results.bill_summary: Modifies the physician credentialing reappointment process required for hospital licensure in the State. Replaces the mandate to conduct reappointments at least every two years with a requirement to follow accreditation body standards. Retains requirements to document a physician's pattern of performance by analyzing clinical skills, claims, and other performance data. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Secretary of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: licensed hospitals in Maryland and physicians employed by or holding staff privileges at Maryland hospitals
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State requirements can be handled using existing budgeted resources with no effect on local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH), through the Secretary of Health, licenses hospitals in the state, establishes minimum regulatory standards for hospital credentialing processes, and enforces compliance through penalties or delicensure.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the definition of personal information under the Maryland Public Information Act to include an individual's e-mail address. Requires custodians to deny inspection of school district records regarding a student's personal e-mail address, with specified exceptions. Requires custodians to deny inspection of personal telephone numbers and personal e-mail addresses of State and local government employees. Directs custodians to allow inspection of a notary public's business e-mail address or fallback personal e-mail address. Requires custodians to allow inspection of an occupational or professional licensee's business e-mail address when identified as such.
qa_results.responsible_party: Custodians of public records in Maryland State and local government units
qa_results.stakeholders: Public school students, State and local government employees, notaries public, occupational and professional licensees, and Public Information Act applicants
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends § 4–332 of the General Provisions Article concerning Public Information Act disclosures of notary public applications, commissions, and contact information, which are maintained and administered by the Secretary of State.

The bill explicitly references the Maryland Higher Education Commission in § 4–313, governing its ability to inspect student contact information (including personal email addresses) and prohibiting commercial use or redisclosure of such records.

The bill amends § 4–333 regarding the inspection and disclosure of occupational and professional licensing records, specifically establishing guidelines for releasing licensee business email addresses, an area directly overseen by the Department of Labor.
The bill updates public record disclosure protections for student records across school districts in § 4–313 to include students' personal email addresses and telephone numbers.
The Office of the Attorney General advises state agencies on Maryland Public Information Act compliance and publishes the state's official Public Information Act Manual.
The department licenses numerous health care occupations and professions and serves as the custodian of those licensing records governed by the amended disclosure rules in § 4–333.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Washington County sworn deputy sheriffs and correctional deputies at the rank of sergeant and below to bargain collectively. Subjects any additional funding required by a negotiated agreement to approval by the County Commissioners. Limits the discharge of tenured deputy sheriffs at the rank of major or below strictly to police misconduct. Prohibits covered deputy sheriffs and correctional deputies from engaging in strikes. Specifies that special deputy sheriffs are not State employees for employment security or employee benefits. Establishes that collective bargaining agreements must extend between one and four years.
qa_results.responsible_party: Washington County Sheriff; Washington County Administrator; County Commissioners of Washington County
qa_results.stakeholders: Full-time sworn deputy sheriffs and correctional deputies at the rank of sergeant and below in the Washington County Sheriff's Office, special deputy sheriffs in Washington County, and the Washington County government
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal impact. Washington County expenditures may increase minimally from potential third-party neutral arbitration costs or negotiated agreements, though any funding impact is subject to County Commissioner approval; local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly clarifies that special deputy sheriffs in Washington County are not considered State employees for the purpose of employee benefits, which are overseen and managed centrally by DBM.

The bill clarifies that special deputy sheriffs in Washington County are not State employees for the purpose of employment security (unemployment insurance), which is administered by the Maryland Department of Labor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners for Frederick County to issue a Class B–GSF license to golf simulator facilities. Requires qualifying facilities to be open to the public and have at least five simulator bays with dedicated seating. Authorizes license holders to sell beer, wine, and liquor for on-premises consumption when food is offered on-premises. Caps annual gross sales of alcohol at 35% while requiring at least 50% from bay rentals and 15% from food. Requires licensees to submit an annual gross sales report to the Board before license renewal. Sets the annual license fee at $1,500.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Frederick County
qa_results.stakeholders: golf simulator facility operators and patrons in Frederick County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Frederick County revenues increase by $2,250 in fiscal 2024 for each new license issued (comprising a $750 application fee and $1,500 annual fee) and $1,500 annually thereafter for each renewal. Local enforcement can be handled with existing resources. No state fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller regulates the alcohol industry in Maryland and oversees state sales tax collections. While this bill is local to Frederick County and administered by the local Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal effect, it pertains to alcoholic beverages licensing within the state.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the auctioneer fee allowed as an expense in Garrett County property tax sales. Raises the fee from $8 to $10 for each property sold. Establishes that the fee remains a lien on the property sold at tax sale. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Garrett County Collector of Taxes
qa_results.stakeholders: Auctioneers and property purchasers participating in tax sales in Garrett County, as well as Garrett County property owners subject to tax sales
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Garrett County finances are not materially affected because the auctioneer fee is included in the property sale price and paid by purchasers.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Administrative Office of the Courts serves as an information source for the legislation. While the bill specifically adjusts the allowable auctioneer fee for local property tax sales in Garrett County with no state fiscal effect, matters relating to property tax sales and the foreclosure of rights of redemption fall within the jurisdiction of Maryland's court system.

qa_results.bill_summary: Updates references defining Baltimore City alcoholic beverages districts to align with the Legislative Districting Plan of 2022. Applies updated boundaries to license issuance, license transfers, tasting licenses, and after-hours operational exemptions. Requires the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City to exempt certain license holders from the act. Limits exemptions to holders conducting activities approved by the board on or before February 1, 2022. Mandates that qualifying license holders must have owned the licensed premises continuously since February 1, 2022.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City
qa_results.stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license holders and license applicants in Baltimore City
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on state finances. Minimal local fiscal impact, as the change is technical and does not directly affect Baltimore City operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for state-level regulation and taxation of the alcohol industry. While the bill specifically updates local legislative districting plan references for Baltimore City's alcoholic beverages districts administered by the local Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal effect, it touches the broader alcoholic beverages regulatory framework.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the timing of the annual election of officers for the Talbot County Board of Education. Requires the board to elect a president and a vice president from among its members. Mandates the election occur at the last meeting at the end of each calendar year or in December. Repeals the requirement to elect officers at the first meeting at the beginning of each calendar year.
qa_results.responsible_party: Talbot County Board of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Talbot County Board of Education members
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact; the change is procedural in nature and does not affect Talbot County finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Education Article regarding the internal election timing of officers for the Talbot County Board of Education. While MSDE provides statewide oversight and leadership for Maryland's 24 local school systems, this procedural change has minimal impact and no fiscal effect on the department.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters continuing education requirements for real estate brokers, salespersons, and associate brokers holding an initial license. Requires these initial licensees to complete four 3-clock-hour courses across specified real estate topics. Mandates instruction in contract writing, brokerage disclosures, real estate practice principles, and landlord and tenant laws. Requires at least one 1.5-clock-hour course each in real estate financing and professional ethics. Maintains current continuing education curriculum requirements for licensees holding renewal certificates.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Real Estate Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals initially licensed as real estate brokers, salespersons, or associate brokers in Maryland, and real estate education course providers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Real Estate Commission special fund expenditures increase by approximately $42,600 in FY 2024 for IT programming and consulting, followed by ongoing consulting expenditures of $2,200 to $2,500 annually through FY 2028. Local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Real Estate Commission is a regulatory unit within the Maryland Department of Labor's Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing. The bill alters continuing education curriculum requirements for newly licensed real estate professionals and results in special fund expenditures for the department to update IT tracking systems and engage curriculum consultants.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Comptroller and the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to confer during the 2023 legislative interim. Directs both agencies to identify collaboration methods to enhance access to and raise awareness of Department-administered property tax benefits. Seeks to simplify application processes by reducing or eliminating redundant income reporting for homeowners' and renters' tax credits. Requires a joint report of findings and recommendations to two legislative committees by December 1, 2023. Mandates that the report detail required funding amounts and implementation timelines for any recommended changes.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller; State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland homeowners, renters, disabled veterans, disabled active duty service members, and surviving spouses
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $18,000 in FY 2024 for the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to hire a consultant for the required report. Comptroller operations are handled with existing resources. No effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly directs the Comptroller to confer with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) during the 2023 legislative interim to identify methods to enhance access, raise awareness, and streamline the application process for state property tax benefits, and to submit a joint report of findings and recommendations to the General Assembly by December 1, 2023.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes an alternative pathway to qualify for a real estate appraisal license or certificate. Allows applicants to complete the Practical Applications of Real Estate Appraisal program criteria. Substitutes the program for the required 1,000 or 1,500 hours of supervised trainee experience. Applies to applicants seeking a real estate appraisal license or residential or general real estate certification. Maintains existing requirements including minimum age, examination passage, and good character.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Commission of Real Estate Appraisers, Appraisal Management Companies, and Home Inspectors
qa_results.stakeholders: Applicants for real estate appraiser licenses and residential or general appraisal certificates, real estate appraiser trainees, and certified real estate appraisers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures for the State Commission of Real Estate Appraisers, Appraisal Management Companies, and Home Inspectors likely increase due to additional applicants, but a reliable estimate is not feasible.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters licensing and certification qualification pathways for real estate appraisers, directly impacting the State Commission of Real Estate Appraisers, Appraisal Management Companies, and Home Inspectors, which operates under the Maryland Department of Labor's Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing. The department will experience operational and fiscal impacts from reviewing alternative credentials, issuing licenses/certifications, and managing related regulatory oversight.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Board of County Commissioners for Garrett County to meet in public session at least twice a month. Authorizes the Board to hold public meetings in person or through live video streaming. Prohibits the Board from meeting solely through live video streaming for more than two consecutive meetings. Waives this prohibition only under a formal declaration of a state of emergency.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of County Commissioners for Garrett County
qa_results.stakeholders: Board of County Commissioners for Garrett County and Garrett County residents
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State or Garrett County finances.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals requirements that the Maryland Transit Administration increase transit fares every two or five years based on the Consumer Price Index. Eliminates statutory restrictions on fare increases, including caps and conditions tied to inflation declines. Subjects any future fare modifications to existing public hearing requirements. Retains the prohibition against reducing transit service levels to achieve a specific farebox recovery ratio. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Transit Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: mass transit riders and commuters using Maryland Transit Administration services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund revenues decrease by up to $6.9 million in FY 2024, $7.1 million in FY 2025, $18.1 million in FY 2026, $17.6 million in FY 2027, and $19.8 million in FY 2028 due to foregone mandated fare increases. MTA may mitigate revenue losses by exercising its general authority to raise fares after public hearings. Expenditures are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly applies to the Maryland Transit Administration by repealing statutory requirements that mandated CPI-based increases to its transit fares every two and five years, restoring discretionary fare adjustment authority subject to public hearing requirements.

As the parent department of the Maryland Transit Administration, the Maryland Department of Transportation oversees transit operations and relies on the Transportation Trust Fund, which will experience a direct revenue reduction of up to tens of millions of dollars annually due to the repealed mandated fare increases.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland Historical Trust to transfer money from the Historic Preservation Loan Fund to a qualified cooperating nonprofit organization. Defines qualifying organizations as Maryland-based statewide nonprofits experienced in rehabilitating historic structures, managing preservation funds, and holding preservation easements. Limits the use of transferred funds to acquiring or restoring historic properties, issuing specified loans, and covering administrative costs. Requires recipient organizations to develop a competitive award process and publish program guidelines online. Mandates that recipient organizations submit an annual report to the Trust by June 30 detailing all funds received.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Historical Trust
qa_results.stakeholders: Qualified cooperating nonprofit organizations, historic property owners, and entities or individuals seeking financing to acquire, restore, or rehabilitate historic properties.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures may increase and special fund revenues from loan repayments may decrease in FY 2024 and future years due to transfers from the Historic Preservation Loan Fund; exact amounts cannot be reliably determined.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Historical Trust (MHT) is a unit within the Maryland Department of Planning. The bill alters the authorized uses of MHT's Historic Preservation Loan Fund to allow transfers to qualified cooperating nonprofit organizations and requires MHT coordination and oversight.
The State Treasurer holds and invests the Historic Preservation Loan Fund, which will be impacted by changes in fund balance and expenditure flows authorized by the bill.
The Board of Public Works has statutory oversight and approval authority over certain expenditures and loans from the Historic Preservation Loan Fund financed through general obligation bonds.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Commission to Study Trauma Center Funding in Maryland. Directs the Commission to study the adequacy of State trauma center funding for operating, capital, and workforce costs. Requires the Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems and the Maryland Health Care Commission to provide joint staff. Requires the Commission to submit findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1, 2023. Takes effect June 1, 2023, and terminates at the end of June 30, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Commission to Study Trauma Center Funding in Maryland; Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems; Maryland Health Care Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland trauma centers, trauma physicians and clinical staff, trauma patients, Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems, and the Maryland Health Care Commission
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operational costs are absorbable within existing budgeted resources of the Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems and the Maryland Health Care Commission. Commission travel expense reimbursements are assumed to be minimal. No effect on State revenues or local finances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS's Executive Director serves as co-chair of the newly created Commission to Study Trauma Center Funding in Maryland, and the agency is required to jointly provide staff and expertise for the commission.

The Executive Director of the Maryland Health Care Commission serves as co-chair, the agency jointly provides staff for the Commission, and its members and administrative role with the Maryland Trauma Physician Services Fund are central to the study.
The Secretary of Health (or designee) serves as a member of the Commission and is tasked with appointing several key commission members representing various health and trauma stakeholder groups.
HSCRC is designated a representative on the Commission and co-administers the Maryland Trauma Physician Services Fund, which is a major focus of the Commission's review.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally creates a temporary study commission within the State to analyze and report on trauma center operating, capital, and workforce funding adequacy.
The Commission is mandated to report its findings and recommendations regarding trauma center funding to the Governor on or before December 1, 2023.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands State cemetery oversight laws to cover pet remains and pet interments. Defines pet remains to include whole bodies, body parts, and cremated remains of deceased pets. Imposes a duty of perpetual care on cemetery operators and permit holders offering pet burial or cremation services. Requires preneed burial contracts to include the name of the pet, if applicable. Requires the Director of the Office of Cemetery Oversight to adopt regulations to enforce these provisions.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of Cemetery Oversight, Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: registered cemeterians, registered crematory operators, cemetery and burial goods permit holders, and pet owners purchasing burial or cremation services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal impact on the Office of Cemetery Oversight, which can adopt regulations and enforce provisions using existing budgeted resources; special fund revenues may increase minimally if pet cemeteries register, though specific dollar figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of Cemetery Oversight (OCO) is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor. The bill directly impacts the OCO by redefining interment to include pet remains, imposing perpetual care requirements, and requiring the Director of the OCO to promulgate regulations and oversee compliance.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the mandated annual budget appropriation from the Transportation Trust Fund for operating the Pride of Baltimore II through fiscal 2028. Requires any entity receiving these funds to submit an annual report by December 1. Directs the recipient to submit the report to the Maryland Department of Transportation and specified legislative committees. Requires the report to include expenditure accountings, vessel itineraries, and a multi-year strategic business plan. Extends the termination date of the funding authorization to June 30, 2028.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation; Office of the Governor
qa_results.stakeholders: operators of the replica sailing vessel Pride of Baltimore II, maritime history educators, and Maryland tourists
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund expenditures increase by $500,000 annually from fiscal 2024 through fiscal 2028 for the operation of the Pride of Baltimore II. Revenues and local government finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates an annual appropriation of $500,000 from the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) from FY 2024 through FY 2028 for the operation of the Pride of Baltimore II and requires the fund recipient to submit annual expenditure reports and strategic plans directly to the department.

As the agency responsible for formulating and managing the state budget, DBM is responsible for incorporating and executing the mandated annual appropriation from the Transportation Trust Fund into the state budget.
The bill places a statutory requirement on the Governor to include the annual appropriation for the Pride of Baltimore II in the annual State budget.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the license display requirements for alcoholic beverages license holders in Frederick County. Requires a license holder to frame the license and display it conspicuously in the licensed premises. Removes the statewide requirement that the framed license be under glass within the county. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Frederick County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: alcoholic beverages license holders in Frederick County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. Frederick County finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry. Although this legislation specifically affects local retail license display requirements in Frederick County without state fiscal impact, it relates to the broader regulation and governance of alcoholic beverage licenses in the state.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the annual cap for the Student Loan Debt Relief Tax Credit from $9 million to $18 million. Requires the Maryland Higher Education Commission to reserve $9 million of authorized credits for State employees. Establishes priority for State employees graduating from Maryland institutions where at least 40% of attendees receive federal Pell Grants. Extends the period to prove student loan repayment from two years to three years to avoid credit recapture. Mandates an outreach and marketing plan and an annual report on credit applicants and recipients. Requires the Office of Student Financial Assistance to inform scholarship recipients about the credit.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission; Office of Student Financial Assistance
qa_results.stakeholders: Qualified taxpayers with student loan debt, particularly State employees and graduates of Maryland higher education institutions
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by $9.0 million annually beginning in FY 2024 due to additional personal income tax credits claimed. Expenditures are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) is the primary implementing agency for the bill. It is responsible for reviewing applications, certifying up to $18 million in student loan debt relief tax credits annually, reserving $9 million for qualified state employees, prioritizing applicants, executing outreach campaigns, and submitting an annual report to the Governor and General Assembly.

As the state's coordinating board for higher education and administrator of financial assistance programs, the Commission is directly responsible for certifying the tax credits, prioritizing eligible applicants, conducting outreach to institutions of higher education, and reporting annual program metrics.

The Comptroller administers the State income tax system against which this credit is claimed. The office processes the tax returns, handles refundable credits, manages recapture provisions, and accounts for an estimated $9 million annual decrease in State general fund revenues.
