The bill mandates that MHEC submit an annual comprehensive report to the Governor by January 1 each year regarding application volume, credit awards, and demographic breakdowns of recipients.

The bill requires MHEC to encourage Maryland institutions of higher education to advise new graduates about the credit, especially those entering public service, and creates priority categories for state employees and graduates of Maryland higher education institutions.

As a public institution of higher education in Maryland with high Pell Grant recipient representation, its graduates and employees are directly impacted and targeted for outreach under the bill's prioritization criteria.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Department of Natural Resources to issue an apprentice hunting license to a person under age 17. Allows eligible youth to obtain a license even if previously issued an apprentice hunting license. Requires applicants for a second or subsequent apprentice license to repeat an approved hunter safety course. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Hunters under the age of 17 seeking an apprentice hunting license and supervising adult hunters
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal potential impact on State hunting license fee revenues, with no material effect on State operations or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources is the primary agency responsible for administering Maryland's wildlife conservation and hunting laws. This bill directly authorizes DNR to issue second or subsequent apprentice hunting licenses to youth under the age of 17 and requires DNR to ensure applicants repeat the approved course in firearm competency and hunter safety.

qa_results.bill_summary: Eliminates separate branch license requirements for collection agencies and specified non-depository financial institutions. Authorizes licensees to conduct business at multiple locations under a single license recorded in NMLS. Requires licensees to maintain and update additional business locations and trade names in NMLS. Authorizes the Commissioner of Financial Regulation to levy annual assessments on licensees to support the Non-depository Special Fund. Alters surety bond amounts and calculation factors across regulated non-depository license categories.
qa_results.responsible_party: Commissioner of Financial Regulation; State Collection Agency Licensing Board
qa_results.stakeholders: non-depository financial institutions, collection agencies, mortgage lenders, check cashers, money transmitters, debt management services providers, consumer lenders, sales finance companies, and Maryland consumers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues to the Non-depository Special Fund decrease by approximately $3.0 million annually beginning in fiscal 2024 due to the elimination of branch licensing requirements and associated fees. Special fund expenditures are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation (OCFR) is a major unit within the Department of Labor. OCFR is the primary regulatory and implementing body for this bill, modernizing the licensing, assessments, and oversight of non-depository financial institutions and managing the Non-Depository Special Fund.

The State Treasurer is statutorily designated as the custodian of the Non-Depository Special Fund created/re-established under Section 2-120 of the Financial Institutions Article, responsible for holding, investing, and depositing revenues collected for the fund.

The Comptroller is responsible for accounting for interest earnings on special funds under Section 6-226 of the State Finance and Procurement Article (amended by the bill to exempt the Non-Depository Special Fund) and receives fines and penalties collected under the title into the General Fund.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel and enforcement support to the Commissioner of Financial Regulation and the Collection Agency Licensing Board, and its Consumer Protection Division was consulted in the fiscal note analysis.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Trust Decanting Act governing an authorized fiduciary's power to distribute trust property or modify trust terms. Applies retroactively to express trusts administered in Maryland or governed under Maryland law. Permits fiduciaries to exercise decanting powers without court approval after providing 60 days' advance notice to specified parties. Prohibits decanting that reduces vested interests, diminishes charitable interests, or violates express restrictions in the trust instrument. Authorizes special needs fiduciaries to decant trust property into special needs trusts for beneficiaries with disabilities. Grants the Attorney General the rights of a qualified beneficiary when a trust contains a determinable charitable interest.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Settlors, trustees, authorized fiduciaries, current and remainder trust beneficiaries, individuals with disabilities, and charitable organizations holding trust interests
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material direct effect on State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly grants the Office of the Attorney General the rights of a qualified beneficiary to represent and bind determinable charitable interests, requiring fiduciaries to give notice to the Attorney General prior to decanting and giving the Attorney General authority to consent or object to trust administration changes.

The bill establishes judicial procedures and authorizes courts with trust jurisdiction to review decanting actions, instruct fiduciaries, appoint special fiduciaries, and determine the validity of decanting exercises under the Act.

While the Register of Wills primarily oversees probate of estates and serves as clerk to the Orphans' Court, the agency is consulted on changes to the Estates and Trusts Article concerning fiduciary standards and potential overlaps with testamentary trusts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires memoranda of understanding establishing P-TECH schools to guarantee students receive high school diplomas immediately upon completing graduation requirements. Directs the local county board of education to award the diploma. Applies the requirement regardless of whether the student completes a full six-year pathway sequence. Prohibits construing the change to alter education funding formulas for public schools or community colleges. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Pathways in Technology Early College High (P-TECH) students, local school systems, community college partners, and industry partners
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $14,000 in FY 2024 for the Maryland State Department of Education to update its student accountability system. Local school system expenditures may increase minimally for system updates. State and local revenues and education formula funding are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) oversees public secondary school policy and graduation requirements. The bill requires P-TECH students to receive high school diplomas immediately upon completing graduation requirements, necessitating that MSDE update its student accountability tracking system at an estimated cost of $14,000 in FY 2024.

The Maryland Higher Education Commission coordinates postsecondary education policies in the state, including policies impacting community college partners participating in P-TECH programs, though the bill does not alter community college funding formulas.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the membership of the Board of Directors of the Maryland African American Museum Corporation. Reduces total board membership from 37 members to 25 members. Adds two appointees selected respectively by the President of the Senate and the Speaker of the House. Reduces governor-appointed members with specialized expertise or community representation from 28 to 19. Decreases representatives of African American historical or cultural institutions from four to one. Replaces three previous commission representatives with one member approved by the Commission on African American History and Culture.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland African American Museum Corporation
qa_results.stakeholders: Members and trustees of the Maryland African American Museum Corporation, the Commission on African American History and Culture, Morgan State University, and Maryland African American historical and cultural organizations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 690 directly alters the composition and structure of the Board of Directors of the Maryland African American Museum Corporation, reducing the total membership from 37 to 25.
The bill alters the Governor's statutory appointment authority regarding the Corporation's Board of Directors, reducing the number of gubernatorial appointees from 36 to 22.
The bill explicitly requires that one member of the Corporation's Board of Directors be a representative of Morgan State University, approved by the university's Board of Regents.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting, recruiting, and processing appointments to state boards, including the gubernatorial appointees to this reconstituted board.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes counties and municipal corporations to approve or deny local permits required under a certificate of public convenience and necessity. Requires a county or municipal corporation to approve or deny these permits within a reasonable time. Requires permit decisions to follow local laws to the extent state law does not preempt them. Prohibits conditioning permit approval on conditional use, special exception, or floating zone approvals. Affirms judicial precedent concerning state preemption of local zoning over certificate-approved energy projects.
qa_results.responsible_party: Public Service Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: electric generating station and transmission line developers; county and municipal governments in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State finances or operations. Local government operations and finances may be affected by the requirement to process certificate-related permits within a reasonable timeframe and without certain zoning conditions, though the fiscal impact on any individual local government is likely minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary state regulator responsible for issuing Certificates of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) for generating stations and transmission lines under the Public Utilities Article, which this bill directly amends.

DNR administers the Power Plant Research Program (PPRP), which evaluates the environmental and siting impacts of projects during the PSC's CPCN review process, and was consulted as an information source on the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Adds a registered pharmacy technician to the State Board of Pharmacy, increasing total board membership to 13. Authorizes licensed pharmacists to delegate remote prescription-related data entry to registered pharmacy technicians or registered pharmacy interns under specified conditions. Prohibits registered pharmacy technicians and pharmacy technician trainees from making decisions requiring the professional judgment of a pharmacist. Authorizes registered pharmacy technicians to administer specified vaccines to individuals meeting age thresholds, while prohibiting trainees from administering vaccinations. Extends the termination date of the Board under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act to July 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Pharmacy; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: registered pharmacy technicians, pharmacy technician trainees, registered pharmacy interns, licensed pharmacists, and pharmacy patients
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures for the State Board of Pharmacy are maintained through fiscal 2025. Special fund expenditures may increase minimally for per diem and expenses for the additional board member. Local operations and finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Pharmacy operates within the Maryland Department of Health. The bill extends the Board's termination date under the sunset act, alters board membership, and modifies statutory provisions regarding delegated pharmacy acts and vaccinations.
The bill authorizes the Governor to appoint a newly created registered pharmacy technician member to the State Board of Pharmacy from lists submitted by designated professional associations.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting, managing, and processing nominations and appointments for vacancies on state boards, including the newly added seat on the State Board of Pharmacy.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the allowable uses of grant disbursements from the Rural Maryland Prosperity Investment Fund. Adds agricultural development, cooperative development, and workforce development to the rural entrepreneurship grant category. Defines cooperative development to include feasibility, industry, and market studies, as well as business entity establishment. Defines workforce development to include worker skills training and support for local workforce training organizations. Awards competitive grants to promote economic growth and employment opportunities in rural communities.
qa_results.responsible_party: Rural Maryland Council; Maryland Agricultural Education and Rural Development Assistance Board
qa_results.stakeholders: Rural businesses, agricultural cooperatives, rural workers seeking job training, community colleges, career and technical education centers, and local workforce boards in Maryland rural communities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not affected overall, though grant disbursements from the Rural Maryland Prosperity Investment Fund may be reallocated among eligible recipients, including institutions of higher education. Local community colleges may experience a minimal increase in grant funding for workforce development programs. State and local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Rural Maryland Council directly administers the Rural Maryland Prosperity Investment Fund (RMPIF). The bill modifies the allowable uses and categories of RMPIF grant distributions to include agricultural development, cooperative development, and workforce development.

The Rural Maryland Council is administratively housed within the Department of Agriculture, and the legislation expands allowable grant allocations under RMPIF to specifically include agricultural development.

The bill explicitly expands grant eligibility to include workforce development programs and activities designed to train workers for local employers, intersecting with the Department of Labor's role in workforce training and adult learning.

The legislation modifies grant funding criteria for rural entrepreneurship, small business feasibility, and cooperative business development, which aligns with the Department of Commerce's focus on statewide business development.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Black Bass Conservation Fund within the Department of Natural Resources to further black bass management. Requires the Department to allow purchasers of an angler's license or Chesapeake Bay and coastal sport fishing license to donate. Restricts voluntary donations to individuals purchasing directly through the electronic system rather than authorized vendors. Authorizes fund monies for stocking black bass, enhancing aquatic habitats, and supporting responsible tournaments. Authorizes expenditures for scientific research related to black bass conservation.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Recreational anglers purchasing Maryland fishing licenses, black bass tournament organizers, and the Department of Natural Resources.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in fiscal 2024 from voluntary donations, interest earnings, and black bass management expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Black Bass Conservation Fund within the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) and requires DNR to administer the fund, integrate voluntary donation options into its electronic licensing system, collect donations, and expend fund revenues on bass stocking, habitat enhancement, tournaments, and research.
The bill designates the State Treasurer to hold the Black Bass Conservation Fund separately and invest its moneys, with net interest retained in the fund rather than accruing to the General Fund.
The bill statutorily requires the Comptroller to account for the newly established Black Bass Conservation Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes placement of one speed monitoring system at Maryland Route 333 (Oxford Road) and Bonfield Avenue in Talbot County. Requires warning signage and a proximate device displaying real-time driver traveling speed before activating the system. Allows the Town of Oxford to recover system implementation and administration costs from collected violation fines. Requires remaining fine balances to be remitted to the Comptroller for distribution to the State Highway Administration. Directs the State Highway Administration to use funds solely for roadway and pedestrian safety improvements near the intersection. Abrogates the statutory authority on September 30, 2028.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Highway Administration; Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Motorists traveling on Maryland Route 333 (Oxford Road) in Talbot County; Town of Oxford; pedestrians near the intersection of Maryland Route 333 and Bonfield Avenue
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund revenues and expenditures increase from FY 2024 through FY 2029 to the extent the speed camera is installed, with net revenues dedicated to local roadway and pedestrian safety improvements. General fund revenues may increase negligibly from contested citations in District Court. Local revenues and expenditures increase for system implementation and cost recovery.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT SHA is specifically designated to receive remitted speed monitoring system net revenues distributed via the Comptroller and is required to use those funds solely to cover the costs of roadway and pedestrian safety improvements at the intersection of MD Route 333 and Bonfield Avenue. The bill also references SHA traffic control device standards for signage.

MDOT is the parent agency of the State Highway Administration. The bill directly impacts Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) revenues and expenditures, which increase as fine balances are collected and expended for safety improvements on a state route.

The bill mandates that remaining fine revenues collected by the Town of Oxford be remitted to the Comptroller, who is then responsible for distributing those funds to the State Highway Administration.

The District Court prescribes the uniform citation form and penalty amounts for speed camera violations, and handles any contested citations resulting from the newly authorized speed monitoring system.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland Community Health Resources Commission to set compensation for certain unique staff positions. Authorizes the Comptroller, the Treasurer, and the Attorney General to set pay scales for specific unique positions. Requires consultation with the Secretary of Budget and Management to set pay scales and determine eligible positions. Requires eligible positions to be unique to each agency and require specific skills or experience. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Community Health Resources Commission; Maryland Department of Health; Comptroller of Maryland; Maryland State Treasurer; Office of the Attorney General; Department of Budget and Management
qa_results.stakeholders: Employees in qualifying unique positions within the Maryland Community Health Resources Commission, Office of the Comptroller, Office of the State Treasurer, and Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures increase for the Maryland Community Health Resources Commission and general fund expenditures increase for the Comptroller, Treasurer, and Attorney General beginning as early as fiscal 2024. Exact fiscal amounts are indeterminate because they depend on determinations of eligible positions and salary adjustments made by agency leadership and the Secretary of Budget and Management. State revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly authorizes the Comptroller, in consultation with the Secretary of Budget and Management, to set the pay scales of positions unique to the Office of the Comptroller, resulting in a direct operational and fiscal impact.

The bill grants statutory authority to the State Treasurer, in consultation with the Secretary of Budget and Management, to set the pay scale for positions unique to the Office of the Treasurer, directly impacting agency expenditures and personnel administration.

The bill authorizes the Attorney General, in consultation with the Secretary of Budget and Management, to establish pay scales for positions unique to the Office of the Attorney General, leading to direct personnel and fiscal impacts.

The Secretary of Budget and Management is tasked with consulting with the Comptroller, Treasurer, Attorney General, and the Maryland Community Health Resources Commission to determine eligible positions and consult on pay scales.

The Maryland Community Health Resources Commission (MCHRC) operates within MDH, and the Secretary of Health is statutorily required to consult with the Commission on determining job classifications, grades, and employee compensation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Health Care Commission to provide written findings and recommendations to the Office of Health Care Quality. Applies this mandate when evaluating notices of acquisition or transfer of interest of a nursing home. Requires the Secretary of Health to consider those findings before approving, denying, conditioning, or revoking a license. Mandates inclusion of purchaser quality ratings, three-year compliance surveys, corrective action plans, and patient lawsuits. Directs the Commission to study expanding the Certificate of Need program over nursing home acquisitions by December 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Health Care Commission; Office of Health Care Quality; Secretary of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: nursing home owners, operators, prospective purchasers of nursing homes, and nursing home residents
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures and revenues are not affected, as the Maryland Department of Health and Maryland Health Care Commission can implement the requirements with existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks MHCC with evaluating notices of acquisition or transfer of interest in nursing homes, compiling detailed findings and recommendations on facility quality and performance, transmitting them to the Office of Health Care Quality, and conducting a study regarding the expansion of the Certificate of Need program over nursing home acquisitions.

The bill requires the Secretary of Health to consider MHCC's findings and recommendations before approving, denying, conditioning, or revoking a nursing home operating license. Additionally, units within MDH (the Office of Health Care Quality and the Medicaid Administration) receive these findings and are named as key consulting stakeholders for the required study.

qa_results.bill_summary: Proposes an amendment to the Maryland Constitution establishing a fundamental right to reproductive freedom. Protects an individual's ability to make and effectuate decisions to prevent, continue, or end a pregnancy. Prohibits the State from denying, burdening, or abridging this right directly or indirectly. Permits restrictions only if justified by a compelling State interest achieved by the least restrictive means. Submits the proposed constitutional amendment to Maryland voters at the November 2024 general election.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections; Governor
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland voters, individuals making reproductive and pregnancy decisions, and licensed healthcare providers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State or local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires a proposed constitutional amendment on reproductive freedom to be submitted to Maryland voters at the November 2024 general election, which the State Board of Elections must prepare, certify, and place on ballots statewide.

As the State's chief legal counsel, the Office of the Attorney General provided information for the bill's analysis and is responsible for defending and interpreting state constitutional provisions, including the proposed standard of strict scrutiny regarding reproductive freedom.

The Department of Health regulates health care providers and reproductive healthcare services in Maryland, and constitutionalizing the right to reproductive freedom impacts the regulatory framework and state limits surrounding reproductive healthcare and pregnancy.

Pursuant to the bill and Article XIV of the Maryland Constitution, the official election returns regarding the adoption or rejection of the constitutional amendment are formally reported to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Business Facade Improvement Program in the Department of Housing and Community Development. Requires the Department to distribute program funds to political subdivisions that have at least one sustainable community. Requires participating political subdivisions to distribute grants to qualified businesses improving their facilities' outside appearance. Requires both the Department and participating political subdivisions to develop application processes and award criteria. Mandates an annual state budget appropriation of $5,000,000 to the program beginning in fiscal year 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Qualified businesses in sustainable communities, counties, and municipal corporations in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $1.5 million in bond funds in FY 2024 and by $5.0 million in general funds annually beginning in FY 2025 under a statutory mandate. Local revenues and expenditures increase by $1.5 million in FY 2024 and approximately $4.9 million annually thereafter from grant distribution.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Business Facade Improvement Program within the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD). DHCD is the primary agency responsible for administering the program, developing application processes and rating criteria, distributing funds to political subdivisions, and adopting regulations.
The bill explicitly mandates that for fiscal year 2025 and each fiscal year thereafter, the Governor must include an appropriation of $5,000,000 to the program in the annual state budget bill.

As the principal fiscal and budget agency for the state, DBM oversees budget formulation and must account for the $5,000,000 annual mandated general fund appropriation to the program starting in FY 2025.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Taxpayer Advocate Division in the Office of the Comptroller. Places the division under the administrative control of a Taxpayer Advocate supervised by the Comptroller. Requires a minimum of six division employees, including the Taxpayer Advocate and an information technology webmaster. Directs the division to assist taxpayers and their representatives in resolving tax and debt collection problems. Mandates the division establish a website portal, conduct annual taxpayer surveys, and compile complaint data. Requires the division to propose administrative, legislative, or regulatory changes to resolve systemic taxpayer issues.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Comptroller; Department of Budget and Management
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland taxpayers and their representatives
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $294,700 in FY 2024 to hire four staff members and cover operating expenses, increasing to $401,600 by FY 2028. Revenues and local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly establishes the Taxpayer Advocate Division within the Office of the Comptroller, requiring the Comptroller to appoint staff, oversee the division, establish an electronic taxpayer portal, and absorb personnel and operational expenditures.

The bill explicitly requires the Department of Budget and Management, in coordination with the Comptroller's Office, to make appropriate personnel allocations and provide the ability to reclassify positions for the new division.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires five State departments to develop and oversee the cloud-based 21st Century Financial Systems Enterprise. Mandates consultation with a designated representative from the Modernize Maryland Oversight Commission. Directs the departments to standardize State financial management by requiring all State agencies to participate. Authorizes the departments to collaborate with consultants, assign resources, and establish working groups as needed. Requires the Office of the Comptroller to submit semiannual progress reports through January 1, 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Comptroller; Office of the State Treasurer; Department of Budget and Management; Department of Information Technology; Department of General Services
qa_results.stakeholders: All Maryland State agencies, State accounting personnel, and users of State financial management information systems
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State operations or finances, and has no local effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Comptroller as a primary implementing partner to develop, manage, and oversee the 21st Century Financial Systems Enterprise, and requires the Comptroller's Office to submit semi-annual status reports to the General Assembly through 2027.
The bill explicitly designates DBM as one of the primary departments required to develop, implement, manage, and oversee the modernization of the State's financial management infrastructure.
The bill explicitly designates DGS as one of the partner departments responsible for developing, implementing, and overseeing the new financial management systems enterprise.
The bill explicitly designates DoIT as one of the core departments responsible for setting technology policies and overseeing the cloud-based IT infrastructure transformation.
The bill explicitly names the Treasurer's Office as one of the key departments tasked with overseeing and implementing the 21st Century Financial Systems Enterprise.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifically requires the partner departments to consult with a designated representative from the Modernize Maryland Oversight Commission (MMOC) in planning and implementing the enterprise.

MDOT operates a separate version of the Financial Management and Information System (FMIS) and is undergoing its own modernization effort, making the bill's mandate to standardize financial management across all state agencies directly impactful to their systems.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the placement of speed monitoring systems on highways in residential districts in Anne Arundel County. Restricts placement to highways with a maximum posted speed limit of 35 miles per hour. Requires the speed limit to be established using generally accepted traffic engineering practices. Prohibits system use unless authorized by local law enacted after reasonable notice and a public hearing. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Anne Arundel County; District Court of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Motorists driving in Anne Arundel County, residents of Anne Arundel County residential districts, Anne Arundel County government, and municipal governments in Anne Arundel County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues likely increase minimally beginning in FY 2024 due to contested citations in District Court, with no material expenditure impact. Local revenues increase, potentially significantly, beginning in FY 2024 from citation fines, while local expenditures increase for system procurement, installation, and maintenance, with net balances dedicated to public safety purposes. Specific figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Contested speed camera citations issued under the authorization in Anne Arundel County will be adjudicated in the District Court, impacting court caseloads and generating fine revenues paid into the State general fund.

The bill amends Title 21 of the Transportation Article regarding speed monitoring system authorization on highways in residential districts, affecting transportation safety regulation and state road infrastructure.
The State Highway Administration establishes traffic engineering standards, regulates speed limits, and adopts standards for required signage proximate to speed monitoring systems.
Under statutory provisions governing speed monitoring systems, if a local jurisdiction's net camera revenues exceed 10% of its total revenues, the excess balance must be remitted to the Comptroller.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the information required in written statements from managed care organizations retroactively denying reimbursement. Applies when a managed care organization retroactively denies provider reimbursement due to coordination of benefits. Requires the statement to include the name and address of the entity identified as responsible for payment. Exempts managed care organizations from obtaining an acknowledgment of responsibility before denying a claim. Maintains the acknowledgment requirement for carriers that are not managed care organizations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Medicaid managed care organizations, health care providers, and health insurance carriers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local governmental operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health administers the state's Medicaid program, under which Medicaid Managed Care Organizations (MCOs) operate. This bill amends provisions in the Health-General Article governing MCO procedures for retroactive denial of reimbursement to health care providers.

The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates insurance carriers and enforces the Insurance Article, including § 15-1008 which governs retroactive denials of reimbursement and coordination of benefits requirements for health insurance carriers.

The Department of Budget and Management oversees the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, which contracts with health insurance carriers subject to state insurance statutory standards regarding claims and reimbursement denials.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes licensed certified midwives and nurse-midwives to personally prepare and dispense starter dosages of certain drugs. Permits licensed certified midwives to delegate technical tasks to trained assistants under direct, on-site supervision. Expands definitions of certified medication technicians and certified nursing assistants to include tasks delegated by midwives. Repeals the prerequisite health and science coursework requirement for certified midwife licensure. Authorizes the State Board of Nursing to appoint peer advisory committees regarding certified midwifery practice. Requires the Maryland Department of Health to recommend strategies expanding birthing center access by December 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Nursing; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed certified midwives, licensed registered nurses certified as nurse-midwives, certified medication technicians, certified nursing assistants, birthing centers, and maternity patients
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Nursing and the Maryland Department of Health can implement the requirements using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government operations and finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the State Board of Nursing, a regulatory board within the Maryland Department of Health (MDH), altering licensure standards, scope of practice, and delegation authorities for nurse-midwives and certified midwives. In addition, Section 2 of the bill specifically requires MDH, in consultation with stakeholders, to develop recommendations and submit a report on expanding access to birthing services in birthing centers across the State.

qa_results.bill_summary: Modifies the State forest preservation policy to increase statewide forest land and tree canopy acreage every four years. Replaces conservation thresholds with a standard reforestation ratio of one acre planted for each acre cleared. Establishes a reduced reforestation ratio of one-half acre per cleared acre in designated priority funding areas. Exempts transit-oriented developments and specified multifamily housing projects subject to mandatory reforestation or preservation mitigation. Authorizes local jurisdictions to adopt alternative forest conservation requirements approved by the Department of Natural Resources. Extends the deadline for the Department of Natural Resources to expend Forest Conservation Fund deposits to five years.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: private landowners, residential and commercial developers, local governments, forest mitigation bank operators, and commercial landscaping and nursery contractors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential increase in State PAYGO general fund expenditures and local capital expenditures beginning in FY 2025 for public construction projects clearing forest land. Indeterminate net effect on State and local forest conservation fund fee-in-lieu revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR is the primary state agency responsible for administering the Forest Conservation Act (FCA). The bill requires DNR to update the State Forest Conservation Technical Manual, review and approve local alternative forest conservation programs, administer the State Forest Conservation Fund with updated expenditure timelines, and establish a workgroup to recommend incentives for private landowner forest conservation.

The bill incorporates MDE-identified Tier II and Tier III high-quality watersheds into priority forest retention criteria and cross-references MDE environmental site design and stormwater management standards for reforestation mitigation credits.

The bill alters exemptions from the Forest Conservation Act regarding electric generating stations and solar photovoltaic facilities licensed via Certificates of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) issued by the Commission.

State transportation and infrastructure projects are subject to the Forest Conservation Act's updated reforestation ratios and buffer requirements. The bill also establishes specific reforestation and mitigation ratios for transit-oriented developments defined under the Transportation Article.

The bill defines procedures, timeframes (30-day petition deadline), and evidentiary scopes (limited to the agency record) for judicial review of approved forest conservation plans and priority clearing determinations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The legislation requires the creation of a temporary workgroup to evaluate and recommend incentives for private landowners to conserve forest lands.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires a child on the Autism Waiver registry to remain on the registry during out-of-state military relocations. Allows removal from the registry only upon request by the child's family. Restores eligibility for waiver services if the family relocates back to Maryland after qualifying while out of State. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: military families with children on the Autism Waiver registry
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact because the bill codifies current practice.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health oversees the Maryland Medical Assistance Program, maintains and manages the Autism Waiver registry, conducts eligibility verifications, and will need to pursue any required federal Medicaid waiver amendments.

The Maryland State Department of Education directly administers the Autism Waiver, monitors military family participants relocating out of state, and implements placement on the waiver registry upon their return to Maryland.

The Department of Veterans and Military Families advocates for and assists active-duty service members and their families in navigating and securing state benefits and healthcare services in Maryland.
The Maryland Department of Disabilities coordinates statewide policies and service delivery for individuals with developmental disabilities and works with MSDE and MDH on disability support programs.

qa_results.bill_summary: Approves $30,000,000 in academic facilities bond authority for the University System of Maryland. Allocates $5,000,000 to finance an infrastructure project at the University of Maryland, College Park. Allocates $25,000,000 for systemwide capital facilities renewal projects across constituent institutions and centers. Specifies that issued bonds do not constitute debt or an obligation of the State. Authorizes nonresidential campuses to use property sale proceeds for operating expenses with Board of Regents approval.
qa_results.responsible_party: University System of Maryland; Board of Regents of the University System of Maryland; Board of Public Works
qa_results.stakeholders: University System of Maryland constituent institutions, students, faculty, and nonresidential campuses including University of Maryland Global Campus
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State bond revenues and expenditures increase by $30.0 million in FY 2024 for academic capital projects. Higher education expenditures increase by an estimated $2.5 million annually beginning in FY 2025 for 20 years to pay debt service on the revenue bonds. Nonresidential campus revenues and operating expenditures may increase from expanded authorized uses of property sale proceeds. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly grants academic facilities bonding authority of $30 million to the University System of Maryland for infrastructure and capital renewal projects, and authorizes its Board of Regents to approve the use of property sale proceeds for operating expenses at nonresidential campuses.
Under the statute amended by the bill, the Board of Public Works approves the sale or exchange of real properties by the USM Board of Regents and the standard uses of property sale proceeds.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits reporting a known false emergency or crime to a governmental emergency report recipient with reckless disregard of bodily harm. Establishes misdemeanor penalties of up to three years imprisonment and a $2,000 fine for violations. Elevates the offense to a felony if the response proximately causes serious physical injury, severe emotional distress, or death. Subjects felony violators to maximum penalties of 10 years imprisonment and a $20,000 fine. Classifies a minor's first violation as a civil offense and prohibits Department of Juvenile Services out-of-home placement. Makes violators civilly liable to any individual injured as a result of the violation.
qa_results.responsible_party: Judiciary; Department of Juvenile Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals who report emergencies or crimes, victims of swatting incidents, emergency responders, and juvenile offenders
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances and operations are not materially affected. Potential minimal increases in expenditures may occur for the Office of the Public Defender and the Judiciary due to additional caseloads.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends statutory provisions governing the Department of Juvenile Services by prohibiting a child from being committed to DJS for out-of-home placement if the most serious offense is a first-time violation of the antiswatting provisions.

The bill creates new criminal offenses (misdemeanor and felony), juvenile civil procedures, and a civil cause of action, directly impacting court caseloads, filings, and judicial proceedings managed by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender will be required to provide legal defense representation to indigent individuals and juveniles charged with the new misdemeanor, felony, and juvenile offenses established by the bill.

As the primary state law enforcement agency and a governmental emergency report recipient, the Maryland State Police is directly affected through responding to emergency reports, investigating swatting incidents, and enforcing the new criminal statute.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS oversees incarceration in state correctional facilities and community supervision through the Division of Parole and Probation for individuals convicted of misdemeanor or felony violations under the bill.

The bill specifically encompasses false reports made to public safety answering points (PSAPs), which are overseen and coordinated through the Maryland 9-1-1 Board housed within the Department of Emergency Management.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes concurrent jurisdiction of Maryland juvenile courts with federal courts over certain offenses committed on military installations. Applies to proceedings where a child commits a federal law violation on a U.S. Department of Defense installation. Requires the federal court to waive exclusive jurisdiction and the violation to constitute a crime under State law. Authorizes the Governor to enter agreements establishing concurrent jurisdiction over federal land regardless of prior statutory cessions. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Judiciary; Office of the Governor
qa_results.stakeholders: juveniles alleged to have committed offenses on U.S. Department of Defense military installations in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Procedural measure not expected to materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands the statutory jurisdiction of the State's juvenile courts to exercise concurrent jurisdiction with federal courts over certain offenses committed by juveniles on federal Department of Defense military installations.

The Department of Juvenile Services oversees, assesses, and provides services to youths adjudicated within the Maryland juvenile court system, which may now include children processed under concurrent state jurisdiction for offenses on military installations.

The bill amends General Provisions § 6-202 to expressly authorize the Governor to enter into agreements with the United States to establish full or partial concurrent jurisdiction over any land in the State held by the federal government.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender provides legal representation to eligible juveniles in delinquency proceedings and could be assigned to represent youths charged under state juvenile court jurisdiction for incidents occurring on military installations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Officer and Community Wellness Training Grant Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund. Requires the Governor’s Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services to administer the Fund. Dedicates grants to Mental Health First Aid for Public Safety training and Critical Incident Stress Management peer support training. Authorizes the Governor to include an appropriation for the Fund in the annual budget bill starting in fiscal year 2025. Requires recipient law enforcement agencies to submit expenditure and performance data within 90 days after each grant cycle. Requires the Executive Director to submit an annual report to the Governor and the General Assembly.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services
qa_results.stakeholders: State, county, and municipal law enforcement agencies, sheriffs' offices, and police officers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $27,800 in FY 2024 for administrative staffing, and by approximately $1.1 million annually beginning in FY 2025 to capitalize and administer the fund. Special fund revenues and expenditures increase correspondingly by an assumed $1.0 million annually starting in FY 2025 for grant awards. Local law enforcement grant revenues and expenditures likely increase beginning as early as FY 2025.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The office is designated as the primary administrative agency responsible for managing the newly established Officer and Community Wellness Training Grant Fund, reviewing grant applications, monitoring grantee performance, and reporting annually to the Governor and General Assembly.
The statute explicitly mandates that the State Treasurer hold the Officer and Community Wellness Training Grant Fund as a separate, nonlapsing special fund.
The statute specifically requires the Comptroller, in conjunction with the Executive Director of the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy, to account for the new grant fund.

The bill authorizes the Governor to include an appropriation for the fund in the annual state budget bill beginning in fiscal year 2025 and requires annual reports on fund usage to be submitted to the Governor.
As the state's budget agency, DBM is involved in coordinating discretionary appropriations and general fund expenditures to capitalize the fund and support administrative staffing costs.

Because the definition of eligible law enforcement agencies encompasses state-level law enforcement organizations that enforce general criminal laws, MSP is potentially eligible to receive grant funding for officer mental health and crisis peer support training.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends from 20 to 75 years the minimum retention period for sexual assault evidence collection kits and related evidence. Prohibits law enforcement agencies, health care providers, and hospitals from destroying kits within 75 years of collection. Requires hospitals and child advocacy centers to transfer kits and self-administered kits to law enforcement agencies within 30 days. Requires kits collected before January 1, 2000, to be transferred to law enforcement agencies for testing. Directs the Maryland Sexual Assault Evidence Kit Policy and Funding Committee to submit recommendations by December 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Sexual Assault Evidence Kit Policy and Funding Committee; Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: victims of sexual assault, law enforcement agencies, hospitals, child advocacy centers, and qualified health care providers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material near-term impact on State or local finances. State general fund expenditures and local expenditures may increase in future years should the Department of State Police and local law enforcement agencies need to acquire additional long-term storage facilities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Attorney General to adopt regulations for uniform statewide implementation of sexual assault evidence kit requirements, authorizes the office to direct the transfer of certain pre-2000 kits, and tasks its Consumer Protection Division with consulting on consumer education regarding self-administered kits.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Department of State Police investigates sexual assault cases, receives and maintains custody of evidence collection kits, and will be required to preserve and store kits for 75 years instead of 20 years, with potential long-term fiscal impacts on evidence storage capacity.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Sexual Assault Evidence Kit Policy and Funding Committee is tasked with reporting to the Governor and General Assembly with recommendations on transfer guidelines, guidance on self-administered kits, and victim education resources.
The bill directly amends retention, notice, and storage requirements for healthcare providers and hospitals that perform sexual assault evidence collection exams and store kits.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP coordinates state policies, initiatives, and grant funding related to crime prevention, public safety, and victim services, including sexual assault response.
The Governor's Office receives the mandated recommendations report from the Maryland Sexual Assault Evidence Kit Policy and Funding Committee by December 1, 2023.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services to establish a kit tracking reporting program. Allows victims and victim representatives to track the location, status, and chain of custody of their kits. Requires law enforcement agencies, health care providers, forensic laboratories, and State's Attorneys possessing kits to submit tracking information. Requires entities possessing kits before October 1, 2023, to report tracking data on or before December 31, 2025. Authorizes the Rape Kit Testing Grant Fund to cover kits collected before or after the fund's establishment.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Victims of sexual assault and their representatives, law enforcement agencies, health care providers, forensic laboratories, and State's Attorneys
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $119,400 in FY 2024 for one program manager to administer the program and adopt regulations, growing to $167,400 by FY 2028. Kit tracking software procurement is funded through existing federal grant awards. Local governments, forensic laboratories, and State's Attorneys can implement reporting requirements with existing resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the office (referenced as the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services) to establish and administer the statewide sexual assault evidence collection kit tracking and reporting program, adopt necessary regulations, and administer the Rape Kit Testing Grant Fund.

As a primary law enforcement agency operating the state crime laboratory, the Maryland State Police must report kit location, status, and chain of custody data into the reporting program and comply with all program regulations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the administering agency to develop regulations for the reporting program in consultation with the Maryland Sexual Assault Evidence Kit Policy and Funding Committee.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires impasse declaration and binding arbitration to follow Montgomery County Code during certain Sheriff’s Office collective bargaining negotiations. Applies if the Montgomery County Sheriff and a bargaining representative cannot reach an agreement. Governs negotiations over terms and conditions applicable specifically to Sheriff’s Office employees. Covers nonprobationary deputy sheriffs below the rank of lieutenant and nonprobationary civilian employees. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Montgomery County Sheriff's Office; Montgomery County Labor Relations Administrator
qa_results.stakeholders: Nonprobationary deputy sheriffs below the rank of lieutenant, nonprobationary civilian employees of the Montgomery County Sheriff's Office, and the Montgomery County Sheriff
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. Montgomery County does not anticipate the bill will materially affect local finances or operations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes parties to a collective bargaining agreement for Montgomery Commission employees to request a mediator-arbitrator during an agreement's term. Establishes procedures for mediator-arbitrators to select a final offer if parties reach a bona fide impasse. Requires the Montgomery Commission and the employee organization to share equally the mediator-arbitrator's costs. Requires the Executive Director to submit agreement terms requiring appropriations, fiscal impact, or commission action. Authorizes the Montgomery Commission to accept or reject any submitted term or condition.
qa_results.responsible_party: Housing Opportunities Commission of Montgomery County; Labor Relations Administrator
qa_results.stakeholders: Employees of the Housing Opportunities Commission of Montgomery County and certified employee organizations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Local expenditures for the Housing Opportunities Commission of Montgomery County increase, likely minimally, beginning in fiscal 2024 to cover half of any mediator-arbitrator costs incurred under the bill. Local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends provisions within the Housing and Community Development Article regarding collective bargaining and impasse arbitration for the Montgomery County Housing Opportunities Commission. While DHCD is consulted on housing policy in Maryland, the bill's requirements apply strictly to local commission labor dispute procedures and impose no fiscal or operational impact on the state department.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the composition of the Western Maryland Economic Future Investment Board by adding voting and nonvoting members. Grants voting members final approval authority over Senator George C. Edwards Fund disbursements and selected projects. Authorizes voting members of the Board to elect a chair from among the Board's members. Requires the Board to appoint an Executive Director with a salary not exceeding $75,000. Authorizes the Executive Director to manage administrative affairs and assist in administering the Fund.
qa_results.responsible_party: Western Maryland Economic Future Investment Board; Tri-County Council for Western Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Businesses, local entities, and county governments in Allegany, Garrett, and Washington counties seeking economic development grants and loans
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State or local expenditures or revenues. Existing administrative appropriations within the Senator George C. Edwards Fund accommodate the Executive Director salary of up to $75,000 and minimal board reimbursements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the Department of Commerce's representation on the Western Maryland Economic Future Investment Board, changing the Secretary's appointee from serving as the board chair to a nonvoting member.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the statutory membership, voting structure, officers, and administrative oversight of the Western Maryland Economic Future Investment Board, including establishing an Executive Director position.

The board is required to submit an annual implementation report to the Governor detailing funding, completed projects, and economic metrics, and the Governor oversees executive budget appropriations for the associated fund.
The Comptroller is statutorily designated to account for the Senator George C. Edwards Fund, which supports the program and covers the salary of the newly established Executive Director.
The State Treasurer is tasked with holding and investing the monies of the special, nonlapsing Senator George C. Edwards Fund governed by the legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the definition of Tier I children in full-day prekindergarten programs to include homeless youths. Authorizes Tier II children with disabilities or non-English home backgrounds to enroll in full-day prekindergarten for the 2023–2024 school year. Requires assistant principals on the career ladder to participate in direct classroom student interactions rather than formal classroom teaching. Delays county board selection of curriculum-writing experts until July 1, 2026, conditioned on career ladder establishment. Prohibits requiring schools to collect the alternative income eligibility form until the year after the Department adopts it. Adds a certified school counselor to the Maryland Consortium on Coordinated Community Supports.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Accountability and Implementation Board; Maryland Consortium on Coordinated Community Supports; county boards of education
qa_results.stakeholders: Prekindergarten students and families (including homeless youths, children with disabilities, and English language learners); public and private prekindergarten providers; assistant principals; county boards of education; school counselors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $6.4 million in FY 2024, decrease by $497,700 in FY 2025, and experience minor adjustments through FY 2028. Local government expenditures increase by approximately $1.7 million in FY 2024 and $636,800 in FY 2025, while local school systems receive additional State aid.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is the primary agency responsible for administering public education funding formulas, regulating early childhood and prekindergarten programs, developing and adopting the alternative income eligibility form, and implementing career ladder guidelines for educators under the Blueprint for Maryland's Future.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the statutory composition and terms of the Maryland Consortium on Coordinated Community Supports by adding a certified school counselor designated by the Maryland School Counselor Association.

The Maryland Consortium on Coordinated Community Supports is administratively housed within the Maryland Community Health Resources Commission under the Department of Health, and its membership is expanded by this bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of Health or Office of Health Care Quality to investigate unlicensed assisted living programs. Requires the investigation to determine whether residents suffered neglect, exploitation, or abuse. Subjects operators to immediate prosecution upon credible allegations or findings of neglect, exploitation, or abuse, or upon noncooperation. Provides thirty days to comply with licensing requirements if investigators find no neglect, exploitation, or abuse. Authorizes the Department, Attorney General, State's Attorneys, or local health officers to petition for injunctive relief. Repeals consideration of a facility's ability to pay when the State recommends criminal penalties.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Office of Health Care Quality
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents and operators of unlicensed assisted living programs
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operational requirements can be handled with existing budgeted resources. Imposition of existing penalty provisions and injunctive relief authority are not expected to materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Maryland Department of Health and its Office of Health Care Quality (OHCQ) investigate unlicensed assisted living programs for abuse, neglect, and exploitation, enforce licensure compliance, and authorize petitions for injunctive relief.

The bill was requested by the Office of the Attorney General, authorizes the Attorney General to petition circuit courts for injunctive relief against unlicensed assisted living facilities, and classifies operating without a license as a violation of the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division enforces.
The Department of Aging oversees long-term care advocacy and the protection of rights and welfare for older adults residing in care facilities across Maryland.
The Department of Human Services oversees adult protective services aimed at protecting vulnerable adults from abuse, neglect, and exploitation.

The bill establishes provisions allowing state entities to petition circuit courts for injunctive relief and modifies statutory factors in criminal felony prosecutions concerning unlicensed assisted living programs.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits selling or offering essential goods or services designated by the Governor at prices 15% or more above pre-emergency levels. Prohibits charging 15% or more above average prices for emergency cleanup repair or reconstruction services during and 90 days post-emergency. Permits price increases directly attributable to increased supplier costs, labor, materials, or documented three-year seasonal pricing. Establishes violations as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices enforceable under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act civilly. Requires the Secretary of State to establish an electronic notification system for emergency declarations and covered goods. Requires the Office of the Attorney General to provide 20 days' advance notice before filing an enforcement action.
qa_results.responsible_party: Secretary of State; Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Consumers and businesses purchasing essential goods or services; merchants, retailers, and contractors selling essential goods, services, and emergency repair or reconstruction services during declared states of emergency
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $25,000 in FY 2024 for the Secretary of State to implement the electronic notification system, followed by minimal ongoing annual licensing costs. The Office of the Attorney General can enforce the bill using existing resources. The bill has no material fiscal effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 775 statutorily requires the Secretary of State to establish and maintain an electronic notification system for individuals to register and receive notices regarding declared states of emergency, price gouging protections, and covered essential goods and services, with an estimated fiscal impact of $25,000 in FY 2024.

The bill designates price gouging as an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice enforced by the Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division, and explicitly requires OAG to provide at least 20 days' pre-action notice to potential violators.

The bill's price protections are triggered by a state of emergency declared by the Governor and apply to specific categories of essential goods and services designated by the Governor via declaration or executive order.
The bill authorizes civil enforcement actions and private causes of action for damages under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which are adjudicated in the Maryland court system.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires each licensed cigarette wholesaler to submit complete and accurate quarterly information as the Comptroller requires. Expands the scope of required wholesaler reporting to facilitate compliance with Title 16. Authorizes the Comptroller to disclose reported information to the Attorney General and the Executive Director. Authorizes the Attorney General to impose a civil penalty up to $1,000 for each reporting violation. Treats each incomplete or inaccurate submission as a separate violation. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland; Maryland Office of the Attorney General; Alcohol and Tobacco Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed cigarette wholesalers in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State operations or finances, and it does not affect local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs reporting requirements submitted to the Comptroller's Office by licensed cigarette wholesalers, requiring complete and accurate disclosures in the form and manner prescribed by the Comptroller and permitting information sharing for enforcement.

The bill was requested by the Office of the Attorney General and authorizes the Comptroller to disclose wholesaler reporting data to the Attorney General to aid in enforcing compliance with state cigarette and tobacco laws.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes bicounty commissioners and applicants to the Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission from Montgomery County to submit financial statements electronically. Authorizes the Montgomery County Council, with County Executive approval, to discipline commissioners following written notice and a public hearing. Prohibits commissioners from Montgomery County from engaging in specified political campaign activities or seeking public office during their tenure. Prohibits former commissioners from representing clients for compensation on board matters for one year after leaving office. Requires commissioners from Montgomery County to complete designated ethics and planning training within three months after appointment. Prohibits the chair of the Montgomery County Planning Board from engaging in any other full-time employment while serving.
qa_results.responsible_party: Montgomery County Council; Montgomery County Executive; Montgomery County Planning Board; Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission; State Ethics Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Commissioners and applicants to the Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission from Montgomery County, former commissioners, and the chair of the Montgomery County Planning Board
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. The bill does not materially affect Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the General Provisions Article regarding financial disclosure filings for bicounty commissioners and applicants, requiring electronic filings to be made with the State Ethics Commission and requiring the Commission to promptly delete statements of unappointed applicants upon notification. It also mandates ethics training on Maryland Public Ethics Law for newly appointed commissioners.

The bill explicitly requires newly appointed commissioners from Montgomery County to successfully complete the Maryland Department of Planning's Planning Commissioner, Planning Board and Board of Appeals Education Course within the first three months of appointment.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a county or municipal corporation to request assignment of a tax sale certificate when a foreclosure action lacks timely prosecution. Requires the certificate holder to forfeit all rights and acquisition payments if the court grants the assignment motion. Permits a court to strike a foreclosure judgment and vest title in local government after 105 days of purchaser nonpayment. Authorizes local governments to withhold property from tax sale if they intend to demolish unsafe or uninhabitable vacant structures. Requires tax collectors to deliver a certificate of sale to the local governing body for each withheld property.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governing bodies of counties and municipal corporations; local tax collectors; Maryland Circuit Courts
qa_results.stakeholders: Counties and municipal corporations; holders of tax sale certificates; owners of tax-delinquent and blighted properties
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected. Local government finances face an indeterminate net impact depending on the costs to acquire, maintain, or demolish affected properties weighed against potential future tax collections or proceeds from subsequent property transfers.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies judicial procedures in tax sale foreclosure actions, requiring circuit courts to adjudicate motions to assign certificates of sale, issue show-cause orders to certificate holders, strike final judgments, and direct tax collectors regarding deed execution.

The bill relates to local government acquisition and demolition of vacant, unsafe, and blighted structures for redevelopment, which intersects with DHCD's community revitalization, blight elimination, and housing policies.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Equitech Growth Fund and the Equitech Growth Commission within the Maryland Technology Development Corporation. Requires the corporation to award financial assistance to public, nonprofit, or private entities for workforce development and infrastructure. Mandates an annual State budget appropriation of $5,000,000 for fund awards from fiscal year 2025 through 2033. Requires the commission to develop a comprehensive 10-year strategic plan for growing Maryland's innovation economy by July 1, 2025. Sunsets the provisions establishing the Equitech Growth Commission on June 30, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Technology Development Corporation
qa_results.stakeholders: Emerging and advanced industry businesses, workforce trainees, public and private entities, and institutions of higher education in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures increase by $3.0 million in FY 2024 and by $5.6 million annually from FY 2025 through 2033 to provide $5.0 million in mandated award funding and $0.6 million for administrative expenses. Special fund revenues and expenditures for the fund increase correspondingly. Local revenues and expenditures increase to the extent local entities, including community colleges, receive grants and provide matching funds.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: TEDCO is the primary implementing agency tasked with administering the Equitech Growth Fund, adopting program regulations, awarding financial assistance, staffing the Equitech Growth Commission, and submitting annual reports.

The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) is designated as an ex officio member of the Equitech Growth Commission, aligning with the department's role in statewide economic growth and business attraction.
The Secretary of Labor (or designee) serves as an ex officio member of the Equitech Growth Commission to help guide workforce development initiatives targeted by the fund.
The State Superintendent of Schools (or designee) serves as a member of the Equitech Growth Commission to advise on workforce pathways and education strategies for the innovation economy.
The Executive Director of MEDCO (or designee) is named as a statutory member of the Equitech Growth Commission to assist in strategic planning and infrastructure development.
The USM Chancellor (or designee) is a statutory member of the commission; USM institutions are also eligible recipients for financial assistance and workforce development awards from the fund.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a temporary state commission, the Equitech Growth Commission, tasked with developing a 10-year strategic plan for growing Maryland's innovation economy.

The Governor is responsible for appointing several members to the Equitech Growth Commission, is mandated to include specific appropriations in the annual budget bill, and receives reports and strategic plans required by the bill.
DBM oversees the state budget execution, which includes the mandated general fund appropriation of $5.0 million annually from FY 2025 through FY 2033 for the fund.
The State Treasurer is required to hold the newly created Equitech Growth Fund separately as a special, nonlapsing fund.
The Comptroller is required to account for the newly established Equitech Growth Fund.

Morgan State University is explicitly identified in the statute as one of the eligible HBCUs from which the Governor may appoint an institutional president to serve on the Commission, and is also an eligible recipient of fund awards.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date of the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission minority business enterprise utilization program to July 1, 2028. Merges the separate minority business enterprise programs for construction contracts and goods and services into a single program. Adopts the State definition of minority business enterprise under the State Finance and Procurement Article. Standardizes certification requirements by requiring alternative certification programs to substantially duplicate State standards. Requires prime contractors to submit monthly compliance reports and give advance notice before terminating certified subcontractors. Repeals county-specific geographic participation targets and the sheltered market program.
qa_results.responsible_party: Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission; Office of Supplier Diversity and Inclusion
