qa_results.stakeholders: Minority- and women-owned business enterprises; prime contractors bidding on Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission procurements; Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State finances. The bill has no material fiscal effect on Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission finances, as the commission can continue operating its existing minority business enterprise program within existing resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill aligns the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission's (WSSC) Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) definition, standards, and criteria directly with the State's MBE program under Title 14, Subtitle 3 of the State Finance and Procurement Article, which is monitored and coordinated by the Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs.

The Maryland Department of Transportation acts as the State's official MBE certification agency under § 14-303(b) of the State Finance and Procurement Article. Under the bill, WSSC's MBE program directly incorporates and recognizes MDOT's certifications and certification standards.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Class B and specified Class C licensees in Prince George's County to sell beverages by the glass or bottle. Establishes a statutory framework for inspections of licensed premises conducted by or on behalf of the county licensing board. Requires inspectors to deliver an inspection report to the license holder and the board within five business days. Requires the board to establish a standard fine structure and publish annual inspection totals and penalty schedules online. Establishes a workgroup to study safe event promotion practices and report recommendations by December 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Prince George's County
qa_results.stakeholders: Holders of Class B and Class C beer, wine, and liquor licenses, licensed premises operators, and event promoters in Prince George's County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal impact. The bill is not anticipated to materially affect Prince George's County revenues, and the county can handle inspection reporting, standard fine structure implementation, and workgroup staffing with existing budgeted resources. Specific dollar figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Workgroup to Study Best Practices for Safe Event Promotion and the Leveraging of Alcoholic Beverages Licenses in Prince George's County to study event promotion and local alcohol licensing practices and report findings to local and state officials.

The bill explicitly references written reports of violations forwarded by uniformed officers of the State Police as a basis for the Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners to inspect licensed premises and take appropriate action.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to establish a step therapy exception process. Mandates granting an exception request under specified clinical circumstances, including contraindication, expected ineffectiveness, or prior patient stability. Prohibits carriers and pharmacy benefits managers from requiring multiple prior authorizations for different dosages of the same drug. Excludes non-partial-agonist opioids from the single prior authorization restriction. Requires private review agents to decide electronic authorization requests in real time or within one business day.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Insured individuals and enrollees with prescription drug coverage; health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations; pharmacy benefits managers; health care prescribers; private review agents
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration in FY 2024 from $125 rate and form filing fees. Indeterminate but potentially significant cost increase for the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program due to reduced step therapy utilization. No material fiscal impact on local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates health insurance carriers, nonprofit health service plans, HMOs, and private review agents in Maryland. It is responsible for reviewing policy and contract form filings for compliance with the bill's new step therapy and prior authorization requirements and collects associated filing fees.

The Department of Budget and Management administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program. The program provides prescription drug coverage through a pharmacy benefits manager (PBM) that is subject to the bill's mandates, potentially leading to significant fiscal impacts on state health benefit expenditures.

The Maryland Health Benefit Exchange operates the state's health insurance marketplace, where qualified health plans issued by commercial carriers must adhere to Maryland insurance laws, including step therapy and prior authorization protocols.

The Department of Health oversees public health policy and healthcare financing, and was consulted for the bill's fiscal note; however, Medicaid managed care organizations are explicitly exempt from the prior authorization provisions in § 15-854.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes paid emergency medical technicians employed by participating governmental units to participate in the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System. Excludes volunteer emergency medical technicians from membership. Allows an eligible governmental unit's legislative body to approve participation if at least 60% of technicians petition. Grants members credit for employment with the participating governmental unit before the effective date of participation. Transfers qualifying local plan or State system assets and accumulated contributions to the pension system upon participation.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System
qa_results.stakeholders: paid emergency medical technicians and participating governmental units, including counties and municipal corporations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Local expenditures may increase for eligible governmental units that elect to participate in the pension system, with all costs borne by the participating local government.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency operates and manages the State Retirement and Pension System, including the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System (LEOPS). This bill expands LEOPS eligibility to paid emergency medical technicians employed by participating governmental units and requires the Board of Trustees and the agency to process elections, transfer credits/contributions, and administer benefits.

qa_results.bill_summary: Mandates membership in the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System if the Frostburg City Police Department becomes a participant. Applies to permanent full-time officers employed before, through, or after the department's effective participation date. Grants eligibility and creditable service for prior employment with the department upon joining the system. Terminates an officer's membership and benefit rights in the Employees' Pension System upon transfer. Exempts transferring officers from paying member contribution rate differences under Title 37.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Retirement Agency; Frostburg City Police Department
qa_results.stakeholders: Permanent full-time local law enforcement officers of the Frostburg City Police Department and the City of Frostburg
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Contingent on the City of Frostburg joining the system, local employer pension contributions increase by approximately $130,300 annually due to higher contribution rates net of an amortized new entrant credit. No impact on local revenues or other participating governmental units.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System, including the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System (LEOPS) and the Employees' Pension System (EPS). This bill directly governs the transfer of service credit, member accounts, and asset liabilities between EPS and LEOPS if the Frostburg City Police Department joins LEOPS as a participating governmental unit.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Baltimore Regional Transit Commission to provide input and engage in advocacy for Baltimore region public transit systems. Directs the Baltimore Metropolitan Council to provide staff for the Commission. Requires the Maryland Transit Administration to allocate operational funding for one senior planner and two junior planner positions. Requires the Commission to review and comment on regional budget requests, service changes, and capital needs reports. Mandates that the Commission review and approve any update to the Central Maryland Regional Transit Plan. Requires annual reporting of findings and recommendations to the Maryland Transit Administration, the Governor, and the General Assembly.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore Regional Transit Commission; Maryland Transit Administration; Baltimore Metropolitan Council
qa_results.stakeholders: Transit riders, business communities, and transit labor union employees in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Anne Arundel County, and Howard County, as well as the Maryland Transit Administration.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund expenditures increase by $431,300 in FY 2024 and by $575,000 annually thereafter to fund three planner positions at the Baltimore Metropolitan Council. Local governments can participate using existing resources. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Baltimore Regional Transit Commission specifically to oversee, review, and comment on MTA transit operations, budgets, and plans in the Baltimore region. In addition, MTA is required to directly fund the commission's operational and staffing expenses via the Transportation Trust Fund.

MDOT is the parent department of MTA, and the Secretary of Transportation (or designee) serves as an ex officio member with tie-breaking voting authority. The commission also reviews Consolidated Transportation Program priorities and utilizes Transportation Trust Fund expenditures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally creates a new regional transit oversight and advisory body, the Baltimore Regional Transit Commission, within state law.
The Governor is responsible for appointing seven members across four jurisdictions to the newly created commission and receives an annual report of the commission's findings and recommendations.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments to state boards and commissions, which includes the seven gubernatorial seats on the newly established commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters collective bargaining agreement implementation rules for Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission employees. Subjects agreement terms with fiscal impacts, required appropriations, or required regulation adoptions to county council approval. Requires approval by both the Montgomery County Council and the Prince George's County Council. Authorizes either party to request mediator-arbitrator services during the term of an existing agreement. Establishes dispute resolution procedures and requires the mediator-arbitrator to select the more reasonable final offer. Requires the Commission and the employee organization to share mediator-arbitrator costs equally.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission; Montgomery County Council; Prince George's County Council
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission employees and certified employee organizations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State effect. Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission expenditures increase, likely minimally, beginning in fiscal 2024 to pay for half of mediator-arbitrator services. Local revenues are unaffected.

qa_results.bill_summary: Subjects 25% of a debtor's net recovery on a workers' compensation claim to execution on child support arrearage judgments. Applies this execution standard to workers' compensation indemnity benefits, including weekly benefits or settlement proceeds. Defines net recovery after deducting attorney's fees, expenses, medical bills, and satisfaction of liens or subrogation claims. Includes liens or subrogation claims arising under a workers' compensation insurance plan in the net recovery calculation. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Judiciary; Child Support Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: parents owed child support arrearages, individuals owing child support arrearages who receive workers' compensation benefits, and workers' compensation insurers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Human Services oversees the Child Support Administration, which enforces child support orders and collects arrearages. This bill allows up to 25% of net recovery from workers' compensation indemnity benefits to be subject to execution for child support arrearages.

The bill alters statutory exemptions from execution on a judgment within the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article, affecting garnishment and enforcement proceedings overseen by the Maryland court system.
The Commission adjudicates workers' compensation claims and oversees awards and settlements, which are directly subject to the execution for child support arrearages under this legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits institutions of higher education from contracting with a regulated gaming entity or its agent under certain compensation terms. Bars contracts if the institution receives commissions, bonuses, or incentive payments for securing student wagering participation. Prohibits institutions from contracting with sports marketing entities if either entity receives incentives for student wagering. Permits other contracts between institutions of higher education and regulated gaming entities or sports marketing entities. Subjects permitted contracts formed by public institutions of higher education to inspection under the Maryland Public Information Act. Protects existing obligations and contract rights from impairment under the Act.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Public Institutions of Higher Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland institutions of higher education, college students, regulated gaming entities, and sports marketing entities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The bill does not affect gaming revenues or expenditures in the State and does not affect State funding of institutions of higher education.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly restricts public institutions of higher education, including USM constituent universities, from entering into certain sports wagering contracts or promotional partnerships that incentivize student betting, and subjects permissible contracts to the Maryland Public Information Act.

As an independent public institution of higher education, Morgan State University is directly prohibited from entering into sports wagering incentive contracts and must make allowable contracts available under the Maryland Public Information Act.

As a public institution of higher education, St. Mary's College of Maryland is directly subject to the prohibition against entering into contracts with gaming or marketing entities that provide compensation based on student sports wagering participation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency licenses and regulates the mobile sports wagering licensees, sports wagering licensees, and online sports wagering operators defined and affected by the contracting prohibitions in this bill.

MHEC is the coordinating board responsible for postsecondary education policy and governance across Maryland's public, private nonprofit, and for-profit institutions of higher education, all of which fall under the scope of this legislation.

As the state's regulatory and coordinating body for public and private postsecondary institutions, the commission oversees policy compliance for institutions impacted by the prohibition on sports wagering contracts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the calculation and remittance process for administrative fees paid to the State Retirement and Pension System. Defines administrative fees as actual operating expenses incurred as of June 30 of the second prior fiscal year. Requires the Board of Trustees to certify the payable amount to each local employer by October 1. Directs local employers to pay 25 percent of the certified amount across four quarterly dates each year. Requires reimbursement of administrative fees to system accumulation funds on or before June 30 each year.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System; State Retirement Agency
qa_results.stakeholders: Participating employers in the State Retirement and Pension System, including State agencies, local school boards, community colleges, and participating governmental units
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Largely procedural in nature with no material effect on State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the funding of administrative and operational expenses for the State Retirement Agency and the Board of Trustees of the State Retirement and Pension System, altering the timing and formula used to calculate and collect administrative fees.

The Board of Trustees must certify membership percentages and provide official notice of local employer fee estimates and certifications to the Secretary of Budget and Management for state budget integration.

The Comptroller is statutorily directed to execute the right of setoff against funds owed to local participating employers if they become delinquent in remitting their required administrative fees to the retirement system.

The bill mandates that the Governor include in the annual budget bill an appropriation to the accumulation funds of the State Retirement and Pension System equal to the authorized administrative fees.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters amortization periods for certain unfunded liabilities and surpluses of the State Retirement and Pension System. Continues amortizing existing liabilities or surpluses accrued as of June 30, 2023, until June 30, 2039. Amortizes annual experience gains and losses over 15 years and actuarial assumption changes over 25 years. Amortizes new legislation effects over 10 to 15 years and early retirement incentives over five years. Authorizes the Board of Trustees to adjust amortization periods to mitigate tail volatility in contribution rates. Prohibits the Board from certifying contribution rates below the actuary-determined normal cost.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Trustees of the State Retirement and Pension System
qa_results.stakeholders: Members, retirees, and participating employers of the State Retirement and Pension System, and Maryland State government employees
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in State pension liabilities beginning in fiscal 2024, but not expected to have a discernible effect on State pension contributions. No effect on revenues or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency directly administers the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS). The bill directly modifies how the SRPS Board of Trustees calculates amortization periods for unfunded liabilities and surpluses, sets contribution rates, and works with the system's actuary.

The Department of Budget and Management oversees the state budget, fiscal planning, and state employee benefits. Adjustments to the amortization schedule and contribution rate volatility for the State Retirement and Pension System impact long-term state pension funding obligations within the executive budget.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes an autonomous vehicle converter to sell, transfer, lease, offer for sale, or resell a converted autonomous vehicle. Authorizes the converter to take the same actions for vehicles purchased with the intent to convert them. Restricts these authorizations solely to motor vehicles intended for commercial or industrial use. Excludes autonomous vehicle converters from statutory definitions of vehicle dealers, distributors, factory branches, and manufacturers. Prohibits an autonomous vehicle converter from being licensed as a manufacturer, distributor, factory branch, or dealer.
qa_results.responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: autonomous vehicle converters and commercial or industrial motor vehicle operators
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State operations or finances and does not directly affect local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) regulates automotive businesses, including motor vehicle dealers, manufacturers, distributors, and factory branches under Title 15 of the Transportation Article. HB 806 explicitly excludes autonomous vehicle converters from these licensing categories and permits them to sell, lease, and transfer converted autonomous vehicles without obtaining dealer or manufacturer licenses from the MVA.

The Maryland Department of Transportation oversees the state's transportation network and houses the Motor Vehicle Administration, which administers vehicle laws under the Transportation Article amended by this bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Protects individuals and health care practitioners from out-of-state legal actions and investigations relating to legally protected health care. Prohibits judges from compelling witness testimony or evidence and issuing wiretap orders for out-of-state investigations of lawful reproductive care. Bars the Governor from surrendering individuals under out-of-state extradition demands for lawful reproductive health care activities. Forbids State and local agencies from expending resources or assisting interstate investigations into legally protected health care. Prohibits health occupations boards and medical liability insurers from taking disciplinary or adverse actions against practitioners providing protected care. Exempts high-deductible health plans from abortion coverage mandates if excluded from federal preventive care safe harbor rules.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; Health Occupations Boards; Maryland Insurance Administration; Governor of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Health care practitioners providing reproductive health services, patients receiving reproductive health care, medical professional liability insurers, State and local government employees, and individuals facing out-of-state investigations regarding reproductive health care.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material fiscal impact. The Department of Legislative Services determined that the bill's provisions are procedural in nature and will not materially affect State or local governmental operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly restricts the Governor's authority under the Uniform Criminal Extradition Act, prohibiting the surrender of any individual demanded by another state if the alleged violation relates to providing, procuring, or aiding in legally protected reproductive health care that is lawful in Maryland.

The bill establishes statutory restrictions and procedures for Maryland courts, prohibiting judges from compelling witness attendance in out-of-state prosecutions, barring ex parte wiretap orders for reproductive health investigations, requiring sworn statements for foreign subpoenas, and restricting the filing of foreign judgments.

The bill directly prohibits health occupations boards (which operate under and in coordination with the Department of Health) from revoking, suspending, or taking adverse disciplinary actions against licensed health care practitioners for providing legally protected reproductive health care.

The bill tasks the Insurance Commissioner with making determinations regarding high-deductible plan safe harbor exemptions under the Internal Revenue Code and prohibits medical professional liability insurers from taking adverse actions against health care practitioners providing legally protected health care.

As the State's central personnel agency, DBM oversees state employee policies and personnel administration, directly aligning with the bill's enactment of § 2-312 of the State Personnel and Pensions Article prohibiting State employees and agencies from expending time, money, or resources on interstate investigations of legally protected health care.

The Secretary of State processes extraditions on behalf of the Governor, an administrative function directly affected by the bill's prohibition on extraditing individuals facing out-of-state charges relating to legally protected health care.

The bill limits the Attorney General's ability to seek ex parte wiretap and electronic surveillance orders relating to legally protected health care and involves legal defense guidance for state agencies regarding interstate subpoenas and investigations.

The bill specifically limits the State Prosecutor's authority to apply for ex parte wiretap and electronic communication interception orders when investigating matters related to legally protected health care.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date for the State Minority Business Enterprise Program to July 1, 2025. Continues Minority Business Enterprise participation requirements for offshore wind projects and video lottery terminal operations through July 1, 2025. Postpones the submission deadline for the comprehensive disparity study and related analyses to late 2024. Extends the deadline for establishing capital project minority business enterprise policies and guidelines to July 1, 2025. Requires reports on brokerage and investment management services and capital project subgoals by December 31, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs; Maryland Department of Transportation; Board of Public Works; Office of the Attorney General; Public Service Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Certified minority business enterprises; State procurement prime contractors and subcontractors; offshore wind project applicants; video lottery facility applicants and licensees
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State or local finances. Extending due dates for the disparity study, related analyses, and program termination dates does not affect the total cost of the studies.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOSBA is directly responsible for administering the MBE program, establishing implementation guidelines, and completing multiple required reports and studies regarding MBE subgoals, disparity analyses, and race/gender-neutral approaches.

MDOT serves as the State's official MBE certification agency and is required to conduct and submit the disparity study and related analyses for offshore wind projects and P3s under the extended deadlines.

The bill mandates that the MBE certification agency and GOSBA consult with the Attorney General when analyzing disparity studies, establishing implementation policies and guidelines, and evaluating constitutional compliance.
The Board designates the state certification agency, adopts regulations regarding data collection for disparity studies, and oversees MBE goal requirements for public-private partnerships.
The bill extends the statutory termination date for MBE participation requirements and progress reporting associated with offshore wind energy projects approved by the PSC.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters and extends the termination date for statutory MBE participation goals applied to video lottery terminal licensees and facility operations.
As the State's central procurement authority, DGS is directly impacted by the one-year extension of the statutory MBE program across state contracts.

The bill extends the reporting deadline for the study evaluating MBE participation and race/gender-neutral approaches in brokerage and investment management services used by the State Retirement and Pension System.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires hospitals to include fentanyl testing whenever conducting a diagnostic urine drug screening on an individual. Mandates that hospitals report deidentified positive fentanyl test results to the Maryland Department of Health. Directs hospitals to submit these reports through the State-designated health information exchange. Exempts any hospital that does not have chemical analyzer equipment. Preserves existing statutory civil and criminal immunity for individuals seeking or receiving emergency medical assistance. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland hospitals, hospital patients undergoing diagnostic urine drug screening, and individuals experiencing or reporting drug overdoses
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local governmental operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires hospitals that detect fentanyl during urine drug screenings to report deidentified test results to the Maryland Department of Health through the State-designated health information exchange.

The Commission oversees and designated the Chesapeake Regional Information System for Our Patients (CRISP) as Maryland's State-designated health information exchange, which is the platform mandated by the bill for reporting positive fentanyl test results.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits health information exchanges and electronic health networks from disclosing mifepristone data and sensitive health service codes without authorization. Restricts disclosures of abortion care records except for claims adjudication or with specific written patient consent. Establishes the Protected Health Care Commission to recommend sensitive health services designated as legally protected health care. Requires the Maryland Health Care Commission to adopt regulations shielding patient data related to legally protected health care. Shields identifying information of ambulatory surgical and abortion facilities and investigated licensees under the Public Information Act. Clarifies that health insurers providing labor and delivery coverage must cover abortion care services without cost-sharing.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Health Care Commission; Maryland Department of Health; Secretary of Health; Protected Health Care Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Patients seeking abortion and reproductive health services, licensed health care providers, health information exchanges, electronic health networks, and health insurers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Maryland Health Care Commission special fund expenditures increase by $100,000 in fiscal 2024 only for contractual services to develop confidentiality policies and standards. General fund fine revenues and local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 812 directly expands the purpose of MHCC to establish policies and standards protecting the confidentiality of legally protected health care information. MHCC is required to adopt emergency regulations restricting data exchange through health information exchanges and electronic health networks, and to submit quarterly implementation reports to legislative committees. The fiscal note also identifies a $100,000 expenditure in FY 2024 for MHCC contractual services.

The Secretary of Health is tasked with identifying and regulating procedure, diagnosis, medication, and related codes for legally protected health care, adopting emergency regulations, and responding to semiannual reports. In addition, the Department of Health is required to provide staff for the newly created Protected Health Care Commission.

The bill amends Insurance Article § 15-857 to clarify requirements for health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and HMOs offering labor and delivery coverage to cover abortion care services without cost-sharing notwithstanding grandfathered plan exceptions, subject to exemptions granted by the Insurance Commissioner.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally establishes the Protected Health Care Commission to advise and issue semiannual recommendations to the Secretary of Health regarding sensitive health services that should be classified as legally protected health care.
The Attorney General (or their designee) is designated as an ex officio statutory member of the newly established Protected Health Care Commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the State-Based Young Adult Health Insurance Subsidies Pilot Program through June 30, 2026. Authorizes the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange to designate funds providing up to $20,000,000 in annual subsidies. Requires the Exchange to establish subsidy eligibility and payment parameters for calendar years 2022 through 2025. Requires the Exchange, in consultation with the Maryland Insurance Administration, to study available subsidies and waiver options. Requires the Exchange to report its study findings and recommendations to legislative committees by December 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Health Benefit Exchange; Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Young adults in Maryland purchasing individual market health benefit plans
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Maryland Health Benefit Exchange Fund special fund expenditures increase by up to $10.0 million in FY 2024, up to $20.0 million in FY 2025, and up to $10.0 million in FY 2026 to fund subsidies. General fund revenues decrease only to the extent that unspent premium tax reversions are reduced. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHBE is the primary agency responsible for administering the State-Based Young Adult Health Insurance Subsidies Pilot Program. The bill extends the program's sunset date through FY 2026, authorizes up to $20 million annually in subsidies from the MHBE Fund, requires data tracking, and mandates that MHBE conduct a study and report on subsidy availability and the State's 1332 waiver.

The Maryland Insurance Commissioner and the Administration are statutorily consulted by MHBE in establishing subsidy eligibility and payment parameters, as well as in conducting the mandated study and report regarding federal and State health insurance subsidies and the 1332 waiver.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to cover recommended follow-up diagnostic imaging for lung cancer. Mandates coverage of diagnostic ultrasound, magnetic resonance imaging, computed tomography, and image-guided biopsy. Limits cost-sharing for lung cancer screening and diagnosis to amounts no greater than those for breast cancer screening. Permits high-deductible health plans to subject follow-up diagnostic lung imaging to plan deductibles. Directs the Maryland Department of Health to assess cancer screening outreach, education, and health disparities. Requires the department to establish an advisory stakeholder workgroup and report findings by January 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, health maintenance organizations, individuals recommended for lung cancer screening, and communities affected by cancer health disparities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $28,900 in fiscal 2024 only for contractual staff at the Maryland Department of Health to conduct the assessment and convene the workgroup. Minimal increase in special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration from form filing fees. Potential increase in local government expenditures to the extent insurance premiums rise for fully insured employee plans.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that MDH conduct an assessment on outreach, education, and health disparities in cancer screening, convene a stakeholder workgroup to provide recommendations, and report findings to the General Assembly, requiring additional general fund expenditures in FY 2024.

MIA regulates the commercial health insurance market in Maryland and is responsible for overseeing compliance with the new coverage mandates and cost-sharing limits for lung cancer screening, as well as reviewing policy form filings.

DBM administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, which may experience an indeterminate fiscal impact from the mandated coverage of follow-up lung cancer diagnostic imaging.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a cancer screening stakeholder workgroup convened by MDH to advise on cancer screening disparities and develop outreach recommendations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs to develop a scorecard evaluating State government units. Directs the scorecard to evaluate unit performance toward meeting statewide Minority Business Enterprise and Veteran-Owned Small Business Enterprise goals. Requires the Office to develop a grading scale as a weighted system reflecting each unit's contribution toward the goals. Mandates annual publication of each unit's achieved grades on the Office's website. Requires the Office to submit the published information to the General Assembly within 30 days of website publication.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs
qa_results.stakeholders: State procurement agencies and units of State government, certified Minority Business Enterprises, and Veteran-Owned Small Business Enterprises.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State agencies can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources, resulting in no net impact on state expenditures or revenues. Local governments experience no fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs to develop a scorecard and weighted grading scale evaluating State agencies on their MBE and VSBE participation goals, publish the grades annually on its website, and submit the results to the General Assembly.

The Governor's Office oversees executive branch operations, and the Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs is a coordinating office within the Executive Department responsible for statewide procurement equity initiatives.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Division of State Documents to make at least the 15 most recent Maryland Register issues searchable online. Directs promulgating units altering proposed regulations before publication to notify reviewing entities and follow specified withdrawal or certification procedures. Extends the review period after an administrative hold override notice from 30 days to 60 days. Requires the Department of Legislative Services to adopt procedures for submitting proposed regulations, emergency regulations, work plans, and evaluation reports. Mandates that the Administrator develop and maintain a comprehensive electronic filing and tracking system by October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Division of State Documents; Department of Legislative Services; Joint Committee on Administrative, Executive, and Legislative Review
qa_results.stakeholders: State agencies and units promulgating regulations; subscribers to the Maryland Register; members of the public seeking regulatory information
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $124,200 in FY 2024 and $122,700 in FY 2025 for DSD contractual staff and operating support, with ongoing general fund spending of $39,000 annually. Special fund revenues and expenditures decrease by $29,300 in FY 2024 and $39,000 annually thereafter due to reduced Maryland Register subscriptions. Electronic filing system modifications could also create significant additional costs. Local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Division of State Documents (DSD), which is administratively housed within the Office of the Secretary of State, is directly responsible for administering the bill's provisions. DSD must make recent issues of the Maryland Register freely searchable online, develop and maintain a new electronic filing system (ELF 2.0) for regulations, and handle revised submission workflows, resulting in direct fiscal impacts from lost subscription revenues and additional operational expenditures.

The bill and fiscal analysis directly involve DoIT in consulting and collaborating with the Division of State Documents on the development, functionality, server hosting, and security of the electronic filing system (ELF 2.0) used by state units to submit and track regulations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters qualifications, disqualifiers, and application fees for possessing regulated firearms and obtaining handgun carry permits. Increases the maximum incarceration penalty from 3 to 5 years for first-time handgun carry violations. Raises the minimum age to obtain a handgun permit to 21 years old, with military exceptions. Increases maximum permit fees to $125 for initial applications and $75 for renewals. Requires the Secretary of State Police to regularly review active permit holders and revoke noncompliant permits. Directs the Department of State Police to email summaries of statutory firearms changes to firearm registrants.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of State Police; State Commission on Criminal Sentencing Policy; Office of Administrative Hearings; Maryland Department of Health; Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: handgun wear, carry, and transport permit applicants and holders; regulated firearm owners; State-certified firearms instructors; individuals convicted of specified criminal violations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues increase by an estimated $5,294,200 in FY 2024 from increased permit application and renewal fees. General fund expenditures increase by at least $2,402,200 in FY 2024 to support 26 positions at the Department of State Police and one position at the State Commission on Criminal Sentencing Policy. Incarceration costs for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services and local detention centers increase minimally due to longer sentences.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of State Police is the primary implementing agency responsible for regulating handgun wear, carry, and transport permits. The bill alters permit qualifications, fee structures, revocation procedures, and mandates regular review of active permit holders, curriculum development, email notifications, and annual reporting.

OAH is statutorily designated to conduct de novo administrative hearings for individuals appealing handgun permit denials, renewals, revocations, or limitations, issue written findings of fact and decisions within 90 days, and submit annual statistical reports to the Governor and General Assembly.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS maintains the Criminal Justice Information System (CJIS) Central Repository required to be regularly reviewed for active permit holder qualifications, and its correctional facilities may experience a fiscal impact due to increased maximum incarceration penalties for certain firearm violations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Commission on Criminal Sentencing Policy (MSCCSP) is explicitly mandated by the bill to produce an annual report disaggregated by jurisdiction, race, and gender on charges, convictions, and sentences, requiring an additional researcher position and ongoing operational funds.
OAG is statutorily required to consult with the Secretary of State Police in the development, publication, update, and distribution of the classroom curriculum for firearms training courses.
MDH is statutorily required to consult with the Secretary of State Police in developing training curriculum topics, specifically suicide prevention, conflict de-escalation, and anger management.

The Maryland Judiciary is affected by judicial appeals arising from OAH decisions regarding handgun permits and the adjudication and sentencing of expanded firearm possession prohibitions and increased penalties.
The Governor is designated as a recipient of mandatory annual reports from the Maryland State Police, the Office of Administrative Hearings, and the State Commission on Criminal Sentencing Policy.

qa_results.bill_summary: Grants the Town of Forest Heights urban renewal powers for blight clearance in areas zoned for commercial use. Requires the municipal legislative body to adopt a resolution defining the blighted area before initiating any project. Authorizes the municipality to acquire property through eminent domain with just compensation and transfer property to private persons. Authorizes the town to levy taxes, make appropriations, and issue general obligation bonds and revenue bonds. Permits the town to establish a separate public body or agency to carry out urban renewal activities.
qa_results.responsible_party: Town of Forest Heights
qa_results.stakeholders: Commercial property owners, businesses, and redevelopers in blighted commercial areas in the Town of Forest Heights
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State tax revenues may experience a minimal increase with no effect on expenditures. Town of Forest Heights expenditures may increase for land acquisition, legal fees, and urban renewal projects, potentially offset by revenues from property sales and expanded municipal and county tax bases.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHCD is responsible for community revitalization and redevelopment initiatives across Maryland communities. While the bill directly grants urban renewal and blight clearance authority to the Town of Forest Heights, DHCD coordinates and supports local revitalization efforts and served as an information source for the bill's fiscal analysis.

MDP provides technical assistance, data analysis, and guidance to local governments regarding comprehensive land use planning and sustainable redevelopment. The bill requires urban renewal plans to conform substantially to municipal master planning, and MDP served as an information source for the legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Prince George's Gateway Development Authority in Prince George's County. Requires the Authority to support the development and approval of a comprehensive neighborhood revitalization plan for six target municipalities. Authorizes the Authority to manage appropriated funds from target municipalities, Prince George's County, and the State. Authorizes the Authority to receive donated consultant services and manage staff and consultants. Requires the Authority to report its revitalization strategy to the Governor and designated legislative committees by October 31, 2025. Abrogates the Act after September 30, 2028.
qa_results.responsible_party: Prince George's Gateway Development Authority
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents, businesses, and local governments in the Prince George's County target area, including the City of Mount Rainier, Town of Brentwood, Town of Cottage City, City of Bladensburg, Town of Colmar Manor, and Town of North Brentwood.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No direct State or local fiscal effect. State and local authority members are assumed to provide staffing and expense reimbursements within existing resources. The bill authorizes the Authority to manage appropriated funds from the State, Prince George's County, and municipalities, but does not mandate any appropriations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) serves as a statutory member of the newly established Prince George's Gateway Development Authority under the Economic Development Article.

The Secretary of Housing and Community Development (or designee) is designated as an ex-officio member of the Authority, which is tasked with creating a comprehensive neighborhood revitalization and housing plan.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Prince George's Gateway Development Authority, a temporary statutory authority charged with formulating a neighborhood revitalization strategy and reporting to state leadership before sunsetting in 2028.
The Authority is statutorily required to submit its comprehensive neighborhood revitalization strategy report to the Governor on or before October 31, 2025.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires new residential construction of single-family detached houses, duplexes, and townhouses to include electric vehicle charging infrastructure. Mandates that each new unit with a garage, carport, or driveway feature one EVSE-installed or EV-ready parking space. Authorizes counties and municipal corporations to require a greater number of electric vehicle parking spaces. Directs the Maryland Energy Administration to study the costs of electric vehicle parking at multifamily residential buildings. Requires the Administration, in consultation with the Department of the Environment, to report findings by December 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Energy Administration; Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: Residential home builders, purchasers of newly constructed single-family homes, duplexes, and townhouses, and county and municipal governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by up to $250,000 in FY 2024 only for the Maryland Energy Administration to hire a consultant for the required multifamily building study. State revenues are unaffected. Local governments can enforce the requirements using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MEA is tasked with conducting a comprehensive study on the costs, emissions impacts, and payment mechanisms associated with electric vehicle charging infrastructure at multifamily residential buildings, with a dedicated special fund expenditure of up to $250,000 to complete the required analysis and report.

MDE is statutorily required to consult with the Maryland Energy Administration on the required study to project the number of electric vehicles on Maryland roads from 2024 through 2050 under the Advanced Clean Cars II standards.

The Governor is a required recipient of the final study and policy recommendations regarding multifamily residential electric vehicle charging infrastructure submitted by the Maryland Energy Administration.

qa_results.bill_summary: Directs the Public Service Commission to expand the EV Pilot Program to new and existing multifamily dwellings in underserved communities. Requires the Commission to terminate this expansion on December 31, 2025. Requires electric companies operating public charging networks to maintain federal or Commission-approved uptime standards. Requires participating electric companies to maintain adequate staff to monitor, assess, and repair charging stations. Mandates quarterly submission of detailed charging station operational, uptime, and cost data to the Commission. Authorizes the Commission to impose civil penalties or take remedial action for uptime noncompliance.
qa_results.responsible_party: Public Service Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: electric companies operating public EV charging networks, electric vehicle owners, and residents of multifamily dwellings in underserved communities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material direct impact on state or local finances; the Public Service Commission can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. Electricity rates paid by all electric customers, including state and local governments, may experience a limited increase through utility cost recovery.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 834 directly mandates the Public Service Commission (PSC) to expand and oversee the EV Pilot Program for multifamily dwellings in underserved communities, establish and monitor charging station uptime and reporting requirements, evaluate utility compliance, and assess civil penalties or remedial actions for noncompliance.

The bill impacts utility rate recovery, service reliability, and electric vehicle charging program parameters before the Public Service Commission. The Office of the People's Counsel represents residential consumers in PSC proceedings concerning utility service quality, reliability, and the rate impacts associated with utility capital expenditures and pilot program costs.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Baltimore Regional Water Governance Task Force to study approaches to regional water and wastewater governance. Directs the task force to review prior utility business studies and evaluate alternative regional governance and financing models. Requires the task force to analyze fiscal implications, efficiencies, transition costs, and customer rate stability for each model. Mandates consultation with the Maryland Department of the Environment and the Maryland Environmental Service. Requires the task force to report its findings and legislative recommendations by January 30, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore Regional Water Governance Task Force; Mayor of Baltimore City; County Executive of Baltimore County; Maryland Department of the Environment; Maryland Environmental Service
qa_results.stakeholders: Water and wastewater customers, ratepayers, and local governments in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Anne Arundel County, Carroll County, Harford County, and Howard County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal local expenditure impact for Baltimore City and Baltimore County to provide task force staffing and member expense reimbursements, absorbable within existing resources. State consultation costs for the Maryland Department of the Environment and the Maryland Environmental Service are absorbable within existing budgeted resources. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly establishes the Baltimore Regional Water Governance Task Force as a temporary public body to study, assess, and make recommendations on water and wastewater governance models in the Baltimore region.
The bill statutorily requires the Task Force to consult with the Department of the Environment in developing its recommendations and final report concerning regional water and wastewater systems.
The bill statutorily requires the Task Force to consult with the Maryland Environmental Service in developing its recommendations and final report regarding water supply and wastewater governance.
The Governor is tasked with appointing two members to the Task Force and will receive the Task Force's final report and recommendations.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing the appointment of the two Task Force members designated to be appointed by the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of Housing and Community Development to establish and maintain a common ownership community website. Directs the website to provide information on the current rights and responsibilities of individuals living in common ownership communities. Requires the website to include a hyperlink to each local common ownership community program in Maryland. Mandates the annual posting of information and General Assembly website hyperlinks for relevant statewide legislation enacted in the prior session. Requires the department to post this legislative update on or before June 1 each year.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents and unit owners of condominiums, cooperative housing corporations, and homeowners associations, as well as local common ownership community programs
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $90,000 in FY 2024 to develop the website, with indeterminate annual increases in subsequent years for maintenance and updates. Local finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 844 directly requires the Department of Housing and Community Development to establish, host, and annually maintain a website providing information on the rights and responsibilities of individuals living in common ownership communities (COCs), resulting in an estimated fiscal impact of $90,000 in FY 2024 and ongoing maintenance costs.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Indirect Potable Reuse Pilot Program in the Maryland Department of the Environment. Authorizes the department to issue permits regulating reclaimed water use as a source for drinking water facilities. Requires the department to accept permit applications from July 1, 2023, through June 30, 2024. Mandates advanced treatment including reverse osmosis, ultraviolet disinfection, and storage in an environmental buffer for at least 180 days. Authorizes the department to renew qualifying potable reuse permits on or after July 1, 2028.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: public water systems, drinking water treatment facilities, local governments operating water utilities, and water treatment engineering contractors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $25,000 in FY 2023 and $139,900 in FY 2024 to hire two contractual regulatory and compliance engineers at the Maryland Department of the Environment, with ongoing costs through FY 2028. State revenues are unaffected because there is no permit fee. Participating local governments incur potential indeterminate cost increases to construct, upgrade, and operate treatment facilities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Indirect Potable Reuse Pilot Program within MDE. MDE is the primary implementing agency responsible for developing standards, reviewing and issuing potable reuse permits, conducting inspections, adopting regulations, and submitting a report on the program.

MDH's Laboratories Administration provides analytical support and water testing services for MDE, and the fiscal note notes potential workload and staffing impacts related to complex testing for PFAS and other contaminants under the pilot program.
The bill requires the Department of the Environment to submit a report to the Governor by December 31, 2024, regarding the status and recommendations for the pilot program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the timeframe for a person in interest to request corrections to autopsy findings and conclusions. Increases the filing window from 60 days to 180 days after the medical examiner files the report. Covers findings and conclusions regarding the cause and manner of death on a death certificate. Excludes autopsy findings that result in a determination of homicide. Maintains the right of a person in interest to appeal any denial to the Secretary of Health.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Chief Medical Examiner; Maryland Department of Health; Office of Administrative Hearings
qa_results.stakeholders: Persons in interest of a deceased individual (such as spouses, adult children, parents, adult siblings, grandparents, or legal guardians)
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures and revenues are not materially affected. The Maryland Department of Health and the Office of Administrative Hearings can absorb any minor increase in requests and hearings using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Chief Medical Examiner is a unit within the Maryland Department of Health (MDH). The bill directly modifies the timeline for persons of interest to request corrections to autopsy findings and conclusions from MDH's medical examiners and affects appeals directed to the Secretary of Health.

When the Chief Medical Examiner denies a request to correct cause and manner of death findings, appeals are referred to the Office of Administrative Hearings for a contested case hearing before an administrative law judge.
Decisions by the Secretary of Health that reject an administrative law judge's findings can be appealed to the circuit courts, which are supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Division of Rehabilitation Services and the Developmental Disabilities Administration to enter into a memorandum of understanding. Mandates that the agreement include data sharing of medical and psychological records for mutual clients. Specifies that the data sharing agreement must expedite decisions regarding eligibility for services. Defines covered records to include medical documentation, psychological information, school documentation, and other relevant information. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Division of Rehabilitation Services; Developmental Disabilities Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals with disabilities and developmental disabilities who are mutual clients of the Division of Rehabilitation Services and the Developmental Disabilities Administration
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State or local fiscal impact. The Maryland State Department of Education and the Maryland Department of Health can implement the data sharing memorandum of understanding using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS), a division within the Maryland State Department of Education, enter into a memorandum of understanding with the Developmental Disabilities Administration to share medical and psychological data of mutual clients.

The bill directly mandates that the Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA), a unit within the Maryland Department of Health, enter into a memorandum of understanding with the Division of Rehabilitation Services to share client records to expedite eligibility determinations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission to contract for utility services to certain Prince George's County border properties. Permits the District of Columbia or the District of Columbia Water and Sewer Authority to provide water and sewer services. Requires contracts to allocate maintenance costs, assign billing duties, and mandate master meters for multifamily housing units. Establishes usage-based service rate setting procedures and mandates specific customer notices, including potential higher service rates. Limits the ability of the Commission and the District entities to reduce customer services. Terminates all provisions five years after the enactment date.
qa_results.responsible_party: Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners, developers, and residents of qualifying border properties in Prince George's County; Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission; District of Columbia Water and Sewer Authority
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not materially affected. The bill does not materially affect Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT was consulted as an information source during the legislative review process, as the legislation specifically targets transit-oriented border properties located within one-half mile of mass transit rail stations and regional transit districts.

The bill explicitly references the requirement to assess fees under the Environment Article, specifically the Bay Restoration Fee administered by MDE, for customer accounts served under the cross-border water and sewer contracts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Environmental and Natural Resources Crimes Unit within the Office of the Attorney General. Charges the unit with investigating and prosecuting violations of State criminal environmental and natural resources laws. Authorizes the unit to prosecute any other criminal offense discovered during an investigation. Grants the unit the full powers, rights, privileges, and duties of a State's Attorney. Authorizes designated attorneys to issue subpoenas for specific records to further criminal investigations. Requires the Attorney General to report annually by November 30 on the unit's activities.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Persons subject to investigation or prosecution for State criminal environmental and natural resources violations, and small businesses in resource-based industries.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $566,200 in FY 2024 to fund four new positions, start-up costs, and operating expenses, rising to $796,000 by FY 2028. State general and special fund revenues, as well as local revenues, may increase beginning in FY 2024 from criminal penalties and restitution, but the exact increase is indeterminate.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly establishes the Environmental and Natural Resources Crimes Unit within the Office of the Attorney General to investigate and prosecute criminal violations of environmental and natural resources laws.

The new unit is tasked with prosecuting violations of State criminal environmental laws, and the Attorney General must report annually on actions taken by the Department of the Environment in response to findings and recommendations of the unit.

The unit investigates and prosecutes violations of criminal natural resources laws, and the Attorney General must report annually on actions taken by the Department of Natural Resources in response to findings and recommendations of the unit.

The bill requires the Attorney General to cooperate with the Secretary of Budget and Management to establish minimum salaries, qualifications, and training and experience standards for positions within the unit.
The unit is granted authority to issue subpoenas enforceable in State circuit courts and to exercise grand jury powers across counties.
The Attorney General is mandated to submit an annual report to the Governor detailing the unit's activities and any agency actions taken in response to its findings.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Baltimore City to honor certificates of guarantee issued by approved nonprofit contractor associations or their wholly owned subsidiaries. Permits contractors to use these certificates to satisfy county bond requirements for public improvements and other purposes. Clarifies that Baltimore City is not required under state insurance law to honor the certificates. Exempts these certificates of guarantee from the state Insurance Article. Takes effect June 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore City; Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Contractors bidding on or performing public improvements and construction in Baltimore City, nonprofit associations of contractors and their subsidiaries, and Baltimore City government
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The Maryland Insurance Administration can enforce the provisions with existing budgeted resources. Baltimore City finances are not affected because the authority to honor certificates of guarantee is permissive.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Insurance Article regarding certificates of guarantee. While these instruments are exempt from general insurance regulation, the Maryland Insurance Administration oversees the Insurance Article and can implement or enforce the provision within existing budgeted resources.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters requirements governing related event promoter's permits for Central Intercollegiate Athletic Association Tournament events in Baltimore City. Expands the definition of related events to include events selling tickets at the door or imposing cover charges. Reduces the permit application deadline from 90 days to 30 days before a scheduled event. Requires the Board of License Commissioners to act on permit applications within 7 days instead of 14 days. Bases permit fee tiers on location capacity determined by the Baltimore City Fire Marshal rather than anticipated attendance. Extends the termination date of the permit program by two years to June 30, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City; Baltimore City Fire Department, Fire Marshal; Alcohol and Tobacco Commission, Executive Director
qa_results.stakeholders: Related event promoters, participating alcoholic beverages license holders, and attendees of CIAA Basketball Tournament social events in Baltimore City
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact and is not anticipated to materially affect Baltimore City operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill updates the Alcoholic Beverages Article by striking an obsolete reference to the Comptroller's enforcement authority regarding State caterer's license violations and replacing it with the Executive Director of the Alcohol and Tobacco Commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City to issue specific alcoholic beverages licenses in the 40th district. Permits issuing a Class C beer, wine, and liquor license in the 3600 block of Hickory Avenue. Authorizes a Class A-7 license in the 1200 block of West North Avenue under specified conditions. Exempts this Class A-7 license from the distance restriction near a place of worship or school. Prohibits sales before 10 a.m. or after 10 p.m. between the 1000 and 3200 blocks of West North Avenue.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City
qa_results.stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license applicants and holders in Baltimore City's 40th legislative district, Penn North Community Association, and local consumers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Baltimore City revenues increase minimally beginning in fiscal 2024 from license application and renewal fees to the extent new licenses are issued. There is no state fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for regulating the state's alcohol industry. While the bill specifically authorizes local licensing actions administered by the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners and has no state fiscal impact, it relates to the broader statutory framework governing alcoholic beverage regulation in Maryland.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the St. Mary’s County Metropolitan Commission to obtain county approval before submitting loan applications backed by county credit. Exempts refinancing or refunding transactions with no additional debt liability from the county approval requirement. Mandates studies, public notices, and hearings for new water and sewerage facilities in the county. Authorizes the commission to pay in full or in part for moving structures that impede water or sewer projects. Exempts excess revenue from debt sales or transfers by the commission from state and local taxation.
qa_results.responsible_party: St. Mary's County Metropolitan Commission; Commissioners of St. Mary's County
qa_results.stakeholders: Property owners, residents, and public service corporations in St. Mary's County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. The bill does not materially affect St. Mary's County operations or finances, as the provisions primarily codify and streamline existing procedural practices.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 887 pertains to the expansion, extension, and financing of local public water supply and sewerage systems governed by the St. Mary's County Comprehensive Water and Sewerage Plan. While the bill strictly alters St. Mary's County public local laws with no state fiscal effect, MDE oversees statewide water and sewerage planning and regulations and served as an information source on the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters application requirements for the Homeowners' Property Tax Credit for qualified homeowners. Defines a qualified homeowner as an individual receiving gross income solely from Social Security, a pension, or an annuity. Requires qualified homeowners to submit the full application only in their first year and every third year thereafter. Authorizes qualified homeowners to submit an abbreviated certification instead of the full application in intervening years. Prohibits the Department from requiring additional proof of income from homeowners who submit the certification.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland homeowners applying for the Homeowners' Property Tax Credit whose gross income is derived solely from Social Security, a pension, or an annuity
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact, as the State Department of Assessments and Taxation can implement the altered application process with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board hears appeals regarding real property tax assessment matters, exemptions, and property tax credits administered by the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT). Changes to the application, eligibility, and certification processes for the Homeowners' Property Tax Credit under the bill may affect matters subject to appeal before the local boards.

The Maryland Tax Court serves as the highest administrative body reviewing appeals from final decisions of taxing authorities and the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board, including disputes concerning eligibility for state property tax credits.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes that a hernia caused as a result of repetitive trauma may be considered an occupational disease. Authorizes workers' compensation benefits for these repetitive trauma hernias under statutory standards governing occupational diseases. Requires claimants to demonstrate that the condition arose out of and in the course of employment. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Workers' Compensation Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Covered employees experiencing repetitive trauma hernias, employers, and workers' compensation insurers (including Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company)
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material fiscal impact on State or local government finances or operations, as repetitive trauma hernias are relatively rare and existing statutory burden-of-proof standards still apply.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Workers' Compensation Commission is the primary agency responsible for administering Maryland's Workers' Compensation Law and adjudicating claims. This bill directly amends the statutory requirements for compensable hernia claims, expanding coverage to include repetitive trauma as an occupational disease.

Operating as Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company, the agency is the state's largest workers' compensation insurer and acts as the third-party administrator handling claims for State of Maryland employees. It directly assesses and pays claims that may arise under this expanded hernia provision.

The Subsequent Injury Fund reviews and investigates workers' compensation claims involving pre-existing conditions that exacerbate an employee's disability and was consulted for the fiscal analysis of this bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a statutory framework governing the expiration and extension of alcoholic beverages licenses in Garrett County. Causes an inactive license to expire six months after closing operations unless an extension or transfer applies. Reduces the minimum room requirement for hotel and motel Class B licenses from 25 to 10 rooms. Authorizes gift basket permit holders to purchase alcoholic beverages from a wholesaler or a retail license holder. Authorizes holders of multiple day or multiple event licenses to hold another license of a different class. Expands authorized Sunday on-premises sales hours for specified licenses to begin at 6:00 a.m. instead of 10:00 a.m.
qa_results.responsible_party: Garrett County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license and permit holders, hotels, motels, clubs, and gift basket retailers in Garrett County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect, as the Judiciary can handle any workload increase within existing budgeted resources. Garrett County finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill includes provisions regarding judicial review of decisions by the Garrett County Board of License Commissioners and references circuit court actions. The fiscal note confirms that the Judiciary/Administrative Office of the Courts can handle any associated increase in workload using existing budgeted resources.

qa_results.bill_summary: Converts the Community Solar Energy Generating Systems Pilot Program into a permanent program. Requires newly constructed community solar systems to serve at least 40% of output to low- and moderate-income subscribers. Authorizes consolidated billing and limits residential subscription rates to the monetary value of the bill credit.
