The Maryland Center for School Safety is designated as a mandatory member of the newly established Commission on Hate Crime Response and Prevention.
The Maryland Commission on Civil Rights is statutorily designated to have a representative serve as a member of the Commission on Hate Crime Response and Prevention.

The Commission is required to report annually to the State Department of Education on policy recommendations to address hate crimes that occur in schools. Additionally, the Maryland Center for School Safety resides within MSDE.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally creates a new permanent state advisory and policy body, the Commission on Hate Crime Response and Prevention.

The bill designates a representative of the Maryland Coordination and Analysis Center (MCAC), which operates under the Maryland State Police as the state's intelligence fusion center, to serve as a commission member.
The bill creates a statutory mandate requiring the Governor to include funding in the annual state budget starting in fiscal 2025 to support the commission and staff.
DBM is responsible for state budget preparation and execution, and the bill establishes a mandated annual appropriation beginning in fiscal year 2025.

qa_results.bill_summary: Reduces maximum civil fines for smoking cannabis in a public place to $50 for first violations and $150 thereafter. Prohibits law enforcement officers from stopping or searching persons, vehicles, or vessels based solely on burnt or unburnt cannabis odor. Bars stops or searches based solely on personal use cannabis possession or nearby cash lacking distribution indicia. Limits vehicle and vessel searches during cannabis impairment investigations to readily accessible areas or those containing relevant evidence. Excludes evidence obtained in violation of these provisions, including consensual evidence, from admissibility in any trial or proceeding.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of State Police; Department of Natural Resources Police; Maryland Transportation Authority Police; Maryland Transit Administration Police; Judiciary of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Law enforcement officers, motor vehicle drivers, vessel operators, individuals possessing or using cannabis, criminal defendants, and prosecutors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal decrease in State general fund revenues and incarceration expenditures due to lowered public smoking fines and fewer arrests and convictions. Local revenues and detention expenditures also decrease minimally from fewer fine collections and reduced local jail commitments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police is directly governed by the bill's restrictions on initiating stops or searches based solely on the odor of cannabis, personal use possession, or the presence of cash, as well as the limitations on vehicle searches during impaired driving investigations.

The Judiciary and state courts are directly impacted by adjudicating suppression motions under the new statutory exclusionary rule, handling altered civil fine amounts for smoking cannabis in public, and managing associated court caseloads and fine revenues.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender represents indigent clients who will be directly affected by these search, seizure, and stop limitations, and its attorneys will litigate suppression issues under the bill's new evidentiary exclusion provisions.

The bill explicitly restricts searches of vessels and references violations under § 8-738 of the Natural Resources Article, directly affecting enforcement operations and vessel stops conducted by the Natural Resources Police.
The bill specifically references impaired driving under § 21-902 of the Transportation Article and governs search procedures during traffic stops conducted by MDOT modal law enforcement divisions.

The Maryland Transportation Authority operates its own sworn police force that conducts traffic stops and enforcement on state toll facilities and highways, directly subjecting its officers to the bill's stop and search limitations.

The Maryland Transit Administration maintains a sworn police force responsible for transit enforcement, directly impacting their procedures regarding pedestrian stops, vehicle searches, and enforcement of public smoking restrictions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill is anticipated to have a minimal fiscal impact on state incarceration expenditures by reducing the number of arrests, charges, and convictions leading to commitments in state correctional facilities.

The Office of the Attorney General represents the state in appellate litigation concerning Fourth Amendment questions, statutory search limitations, and evidentiary suppression disputes arising under this Act.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a nonrefundable State income tax credit for an individual or business entity that owns a restaurant in Maryland. Sets the credit amount equal to the first $500 of the purchase price of an automated external defibrillator. Limits the credit to restaurant locations with annual gross income of at least $400,000. Restricts the credit to one automated external defibrillator per location, claimable only once per location. Caps the credit at the lesser of $1,500 or State income tax liability per taxable year. Prohibits carrying over unused credit amounts to any other taxable year.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners of restaurants in Maryland with annual gross income of at least $400,000
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues decrease by an estimated $1.12 million in FY 2024, $1.40 million in FY 2025, and $281,000 in FY 2026 across the general fund, Higher Education Investment Fund, and Transportation Trust Fund. General fund expenditures for the Comptroller's Office increase by $63,000 in FY 2024 for tax system updates. Local highway user revenues decrease by an estimated $69,000 total from FY 2024 through FY 2026.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is responsible for administering the state's income tax system, implementing and processing the new automated external defibrillator (AED) tax credit, and updating tax forms and software systems, incurring $63,000 in implementation expenditures in FY 2024.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS oversees and regulates the Maryland Public Access AED Program, under which facilities must register AEDs, assign coordinators, and maintain equipment, providing key regulatory oversight and operational context for the AED acquisitions incentivized by this bill.

The bill's corporate income tax credits reduce distributions to the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF), resulting in special fund revenue losses and reductions in local highway user revenue grants administered through MDOT.

qa_results.bill_summary: Revises the governance, operations, and ethics requirements for the Prince George’s County Board of Education. Expands the voting rights of the student board member to include operating budgets and student discipline. Establishes annual retreats, self-evaluations, and professional development requirements for elected school board members. Mandates the county board retain legal counsel and cover defense costs for members acting without malice. Increases annual compensation for the board chair to $30,000 and elected members to $27,000 in 2026. Requires candidates for elected board seats to reside in their district for one year before the election.
qa_results.responsible_party: Prince George's County Board of Education; Prince George's County Public Schools; Maryland State Board of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Prince George's County Board of Education members and candidates, Prince George's County Public Schools students, and Prince George's County Public Schools
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal impact. Prince George’s County Board of Education expenditures increase by $48,400 in FY 2027 and $83,000 annually thereafter for member compensation increases, alongside an indeterminate expenditure increase beginning in FY 2024 for member legal defense fees.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the authority and procedures of the State Board of Education regarding the removal of Prince George's County Board of Education members, allowing the State Board to remove a member for specified causes without requiring gubernatorial approval.
The bill eliminates the requirement that the Governor approve the removal of a member of the Prince George's County Board of Education by the State Board of Education.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the severance tax on oysters caught on Maryland natural oyster bars from $1 to $2 per bushel. Raises the inspection tax on marketable out-of-state oyster shell shipments from 30 cents to $1 per bushel. Requires $1 of each $2 severance tax collected to be used by designated county oyster committees for oyster bar repletion. Repeals an obsolete allocation requirement that dedicated a prior tax increase to the oyster seed program. Clarifies tax payment obligations when licensed harvesters sell oysters directly to consumers in the State.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: licensed oyster harvesters and sellers, oyster buyers and receivers, out-of-state oyster shippers, and county oyster committees in 11 specified counties
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Fisheries Research and Development Fund increase by approximately $580,900 annually beginning in fiscal 2024 due to increased tax collections and repletion expenditures. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1084 directly impacts the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) as it increases the oyster inspection tax and severance tax, which are collected by DNR and credited to the Fisheries Research and Development Fund. The department oversees these funds to support natural oyster bar repletion alongside county oyster committees, generating an estimated $580,900 annually in special fund revenues and expenditures.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Department of Natural Resources to allow hunting of game birds and mammals on Sundays in Wicomico County. Applies this hunting authority to private property and designated public land from 30 minutes before sunrise until 10:30 a.m. Lifts the morning time restriction on specified Sundays during deer firearms and deer bow hunting seasons. Reduces the archery hunting safety zone in Wicomico County from 150 yards to 50 yards from occupied structures.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Hunters, archery hunters, property owners, and outdoor sports businesses in Wicomico County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 1087 directly authorizes the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) to allow and regulate hunting on Sundays on private property and designated public lands in Wicomico County, and oversees enforcement of hunting regulations and safety zones.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the property tax exemption for real property owned by nonprofit fire companies or rescue squads in Baltimore County. Specifies that the exemption applies only under certain exclusive use criteria. Requires the real property to be actually used exclusively for fire company or rescue squad purposes. Alternatively covers real property not used for any purpose that will be used exclusively for squad purposes in the future. Takes effect June 1, 2023, and applies to taxable years beginning after June 30, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation; Baltimore County
qa_results.stakeholders: Incorporated, nonprofit fire companies and rescue squads in Baltimore County, and Baltimore County government
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Annuity Bond Fund revenues and Baltimore County property tax revenues will not be significantly affected. State and local expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The board adjudicates appeals regarding real property tax assessments and exemptions, including disputes over eligibility for exemptions granted to nonprofit entities such as fire companies and rescue squads.
The Maryland Tax Court serves as the highest administrative body hearing appeals from Property Tax Assessment Appeals Boards concerning real property tax exemptions and assessments.
The Treasurer manages the Annuity Bond Fund, which receives state property tax revenue used for general obligation debt service and is referenced in the fiscal note regarding state revenue impacts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Prince George's County to establish business improvement districts and exempts the county from statewide district law. Lowers the parcel owner petition threshold for establishing or expanding a district from 80% to 51%. Permits condominium and cooperative housing corporations within a proposed district to petition to join. Establishes a district board of at least nine members, retaining local state legislators as nonvoting members. Requires the county to impose a district tax on nonexempt property owners to fund district operations. Mandates a review of each district's effectiveness and desirability by the county every three years.
qa_results.responsible_party: Prince George's County Government
qa_results.stakeholders: Commercial property owners, commercial tenants, residential property owners, condominium and cooperative housing corporations, and small businesses in Prince George's County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. Prince George's County expenditures may increase minimally to hold additional public hearings. Local revenues and expenditures will be affected depending on the number of districts established or expanded, though district administrative costs are recoverable through district taxes.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland serves as the state's chief tax and financial officer and was consulted as an information source on the fiscal note regarding tax provisions. However, the business improvement district tax authorized by the bill is collected and administered locally by Prince George's County, resulting in no direct state fiscal or administrative impact.

The bill amends the Economic Development Article to establish a framework for business improvement districts in Prince George's County aimed at promoting business and economic vitality. While relevant to the Department of Commerce's overarching economic development mission, the bill grants local authority directly to Prince George's County and does not assign regulatory or administrative duties to the department.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Baltimore County to honor certificates of guarantee issued on behalf of contractors for county bond requirements. Applies to instruments issued by an approved nonprofit contractor association or its wholly owned subsidiary. Permits contractors to use certificates to satisfy bond requirements for public improvements or other county requirements. Specifies that Baltimore County is not required to honor any certificate of guarantee. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore County; Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Baltimore County; contractors performing public works or improvements; nonprofit associations of contractors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal impact; the Maryland Insurance Administration can enforce the bill with existing budgeted resources. Baltimore County finances are expected to experience minimal impact because honoring the certificates is permissive rather than mandatory.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends Section 1-203 of the Insurance Article to allow Baltimore County to accept certificates of guarantee from contractor associations for county bond requirements. The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates insurance under this article and can handle oversight with existing resources.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a governing board for each library designated as a regional resource center. Reconstitutes the former board of advisors as a regional advisory council composed of member library system directors. Requires each governing board to appoint a center director, approve the annual budget, and determine center policies. Designates the Board of Trustees of the Washington County Free Library as the Western Maryland center governing board. Repeals requirements that a selected regional center be the strongest and most centrally located regional library.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Library Board; Maryland State Library Agency; State Librarian
qa_results.stakeholders: regional resource centers, participating public library systems, library trustees, regional library staff, and library patrons in Western Maryland, Southern Maryland, and the Eastern Shore
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State or local fiscal impact. Any expense reimbursements for governing board members are expected to be covered with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Library Agency (through the State Library Board and State Librarian) provides direct oversight, standards, and regulatory approval for regional resource centers, including approving center establishment, approving independent auditors, and receiving annual financial and operational reports.
The bill explicitly subjects the regional resource centers and their governing boards to audits by the Office of Legislative Audits regarding any State funds received.

The bill stipulates that any selection of location and plans for the erection of regional resource center buildings by a governing board is subject to the approval of the Governor, as well as the State Library Board.

The bill requires that the appointed director of a regional resource center must be eligible for certification as a professional library director by the State Superintendent of Schools under MSDE regulations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Locally Operated Transit System Grant Program administered by the Maryland Department of Transportation. Directs the program to provide funding to locally operated transit systems throughout the State. Authorizes transit systems to use grants for capital, operating, planning, and other eligible expenses determined by the department. Permits grant funds to be sourced from specified federal and State public transportation programs. Requires total program grants to exceed $107,997,575 adjusted for inflation beginning in fiscal year 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation
qa_results.stakeholders: locally operated transit systems in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal effect. The bill codifies an existing grant program within the Maryland Department of Transportation without affecting overall funding levels.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill statutorily establishes and requires the Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) to administer the Locally Operated Transit System Grant Program, determining eligible expenses and sourcing funds from designated federal and State transportation programs.

As the modal administration within MDOT responsible for directing funding and technical assistance to locally operated transit systems throughout Maryland, the MTA is directly involved in the operational execution of grants to local transit providers.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the governing body of Harford County to enact a local law setting membership and terms for its Advisory Plumbing Board. Repeals statutory requirements that the board consist of a physician, a plumber, and one other individual. Repeals the specific four-year term requirement previously mandated in state law. Retains the requirement that the county governing body appoint an Advisory Plumbing Board upon adopting a plumbing code.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governing Body of Harford County
qa_results.stakeholders: Members of the Harford County Advisory Plumbing Board and Harford County officials administering the county plumbing code
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The bill codifies current county appointment practices and does not affect Harford County finances.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to survey hospitals on operating room resource availability for dentist use. Directs both agencies to conduct a regional needs assessment for dental procedures that require anesthesia or moderate sedation. Requires both agencies to develop regional plans ensuring appropriate operating room space for Maryland Medical Assistance Program recipients. Mandates consultation with the Maryland Hospital Association and the Maryland Ambulatory Surgery Association during the assessment. Requires the agencies to submit a joint final report to specified legislative committees by December 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Health Care Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland Medical Assistance Program recipients, licensed dentists, anesthesiologists, acute care hospitals, and ambulatory surgery centers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Health Care Commission can complete the required survey, needs assessment, and regional plans using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1146 directly tasks the Maryland Department of Health with conducting a hospital survey on operating room availability for dentists, co-conducting a regional needs assessment for dental procedures requiring anesthesia, co-developing regional access plans for Medicaid recipients, and submitting a joint report to the General Assembly.

HB 1146 directly mandates that the Maryland Health Care Commission jointly conduct a regional needs assessment regarding dental procedures requiring anesthesia or sedation, jointly develop regional plans to ensure operating room space for Medicaid recipients, and jointly report findings to legislative committees.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access to recommend improvements across the behavioral health continuum. Creates a three-year value-based purchasing pilot program in the Maryland Department of Health for intensive care coordination. Mandates a $600,000 annual state appropriation for the pilot program in fiscal years 2025 through 2027. Extends telehealth payment parity and coverage for audio-only telephone conversations through June 30, 2025. Directs the Maryland Department of Health to apply for federal planning grants and certified community behavioral health clinic demonstration programs. Requires the Maryland Health Care Commission to study telehealth delivery and payment parity by December 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Health Care Commission; Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals with behavioral health conditions, specialty behavioral health care providers, Medicaid recipients, health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $397,700 in FY 2024 for contractual staff and consultant costs, and by roughly $723,300 to $734,300 annually from FY 2025 through FY 2027, reflecting a mandated $600,000 annual appropriation for the pilot program and ongoing staffing. Continued telehealth coverage has an indeterminate impact on overall Medicaid expenditures. Local health benefit expenditures may increase minimally to maintain telehealth reimbursement parity.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is the primary implementing agency for the bill; it is required to staff the new Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access, administer the Behavioral Health Care Coordination Value-Based Purchasing Pilot Program, apply for federal CCBHC planning grants and demonstration programs, and maintain extended Medicaid telehealth coverage and payment parity.

The bill explicitly mandates MHCC to conduct an in-depth study and submit recommendations to the General Assembly regarding telehealth delivery and payment parity across audio-only and audiovisual services. MHCC's Executive Director is also a designated member of the newly formed commission.

The Maryland Insurance Commissioner is a designated member of the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access, and MIA oversees commercial health insurers complying with the two-year extension of telehealth requirements and payment parity.

The Governor is required to jointly designate the chair of the new commission, appoint numerous stakeholder members, mandate an annual budget appropriation of $600,000 for the pilot program for FY 2025–2027, and receive annual reports from the commission and MDH.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally creates a significant new state body—the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access—along with four mandated specialized workgroups to develop long-term statewide behavioral health strategies.

The Executive Director of HSCRC is designated as an ex officio member of the commission, and the bill references HSCRC's rate-setting authority in relation to hospital facility fees for telehealth services.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Executive Director of the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy (identified in statute as Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services) is named as a member of the commission to address criminal-justice and youth behavioral health challenges.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of DPSCS is designated as a member of the commission to address the behavioral health needs of the state's forensic, court-ordered, and incarcerated populations.
The Secretary of Juvenile Services is named as a commission member to provide expertise on youth behavioral health issues and juvenile justice-involved youth.
The Secretary of Disabilities is designated as a commission member to focus on behavioral health access for individuals with developmental and complex disabilities.
The Secretary of Human Services serves as an ex officio member of the commission to coordinate behavioral health access across social services and vulnerable populations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: A representative of the Office of the Public Defender is designated as a member of the commission to advise on court-ordered treatment, forensic populations, and criminal justice-involved behavioral health.
The Office of Appointments will assist the Governor in vetting and appointing the 22 gubernatorial appointees across diverse stakeholder categories to the newly created commission.
DBM is responsible for managing executive budget operations, which includes executing the bill's mandated annual appropriation of $600,000 for the pilot program in fiscal years 2025 through 2027.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the use of $30,000,000 appropriated to the Dedicated Purpose Account in the fiscal 2023 budget bill. Requires Medicaid funds to provide community services to individuals on waitlists for specified home- and community-based waiver programs. Authorizes funding to expand provider capacity, hire and retain staff, and increase reimbursement rates across these waivers. Extends provider capacity expansion provisions to include the Autism Waiver. Authorizes annual budget funding beginning in fiscal year 2024 to hire and retain waiver providers.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals on waitlists or registries for Medicaid waiver programs and community-based service providers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No net impact on State revenues or expenditures because the bill redirects existing appropriations rather than requiring new funding. Up to $20.0 million in fiscal 2023 Dedicated Purpose Account funds is repurposed to provide community services to individuals on waiver waitlists and expand provider capacity.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the state's Medicaid program and the specified Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS) waiver programs, expanding provider capacity, and executing plans to reduce waiver waitlists.

The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) jointly develops plans with MDH regarding the Autism Waiver, applies to CMS for waiver expansions, and receives a dedicated transfer of at least $10 million for students with disabilities.
DBM is responsible for processing the budget amendments to transfer funds from the Dedicated Purpose Account and overseeing state budget allocations required to reduce waiver program waitlists.

The Governor's Office receives the waiver reduction plans developed by MDH and is statutorily directed to include sufficient funds in the annual state budget bill to carry out waitlist reduction and provider retention goals.

qa_results.bill_summary: Subjects shared appreciation agreements to the Maryland Mortgage Lender Law and state credit regulations. Classifies funds advanced under a shared appreciation agreement as loans under revolving and closed end credit laws. Governs agreements that allow readvancing repaid funds under revolving credit provisions regardless of written election. Places agreements that do not allow readvancing under closed end credit provisions regardless of written election. Authorizes the Commissioner of Financial Regulation to adopt regulations regarding enforcement and compliance.
qa_results.responsible_party: Commissioner of Financial Regulation
qa_results.stakeholders: Homeowners entering into shared appreciation agreements and credit grantors, lenders, or brokers offering or servicing them
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances and operations are not materially affected because the bill generally codifies and clarifies existing practice. Certain small business lenders offering shared appreciation agreements may incur licensing and compliance costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill grants regulatory and enforcement authority over shared appreciation agreements to the Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation (OCFR), which is a regulatory agency within the Maryland Department of Labor.

The Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General advises on and enforces consumer protection laws concerning credit transactions and lending practices under the Commercial Law Article.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Medical Assistance Program, Maryland Children's Health Program, and specified health insurance carriers to cover pharmacist services. Mandates coverage to the same extent as services rendered by any other licensed health care provider. Prohibits conditioning reimbursement on employment by a physician, pharmacy, or facility, or acting under physician orders. Requires the Maryland Department of Health to obtain any necessary federal program waivers by January 1, 2024. Applies to policies, contracts, and health benefit plans issued, delivered, or renewed on or after January 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed pharmacists, pharmacies, Medicaid and Maryland Children's Health Program enrollees, covered insured individuals, health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in fiscal 2024 (51% federal funds, 49% general funds) due to potential increased billing for covered services in Medicaid and the Maryland Children's Health Program, with federal revenues increasing accordingly. Expenditures for local governments purchasing fully insured health plans may also increase.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) and the Maryland Children's Health Program, both administered by the Department of Health, to cover services rendered by licensed pharmacists. The bill specifically directs the department to apply for and obtain any necessary federal waivers or state plan amendments, resulting in an indeterminate fiscal impact.

The bill amends Insurance Article § 15-716, requiring private insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to reimburse pharmacists for services within their lawful scope of practice. As the state's insurance regulator, the agency oversees carrier compliance with this coverage requirement.

The department oversees the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program and the overall state budget, including general fund expenditures associated with state health programs, although the fiscal impact on the state employee plan is determined to be non-material.

The agency regulates and offers individual and small group health benefit plans through Maryland Health Connection, which must conform to state insurance mandate revisions regarding pharmacist reimbursement parity.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to adopt regulations establishing appropriate food service facility standards. Applies these standards to licensed residential behavioral health programs with fewer than 17 residents. Covers low-intensity, medium-intensity, high-intensity, and intensive residential substance-related disorder treatment programs. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Operators and residents of licensed residential behavioral health treatment programs with fewer than 17 residents
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health can adopt regulations within existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected, and local finances experience no material impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland Department of Health to adopt regulations establishing appropriate food service facility standards for residential behavioral health programs with fewer than 17 residents.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a therapy management contract to be entered into orally or in writing, including electronic form. Requires parties to reduce an oral therapy management contract to writing within 30 days after entering into it. Repeals the requirement that a therapy management contract be initially written. Replaces the requirement that parties sign the contract with a requirement that they agree on it. Applies to licensed pharmacists, authorized prescribers, and patients under a prescriber-pharmacist agreement.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Pharmacy
qa_results.stakeholders: licensed pharmacists, authorized prescribers, and patients entering into therapy management contracts
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local governmental operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health oversees health occupations and regulatory boards, including the State Board of Pharmacy under Title 12 of the Health Occupations Article, which regulates pharmacist practice, protocols, and therapy management contracts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands qualifications for foreign-trained faculty members at the University of Maryland School of Dentistry to take the ADEX examination. Qualifies general dentists who complete a general dental practice residency or an advanced education in general dentistry program. Qualifies general dentists who are board certified by the American Board of General Dentistry. Requires applicants to have completed at least seven consecutive years as full-time faculty members at the school. Requires applicants to submit a written letter of support from the University of Maryland School of Dentistry.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Dental Examiners
qa_results.stakeholders: foreign-trained dentist faculty members at the University of Maryland School of Dentistry
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Board of Dental Examiners special fund revenues increase minimally beginning in fiscal 2024 from license fees, with expenditures absorbed within existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Dental Examiners is an occupational licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Health responsible for qualifying applicants, administering licensing standards, and regulating dental professionals in Maryland.

The bill directly impacts full-time foreign-trained dental faculty at the University of Maryland School of Dentistry (a constituent institution of the University System of Maryland) and requires the school to provide written letters of support for qualifying candidates.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Labor to study expedited occupational and professional licensing for service members, veterans, and military spouses. Directs the department to conduct the study in consultation with the Maryland Department of Veterans Affairs. Examines the utilization of military experience, education, and training credit toward State licensing requirements. Evaluates outreach efforts, website visibility, and best practices compared to other states. Mandates reporting of findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by June 30, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Maryland Department of Veterans Affairs
qa_results.stakeholders: Service members, veterans, and military spouses seeking occupational and professional licenses in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures and revenues are not affected; the Maryland Department of Labor and Maryland Department of Veterans Affairs can conduct the study and report using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor is the primary implementing agency tasked with conducting the study on expedited licensing utilization for service members, veterans, and military spouses and reporting the findings.

The Department of Veterans and Military Families (referenced in statute as the Department of Veterans Affairs) is statutorily required to be consulted by the Department of Labor in conducting the study and preparing the report.
The bill requires the Department of Labor, in consultation with the Department of Veterans Affairs, to submit the final report and recommendations of the study to the Governor by June 30, 2024.

qa_results.bill_summary: Updates statutory references from the Comptroller of Maryland to the Executive Director of the Alcohol and Tobacco Commission. Clarifies the Executive Director's authority to issue licenses, conduct inspections, and enforce laws governing alcoholic beverages and tobacco. Grants concurrent enforcement, search, and seizure powers to the Commission and the Comptroller. Authorizes the Executive Director to seize contraband property and sell forfeited conveyances at public auction. Repeals obsolete provisions and penalties relating to alcoholic beverage tax stamps.
qa_results.responsible_party: Alcohol and Tobacco Commission; Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Alcoholic beverage manufacturers, wholesalers, retailers, common carriers, and tobacco product licensees and distributors in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State or local fiscal impact because the bill codifies existing practices and administrative responsibilities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill updates numerous sections across the Maryland Code to remove obsolete references to the Comptroller and reassign regulatory and enforcement duties over alcohol and tobacco to the Alcohol and Tobacco Commission, while clarifying joint and retained tax administration and enforcement authorities of the Comptroller.

The bill amends the Health - General Article to require the Maryland Department of Health to collaborate and consult with the Executive Director of the Alcohol and Tobacco Commission, along with the Comptroller, to develop ongoing strategies for enforcing prohibitions on tobacco and cannabinoid sales to minors.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the State's Attorney of Calvert County to designate the county attorney or an assistant county attorney to prosecute civil infractions. Requires the designation to receive the approval of the county commissioners. Allows a designated attorney to exercise the powers of the State's Attorney regarding civil infractions. Applies solely to civil infraction proceedings within Calvert County. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: State's Attorney of Calvert County; County Commissioners of Calvert County; Calvert County Attorney's Office
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals cited for civil infractions in Calvert County; State's Attorney of Calvert County; Calvert County Attorney and assistant county attorneys
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not materially affected. Any operational impact on Calvert County is not expected to materially affect local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Civil infractions prosecuted under this authority are adjudicated within the Maryland court system, for which the Administrative Office of the Courts provides administrative and operational support. AOC was also consulted as an information source for the bill's fiscal analysis.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a person convicted of specified misdemeanor hunting offenses to file a petition for record expungement. Applies to hunting without a license, failing to wear fluorescent clothing, and other specified natural resources violations. Prohibits filing a petition earlier than 10 years after satisfying all sentences imposed for the convictions. Requires courts and law enforcement agencies to remove eligible records from public inspection upon court order. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals convicted of specified misdemeanor hunting offenses under the Natural Resources Article
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures increase for the Judiciary through fiscal 2026 to process additional expungement petitions, though the exact cost cannot be reliably determined. General fund revenues increase minimally from expungement petition filing fees. Local finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands eligibility for expungement of convictions for specified hunting offenses, requiring the District Court and Circuit Court clerks to process new petitions for expungement and manage court record expungements, resulting in an operational and fiscal impact.

The bill authorizes expungement for specific misdemeanor hunting offenses regulated under Title 10 of the Natural Resources Article, impacting police and administrative enforcement records maintained by DNR and its Natural Resources Police.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases death and burial benefits under the Calvert County Length of Service Award Program for volunteer emergency personnel. Raises the maximum death benefit for a qualified volunteer with 25 years of service from $6,000 to $10,000. Raises the maximum burial benefit for specified volunteers from $240 to $336 for each year of certified service. Increases the line-of-duty death benefit for a qualified volunteer from $6,000 to $10,000. Authorizes the Calvert County Board of County Commissioners to approve benefit increases matching cost-of-living increases for county employees.
qa_results.responsible_party: Calvert County Board of County Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Calvert County volunteer fire company, rescue squad, and rescue dive team members and their beneficiaries
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Calvert County expenditures may increase by at least $450,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2024 due to potential cost-of-living benefit increases, along with minimal expenditure increases for higher death benefits. State revenues and expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill references the State Workers' Compensation Commission as the determining entity for whether a qualified volunteer's death occurred in the line of duty, which qualifies the individual's estate or beneficiary for an increased death benefit.

qa_results.bill_summary: Excludes specified electric generating facilities and multi-unit combinations from the statutory definition of generating station. Authorizes construction of qualifying solar photovoltaic combinations up to 14 megawatts cumulative capacity without a certificate of public convenience and necessity. Requires each individual unit within an exempt combination to produce not more than 2 megawatts and be separately metered. Requires electric companies to provide meter aggregation upon written request to qualifying eligible customer-generators. Includes agricultural users, nonprofits, local governments, State units, and public senior higher education institutions as eligible entities. Mandates customer-generators provide written allocation instructions for excess generation credits before meter aggregation begins.
qa_results.responsible_party: Public Service Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: electric companies, solar energy developers, agricultural electricity customers, nonprofit organizations, municipal and county governments, State agencies, and public senior higher education institutions
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected, though state agencies may review fewer Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity applications. Local government expenditures may increase significantly in some jurisdictions if local officials choose to study, regulate, or review projects that bypass the state certificate process.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary implementing agency responsible for regulating electric utilities, issuing Certificates of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN), processing CPCN exemptions, and overseeing net energy metering and meter aggregation regulations.

The Department of Natural Resources, through its Power Plant Research Program (PPRP), participates directly in reviewing CPCN applications and environmental impact evaluations, and may see a reduction in CPCN applications to review under the bill.

The Department of the Environment participates in environmental evaluations of CPCN applications and regulates brownfield and landfill sites referenced in the bill's definitions, and may have fewer CPCN applications to review.
The Office of the People's Counsel represents residential utility consumers in Public Service Commission proceedings related to utility rates, grid safety, and renewable generation regulations.
The Maryland Energy Administration manages the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF), which receives any unreturned or abandoned application deposits from escrow accounts under the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Task Force on Preventing and Countering Elder Abuse. Directs the Maryland Department of Aging to provide staff for the Task Force. Requires the Task Force to study existing laws, policies, and practices relating to elder abuse. Requires recommendations on statutory, policy, and practice changes regarding funding, oversight, and prosecution. Directs the Task Force to submit a preliminary report by December 31, 2023. Requires a final report by December 31, 2024, before the act terminates June 30, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Aging; Task Force on Preventing and Countering Elder Abuse
qa_results.stakeholders: older adults in Maryland, victims of elder abuse, legal advocates, and elder care service providers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $26,500 in fiscal 2024 and $11,400 in fiscal 2025 for part-time contractual staff to assist the Task Force. State revenues are unaffected, and local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Aging is the primary agency tasked with staffing the Task Force on Preventing and Countering Elder Abuse. The Secretary of Aging and the Maryland Long-Term Care Ombudsman serve on the task force, and the agency incurs a direct fiscal impact for hiring contractual staff.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly establishes a temporary entity, the Task Force on Preventing and Countering Elder Abuse, to study laws and make recommendations on elder abuse prevention and prosecution.
The Governor is responsible for designating the chair of the Task Force, appointing 11 members, and receiving preliminary and final reports from the Task Force.
The Attorney General or their designee is designated as a statutory member of the Task Force, which will study laws and prosecution methods relating to elder abuse.
The Task Force includes the Maryland Chief Medical Examiner and a representative of the Office of Health Care Quality, both of which are units within the Maryland Department of Health.
The Task Force includes the Director of the Office of Adult Services (which oversees Adult Protective Services within the Department of Human Services).
The bill requires the Governor to appoint a representative of the Maryland Health Care Commission to serve as a member of the Task Force.
The bill mandates that a representative of the Maryland State Police be appointed by the Governor to serve on the Task Force.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointees, which includes multiple members and the chair of the newly created Task Force.
The bill includes representation from the Circuit Court Guardianship program and discusses judicial and court recognition and adjudication of elder abuse crimes.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits parking certain trucks, tractors, trailers, school buses, and passenger buses on streets or highways in Sharpsburg. Excludes Class A passenger vehicles and qualifying Class E trucks. Allows parking when essential to the immediate use of the vehicle. Imposes a separate fine for each vehicle in a combination tractor and trailer. Treats each day of a violation as a separate offense.
qa_results.responsible_party: Town of Sharpsburg
qa_results.stakeholders: Drivers and owners of commercial trucks, tractors, trailers, school buses, and passenger buses in the Town of Sharpsburg
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local finances or operations. Local enforcement can be handled with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Maryland Vehicle Law within the Transportation Article to restrict the parking of specified vehicle classes on streets and highways in the Town of Sharpsburg.
The District Court and judicial system process citations and contested violations under the Maryland Vehicle Law, including statutory parking restrictions and fines.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes minimum compensation rates for election judges across Maryland. Mandates daily pay of at least $250 for first-time election judges for each election day and early voting day served. Requires returning election judges to receive at least $100 more per day than first-time judges. Sets compensation at a minimum of $50 for completing each required course of instruction. Directs the State Board of Elections to reimburse local boards $50 per returning judge and to implement a recruitment marketing campaign.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Elections; local boards of elections
qa_results.stakeholders: election judges, returning election judges, local boards of elections, and county governing bodies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by approximately $1.6 million to $2.1 million annually beginning in FY 2024 for returning judge reimbursements and marketing costs. Local government expenditures increase collectively by approximately $3.2 million to $3.8 million annually beginning in FY 2024 to fund higher compensation and marketing shares. Revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland State Board of Elections (SBE) to reimburse local boards of elections for $50 of the extra compensation paid to each returning election judge and to develop and provide a comprehensive marketing campaign to recruit election judges statewide, resulting in significant annual general fund expenditures.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires health insurance carriers and the Maryland Medical Assistance Program to provide coverage for biomarker testing supported by medical and scientific evidence. Applies the mandate to commercial health benefit plans beginning January 1, 2024, and to Medicaid beginning July 1, 2025. Prohibits cost-sharing for biomarker testing from exceeding deductibles, copayments, or coinsurance required for similar coverages. Requires coverage to be provided in a manner that limits disruptions in care, including repeated biospecimen sampling. Directs the Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Health Care Commission to submit comprehensive evaluation reports by specified dates.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Health Care Commission; Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland Medical Assistance Program enrollees; commercial health insurance policyholders; health insurers; nonprofit health service plans; health maintenance organizations; managed care organizations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Medicaid expenditures increase by an indeterminate but potentially significant amount beginning in FY 2026 (60% federal funds, 40% general funds), matching federal fund revenue increases, potentially offset by indeterminate downstream treatment savings. Minimal special fund revenue increase for the Maryland Insurance Administration in FY 2024 from rate and form filing fees. Potential expenditure increases for local governments purchasing fully insured health plans.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), which is administered by the Maryland Department of Health, provide coverage for biomarker testing beginning July 1, 2025. The department is also required to submit a comprehensive report on the fiscal and access impacts to the Governor and the General Assembly by December 1, 2024.

Section 3 of the bill specifically mandates that the Maryland Health Care Commission study and report to the General Assembly by December 1, 2025, on the impact of biomarker testing coverage across demographic groups and payer types.

The bill establishes an insurance coverage mandate for private health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and HMOs delivering policies in the state, which the Maryland Insurance Administration regulates, reviews policy form filings for, and collects related filing fees from.
The bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to submit its formal report regarding biomarker testing implementation, fiscal impact, and recommendations to the Governor by December 1, 2024.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Teacher Development and Retention Program as a pilot program to incentivize college students to pursue teaching careers. Delays high staff qualification requirements for eligible prekindergarten providers until the 2027–2028 school year. Expands the renamed Nancy Grasmick Public School Professional Award to include public school mental health professionals. Modifies eligibility criteria and service obligations for the Teaching Fellows for Maryland scholarship program. Requires the Maryland State Department of Education to maintain an educator recruitment, retention, and diversity dashboard.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Maryland Higher Education Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: public school teachers, teacher candidates, public school mental health professionals, eligible prekindergarten providers, local school systems, and higher education institutions
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $15.7 million in fiscal 2024, including $10.0 million to capitalize the Teacher Development and Retention Fund and $5.0 million for expanded loan assistance awards. General fund expenditures remain at $5.2 million annually in fiscal 2025 and 2026. Special fund expenditures from the new fund total an estimated $16.3 million through program termination in fiscal 2029. Local school boards can likely meet reporting mandates using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is a primary implementing agency for the bill. It is required to establish teacher recruitment and retention goals in consultation with MHEC, create and maintain the Maryland Educator Recruitment, Retention, and Diversity Dashboard, identify high-needs schools and content shortages, and establish standards for early childhood alternative teacher preparation programs.

MHEC (and its Office of Student Financial Assistance) is a primary implementing agency responsible for administering the new Teacher Development and Retention Program and Fund, overseeing the expanded Nancy Grasmick Public School Professional Award within the Janet L. Hoffman LARP, modifying the Teaching Fellows for Maryland program, and commissioning an independent program evaluation.

USM institutions house teacher preparation programs directly affected by the bill's recruitment and retention goals, student reporting requirements, and practicum standards. Several USM constituent institutions meet the Pell Grant eligibility threshold for the new Teacher Development and Retention Program stipends.

As an HBCU with a teacher preparation program and an undergraduate population with over 40% Pell Grant recipients, Morgan State University is directly eligible and targeted for educator recruitment, retention initiatives, and student stipends under the bill.

Saint Mary's College operates educator preparation programs (such as its Master of Arts in Teaching) impacted by the bill's revisions to teacher preparation requirements, scholarships, and retention initiatives.
The bill explicitly tasks the State Treasurer with holding separately and investing the moneys of the newly established Teacher Development and Retention Fund.
The bill specifies that the Comptroller must account for the newly established Teacher Development and Retention Fund.

DBM oversees the state budget and fiscal planning, which includes significant general fund expenditures ($15+ million in FY 2024) and ongoing out-year funding for the programs established or expanded under the bill.
This legislation is an Administration priority bill introduced by request to address statewide teacher shortages and requires executive reporting on program evaluation results.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires an adult family member to provide a death certificate or disability evidence to the State Real Estate Commission. Prohibits the family member from carrying on the broker's business until submitting this documentation. Authorizes a business to designate another licensed broker if documentation is not provided within a reasonable time. Authorizes a business to designate another licensed broker if a broker is terminated for any reason. Requires the Commission to approve the designation under specified conditions regarding license surrender and broker standing.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Real Estate Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: licensed real estate brokers, family members of disabled or deceased real estate brokers, and real estate brokerage businesses
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Does not materially affect State finances or operations; the State Real Estate Commission can implement the bill with existing resources. No local effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Maryland Real Estate Brokers Act administered by the State Real Estate Commission, which is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor's Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing. The Commission is responsible for receiving documentation and approving broker designations following death, disability, or termination.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a court to award reasonable attorney's fees and related costs to a prevailing parent of a child with a disability. Includes expert witness fees and costs within allowable judicial awards. Prohibits fee awards for services performed after a written settlement offer made over 14 days before proceedings. Applies this prohibition if the parent rejects the offer and achieves relief not more favorable than offered. Authorizes fee and cost awards if the prevailing parent was substantially justified in rejecting the settlement offer.
qa_results.responsible_party: Judiciary; Maryland State Department of Education; local school systems
qa_results.stakeholders: parents of children with disabilities, children with disabilities, local school systems, public education agencies, and attorneys and expert witnesses in special education proceedings
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State agency expenditures are not significantly affected. Local school systems face an indeterminate increase in expenditures beginning in fiscal 2024 to pay awarded attorney's fees and related costs, expected in 10 or fewer cases annually. Revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE oversees the state's public education system and special education programs under IDEA. It is explicitly identified as a public agency subject to due process proceedings and is responsible for making staff available for mediation and ensuring statewide compliance with special education dispute resolution.

The bill authorizes state circuit courts to award reasonable attorney's fees, expert witness fees, and related costs to prevailing parents in special education appeals, directly impacting court proceedings administered and supported by the Judiciary.

Due process complaints concerning special education are filed with OAH, and its administrative law judges preside over the underlying hearings that form the basis of the judicial actions and fee dispute rules addressed by the bill.

The Maryland School for the Deaf is explicitly defined as a 'public agency' under § 8-413, making it subject to special education due process complaints and potential judicial actions where attorney's fees and expert witness costs may be awarded.

The Juvenile Services Education Program is explicitly designated as a 'public agency' under the bill, exposing it to potential due process complaints and court-ordered awards of attorney's fees and related costs in special education disputes.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Governor to annually proclaim January 27 as Maryland Holocaust Remembrance Day. Requires the proclamation to declare the day one of reflection, recollection, and determination. Calls on Maryland families, educators, religious communities, political bodies, and media to remember the Holocaust. Requires the proclamation to include a pledge spreading Holocaust lessons and realities to future generations. Seeks to ensure society never forgets and bears witness against prejudice, bigotry, ignorance, and hate.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland families, educators, religious communities, political bodies, and media
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. Commemorating Maryland Holocaust Remembrance Day does not affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly requires the Governor to annually issue an official proclamation designating January 27 as Maryland Holocaust Remembrance Day, including specific declarations regarding reflection and education.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date for laws governing Maryland Insurance Commissioner enforcement of clean claims requirements. Applies to administrative services organizations administering the delivery system for specialty mental health services. Continues subjecting administrative services organizations to interest on unpaid clean claims and specified fines and penalties. Prolongs the Insurance Commissioner's authority to investigate potential clean claims violations. Extends the statutory provisions for two additional years through May 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Commissioner; Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: administrative services organizations administering specialty mental health services under Medicaid, specialty mental health providers, and Medicaid managed care organization enrollees
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No net impact on State expenditures, as the Maryland Insurance Administration can handle enforcement using existing budgeted resources. MIA special fund revenues may increase indeterminately from fiscal 2023 through fiscal 2025 if penalties or fines are assessed.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly extends the enforcement authority and regulatory duties of the Maryland Insurance Commissioner over administrative services organizations (ASOs) that process specialty mental health services claims, including conducting investigations and potentially assessing fines.

The Maryland Department of Health administers the Medicaid program and oversees the delivery system for specialty mental health services. Under the extended provisions, the Insurance Commissioner must provide findings of any investigated claims violations directly to MDH.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts certain State retirees rehired by the Maryland Department of Health from statutory retirement allowance earnings limitations. Applies to retirees rehired for up to five years to administer federally funded COVID-19 grants. Extends the exemption to retirees serving on the COVID Unified Command for staffing support or contact tracing. Applies retroactively to January 1, 2020. Sunsets on December 31, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; State Retirement Agency
qa_results.stakeholders: State retirees rehired by the Maryland Department of Health to support COVID-19 pandemic response projects and grants
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State pension liabilities or contribution rates. Any retirement benefit offsets already deducted in 2023 must be repaid to affected rehired retirees. No effect on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly applies to retirees rehired by the Maryland Department of Health to administer COVID-19 grants or serve on the COVID Unified Command, and was requested by the department.

The agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System and is responsible for implementing the earnings limitation exemption, waiving benefit offsets, and refunding any offsets previously deducted.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts certain applicants for video lottery employee licenses from mandatory disqualification due to criminal history or current prosecution. Applies when the conviction, active parole, probation, or prosecution involves a nonviolent misdemeanor offense other than a gambling crime. Requires the applicant to have participated in and completed a qualifying problem-solving court program. Defines problem-solving courts to include drug, DUI, veterans', mental health, or reentry courts. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Applicants for video lottery employee licenses who completed a problem-solving court program for a nonviolent misdemeanor and video lottery operation licensees
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. Changes to licensing qualifications are not anticipated to significantly affect application volumes, licensing fee revenues, administrative expenses, or court caseloads.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1288 directly alters the licensing disqualification criteria enforced by the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission for video lottery employee license applicants.

The bill references programs under the Judiciary's Office of Problem-Solving Courts, and the Administrative Office of the Courts evaluated the potential operational impact on requests to problem-solving courts and trial court caseloads.

qa_results.bill_summary: Modifies prior authorizations of State debt for various local and miscellaneous capital grant projects across Maryland. Extends expenditure and encumbrance termination dates for specified grants through June 1, 2030. Removes matching fund requirements and historic easement conveyance obligations for selected grantees. Alters authorized uses, project scopes, locations, and designated recipients for multiple capital grant awards. Conditions Baltimore City grant expenditures for the Reach Partnership Field on adopting a renaming resolution.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Public Works; Department of General Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Capital grant recipients, including local governments, nonprofit organizations, educational institutions, and healthcare facilities across Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected because the bill alters existing grant conditions, deadlines, and recipients rather than creating new debt authorizations. Local governments experience no fiscal impact unless acting as a designated grant recipient.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of General Services administers and manages the State's capital grant programs and state-funded capital improvement projects, directly overseeing the implementation of capital budget debt authorizations modified by this bill.

The Board of Public Works oversees State capital expenditures and is the entity responsible under Maryland law for certifying matching funds and approving disbursements for authorizations of State debt altered by this legislation.
The State Treasurer manages State debt issuance, the State's bond funds, and serves on the Board of Public Works, which oversees authorizations and changes to general obligation bond-funded grants.

The Maryland Historical Trust is a unit within the Department of Planning; this bill specifically repeals a statutory requirement that a capital grantee grant and convey a historic easement to the Trust.

The bill amends capital grant authorizations specifically dedicated to the Historic St. Mary's City Fort to 400 Commission, modifying authorized uses, scope of work, and grant allocations for Phase 2 design and surveys.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters provisions governing criminal background investigations for individuals who care for or supervise children. Requires covered child care facilities and schools to apply to the Central Repository for criminal history records checks. Directs the Central Repository to forward criminal history record information to the individual and authorized licensing agencies. Defines employees to include contractors and subcontractors with direct, unsupervised, and uncontrolled access to children. Requires immediate removal of a child from an emergency out-of-home placement if an individual refuses follow-up fingerprints.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Child care centers, family child care homes, nonpublic and public schools, child care employees, contractors, volunteers, and individuals seeking adoption or guardianship
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State or local finances or operations. The changes conform Maryland statute to federal requirements to allow continued access to national criminal history records checks.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS requested this departmental legislation. The Criminal Justice Information System Central Repository (CJIS-CR) is housed within DPSCS and is responsible for conducting the State and national criminal history records checks, collecting fees, and disseminating record information to authorized agencies in compliance with federal standards.

DHS oversees local departments of social services, foster care, adoptions, and child placement programs. The bill directly impacts procedures for criminal history checks and emergency out-of-home child placements managed by local departments.

MSDE regulates licensed child care centers, registered family child care homes, informal child care providers, and schools. The bill dictates that the Central Repository forward criminal history records to MSDE and requires MSDE to conduct cross-reference checks against the central sex offender registry.

MDH licenses home health and residential service agencies providing services to minors, as well as day and residential camps, which are categorized as facilities whose employees and operators must obtain criminal history records checks under this subtitle.

Facilities under Title 9 of the Human Services Article (juvenile detention, correction, or treatment facilities) are listed among facilities requiring background checks, although direct employees of DJS are explicitly exempted under the definition of employee in this subtitle.

qa_results.bill_summary: Urges the U.S. General Services Administration to select Greenbelt or Landover, Maryland, for the new Federal Bureau of Investigation headquarters. Highlights Maryland's established role in national defense and cybersecurity infrastructure. Notes that locating the facility in Prince George's County promotes equity and workforce diversity. Commits the General Assembly to supporting employee relocation and necessary transportation infrastructure improvements. Directs the Department of Legislative Services to transmit copies of the resolution to federal and state officials.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Legislative Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Prince George's County, Federal Bureau of Investigation personnel, and federal contractors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Compliance with the joint resolution does not directly affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The resolution designates Governor Wes Moore as an official recipient of the joint resolution and directly concerns intergovernmental coordination and federal relations regarding the location of a major federal facility in Maryland.

The joint resolution advocates for bringing the consolidated Federal Bureau of Investigation headquarters to Maryland, which directly intersects with the Department of Commerce's core mission of attracting major employers, stimulating economic development, and job growth.

The resolution emphasizes Maryland's commitment to supporting the FBI headquarters through mass transit access and infrastructure improvements at the Greenbelt and Landover finalist sites, aligning with MDOT's responsibilities for state transit and roadway infrastructure.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits wearing, carrying, or transporting firearms in areas for children and vulnerable individuals, government areas, and special purpose areas. Requires government buildings to display conspicuous signage at main entrances indicating firearms are prohibited. Prohibits carrying a firearm into another person's dwelling or onto private property without express permission or posted authorization. Restricts handgun permit holders to carrying concealed from view under clothing or within an enclosed case. Repeals the authority of the Secretary of State Police to limit handgun permit times and geographic areas. Establishes misdemeanor penalties of up to one year of imprisonment, a fine up to $1,000, or both.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of State Police; Secretary of State Police
qa_results.stakeholders: firearm owners, handgun permit holders, private property owners, and operators of restricted sensitive facilities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in State general fund revenues and expenditures from misdemeanor penalty provisions. Potential minimal one-time increase in State and local expenditures in FY 2024 to post required signage at owned or leased government buildings.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Police oversees handgun wear, carry, and transport permits. The bill directly alters the authority of the Secretary of State Police regarding handgun permits, eliminating certain discretionary limitations and mandating statutory concealed carry restrictions.

The bill establishes new criminal misdemeanor prohibitions on carrying firearms in sensitive areas and on private property, which will be adjudicated in the state court system. It also explicitly preserves the authority of court administrative heads to adopt rules prohibiting weapons in court facilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates new misdemeanor crimes subject to imprisonment for up to one year, directly impacting OPD's caseload for defending indigent individuals charged under these new provisions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates new misdemeanor penalties carrying potential incarceration, which could have an impact on detention and correctional facilities and supervision managed by the department.
