As the primary manager of state-owned and leased facilities, DGS is affected by the requirement that government-owned or leased buildings post clear and conspicuous signage prohibiting firearms at main entrances.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the requirement that the Department of Natural Resources make available and issue documents in a digital or electronic format. Applies this mandate to all licenses, stamps, permits, registrations, and certificates authorized under the Natural Resources Article, subject to specified exceptions. Exempts thirteen specific items, including charter boat licenses, vessel certificates of title, and various registration decals and stickers. Authorizes individuals to satisfy possession or display requirements by presenting qualifying documents in a digital or electronic format. Retains requirements to attach, affix, or display associated numbers, stickers, or decals on a vehicle, vessel, dock, or gear.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Holders and applicants of Department of Natural Resources licenses, stamps, permits, registrations, and certificates, including hunters, anglers, boaters, and commercial harvesters
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal effect, as the Department of Natural Resources can implement the bill with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 10 directly expands the requirement for the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) to issue nearly all licenses, stamps, permits, registrations, and certificates in a digital or electronic format upon request, and allows individuals to satisfy possession or display requirements via electronic format.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the maximum outstanding debt secured by future federal aid that the Department of Transportation may issue to $1,000,000,000. Restricts bond proceeds to six specified transit and highway infrastructure projects. Extends the maximum maturity of these bonds from 12 years to 15 years after issue. Repeals the secondary pledge of State tax revenue and excludes these bonds from State tax supported debt. Establishes the Maryland Commission on Transportation Revenue and Infrastructure Needs to recommend sustainable transportation funding options.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation; Department of Legislative Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland Department of Transportation, transit riders, motorists, local governments, and transportation construction contractors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund expenditures increase by $100,000 in FY 2024 and $50,000 in FY 2025 for contractual staff support for the commission. The bill expands MDOT's authority to issue up to $1.0 billion in debt backed by future federal aid for specified capital projects. There is no direct local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT is the primary implementing agency. The bill expands MDOT's bonding authority for debt backed by future federal aid up to $1.0 billion for specific projects, alters bond terms, and requires MDOT to provide staff support and funding for the Maryland Commission on Transportation Revenue and Infrastructure Needs.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill statutorily creates the Maryland Commission on Transportation Revenue and Infrastructure Needs to study and recommend changes to the state's transportation funding and revenue structure.

MTA transit projects, including the Baltimore Red Line and procurement of zero-emission buses and related infrastructure, are specifically authorized for financing under the expanded federal aid bond proceeds, and the Commission membership includes a representative from the MTA core service area.

SHA highway corridor projects, including improvements to MD Route 2/Route 4 (Thomas Johnson Bridge), MD Route 90, and Interstate 81, are specifically authorized to receive financing from the bond proceeds under the bill.

The Treasurer chairs the Capital Debt Affordability Committee (CDAC). The bill amends State Finance and Procurement Section 8-104 to alter the definition of State tax-supported debt reviewed by CDAC by removing certain debt backed by future federal aid.
The Secretary of Budget and Management is designated by statute as an ex officio member of the Maryland Commission on Transportation Revenue and Infrastructure Needs.
The Secretary of Commerce is designated by statute as an ex officio member of the Maryland Commission on Transportation Revenue and Infrastructure Needs.
The Secretary of Planning is designated by statute as an ex officio member of the Maryland Commission on Transportation Revenue and Infrastructure Needs.

The Governor is responsible for appointing members and designating the chair of the Maryland Commission on Transportation Revenue and Infrastructure Needs, and receives interim and final reports from the Commission.
MDTA debt backed by federal aid under Title 4, Subtitle 3 is included in the statutory debt limits and provisions amended under the bill.
The Board of Public Works is required under existing statutory provisions to approve the issuance of transportation debt and bonds backed by federal aid prior to their issuance.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters application requirements for a real property tax exemption on dwellings owned by disabled veterans or surviving spouses. Permits applicants to submit a U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs rating decision showing its effective date. Provides this rating decision as an alternative to the department-issued disability certification form. Prohibits unauthorized inspection of the submitted rating decision. Restricts inspection solely to the disabled veteran and appropriate state, county, or municipal employees. Applies to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Disabled veterans, surviving spouses of disabled veterans, and county and municipal tax assessment offices
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The State Department of Assessments and Taxation can implement the changes with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the documentation requirements for disabled veterans and their surviving spouses to apply for a 100% property tax exemption on their dwelling house. DVMF is responsible for assisting and advocating for Maryland veterans and their families regarding state benefits and housing-related programs.

PTAAB hears appeals regarding disputes over real property tax exemptions and credits following decisions made by local supervisors of assessments. Changes to acceptable documentation for granting exemptions may indirectly affect appeals brought before the board.

qa_results.bill_summary: Shortens waiting periods for filing petitions to expunge records of certain misdemeanor and felony convictions. Adds misdemeanor malicious destruction of property to the list of convictions eligible for expungement. Reduces general waiting periods to 5 years for eligible misdemeanors and 7 years for eligible felonies. Sets waiting periods at 10 years for first-degree burglary, second-degree burglary, and felony theft. Specifies that unpaid court fees or costs do not bar an individual from receiving an expungement. Requires courts to waive all court fees and costs associated with an expunged charge.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; Department of State Police
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals seeking criminal record expungements; crime victim compensation funds; state courts; law enforcement record custodians
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal decrease in special fund revenues from waived court costs and fees, with no material impact on general fund revenues. Potential minimal increase in general fund expenditures for the Judiciary and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services to process an initial influx of expungement petitions. No material local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Judiciary and trial courts are directly responsible for processing petitions for expungement, modifying waiting periods under the Maryland Electronic Courts (MDEC) system, and implementing the requirement to waive outstanding court fees and costs.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department's Criminal Justice Information System (CJIS) acts as the central repository for criminal records and must execute expungement orders, while the Division of Parole and Probation tracks sentence completion dates and related fee collections.
As the primary state law enforcement agency holding criminal history and arrest records, the department receives, processes, and complies with court-issued expungement orders.
DBM houses the Central Collection Unit (CCU), which handles collection of delinquent court costs and fees that are now subject to mandatory waiver upon expungement.
The State Archives serves as the custodian of permanent judicial and government records and must comply with court expungement orders for archived records.
MDOT agencies and police units maintain transportation-related law enforcement and licensing records that may be subject to expungement orders under the expanded and accelerated provisions.
The Natural Resources Police maintain citation and arrest records for specific Natural Resources Article violations eligible for expungement under § 10-110.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands paid disaster service leave eligibility for State employees belonging to qualifying volunteer emergency and disaster organizations. Authorizes appointing authorities to waive approval requirements and increase leave days during prolonged or recurrent disasters. Retains State employee status under workers' compensation and tort claims for Maryland Incident Management Team members on disaster leave. Replaces military leave provisions with uniformed services leave under federal definitions. Defines emergency manager within State emergency management law.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Budget and Management; Maryland Department of Emergency Management
qa_results.stakeholders: State employees serving in uniformed services or volunteer disaster response organizations, including the Civil Air Patrol, Coast Guard Auxiliary, volunteer fire and rescue companies, and community emergency response teams
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material impact on State finances or operations. Expenditures may increase minimally in limited situations if agencies incur overtime or temporary coverage costs for employees on disaster leave during emergencies.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the State's central personnel agency, DBM is directly tasked with adopting regulations for paid uniformed services leave and maintaining records of State employees' use of uniformed services administrative leave.

The bill amends the Public Safety Article governing MDEM by defining 'emergency manager' and modifies disaster service leave provisions for State employees engaging in emergency response organizations, including the Maryland Incident Management Team.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Governor to include a $1,000,000 appropriation in the annual budget bill for the Maryland Nonprofit Development Center Program Fund. Mandates this funding in fiscal year 2024 or alternatively in fiscal year 2025. Dedicates the appropriation to loans issued under the Nonprofit, Interest-Free, Micro Bridge Loan Account. Repeals the transfer of video lottery terminal proceeds from the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Businesses Account to the loan account.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Commerce; Office of the Governor
qa_results.stakeholders: Nonprofit entities in Maryland seeking bridge loans, and small, minority, and women-owned businesses eligible for investment capital from the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Businesses Account
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $1.0 million in FY 2025 due to a mandated appropriation for the Maryland Department of Commerce. Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Maryland Nonprofit Development Center Program Fund increase correspondingly by $1.0 million in FY 2025 to provide micro bridge loans, with further special fund activity beginning as early as FY 2026 as loans are repaid and reissued. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Nonprofit Development Center Program and the NIMBL Account are administered by the Department of Commerce, which experiences a direct fiscal impact of a $1.0 million general fund increase in FY 2025 to fund interest-free micro bridge loans.
DBM is responsible for state budget preparation and execution, and this bill establishes a statutory mandated appropriation of $1.0 million for FY 2025.
The bill mandates that the Governor include a specific $1.0 million appropriation in the annual state budget bill for the NIMBL Account.

The bill amends the statute governing distributions by the Comptroller of video lottery terminal proceeds by repealing the requirement to divert funds from the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Businesses Account to the NIMBL Account.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the statutory definition of public safety officer for local property tax credits on qualifying dwellings. Repeals the $2,500 cap on the maximum property tax credit local jurisdictions may grant. Requires county and municipal governing bodies that grant the credit to define public safety officer by law. Authorizes local governing bodies to establish the credit's amount, duration, and additional eligibility requirements. Applies the changes to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governing bodies of Maryland counties and municipal corporations
qa_results.stakeholders: Public safety officers who own qualifying dwellings and Maryland county and municipal governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential decrease in county and municipal property tax revenues beginning in fiscal 2024 to the extent local jurisdictions authorize the credit, expand eligibility, or increase credit amounts. State revenues and expenditures are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters eligibility criteria and local authority regarding property tax credits under the Tax - Property Article. While the fiscal impact is local and administrative execution falls to local jurisdictions, the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board hears disputes and appeals regarding property tax exemptions and credits.

The Maryland Tax Court serves as the highest administrative body for tax disputes, hearing appeals from final decisions of local taxing authorities and Property Tax Assessment Appeals Boards regarding property assessments and tax credits.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires an appointee for a civil commission to contact the circuit court clerk to coordinate oath administration. Directs the clerk to administer the oath of office and present the commission. Alters the required reporting frequency from monthly to regularly when clerks notify the Secretary of State of qualifying officers. Repeals obsolete statutory provisions regarding the collection and payment of taxes on commissions.
qa_results.responsible_party: Clerks of the Circuit Courts; Secretary of State
qa_results.stakeholders: Appointees for civil commissions; clerks of the circuit courts; public officers taking oaths of office
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact because the bill codifies existing practice.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the statutory reporting requirements to the Secretary of State, requiring clerks of the circuit court to regularly report names and offices of individuals taking oaths of office under civil commissions, which the Secretary of State must preserve and certify.

The bill alters statutory duties and procedures for the clerks of the circuit courts regarding the presentation of civil commissions, scheduling oaths of office with appointees, and reporting to the Secretary of State.
The bill repeals an obsolete statutory requirement that required circuit court clerks to remit taxes collected on civil commissions to the State Treasurer.
The bill involves the administration and presentation of civil commissions issued by the Governor for gubernatorial appointees.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Apprenticeship and Training Council and its consultants to include representation by individuals who are Asian, Black, and Latino. Establishes the Apprenticeship 2030 Commission to examine and recommend strategies to expand registered apprenticeships. Directs the Commission to target growing registered apprenticeships to at least 60,000 by 2030. Requires the Commission to report findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1, 2023. Abrogates the Commission on December 31, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Apprenticeship 2030 Commission; Department of Legislative Services; Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: high school students, unemployed and underemployed adults seeking apprenticeships, employers, labor organizations, and members of the Apprenticeship and Training Council
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $36,900 in FY 2024 for the Maryland Department of Labor to hire contractual staff to support the commission. No effect on local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the membership and diversity requirements for the Apprenticeship and Training Council housed within MD Labor's Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning. Additionally, the Secretary of Labor serves on the newly established Apprenticeship 2030 Commission, and MD Labor incurs direct general fund expenditures to staff and support the commission.

The chair of the Governor's Workforce Development Board and the chair of the board's Career and Technical Education (CTE) Committee both serve on the Apprenticeship 2030 Commission. The bill also establishes legislative intent regarding policies between the commission and the CTE Committee.

The State Superintendent of Schools (or designee) is designated as a member of the Apprenticeship 2030 Commission, which is tasked with achieving the Blueprint for Maryland's Future target of having 45% of high school graduates complete an apprenticeship.

The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) serves as a member of the Apprenticeship 2030 Commission to examine high-demand industry sectors with skill shortages and business needs for workforce development.

The Secretary of Higher Education (or designee) serves on the Apprenticeship 2030 Commission to examine postsecondary pathways and explore degree apprenticeships in fields requiring higher education credentials.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally creates a temporary statutory study and advisory body, the Apprenticeship 2030 Commission, which is required to evaluate apprenticeship targets and report findings to state leadership before sunsetting.

The Governor appoints members to the Apprenticeship and Training Council, appoints employer representatives to the Apprenticeship 2030 Commission, jointly selects the commission chair, and receives the commission's final report.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments to the Apprenticeship and Training Council and the Apprenticeship 2030 Commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals public notice requirements for taxing authorities setting a real property tax rate exceeding the constant yield rate. Requires taxing authorities intending to increase real property tax rates above current rates to provide public notice and hold a hearing. Mandates publishing the notice in a general-circulation newspaper and on the taxing authority's website or an accessible public posting. Requires assessment notices to state that property taxes owed may increase if assessments increase without a tax rate increase. Requires counties to display prior and current taxable year property tax rates on annual property tax bills.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation; Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Real property owners and county and municipal taxing authorities in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Local expenditures may decrease due to fewer required public notices of tax rate increases, though county expenditures may increase in FY 2023 to update information on annual property tax bills. Local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Under § 6-308(I) of the bill, the Director of the State Department of Assessments and Taxation is required to report any taxing authority that appears to violate the property tax rate notice requirements to the Attorney General. The Office of the Attorney General is mandated to investigate these reports and institute legal action to compel compliance.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters reporting requirements for student Free Application for Federal Student Aid data. Repeals the requirement for county boards of education to report high school FAFSA completion data. Requires the Maryland Higher Education Commission to provide student FAFSA data access to the Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center. Requires the Center to report annual FAFSA submission data to specified legislative committees by December 15 from 2023 through 2028. Requires the Center to disaggregate the reported information by county and other student subgroups.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center; Maryland Higher Education Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland high school students submitting financial aid applications and local boards of education
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material impact on State finances, as the MLDS Center and MHEC can implement the requirements using existing resources. Local school system expenditures may decrease minimally due to the elimination of reporting mandates.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland Longitudinal Data System (MLDS) Center to receive FAFSA data, disaggregate it by county and student subgroups, and submit an annual report to legislative committees through 2028.

The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) to provide the MLDS Center with access to student FAFSA data from the Federal Student Aid Internet Gateway and the Office of Student Financial Aid.
The bill requires the commission to provide the MLDS Center with access to student FAFSA data collected via the Federal Student Aid Internet Gateway and the Office of Student Financial Aid.
The bill amends the Education Article regarding high school student FAFSA reporting and repeals the requirement for local school boards under MSDE's purview to collect and report this data directly.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the maximum Deferred Retirement Option Program participation period from 5 to 7 years for eligible law enforcement retirement systems. Expands eligibility for State Police Retirement System and Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System members with less than 32 years of service. Authorizes active program participants as of July 1, 2023, to elect to extend their participation. Requires members seeking an extension to submit an election form on or before December 31, 2023. Prohibits any extension that results in a member participating in the program past age 60.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System
qa_results.stakeholders: Members of the State Police Retirement System and Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System; local law enforcement agencies participating as governmental units
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State pension contributions decrease by $400,000 in FY 2025 ($220,000 for SPRS and $180,000 for LEOPS), with out-year savings reflecting actuarial assumptions. Local pension contributions for participating governmental units decrease by approximately $150,000 beginning in FY 2025. No effect on State or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS), which includes both the State Police Retirement System (SPRS) and the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System (LEOPS). The agency is directly responsible for implementing the alterations to the Deferred Retirement Option Program (DROP), processing DROP applications and extension elections, and managing pension liability and contribution calculations.

The bill directly impacts Maryland State Police officers participating in the State Police Retirement System (SPRS) by expanding DROP eligibility and participation limits from 5 to 7 years. Additionally, the Maryland State Police Secretary and Director of Human Resources are required to review and sign off on binding letters of resignation and DROP extension agreements.

As the State's central budget and personnel agency, DBM oversees state employee benefits and monitors statewide employer pension contribution rates, which are projected to decrease by $400,000 in FY 2025 and similar amounts in out-years due to the actuarial impact of the DROP extension.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes eligible customer-generators to accrue net excess generation indefinitely instead of only for up to 12 months. Excludes eligible customer-generators served by a municipal electric utility or an electric cooperative from indefinite accrual. Shifts the end of the standard 12-month net excess generation accrual cycle from April to August. Requires electric companies to pay customer-generators for remaining indefinitely accrued generation within 15 days of account closure. Directs the Public Service Commission to establish a valuation method for indefinitely accrued net excess generation. Allows community solar subscribers to accrue virtual net excess generation indefinitely and repeals the 200% baseline usage cap.
qa_results.responsible_party: Public Service Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: eligible customer-generators, community solar energy generating system subscribers, electric companies, municipal electric utilities, and electric cooperatives
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on state revenues. The Public Service Commission can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Public Service Commission with establishing a method to calculate the value of accrued net excess generation for customer-generators electing indefinite accrual, and oversees electric company net metering and community solar regulations.

The Office of the People's Counsel represents the interests of residential utility customers in proceedings before the Public Service Commission regarding electric utility rates, billing rules, and net metering tariffs.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the State Board of Social Work Examiners to issue conditional licenses for bachelor or master social work. Applies when administrative delays or unforeseen circumstances prevent examination availability for at least 15 business days. Limits eligibility to applicants who meet all education and experience requirements except passing the examination. Requires conditional licensees to practice exclusively under the supervision of a Board-approved supervisor. Establishes that a conditional license remains valid until 180 days after the examination becomes readily available. Mandates annual reports to the General Assembly on examination availability and conditional licensing beginning December 31, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Social Work Examiners
qa_results.stakeholders: Applicants for bachelor social work and master social work licenses, board-approved social work supervisors, and social work clients
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate increase in State Board of Social Work Examiners special fund revenues and expenditures beginning as early as fiscal 2024 if conditional licenses are issued. The FY 2024 state budget included $75,000 in general funds for board operations contingent on enactment of this bill or other legislation. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Social Work Examiners is a health occupations licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Health. MDH and the Board are directly responsible for implementing the bill's provisions, issuing conditional licenses to bachelor and master social workers during exam delays, and submitting required annual reports.

As the state's primary social services agency, DHS employs a large workforce of bachelor- and master-level social workers across local departments; provisions allowing conditional licensure during examination delays directly affect the onboarding and practice eligibility of DHS caseworkers and staff.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to develop and implement a public awareness campaign encouraging mental health advance directives. Mandates outreach initiatives supporting state agencies, local health authorities, health care facilities, academic institutions, and religious organizations. Requires the Behavioral Health Administration and Maryland Health Care Commission jointly to study database access for crisis responders. Directs both entities to report their study findings to specified legislative committees by December 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Behavioral Health Administration; Maryland Health Care Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals receiving or seeking mental health services and their families, behavioral health providers, and emergency first responders
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $140,700 in FY 2024 for the Maryland Department of Health to hire one program manager and procure campaign materials. Ongoing expenditures range between $87,400 and $100,400 annually. Local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is the primary implementing agency tasked with developing and executing the statewide public awareness campaign regarding mental health advance directives. Additionally, its Behavioral Health Administration (BHA) must jointly conduct a study and report on database access for first responders.

MHCC is required to collaborate jointly with the Behavioral Health Administration to study how first responders and crisis providers can access the advance directives database and submit a report of findings to the General Assembly.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is specifically designated in the bill to participate in outreach and awareness initiatives for mental health advance directives, and has potential operational adjustments regarding mental health services in correctional facilities.
The Maryland State Police is specifically enumerated in the statute to support and engage in outreach initiatives to inform individuals about mental health advance directives.

The department (referenced in the bill as the Department of Veterans Affairs) is specifically designated to take part in outreach efforts to inform veterans and their families about mental health advance directives.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Governor to include a $500,000 appropriation in the annual budget bill for fiscal years 2025 through 2028. Directs these funds to the Prince George's County Office of the County Executive. Mandates that the funding support the Prince George's County Reentry Employment Incentive Program. Prohibits these funds from supplanting other funding available for reentry employment incentives in the county. Terminates the statutory funding mandate on June 30, 2028.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor; Prince George's County Office of the County Executive
qa_results.stakeholders: Prince George's County government, formerly incarcerated county residents seeking employment, and employers participating in the Prince George's County Reentry Employment Incentive Program
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $500,000 annually from FY 2025 through FY 2028 for the mandated appropriation. Prince George's County revenues and expenditures increase by matching amounts of $500,000 annually over the same period as grant funds are received and distributed.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Governor to include an appropriation of $500,000 in the annual budget bill for fiscal years 2025 through 2028 for the Prince George's County Reentry Employment Incentive Program.

As the agency responsible for preparing and supervising the annual state budget on behalf of the Governor, DBM must incorporate and manage this $500,000 statutory mandated appropriation from FY 2025 through FY 2028.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the Maryland Aviation Commission from nine to 13 voting members. Requires two gubernatorial appointees recommended by the Anne Arundel County Senate delegation and two by Howard County. Directs the Commission to establish policies mitigating negative impacts of local aviation and airport industries. Requires the Commission to consider advice from airport employees, local governments, and nearby communities. Mandates member orientation and subjects the Commission to enhanced Open Meetings Act livestreaming requirements. Expands the annual report to include community health impacts and mitigation initiatives.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Aviation Commission; Maryland Department of Transportation
qa_results.stakeholders: Communities near State-owned airports, airport workers and their representatives, local governments in Anne Arundel and Howard counties, and aviation industry stakeholders
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund expenditures may increase minimally for the Maryland Aviation Commission to comply with enhanced Open Meetings Act requirements. Special fund revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Aviation Commission directly oversees and directs the Maryland Aviation Administration in developing airport management policy, approving regulations, and establishing policies for State-owned airports such as BWI Thurgood Marshall Airport.

The Maryland Secretary of Transportation serves as the Chairman of the Maryland Aviation Commission, and MAA is a modal administration under MDOT. The fiscal note also notes potential minimal expenditures from the Transportation Trust Fund.
The Governor is responsible for appointing 12 members to the Maryland Aviation Commission with the advice and consent of the Senate, subject to newly specified recommendation and experience criteria.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and processing candidates for state boards and commissions, which includes the four additional seats and specific delegation recommendations for the Maryland Aviation Commission.
The Secretary of Commerce is designated by statute to serve as an ex officio, nonvoting member of the Maryland Aviation Commission.
The Commission's annual estimate of operating expenditures included in its report to the General Assembly is subject to review by the Department of Budget and Management.

qa_results.bill_summary: Clarifies the statutory General Fund mandate calculation for the Maryland State Arts Council beginning in fiscal year 2025. Requires the Governor to include a mandated General Fund appropriation in the annual budget bill using a specified formula. Calculates the appropriation using prior-year admissions and amusement tax distributions increased by the General Fund growth adjustment. Adds the prior-year General Fund appropriation adjusted for growth and subtracts the prior-year tax distributions. Repeals an uncodified requirement that previously included those tax distributions in the prior fiscal year appropriation.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor; Department of Budget and Management; Maryland State Arts Council
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland State Arts Council, arts organizations, and individual artist grant recipients
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State expenditures or revenues, assuming the Department of Budget and Management continues its current interpretation and calculation methodology. Local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Arts Council (MSAC) operates within the Department of Commerce, and this bill directly alters and clarifies the statutory formula governing MSAC's annual mandated General Fund appropriation.

DBM is responsible for calculating and preparing the Governor's annual budget bill, and the bill codifies and clarifies DBM's interpretation and methodology for calculating MSAC's mandated funding appropriation.
The bill mandates that the Governor include a specific calculated General Fund appropriation for the Maryland State Arts Council in the annual state budget bill.
The Comptroller collects and distributes the admissions and amusement tax revenues under § 2-202 of the Tax - General Article that are integrated into MSAC's statutory funding formula.
The bill reaffirms statutory authority for the Legislative Auditor to conduct audits and reviews of grant recipients from the Maryland State Arts Council.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Task Force to Study Crime Classification. Requires the task force to study and recommend a method for classifying crimes and civil offenses under State law. Directs the task force to identify and logically categorize all existing State crimes and civil offenses. Requires the Office of the Attorney General to provide staff for the task force. Mandates reporting of findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly by December 31, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General; Task Force to Study Crime Classification
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals charged with civil or criminal offenses in Maryland, crime victims, criminal justice practitioners, and legal professionals
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $177,400 in FY 2024 only for contractual staffing within the Office of the Attorney General. Task force expense reimbursements are minimal and absorbable within existing budgeted resources. Revenues and local governments are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General is named as a member of the Task Force, is required to provide primary staff support, and incurs a direct fiscal impact of at least $177,400 in FY 2024 to hire contractual personnel.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Defender, or the Public Defender's designee, is designated as a formal voting member of the Task Force to Study Crime Classification.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a temporary state body, the Task Force to Study Crime Classification, tasked with studying and making recommendations regarding the classification and categorization of crimes and civil offenses in Maryland.
The Task Force is required to report its findings and recommendations regarding crime and civil offense classification directly to the Governor on or before December 31, 2023.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of the Environment's Office of Recycling to hire an independent consultant for a statewide recycling needs assessment. Directs the Office of Recycling to report the assessment results to the Governor and the General Assembly by July 30, 2024. Requires the Department to approve a single producer responsibility organization to represent producers by October 1, 2023. Establishes a Producer Responsibility Plan Advisory Council to recommend policies for a packaging materials producer responsibility program. Requires the Advisory Council to report findings and recommendations to the Governor and specified legislative committees by December 1, 2024. Alters the definition of organics recycling to include processing compostable packaging materials.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment; Office of Recycling
qa_results.stakeholders: producers of packaging materials, local governments, recycling and composting processors, solid waste collectors, and Maryland residents
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $532,100 in FY 2024 and $12,100 in FY 2025 to fund an independent consultant and a part-time contractual employee. State and local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Maryland Department of the Environment's Office of Recycling with procuring an independent consultant to conduct a statewide recycling needs assessment, approving a single producer responsibility organization, providing staff support to the newly established advisory council, and submitting required reports.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new state advisory body, the Producer Responsibility Plan Advisory Council, charged with providing advice, evaluating policies, and reporting recommendations on establishing an extended producer responsibility program for packaging materials in Maryland.

The Governor's Office receives the required reports on the results of the statewide recycling needs assessment by July 30, 2024, and the findings and recommendations of the Producer Responsibility Plan Advisory Council by December 1, 2024.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits a person from knowingly or intentionally accessing and intentionally viewing certain visual representations of child pornography. Covers depictions of actual children or indistinguishable computer-generated images of children under 16 years of age. Applies to depictions involving sadomasochistic abuse, sexual conduct, or sexual excitement. Establishes a misdemeanor penalty of up to five years imprisonment, a $2,500 fine, or both for first offenses. Classifies repeat offenses as a felony punishable by up to 10 years imprisonment, a $10,000 fine, or both. Maintains existing affirmative defenses for individuals who promptly destroy representations or report them to law enforcement.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals charged with or convicted of child pornography offenses; victims of child sexual exploitation; state and local law enforcement agencies; state and local correctional facilities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in State and local revenues and expenditures resulting from expanded application of existing criminal fines and incarceration penalties.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands criminal offenses under child pornography laws, subjecting convicted individuals to imprisonment in State correctional facilities for up to 5 years (misdemeanor) or 10 years (subsequent felony), resulting in a fiscal and operational impact on state incarceration resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands the scope of criminal acts related to viewing and accessing child pornography, which will require OPD to provide legal representation for indigent individuals charged under this statute.
The bill introduces new punishable misdemeanor and felony offenses to be adjudicated in the District Court and Circuit Courts, affecting judicial caseloads and court fee/fine administration.

As the primary state law enforcement agency responsible for investigating criminal violations and digital crimes, MSP investigates child exploitation offenses and receives reports referenced under the statute's affirmative defense provisions.
The OAG represents the State in civil and criminal appeals resulting from convictions under Maryland's criminal laws, including prosecutions brought under expanded child exploitation statutes.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program coverage to domestic partners. Construes statutory terms denoting spousal relationships to include a party to a domestic partnership. Applies all Program provisions that govern spouses to individuals in domestic partnerships. Requires domestic partnerships to satisfy defined statutory criteria under the Health – General Article. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Budget and Management
qa_results.stakeholders: State employees, State retirees, and their domestic partners and dependents
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate increase in State expenditures for the Department of Budget and Management beginning in FY 2024 to provide health and welfare benefits for additional enrollees and update administrative and payroll systems; local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DBM administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program through its Employee Benefits Division. The bill directly requires DBM to extend health and welfare benefits to domestic partners of state employees and retirees, necessitating system updates for eligibility and payroll deductions and resulting in increased state benefit expenditures.

As the agency that pays state employees and administers state payroll via the Central Payroll Bureau, the Comptroller may coordinate with DBM on post-tax payroll deductions and imputed income reporting on W-2 forms for domestic partner health benefits.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires resident taxpayers to add back certain tax credits when calculating Maryland adjusted gross income. Applies the addition modification to credits claimed for income taxes imposed on pass-through entities by other states. Covers out-of-state taxes that are deductible in determining the entity's income under the Internal Revenue Code. Takes effect July 1, 2023, and applies to all taxable years beginning after December 31, 2022.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland resident members of pass-through entities paying income taxes to other states
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues and local income tax revenues may increase beginning in fiscal 2024 due to added tax liability; specific estimates are unavailable. State and local expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill was requested by the Office of the Comptroller and directly impacts the administration, collection, and enforcement of state income taxes by creating an addition modification for certain credits claimed for taxes paid by pass-through entities to other states.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Comptroller to determine within one year of delivery whether nonmonetary abandoned property has commercial value. Authorizes the Comptroller to decline offering property for sale if it lacks commercial value. Permits the Comptroller to return, destroy, or otherwise dispose of property not offered for sale. Repeals the requirement to publish advance notice of sales in a local newspaper. Requires the Comptroller to give reasonable notice to the public before any sale.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Holders of abandoned property, previous owners of unclaimed property, auction purchasers, and the general public
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected, though the Comptroller may realize operational efficiencies and savings from reduced property storage costs. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller serves as the Administrator of abandoned and unclaimed property in Maryland. The bill directly alters the Comptroller's statutory duties by establishing procedures to assess the commercial value of nonmonetary abandoned property, authorize its disposal or destruction if it lacks commercial value, and update public notice requirements for auctions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Corrects an erroneous statutory cross-reference to the federal Internal Revenue Code regarding the federal work opportunity credit. Updates the cross-reference within the definition from Section 51 to Section 38 of the Internal Revenue Code. Clarifies eligibility for employers and not-for-profit entities claiming the State income tax credit. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Employers and not-for-profit entities claiming the Maryland Work Opportunity Tax Credit for qualified employees
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State or local finances because the bill makes only technical corrections.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This departmental bill was introduced at the request of the Office of the Comptroller to correct a technical cross-reference to the Internal Revenue Code regarding the Maryland Work Opportunity Tax Credit, which the Comptroller administers as the state's chief tax collection authority.

qa_results.bill_summary: Limits eligibility for the State child and dependent care tax credit to resident taxpayers. Defines a taxpayer as an individual or married couple filing a joint income tax return. Prohibits nonresident taxpayers from claiming the credit for qualifying dependent care expenses. Applies the restriction to all taxable years beginning after December 31, 2022. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Comptroller
qa_results.stakeholders: Nonresident income tax filers who incur qualifying child and dependent care expenses
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues increase by an estimated $332,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2024 due to the elimination of the credit for nonresident taxpayers. Expenditures are unaffected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This is a departmental bill introduced at the request of the Office of the Comptroller. As the state's tax administration and revenue collection agency, the Comptroller is responsible for implementing the altered eligibility criteria for the child and dependent care income tax credit, adjusting tax forms and filing instructions, and processing returns.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the mandated annual appropriation for the National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund to $12,000,000 beginning in fiscal 2025. Requires the Governor to include this appropriation in the annual operating or capital budget. Restricts fund use to community enhancement projects within specified sustainable communities in Montgomery and Prince George's counties. Repeals a scheduled requirement limiting fund use starting in fiscal 2024 to areas inside Interstate 495. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: community development organizations, local governments, housing authority entities, and small businesses in designated sustainable communities in Montgomery County and Prince George's County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State pay-as-you-go general fund or general obligation bond expenditures increase by $5.0 million annually beginning in fiscal 2025 to meet the increased mandated appropriation. Special fund revenues and expenditures increase commensurately by $5.0 million annually. Local government revenues and expenditures increase to the extent eligible local jurisdictions receive additional program funding.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) is the primary implementing agency that administers the National Capital Strategic Economic Development Program and Fund, overseeing the disbursement of funds for community enhancement projects in eligible sustainable communities.

The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for preparing and supervising the execution of the annual state budget, which must accommodate the bill's increased statutory mandated annual appropriation of $12 million starting in fiscal year 2025.
The bill mandates that the Governor include an increased annual appropriation of $12 million in the operating or capital budget for the fund beginning in fiscal year 2025.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes that a sheriff's sale of real property extinguishes any subordinate lien or interest on the land sold. Requires judgment creditors to send notice of execution sales to property owners, occupants, and subordinate interest holders. Permits sheriffs to use assessment records instead of appraisals when levying on certain real property. Protects local government judgment liens for property maintenance or nuisance violations from debtor exemption claims. Authorizes the Judiciary to transfer up to $12,000,000 to the Circuit Court Real Property Records Improvement Fund.
qa_results.responsible_party: Judiciary; county sheriffs
qa_results.stakeholders: judgment creditors, judgment debtors, real property owners, subordinate lienholders, occupants of levied properties, and local governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues for the Circuit Court Real Property Records Improvement Fund increase by up to $12.0 million in fiscal 2023, offset by an equivalent general fund revenue decrease from the authorized transfer of Judiciary appropriations. Local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Maryland Judiciary and the Administrative Office of the Courts by altering statutory court procedures for money judgments and sheriff's sales of real property (including required court filings and affidavits). Additionally, it specifically authorizes the Judiciary to transfer up to $12.0 million of its FY 2023 General Fund appropriation to the Circuit Court Real Property Records Improvement Fund, which is managed and supervised by the State Court Administrator.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the investigative jurisdiction of the Independent Investigations Division within the Office of the Attorney General. Grants the Attorney General exclusive authority to prosecute criminal offenses discovered during Division investigations. Permits a State's Attorney to prosecute only if requested by the Attorney General. Authorizes State's Attorneys to refer police-involved incidents causing serious bodily injury to the Division. Repeals the requirement that the Division submit investigative reports to local State's Attorneys. Requires the Division to submit an annual activity report to the Governor and General Assembly by January 31.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General; Independent Investigations Division
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland law enforcement agencies; police officers; individuals involved in police-involved incidents; State's Attorneys
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $548,900 in FY 2024 to hire four personnel, increasing to $729,700 by FY 2028. State revenues are not affected. Local finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly concerns the Independent Investigations Division (IID) within the Office of the Attorney General, expanding its investigative jurisdiction and granting the Attorney General exclusive prosecutorial authority over certain police-involved incidents. It also carries a direct fiscal impact requiring additional staff and funding for the agency.

The statute explicitly authorizes the IID to detail police officers employed by the Department of State Police to investigate alleged criminal offenses committed by police officers, and MSP is also subject to the mandatory incident reporting and investigation cooperation requirements.

The bill requires the IID to submit an annual report of its activities to the Governor by January 31 each year and mandates that the Governor include sufficient funding in the State budget for the operation of the Division.

The bill involves judicial procedures including the issuance and enforcement of subpoenas in circuit courts, applications for injunctive relief, grand jury utilization, and court prosecutions handled by the Attorney General.

qa_results.bill_summary: Replaces the statutory term "inmate" with "incarcerated individual" throughout the Annotated Code of Maryland. Renames inmates as incarcerated individuals in every State law, executive order, rule, regulation, policy, and document. Directs code publishers to correct cross-references and terminology rendered incorrect by the Act. Requires publishers to consult with and receive approval from the Department of Legislative Services. Mandates that publishers describe any correction in an editor's note following the affected section.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Legislative Services; publishers of the Annotated Code of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals confined in State and local correctional facilities; State officials, employees, and units
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is the primary state department administering correctional facilities and supervising justice-involved individuals. The bill directly alters the statutory definition of an individual confined in a correctional facility from 'inmate' to 'incarcerated individual' in the Correctional Services Article and requires state correctional policies, regulations, and documents to adopt this terminology.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the County Commissioners of Carroll County to borrow up to $65,600,000 by issuing general obligation bonds. Directs bond proceeds to finance public facilities, water and sewer projects, and loans to volunteer fire departments. Permits borrowing via installment purchase obligations to acquire agricultural land and woodland preservation easements. Requires bond maturities not to exceed 30 years from the date of issue. Mandates the county levy sufficient annual ad valorem property taxes to pay bond principal and interest. Takes effect June 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: County Commissioners of Carroll County
qa_results.stakeholders: Carroll County residents, property owners in Carroll County, and volunteer fire departments in Carroll County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Carroll County bond revenues increase by up to $65.6 million, with county debt service expenditures increasing by an estimated $4.4 million annually over a 20-year period.

qa_results.bill_summary: Renames the Black Bear Damage Reimbursement Fund to the Black Bear Damage Prevention and Reimbursement Fund. Requires the Department of Natural Resources to award grants for projects preventing black bear damage through nonlethal methods. Caps grant funding to leave at least 10% of annual appropriations available for damage reimbursements. Increases the maximum annual black bear damage reimbursement per person from $3,000 to $5,000. Prohibits grant awards for lethal bear removal, stand-alone research, or direct revenue generation. Authorizes the Governor to include an annual budget bill appropriation of at least $50,000 to the fund.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Farmers, landowners, local governments, parks and recreation departments, businesses, tribes, institutions of higher education, and nonprofit organizations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $145,600 in FY 2024, which includes $95,637 for Department of Natural Resources personnel and administrative costs alongside $50,000 in discretionary fund capitalization. Special fund revenues and expenditures increase correspondingly by $50,000 annually. Local governments and higher education institutions may experience indeterminate increases in grant revenues and operational expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR is the primary agency responsible for administering the Black Bear Damage Prevention and Reimbursement Fund, establishing and managing the new nonlethal conflict prevention grant program, verifying bear damage claims, and issuing reimbursements.

Statute requires damage amounts to be determined by extension agents of the University of Maryland Cooperative Extension Service before reimbursements can be made. Additionally, institutions of higher education are eligible grant recipients under the fund.
The statute explicitly mandates that the State Comptroller shall account for the Black Bear Damage Prevention and Reimbursement Fund.
The statute explicitly mandates that the State Treasurer shall hold the Black Bear Damage Prevention and Reimbursement Fund.
The bill authorizes the Governor to include an appropriation of at least $50,000 to the fund in the annual state budget bill.
As a public institution of higher education, Morgan State University is an eligible entity to apply for and receive project grant funding under the expanded fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Class 4 limited winery license holders to prepare, sell, or serve sandwiches and other ready-to-eat light fare. Permits wineries licensed as food establishments to serve additional foods under specified gross receipt ratios. Extends daily operating hours for on-premises consumption and food sales until 10:00 p.m. each day. Repeals the requirement to give the Comptroller advance notice before holding planned promotional events.
qa_results.responsible_party: Alcohol and Tobacco Commission; local licensing boards
qa_results.stakeholders: Class 4 limited winery license holders and winery patrons in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State or local government finances. Small business revenues for Class 4 limited winery licensees may increase due to expanded food service allowances and extended operating hours.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller regulates the alcohol industry in Maryland. The bill directly alters regulatory requirements for Class 4 limited wineries, including repealing the requirement that licensees submit advance notice of certain promotional events to the Comptroller and referencing the Comptroller's oversight of wine storage and reporting.

Class 4 limited wineries must produce wine from Maryland agricultural products and meet fruit cultivation requirements under § 2-206 of the Alcoholic Beverages Article, which authorizes the Secretary of Agriculture to grant percentage exemptions and adopt regulations governing exemptions.

The bill allows wineries to serve and prepare expanded food menus if they obtain a food establishment license under Title 21, Subtitle 3 of the Health - General Article, which is overseen and regulated by the Maryland Department of Health and local health departments.

qa_results.bill_summary: Sets the salary of the Washington County Sheriff at 90% of the salary of the county State's Attorney. Repeals the requirement for the Washington County Salary Study Commission to study and recommend the sheriff's salary. Applies the compensation alteration to the next term of office following the effective date. Allows an individual appointed or elected to fill an unexpired term after the effective date to receive the salary. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Washington County Commissioners; Washington County Salary Study Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Sheriff of Washington County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. Washington County expenditures increase by a minimum of $21,100 in fiscal 2027 and $36,200 annually thereafter to fund the sheriff's increased salary.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of General Services to negotiate third-party body-worn camera contracts upon law enforcement agency request. Requires the Department of General Services to coordinate these contract negotiations with the Department of Information Technology. Requires the Department of General Services to notify law enforcement agencies by posting contracts on eMaryland Marketplace Advantage. Prohibits restricting any law enforcement agency from receiving third-party services to view, edit, redact, or transfer camera data. Requires the Department of Information Technology to study a statewide uniform camera data storage and access system. Requires the Department of Information Technology to report study findings to specified legislative committees by December 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of General Services; Department of Information Technology
qa_results.stakeholders: State, county, and municipal law enforcement agencies; third-party vendors of body-worn cameras and related technology
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by between $200,000 and $400,000 in FY 2024 only for the Department of Information Technology to hire a consultant for the feasibility study, though costs may be mitigated by relevant prior studies. The Department of General Services and the Department of Information Technology can otherwise implement the bill with existing resources. State and local law enforcement agencies may achieve indeterminate administrative efficiencies.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DGS is a primary implementing agency tasked with negotiating third-party contracts for body-worn cameras, equipment, and technology on behalf of law enforcement agencies, posting them on eMaryland Marketplace Advantage, and coordinating with DoIT on the statewide data storage and access feasibility study.

DoIT is directly tasked with conducting a feasibility and cost study regarding a statewide uniform storage and access system for body-worn camera data, reporting findings to legislative committees, and coordinating contract negotiations with DGS, resulting in a direct fiscal impact of up to $400,000.

As the primary state law enforcement agency subject to body-worn camera mandates, MSP is directly impacted as a beneficiary that can request and utilize contracts negotiated by DGS and will be affected by statewide storage and access systems.
DNR operates the Natural Resources Police, an authorized state law enforcement agency that may request DGS to negotiate contracts for body-worn camera acquisition and maintenance.

MDOT oversees state transportation police forces (such as the Maryland Transportation Authority Police and Maryland Transit Administration Police) that qualify as law enforcement agencies eligible to utilize the negotiated procurement contracts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS employs law enforcement and correctional security personnel and is an affected state agency that can benefit from administrative efficiencies under the negotiated body-worn camera contracts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP previously commissioned a relevant feasibility study on body-worn camera costs and data storage, which may provide data to mitigate DoIT study costs and align with the office's criminal justice coordination role.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the membership of the West North Avenue Development Authority in Baltimore City. Adds state economic officials and authority-appointed members to the governing body. Delays the reporting deadline for the comprehensive neighborhood revitalization strategy to December 15, 2023. Requires the revitalization report to include procurement activities undertaken by the authority. Exempts the authority from general state procurement law while retaining minority business enterprise requirements. Terminates the procurement exemption on September 30, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: West North Avenue Development Authority
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents and business owners in the West North Avenue target area and buffer zone in Baltimore City, minority business enterprises, and state contractors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances are not materially affected. The authority will use existing funds to cover an estimated $250,000 expedited contract to complete the revitalization strategy.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly adds the Secretary of Commerce (or the Secretary's designee) as a voting member of the West North Avenue Development Authority.
The bill explicitly adds the Executive Director of the Maryland Economic Development Corporation (or the Executive Director's designee) as a member of the West North Avenue Development Authority.

The Secretary of Housing and Community Development serves on the West North Avenue Development Authority, which is charged with developing a comprehensive neighborhood revitalization plan and housing strategies.
The Secretary of Transportation serves on the Authority, and MDOT serves as the certifying agency for the Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) program to which the Authority remains subject.
The President of Coppin State University, a member institution of the University System of Maryland, serves as the Chair of the Authority and is granted authority to appoint two additional members.
As the state's central procurement authority, DGS is impacted by the provision granting the Authority an exemption from Division II of the State Finance and Procurement Article.
Exempting the Authority from Division II of the State Finance and Procurement Article removes standard procurement oversight and approval mechanisms normally required under the Board of Public Works.
The Governor appoints a member to the Authority and receives the required comprehensive neighborhood revitalization strategy report.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Authority remains specifically subject to the State's Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) program under Title 14, Subtitle 3, which is coordinated and monitored by this office.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes procedures for who may open an ABLE account and request distributions on behalf of an eligible individual. Permits an account to be established by the eligible individual, a selected representative, or designated family members and fiduciaries in a specific priority order. Excludes minors, individuals subject to protective or no-contact orders, and individuals liable for financial exploitation from opening accounts. Authorizes authorized account establishers to request distributions alongside designated beneficiaries. Requires the Maryland 529 Board to adopt procedures for account establishment and operation by authorized third parties.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland 529 Board
qa_results.stakeholders: Eligible individuals with disabilities, their families, legal guardians, and authorized representatives under the Maryland ABLE Program.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues and local revenues may decrease, potentially significantly, beginning in FY 2024 due to additional income tax subtraction modifications. Maryland 529 nonbudgeted fee revenues and distribution expenditures increase with new accounts. State general fund expenditures may decrease if fee revenues offset the existing $300,000 annual State grant to the Maryland ABLE Program.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the governing statutes of the Maryland ABLE Program, which is administered by Maryland 529, establishing procedures and regulatory authority regarding who may establish accounts and receive distributions.
The State Treasurer's Office oversees the Maryland 529 program and its components, including the Maryland ABLE program, making it directly responsible for administrative oversight and implementation.

The bill is projected to impact State personal income tax revenues collected by the Comptroller due to additional subtraction modifications claimed for contributions to and distributions from newly opened ABLE accounts.
The Department of Disabilities works in consultation with Maryland 529 to administer and promote the ABLE program to eligible Maryland residents with disabilities.
The Maryland Department of Health oversees Medicaid and means-tested health programs, for which assets held in ABLE accounts are protected from eligibility determinations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Affordable Life, Wills, and Estate Planning for Seniors Grant Program in the Maryland Legal Services Corporation. Serves clients at least 65 years old with family incomes up to 75% of State median family income. Requires an intake method, outreach mechanisms, and grants to fund legal representation, particularly in rural communities. Primarily covers last will and testaments, powers of attorney, special needs trusts, advance health care directives, and life estate deeds. Mandates an annual State budget appropriation of $225,000 for the program.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Legal Services Corporation
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland seniors aged 65 and older with family incomes up to 75% of the State median family income, and civil legal service grantees
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $225,000 annually beginning in FY 2024, with funding in FY 2024 being discretionary and reflecting a mandated appropriation beginning in FY 2025. Revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the Governor include a $225,000 appropriation for the program in the annual state budget and requires the Maryland Legal Services Corporation to submit an annual report to the Governor detailing the program's implementation and utilization.
As the agency responsible for state budget preparation and fiscal management, DBM must account for and execute the mandated annual general fund appropriation of $225,000 established by the bill.

The program is specifically targeted at Maryland residents aged 65 and older, directly intersecting with the Department of Aging's mission to support older adults' legal advocacy, rights, and access to essential life-planning services.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to apply for federal grant funds for certified community behavioral health clinics. Directs the department to apply to the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration at the Center for Mental Health Services. Mandates submitting the planning, development, and implementation grant application for fiscal year 2025. Requires applying for inclusion in the state certified community behavioral health clinic demonstration program for fiscal year 2026. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Certified community behavioral health clinics, community behavioral health care providers, and individuals seeking mental health or substance use treatment services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No net impact on state or local finances. The Maryland Department of Health can apply for federal grant funds and demonstration program inclusion using existing budgeted resources. Federal planning grant revenues in fiscal 2025 were already anticipated under current operations, and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Senate Bill 362 specifically mandates that the Maryland Department of Health apply to SAMHSA for federal planning, development, and implementation grant funds for FY 2025 and for inclusion in the federal CCBHC demonstration program for FY 2026.

qa_results.bill_summary: Defines "commercial use" under Baltimore City zoning law to include certain multifamily residential developments. Applies this classification to multifamily residential development located within a waterfront commercial zoning district. Requires the development to also be located within a 0.50-mile radius of a commuter rail station. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City; Baltimore City Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals
qa_results.stakeholders: Commercial and residential property developers, landowners, and residents in Baltimore City within waterfront commercial zoning districts near commuter rail stations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to directly affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 371 amends Title 10 of the Land Use Article regarding Baltimore City zoning definitions to classify certain transit-oriented, waterfront multifamily residential developments as commercial use. The Maryland Department of Planning oversees state land use policy and assists local jurisdictions with comprehensive planning.

The bill alters land use definitions to facilitate multifamily residential development in waterfront commercial zoning districts near commuter rail stations, directly interacting with housing development patterns and community revitalization policies overseen by DHCD.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the State Board of Physicians to place a qualifying licensee on emeritus status upon application and fee payment. Exempts physicians on inactive or emeritus status from license expiration terms and continuing medical education requirements. Prohibits licensees on inactive or emeritus status from practicing medicine or delegating medical acts. Permits emeritus status licensees to use titles such as doctor or physician without representing authorization to practice. Requires the Board to reinstate an inactive or emeritus license upon satisfaction of renewal conditions and fee payment.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Physicians
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland-licensed physicians, retired physicians seeking emeritus status, and physicians on inactive status
