qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Board of Physicians workload can be absorbed with existing budgeted resources. Any net impact on special fund revenues from emeritus or inactive status licensee fees is anticipated to be minimal, with no effect on local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Board of Physicians (MBP) is an operating unit and health occupations licensing board within the Maryland Department of Health. The bill directly impacts MDH/MBP operations by establishing rules, fee structures, and application procedures for physician emeritus and inactive status.

qa_results.bill_summary: Limits workers' compensation benefit offsets for covered employees of governmental units or quasi-public corporations. Applies the offset only when employer-paid benefits and workers' compensation benefits cover the same body part. Abrogates the Maryland Supreme Court holding in Spevak v. Montgomery County. Requires application of the offset consistent with Reger v. Washington County Board of Education. Directs local government and firefighter associations to jointly research and report findings by December 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Workers' Compensation Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Covered employees of Maryland governmental units and quasi-public corporations, local governments, the Subsequent Injury Fund, and Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State finances or operations. Local government expenditures likely increase due to higher workers' compensation payouts from narrowed benefit offsets, but specific figures cannot be reliably estimated. Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company expenditures and premium revenues increase correspondingly.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Commission is the independent state agency responsible for administering the Workers' Compensation Law and adjudicating claims, and the bill directly governs its authority under Section 9-610 to determine benefit offsets and make awards.

The Subsequent Injury Fund is explicitly amended in Section 9-610, which alters the circumstances under which municipal or quasi-public benefit payments satisfy the fund's statutory liability for workers' compensation benefits.

Operating as Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company, the entity is directly impacted fiscally as an insurer of local government entities, resulting in increased benefit payouts and adjusted premiums.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the voting and nonvoting membership of the Upper Shore Regional Council. Removes the requirement that three Cecil County commissioners serve as voting members. Designates the Cecil County Executive and two Cecil County Council members as voting members. Requires the Cecil County Council to appoint the two voting council members. Adds unappointed regional county council members as nonvoting members of the council.
qa_results.responsible_party: Upper Shore Regional Council
qa_results.stakeholders: Cecil County Executive, Cecil County Council members, and the Upper Shore Regional Council
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. Minimal local fiscal impact, as the bill alters county representation without changing overall voting membership numbers.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the statutory composition and membership of the Upper Shore Regional Council, an entity encompassed under state regional councils and advisory bodies.

The Upper Shore Regional Council is established under the Economic Development Article to foster regional economic development and coordinate with the Department of Commerce, which was consulted as an information source for the bill.
The Upper Shore Regional Council is one of the five rural regional planning and development councils that partner with and receive support through the Rural Maryland Council.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the County Executive and County Council of Prince George’s County to determine annual compensation for judges of the Orphans’ Court. Repeals fixed statutory salaries of $50,000 for associate judges and $55,000 for the Chief Judge. Prohibits applying compensation changes during a term of office that began before October 1, 2023. Permits compensation changes to take effect at the beginning of a judge’s subsequent term of office. Authorizes salary changes for judges appointed or elected after the effective date to fill an unexpired term.
qa_results.responsible_party: Prince George's County Executive; Prince George's County Council
qa_results.stakeholders: Judges of the Orphans' Court for Prince George's County; Prince George's County government
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Potential indeterminate increase or decrease in Prince George's County expenditures beginning in fiscal 2027 depending on salary determinations by local officials. Local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Administrative Office of the Courts provides administrative and operational support to the Maryland Judicial Branch, of which the county Orphans' Courts are a specialized component.

The Register of Wills serves as the clerk to the Orphans' Court in each county, maintaining probate proceedings and working directly with the Orphans' Court judges whose compensation is affected by this bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Commission to Advance and Strengthen Fire Fighting and Emergency Medical Services Within Maryland. Directs the Commission to study practices and incentives used in other states to attract and retain personnel. Requires the Commission to evaluate the suitability of those practices for Maryland. Mandates that the Maryland Department of Labor provide staff support for the Commission. Requires the Commission to report findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Commission to Advance and Strengthen Fire Fighting and Emergency Medical Services Within Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Career and volunteer firefighters, emergency medical services personnel, and local fire companies in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $25,000 in FY 2024 only for one part-time contractual employee at the Maryland Department of Labor. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor is directly responsible for staffing the Commission to Advance and Strengthen Fire Fighting and Emergency Medical Services Within Maryland, has a representative appointed by the Secretary of Labor serving on the Commission, and incurs a fiscal impact of approximately $25,000 to hire staff.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Executive Director of the Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems (MIEMSS), or their designee, is designated as a mandatory member of the Commission.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally creates a temporary study body—the Commission to Advance and Strengthen Fire Fighting and Emergency Medical Services Within Maryland—to evaluate recruitment and retention policies and report recommendations.
The Executive Director of the Maryland Fire and Rescue Institute (MFRI), which is a branch of the University of Maryland, is designated as a member of the Commission.

The newly created Commission is required to report its findings and recommendations regarding fire fighting and emergency medical services incentives and retention directly to the Governor by December 1, 2023.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the University System of Maryland Board of Regents to transfer up to $150,000,000 to establish a quasi-endowment fund. Requires the transferred funds to come from balances held and invested by the State Treasurer. Authorizes the Board to use investment income from the fund for need-based student financial aid. Requires financial aid spending to follow the University System of Maryland Policy on Endowment Fund Spending Rule.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Regents of the University System of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: University System of Maryland students with financial need; University System of Maryland constituent institutions
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Assuming transfers of $150.0 million occur in FY 2024, University System of Maryland fund balances decrease by $150.0 million with an offsetting increase in quasi-endowment funds. Higher education revenues may increase by an estimated $1.6 million annually beginning in FY 2025 from higher investment yields, and scholarship expenditures may increase by about $6.4 million annually, though returns will vary with market conditions. No local effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the University System of Maryland (USM) Board of Regents, authorizing the transfer of up to $150 million from fund balances to establish a quasi-endowment fund and directing the use of investment proceeds for need-based student financial aid.

The authorized transfers of up to $150 million come directly from fund balances held and invested by the State Treasurer, impacting Treasurer-held investment balances. The agency also receives an annual investment performance report.
The Comptroller of Maryland is designated by statute to receive an annual investment performance report on the university's gift, endowment, and quasi-endowment investment portfolio.
The Governor's Office receives the required annual investment performance report submitted by the USM Board of Regents.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the minimum balance of the Home Improvement Guaranty Fund from $250,000 to $1,000,000. Raises the maximum award to all claimants for a single contractor's acts or omissions from $100,000 to $250,000. Requires the Maryland Home Improvement Commission to assess each contractor $50 if pending claims threaten that $1,000,000 threshold. Requires the Commission to submit a restoration report to legislative committees within 30 days of projecting a balance under $1,000,000. Authorizes proportionate claim payments when approved claims against a contractor exceed $250,000 less prior unreimbursed payments.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Home Improvement Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: licensed home improvement contractors and residential property owners seeking compensation for actual losses from contractor acts or omissions
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Nonbudgeted revenues and expenditures for the Home Improvement Guaranty Fund increase by an indeterminate, but likely significant amount due to higher minimum fund balance requirements and increased claim payout limits. Commission operations can be implemented with existing budgeted resources. Local governments are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Home Improvement Commission (MHIC) is a regulatory unit within the Maryland Department of Labor. The bill directly alters the statutory minimum balance of the Home Improvement Guaranty Fund administered by MHIC, raises the threshold for mandatory contractor assessments, and increases the maximum award limit payable from the fund per contractor.
The State Treasurer acts as the custodian of the Home Improvement Guaranty Fund special account and the expert witness account, and is responsible for investing the fund's increased balances.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of Natural Resources to establish and implement a Restorative Aquaculture Pilot Program. Directs the program to provide financial incentives to aquaculture leaseholders who maintain restorative conditions for at least four years. Authorizes participating leaseholders to satisfy active use lease requirements through shellfish seed planting only. Requires the department to identify restorative metrics considering oyster density, biomass, and habitat complexity. Mandates the adoption of program regulations by October 1, 2024. Terminates the pilot program on September 30, 2029.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland aquaculture leaseholders
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $144,631 in FY 2024 to hire two staff members to administer the program, increasing to $196,800 by FY 2028. Total expenditures exclude the cost of financial incentive payments, which are indeterminate and dependent on program design and participation. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR is the primary implementing agency tasked with establishing, managing, and adopting regulations for the Restorative Aquaculture Pilot Program, as well as administering financial incentives to qualifying leaseholders.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires DNR to consult and coordinate with the statutory Aquaculture Coordinating Council to develop program criteria, metrics, and financial incentive payment rates.
The bill specifies coordination with the University of Maryland Center for Environmental Science (UMCES), a USM institution, to identify and develop metrics and criteria for restorative aquaculture.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the maximum bond issuance by the Maryland Stadium Authority for sports entertainment facilities from $200,000,000 to $220,000,000. Authorizes a nonprofit organization that will own or operate a facility to request financing and construction management services. Requires the Authority to secure an agreement with the nonprofit organization or local jurisdiction before issuing bonds. Requires participating entities to maintain, repair, market, and operate the facility in first-class operating condition. Mandates an annual maintenance assessment report to legislative committees on or before December 31 each year.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Stadium Authority; Board of Public Works
qa_results.stakeholders: nonprofit organizations that own or operate sports entertainment facilities, local governments, and sports facility contractors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Nonbudgeted revenues and expenditures for the Sports Entertainment Facilities Financing Fund increase by $15.0 million in FY 2024 and $5.0 million in FY 2025 from bond proceeds. General fund revenues decrease by $1.1 million in FY 2026 and $1.5 million annually in FY 2027 and FY 2028 to cover debt service payments from State Lottery revenues. Local revenues and expenditures may increase for related facility construction and operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the statutory bonding capacity of the Maryland Stadium Authority for sports entertainment facilities, increasing it from $200 million to $220 million, and authorizes the Authority to receive financing requests and enter into facility agreements with nonprofit organizations.

The Board of Public Works is statutorily required to approve bond issuances by the Maryland Stadium Authority under the altered bond cap, as well as review and approve the financing plans and written agreements established with eligible entities (now including nonprofit organizations).

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends through June 30, 2024, the authority of certain alcoholic beverages manufacturers to sell, deliver, and directly ship products. Limits direct shipment authority to manufacturers authorized by the Alcohol and Tobacco Commission on or before April 6, 2023. Restricts annual direct shipments per consumer to 3,456 ounces of beer or 18 standard 750-milliliter bottles of liquor. Requires reporting of shipped and delivered amounts to the Commission by December 1, 2023, and June 1, 2024. Delays until July 1, 2024, authorization for specified manufacturers to sell up to 288 ounces of beer off-site.
qa_results.responsible_party: Alcohol and Tobacco Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: licensed alcoholic beverages manufacturers in Maryland (including breweries, wineries, and distilleries) and Maryland consumers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal State general fund revenues and expenditures for the Alcohol and Tobacco Commission are maintained through fiscal 2024 due to the extension of authorizations. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill regulates the direct shipment, delivery, and reporting of alcoholic beverages by manufacturers, which requires verification that all applicable sales and excise taxes are paid. According to the agency summary, the Comptroller is responsible for collecting state sales taxes and regulating the alcohol industry.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands eligibility for the film production activity income tax credit to include documentaries and talk, reality, or game shows. Includes compensation for Maryland-domiciled writers, directors, or producers within qualifying direct costs. Increases credit percentages to 28% of qualified direct costs, or 30% for a television series. Increases the annual tax credit cap to $15 million in fiscal 2024, $17.5 million in 2025, and $20 million in 2026. Establishes the Maryland Entertainment Council to study the entertainment industry and submit strategic recommendations by September 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Commerce; Comptroller of Maryland; Maryland Entertainment Council
qa_results.stakeholders: Qualified film production entities, Maryland small or independent film entities, in-state writers, directors, and producers, and Maryland film industry workers and support businesses
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues decrease by $3.0 million in FY 2024, $5.5 million in FY 2025, and $8.0 million in FY 2026 across the general fund, Transportation Trust Fund, and Higher Education Investment Fund due to expanded tax credit caps. State general fund expenditures increase by up to $100,000 in FY 2024 and FY 2025 for council study and evaluation costs. Local highway user revenues decrease by $0.1 million to $0.3 million annually from FY 2024 through FY 2026.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Commerce is the primary agency administering the Film Production Activity Income Tax Credit program, determining project eligibility, issuing tax credit certificates, and providing staff support and funding for the newly created Maryland Entertainment Council.

The Comptroller of Maryland jointly adopts regulations with the Department of Commerce to administer the credit, receives notifications of estimated direct costs, and processes the income tax credits and refunds claimed by qualifying production entities.

The bill requires the Governor to appoint multiple members and honorary cochairs to the Maryland Entertainment Council, tasks the Governor's Senior Advisor on Film, Television, and Entertainment with chairing the Council, and directs the Council to submit preliminary and final reports to the Governor.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally establishes the Maryland Entertainment Council as a temporary advisory body tasked with studying Maryland's film and entertainment industry and providing strategic recommendations to state leaders.

The fiscal note identifies a notable direct fiscal impact on the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF), projecting revenue reductions of $0.5 million to $1.5 million annually from FY 2024 through FY 2026, which correspondingly reduces TTF expenditures for local highway user revenue grants.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the County Commissioners of St. Mary's County to borrow up to $56,000,000 through general obligation bonds. Requires bond proceeds to fund the construction, improvement, or development of specified public facilities. Limits bond maturities to no later than 30 years from their date of issue. Directs the county to levy annual ad valorem property taxes sufficient to pay bond principal and interest. Exempts all issued bonds, refunding bonds, and associated income from Maryland state and local taxation.
qa_results.responsible_party: County Commissioners of St. Mary's County
qa_results.stakeholders: Taxpayers and residents of St. Mary's County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state effect. St. Mary’s County bond proceeds increase county revenues by up to $56.0 million, and county debt service expenditures increase by an estimated $3.8 million annually over a 20-year period.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 457 exempts the principal, interest, and income derived from St. Mary's County's public facilities bonds from state taxation. As Maryland's principal tax collector, the Comptroller oversees the administration of state tax exemptions, although the bill has no direct state fiscal impact.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Task Force to Study Solar Incentives to examine solar development and financial incentives. Requires the Maryland Energy Administration to staff the task force and designate the chair. Directs the task force to study state and federal solar incentives and compliance fee calculations. Requires recommendations regarding renewable energy goals, workforce development, minority business enterprise participation, and efficient land use. Mandates a report of findings and recommendations to the General Assembly by December 15, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Energy Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Solar energy developers, minority business enterprises in solar development, electric utilities, electricity customers, and environmental advocacy organizations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on state revenues or local government finances. The Maryland Energy Administration can staff the task force and provide member expense reimbursements with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MEA is the primary implementing agency for the bill; its Director serves on the Task Force and designates the chair, and MEA is required to provide staff support and absorb travel reimbursement costs for the Task Force.

The Chairman of the Public Service Commission (or designee) serves as a member of the Task Force, which is tasked with studying solar renewable energy credits and alternative compliance fees under the Public Utilities Article overseen by the PSC.
The People's Counsel is designated to appoint a representative of the Office of People's Counsel to serve as a member of the Task Force.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a temporary state body, the Task Force to Study Solar Incentives, to study solar policies and incentives and report findings to the General Assembly.
The Governor is responsible for appointing six members to the Task Force: four representatives of the solar energy industry and two representatives of environmental advocacy groups.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and processing candidates for the six gubernatorial appointments to the Task Force.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes State land conservation goals to conserve 30% of Maryland land by 2030 and 40% by 2040. Requires the Smart Growth Subcabinet to publish an implementation plan by July 1, 2024, and report annually. Creates the Local Land Trust Revolving Loan Program and Fund to finance property acquisitions for conservation. Establishes the 40 x 40 Land Conservation Implementation Grant Program administered by the Maryland Environmental Trust. Authorizes the Governor to include annual budget appropriations for competitive conservation grants and local stewardship capacity building.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Environmental Trust; Smart Growth Subcabinet; Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: local land trusts, private landowners, local governments, schools, and nonprofit conservation organizations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $6,747,711 in FY 2025, by $738,573 in FY 2026, and by ongoing amounts in future years for personnel, fund capitalization, and grants. Special fund revenues increase by $6.0 million in FY 2025 from fund capitalization, with special fund expenditures of $3.0 million annually in FY 2025 and FY 2026 for revolving loans. Local revenues and expenditures likely increase beginning in FY 2025 from participation in conservation grants and partnerships.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Environmental Trust (MET) is a unit of the Department of Natural Resources. The bill tasks MET with administering the Local Land Trust Revolving Loan Program, the Local Land Trust Revolving Loan Fund, the 40 x 40 Land Conservation Implementation Grant Program, and stewardship grants, requiring additional staff and managing multi-million dollar funds. A DNR representative also sits on the new advisory committee.

The Department of Planning plays a central role in the Smart Growth Subcabinet, which the bill tasks with developing, publishing, and updating a plan to meet statewide land conservation goals (30% by 2030 and 40% by 2040) and submitting annual progress reports to the General Assembly.

The bill establishes ambitious land conservation goals that encompass agricultural land preservation, affects transfer tax revenue allocations that support the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF), and includes the department as a member of the Smart Growth Subcabinet.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill statutorily creates the Land Preservation Rapid Response Advisory Committee to review, prioritize, and make recommendations on program loan applications.
The bill specifically directs the State Treasurer to hold the newly created Local Land Trust Revolving Loan Fund separately and invest its moneys.
The bill statutorily mandates that the Comptroller account for the newly established Local Land Trust Revolving Loan Fund.
The bill authorizes the Governor to include annual appropriations in the state budget bill for grant and loan programs and involves executive subcabinet coordination.
The bill authorizes significant new appropriations and special fund structures that impact state budget planning and execution, and the Secretary sits on the Smart Growth Subcabinet.
The department is part of the Smart Growth Subcabinet tasked with implementing state conservation goals, which include carbon and greenhouse gas sequestration and ecological preservation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of the Environment to update sediment control plan specifications by December 1, 2025, and every five years thereafter. Requires the Department to revise water quantity control standards using the most recent precipitation data available. Prohibits applying updates retroactively to active, unexpired projects where construction has commenced. Prohibits authorizing general discharge permits for construction disturbing five or more acres in specified sensitive areas until public notice requirements are met. Requires the Department to extend the public comment period to 60 days upon receiving a timely written request.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: construction permit applicants, land developers, engineering firms, local soil conservation districts, and local governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Maryland Department of the Environment increase by $83,303 in FY 2024 and at least $100,000 annually thereafter for one staff engineer. MDE anticipates additional costs exceeding $500,000 beginning in FY 2024 to update specifications, which may be offset by federal grants. Local government expenditures may increase starting in FY 2026 for training and enforcement.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of the Environment (MDE) is the primary regulatory agency tasked with administering the bill. MDE must review and update specifications for sediment control plans every five years, report to the General Assembly, and implement enhanced public notice and comment requirements for construction stormwater discharge permits.

MDOT SHA holds an NPDES Phase I MS4 permit requiring compliance with state erosion and sediment control programs and conducts substantial roadway construction activities that require sediment control plans and stormwater discharge permits.

MDOT oversees large-scale transportation and infrastructure construction projects that require compliance with sediment control specifications and stormwater discharge permits, potentially experiencing project timeline and compliance cost impacts.

DGS manages planning, design, and construction of state-owned facilities, making it an affected permit holder subject to updated sediment control plan specifications and potential public review delays for capital projects.

MDA oversees soil conservation programs and works closely with local soil conservation districts, which serve as statutory approval authorities for erosion and sediment control plans under the affected statutes.

DNR manages state lands and waterways, interfaces with Critical Area Buffer protections referenced in the bill, and undertakes environmental restoration projects that may interact with the bill's permitting exemptions and water quality standards.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Task Force to Study School Bus Operator Contracts and Wages in Charles County. Requires the Maryland Department of Labor to provide staff for the Task Force. Directs the Task Force to study student transportation, bus driver wages, and multiyear contracts for bus contractors. Requires the Task Force to research best practices in surrounding jurisdictions regarding student transportation facilitation. Mandates a report of findings and recommendations to the Charles County Delegation by September 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Task Force to Study School Bus Operator Contracts and Wages in Charles County; Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: school bus contractors and school bus drivers in Charles County, Charles County Public Schools, and the Amalgamated Transit Union Local 689
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected; the Maryland Department of Labor can staff the task force with existing resources, and member travel expense reimbursements are minimal and absorbable. The bill does not materially affect Charles County finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that the Maryland Department of Labor provide staff and administrative support for the Task Force to Study School Bus Operator Contracts and Wages in Charles County.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a temporary statutory task force—the Task Force to Study School Bus Operator Contracts and Wages in Charles County—to study student transportation, bus driver wages, and multiyear contracts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires counties and municipalities operating minority business enterprise utilization programs to accept State-certified minority business enterprises. Applies to local jurisdictions that maintain their own certification process for procurement programs. Mandates acceptance of any entity certified by the designated State certification agency. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation
qa_results.stakeholders: certified minority business enterprises and county and municipal procurement agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State certification requests for the Maryland Department of Transportation may increase minimally, absorbable within existing budgeted resources. Local governments experience no material fiscal impact, though some may realize indeterminate administrative savings if they discontinue separate certification processes.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT is the designated State certification agency under § 14-303(b) of the State Finance and Procurement Article. The bill requires local governments to accept MDOT's Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) certifications, which could result in an increase in certification applications submitted to MDOT.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office oversees and coordinates the State's Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) program and policies across Maryland, making changes to how state MBE certifications are recognized at the local level relevant to its mission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters planning requirements, advisory committee membership, and property transfer deadlines for the Port of Deposit State Historical Park. Authorizes the Bainbridge Development Corporation to transfer up to 150 acres to the Department of Natural Resources by June 1, 2025. Removes the historic Tome School from required transfer parcels while retaining the Snow Hill archaeological site. Requires transferred property excluded from the park to be preserved in perpetuity based on stakeholder advisory committee recommendations. Requires the Department of Natural Resources to report on park property and funding needs by September 1, 2024. Authorizes the Governor to appropriate at least $400,000 in fiscal year 2025 for archaeological and soil studies.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources; Bainbridge Development Corporation
qa_results.stakeholders: Bainbridge Development Corporation, residents of Cecil County and Port Deposit, and visitors to Port of Deposit State Historical Park
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures may increase by at least $400,000 in fiscal year 2025 if the Governor includes the authorized appropriation for a Phase 1 Archaeological Survey and Soil Study. Revenues are not affected, and there is no direct impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR is the primary agency responsible for administering the Port of Deposit State Historical Park, establishing the stakeholder advisory committee, managing property transferred from the Bainbridge Development Corporation, submitting the required study/report to the General Assembly, and conducting the archaeological survey and soil study.

The Secretary of Planning (or designee) and the Director of the Maryland Historical Trust (which is administratively housed within the Department of Planning) are designated as ex officio members of the stakeholder advisory committee for the historical park.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes and modifies the composition and reporting duties of the Port of Deposit State Historical Park Stakeholder Advisory Committee.
The Chief Archaeologist of MDOT SHA (or their designee) is designated as a voting member of the stakeholder advisory committee to advise DNR on the scope and management of the park.
The Chief Archaeologist of the Maryland Department of Transportation, State Highway Administration, is appointed as a member of the stakeholder advisory committee.
The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) is designated as a nonvoting ex officio member of the stakeholder advisory committee.
The Secretary of the Environment (or designee) is designated as a nonvoting ex officio member of the stakeholder advisory committee.
The bill authorizes the Governor to include an appropriation of at least $400,000 in the annual State budget for fiscal year 2025 to DNR for an archaeological survey and soil study.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters terminology and standards for peer support programs serving fire, rescue, and emergency medical services personnel. Requires peer support programs, services, and specialist training to be evidence-based. Replaces references to counseling sessions with interactions regarding confidentiality protections and disclosures. Directs the Behavioral Health Administration to focus its best-practices report on evidence-based peer support programs. Mandates the administration publish a list of evidence-based training programs on its website following report completion.
qa_results.responsible_party: Behavioral Health Administration; Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
qa_results.stakeholders: members of fire, rescue, or emergency medical services entities; peer support specialists; International Association of Fire Fighters
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact as the changes are technical in nature.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the Behavioral Health Administration, a division within the Maryland Department of Health, develop a report on best practices and professional standards for evidence-based peer support programs and publish the report and a list of training programs on its website.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Behavioral Health Administration to consult with the Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems in developing the report on best practices, professional standards, and guidelines for peer support programs for fire, rescue, and EMS personnel.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the assessment calculation and collection process for the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund. Authorizes the Fund on June 1, 2023, to withdraw money held from prior overassessments into Fund surplus. Prohibits annual assessments on Industry Automobile Insurance Association members when prior overassessment money equals or exceeds the assessment. Requires Association members to refund excess surcharges to policyholders or apply them as expense reductions in subsequent rate filings. Increases the Fund's statutory distribution of uninsured motorist penalty revenue by $2,000,000 for fiscal year 2024. Requires the Fund to report to the General Assembly by July 1, 2023, regarding fund balances and withdrawn money.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund; Industry Automobile Insurance Association; Maryland Insurance Administration; Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund; motor vehicle insurers licensed in Maryland (Industry Automobile Insurance Association members); motor vehicle policyholders; uninsured vehicle owners assessed penalties
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: General fund revenues decrease by $2.0 million in FY 2024 due to a temporary $2.0 million reallocation of uninsured motorist penalty collections to the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund (MAIF). Nonbudgeted MAIF revenues increase by $10.2 million in FY 2023 from accessing prior overassessment reserve balances and by $2.0 million in FY 2024 from the penalty reallocation.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the assessment formula, overassessment withdrawal procedures, and funding allocations for the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund (MAIF), resulting in an increase of nonbudgeted revenues of $10.2 million in FY 2023 and $2.0 million in FY 2024.

The Maryland Insurance Commissioner is tasked with receiving notification of assessment certifications, verifying Board of Trustees calculations, and determining aggregate net direct written premiums for private passenger and commercial auto insurers.

The Motor Vehicle Administration collects vehicle lapsed-security penalties under Section 17-106 of the Transportation Article, and the bill alters the distribution formula for these penalties in FY 2024 to reallocate $2.0 million from the General Fund to MAIF.

As the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration, MDOT oversees the administration of the Transportation Article provisions amended by the bill regarding vehicle security penalties and their statutorily designated fund distributions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the inclusion of certain audio-only telephone conversations under the definition of telehealth through June 30, 2025. Requires the Maryland Medical Assistance Program and private health insurers to provide reimbursement parity through June 30, 2025. Excludes clinic facility fees and room and board fees from required telehealth reimbursement. Directs the Maryland Health Care Commission to study telehealth service delivery and payment parity. Requires the Commission to report its findings and recommendations to the General Assembly by December 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Health Care Commission; Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Health care providers, Medicaid recipients, commercial health insurance enrollees, health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Medicaid expenditures and federal matching fund revenues continue through fiscal 2025, with an indeterminate net impact on total Medicaid spending. Minimal special fund revenue increase for the Maryland Insurance Administration from form filing fees in fiscal 2024. Potential expenditure increases for certain local governments to continue reimbursing specified telehealth services under local health benefit plans.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Maryland Health Care Commission to conduct a comprehensive study on the delivery of health care services through telehealth—including payment parity, clinical effort, and behavioral health reimbursement—and submit a report with recommendations to the General Assembly by December 1, 2024.

The Maryland Department of Health administers the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), which is directly required under the bill to extend coverage of audio-only telehealth and maintain payment parity with in-person care through June 30, 2025.

The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates private health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and HMOs in the state, which are required under the bill to continue reimbursing covered telehealth services at parity with in-person rates through June 30, 2025, resulting in rate and form filings reviewed by the agency.

The bill explicitly references the Health Services Cost Review Commission, clarifying that the telehealth reimbursement requirements do not supersede the commission's authority to set hospital rates and facility fees for hospital-provided telehealth.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the renewal term for a video lottery operation license from 10 years to 15 years. Requires a licensee to file a notice of intent to renew between two and five years before expiration. Requires the licensee to apply for renewal within one year after filing that notice. Requires the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission to renew the license unless finding the licensee unqualified. Requires licensees to pay renewal fees into the Education Trust Fund in equal installments across each five-year period. Distributes 20% of paid renewal fees back to licensees for marketing and promotions exclusively targeting out-of-state audiences.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission; Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: video lottery operation licensees and Maryland public education programs funded by the Education Trust Fund
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues to the Education Trust Fund increase by $225,300 in FY 2026, rising to approximately $2.7 million annually by FY 2032 once all facilities renew. Special fund expenditures from the Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund increase by $1.3 million in FY 2027 and $1.2 million in FY 2028, offset by equal reductions in general fund expenditures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency and its governing Commission are the primary regulators responsible for administering video lottery operation license renewals, establishing application procedures and renewal fees by regulation, reviewing licensee qualifications, providing hearings, and collecting and remitting renewal fees to the Education Trust Fund.

The Comptroller is statutorily directed to disburse funds from the proceeds of video lottery terminals according to the updated distribution formulas upon transmittals from the Commission, including the newly added allocations for out-of-state marketing.

The State Treasurer is statutorily responsible for investing and reinvesting moneys credited to the Education Trust Fund, which will receive increased revenue from the video lottery operation license renewal fees.
License renewal fees are deposited into the Education Trust Fund, which supports public school programs and the Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund administered in conjunction with MSDE.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Attorney General to investigate, prosecute, and remediate civil rights violations on behalf of State residents. Prohibits civil rights actions by the Attorney General against political subdivisions, government units, or their employees. Allows the Attorney General to obtain injunctive relief, restitution, and civil penalties up to $25,000. Establishes the Civil Rights Enforcement Fund to support enforcement activities, education, and community outreach. Requires the Attorney General to coordinate with the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights in overlapping jurisdictions.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General; Maryland Commission on Civil Rights
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland residents experiencing discrimination; businesses and individuals subject to civil rights enforcement actions
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $1,048,706 in FY 2024 to fund 12 positions within the Office of the Attorney General, with ongoing personnel and operating expenses in future years. Special fund revenues and expenditures increase from civil penalties deposited into the newly created Civil Rights Enforcement Fund. General fund revenues increase minimally from fund interest earnings. Local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 540 directly authorizes the Office of the Attorney General to investigate, prosecute, and remediate civil rights violations, seek injunctions and civil penalties, enter into conciliation agreements, and adopt implementing regulations in coordination with the Commission on Civil Rights, requiring dedicated staff and substantial operational resources.

The bill explicitly preserves the authority of the Commission on Civil Rights and requires the Attorney General to coordinate and make referrals with the Commission in areas of overlapping jurisdiction to eliminate duplication of effort, while also allowing the Commission to receive reimbursements from the newly created Civil Rights Enforcement Fund.
The bill establishes the Civil Rights Enforcement Fund and explicitly mandates that the State Treasurer hold the fund separately and invest its moneys in the same manner as other state funds.
The bill establishes the Civil Rights Enforcement Fund and explicitly mandates that the Comptroller account for the fund.

The bill requires civil enforcement actions initiated by the Attorney General to be filed in the circuit courts, which are supported operationally and administratively by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Limits the hours during which a person in possession of a towed vehicle must allow reclamation. Requires storage facilities to make vehicles available for reclamation from at least 6:00 a.m. to midnight, seven days a week. Replaces the prior mandate requiring reclamation opportunities 24 hours per day. Alters parking lot signage requirements to state the revised statutory hours for reclamation. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation; Department of State Police
qa_results.stakeholders: towing company operators, vehicle storage facility operators, parking lot owners and operators, and motor vehicle owners
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in state general and special fund expenditures and local government expenditures in FY 2024 to update signage where applicable. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends Title 21 of the Maryland Transportation Article concerning vehicle towing from parking lots, signage requirements, and hours for vehicle reclamation, which directly falls under transportation laws and may affect state-operated parking facilities.

As the primary state law enforcement agency enforcing the Maryland Vehicle Law, the Maryland State Police regulates and responds to motor vehicle, towing, and property disputes, and was consulted for the bill's fiscal analysis.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Department of Service and Civic Innovation as a principal department of State government. Transfers administration and management of the Maryland Corps Program to the Department. Creates the Young Adult Service Year Option Pathway and Maryland Service Year Option Pathway. Requires participating corps members to be paid at least fifteen dollars per hour or State minimum wage. Authorizes six thousand dollar program completion awards as cash stipends or Maryland 529 account deposits. Mandates annual State budget appropriations to the Maryland Service Year Option Pathway Fund through fiscal 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
qa_results.stakeholders: young adults within three years of high school graduation, Maryland residents pursuing community service, participating employers, and host organizations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $3.6 million in FY 2023 and $11.35 million in FY 2024 under contingent appropriations, alongside a $5.15 million expenditure from the Dedicated Purpose Account in FY 2024. Mandated annual funding for the Maryland Service Year Option Pathway Fund begins at $5.0 million in FY 2024 and increases to $20.0 million by FY 2027. Local expenditures may increase if local governments voluntarily host corps participants.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 551 codifies the Department of Service and Civic Innovation as a principal department in state government and charges it with administering the Maryland Corps Program and the two newly created service pathways.

The bill establishes the Secretary as a member of the Governor's Executive Council, authorizes the Governor to appoint the Secretary and members of the Advisory Board, and transfers programs from executive offices.
The bill designates the Attorney General as legal adviser to the Department and requires the assignment of Assistant Attorneys General, including a designated Counsel to the Department.
The State Treasurer is tasked with holding and investing moneys for the Young Adult Service Year Option Pathway Fund and the Maryland Service Year Option Pathway Fund.
The Comptroller is required to separately account for each revenue source of the newly established pathway special funds and handle fund reversions.
DBM oversees the state budget allocations, mandated appropriations, staffing positions, and the handling and reversions of Dedicated Purpose Account (DPA) funds associated with the bill.

The bill amends the $6,000 program completion award provisions, allowing participants the choice of receiving cash stipends rather than solely requiring deposits into Maryland 529 accounts, potentially reducing Maryland 529 deposits.
The bill explicitly mandates that the Young Adult Service Year Option Pathway Fund and the Maryland Service Year Option Pathway Fund are subject to audit by the Office of Legislative Audits.

The Department of Service and Civic Innovation is required to consult with the Maryland Department of Labor to assess awarding corps participants credit for prior learning experience toward trade or vocational certifications and registered apprenticeships.
The bill requires consultation with MHEC regarding the awarding of academic credit for corps participants' service at postsecondary institutions.
The bill and related budget transfers reassign the Governor's Office on Service and Volunteerism and associated funding from GOCI to the Department of Service and Civic Innovation.
The bill authorizes funds to expand the Maryland Conservation Corps and the Chesapeake Conservation Corps, and expand service opportunities in state and local parks.

Public senior higher education institutions must waive in-state residency requirements for individuals who complete a Maryland Corps service program, and institutions may participate in awarding academic credits.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Tricare Premium Reimbursement Program in the Military Department. Authorizes the Department to award grants to eligible Maryland National Guard members for health and dental premiums. Covers premiums paid under the Tricare Reserve Select Program and the Tricare Dental Program for members and their immediate families. Caps grant awards at up to $60 per month of the total premiums paid by an eligible recipient. Requires the Department to adopt regulations to implement and administer the program.
qa_results.responsible_party: Military Department
qa_results.stakeholders: members of the Maryland National Guard and their immediate families
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by up to $1,000,000 in FY 2024 to fund administrative costs ($280,593) and premium reimbursement subsidies. Out-year expenditures range from $871,300 in FY 2025 to $909,200 in FY 2028 based on projected program participation. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Tricare Premium Reimbursement Program within the Military Department, which is headed by the Adjutant General, requiring the department to adopt regulations, hire staff, and administer premium reimbursement grants.
Members of the Maryland National Guard and their immediate families are the direct beneficiaries of the health and dental insurance premium reimbursement grants established by the bill.
The bill effectuates $1.0 million in contingent general fund appropriations and necessitates the addition of three permanent state positions to administer the new grant program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Accelerates the increase in the State minimum wage to $15.00 per hour beginning January 1, 2024, for all employers. Applies the $15.00 hourly rate to both small and large employers simultaneously. Authorizes employers to pay employees under the age of 18 years at 85% of the minimum wage. Repeals the authority of the Board of Public Works to temporarily suspend scheduled minimum wage increases. Repeals required 4% annual provider reimbursement rate increases for fiscal years 2025 and 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: minimum-wage workers, private and public employers of all sizes, community service providers serving individuals with developmental disabilities or behavioral health conditions, and local governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $206.7 million in both FY 2024 and FY 2025 ($109.1 million general funds, $97.6 million federal funds) for provider reimbursements, with modest increases in state and higher education payroll costs. Federal revenues increase by $97.6 million in FY 2024 and FY 2025 to match the federal share. Local government personnel expenditures increase significantly in FY 2024 and FY 2025 to meet the accelerated wage threshold.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor is the primary regulatory agency responsible for administering and enforcing the Maryland Wage and Hour Law, which sets the state minimum wage accelerated by this bill.

The bill amends the Health - General Article concerning reimbursement rates for community service providers under the Developmental Disabilities Administration, Behavioral Health Administration, and Medicaid, generating a substantial fiscal expenditure impact of over $200 million across FY 2024 and FY 2025.
The bill specifically repeals statutory provisions granting the Board of Public Works the authority to temporarily suspend scheduled increases in the State minimum wage rate.

DBM oversees the state budget and state personnel management. The bill impacts state budget mandates regarding provider rate increases and has potential fiscal implications for state service contracts.
USM institutions experience direct expenditure increases to raise wages for certain exempt, hourly, and undergraduate student workers to meet the accelerated $15.00 per hour minimum wage.
The bill was introduced on behalf of the Administration and directly alters statutory mandates governing the rate increases that must be included in future executive budget proposals.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Recovery Residence Grant Program within the Maryland Department of Health to support operations, services, and programs. Requires the Department to award competitive grants to qualifying nonprofit recovery residences. Limits eligibility to Level I, Level II, or Level III recovery residences certified under National Alliance for Recovery Residences standards. Prohibits participating residences from receiving reimbursement from private insurance or the Maryland Medical Assistance Program. Mandates an annual appropriation of $500,000 for the program in fiscal years 2024 through 2027. Requires the Department to submit an annual implementation report to the Governor and General Assembly.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Certified Level I, Level II, and Level III nonprofit recovery residences, and individuals receiving recovery housing services for substance-related or addictive disorders
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $500,000 annually beginning in FY 2024 to support grant awards and administrative costs, including a mandated appropriation of $500,000 annually from FY 2025 through FY 2027. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly establishes the Recovery Residence Grant Program within the Maryland Department of Health (MDH). MDH is responsible for administering the program, establishing application and award procedures, issuing competitive grants, and reporting annually on grant distribution and outcomes.
The bill mandates a $500,000 appropriation in the annual State budget bill for fiscal years 2024 through 2027, directly impacting DBM's budget development and fiscal planning responsibilities.

The bill requires an annual mandated appropriation of $500,000 to be included in the Governor's budget bill for fiscal years 2024 through 2027 and mandates that MDH submit an annual report on the grant program to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the required annual State budget appropriation for the Maryland Meals for Achievement In-Classroom Breakfast Program. Raises the mandated annual appropriation from $7,550,000 to $12,050,000. Directs funding to schools that make an in-classroom breakfast available to all enrolled students. Requires county boards of education and sponsoring agencies for eligible nonpublic schools to apply for Program funds. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Office of the Governor
qa_results.stakeholders: students in participating public and eligible nonpublic schools, local boards of education, and sponsoring agencies for eligible nonpublic schools
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $4.5 million annually beginning in FY 2024 to fund the increased mandated appropriation. Local school systems receive nearly all of the new State funds to expand school breakfast provision, and participating schools receive up to $10.0 million in additional federal matching funds annually.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Meals for Achievement (MMFA) In-Classroom Breakfast Program is administered by the Maryland State Department of Education in conjunction with county school boards and participating nonpublic schools, and MSDE will oversee and distribute the increased $4.5 million in annual State funding.
As the agency responsible for preparing the Governor's budget and supervising fiscal planning, DBM must incorporate the increased mandated annual appropriation of $12,050,000 into the State budget.
The statute places a direct mandate on the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $12,050,000 for the program in the annual state budget bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the name of a mandated appropriation recipient to the Goodwill Industries of Chesapeake Excel Center in Baltimore City. Applies the altered name to existing mandated annual state budget appropriations of $500,000. Directs these appropriations to occur in each of fiscal years 2024 and 2025. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor; Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Goodwill Industries of Chesapeake Excel Center in Baltimore City and adult students age 21 and older
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal effect. The bill is clarifying in nature and does not alter the amount of funding provided or the intended recipient.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The mandated $500,000 appropriation affected by this name change is budgeted within the Maryland State Department of Education's Aid to Education program.
The Department of Budget and Management prepares the annual state budget and ensures mandated appropriations, such as the funding designated for this center, are properly included and designated.
The statutory provision directly mandates the Governor to include a $500,000 appropriation to the newly designated entity in the annual budget bill for fiscal years 2024 and 2025.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits residential property service agreements from lasting more than one year or binding subsequent purchasers. Bars these agreements from creating property liens or permitting assignments without customer notice or consent. Declares noncompliant service agreements void, unenforceable, and unfair trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act. Prohibits service providers from submitting prohibited agreements to court clerks or government agencies for recording. Establishes misdemeanor criminal penalties for improper recording submissions, including fines up to $1,000 and imprisonment. Authorizes affected property owners to bring circuit court actions for compensatory damages and attorney's fees.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division; Clerks of the Circuit Courts
qa_results.stakeholders: residential property owners, real estate service providers, and subsequent purchasers of residential property
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material impact on State or local finances or operations. The Office of the Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division, can handle the bill's enforcement provisions with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes that a violation of the prohibited residential property service agreement provisions is an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which is enforced by the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General.

The bill directly involves the Judicial Branch by authorizing Clerks of the Circuit Court to deny recording of prohibited service agreements, establishing a civil cause of action in circuit courts to void unlawful agreements and recover damages, and creating a misdemeanor offense punishable in court.

The Department of Labor licenses and regulates real estate professionals through the State Real Estate Commission; although specific annual reporting amendments in earlier drafts were struck, the bill directly regulates agreements commonly used in real estate transactions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Behavioral Health Care Coordination Value–Based Purchasing Pilot Program in the Maryland Department of Health. Requires the department to administer the three-year pilot program for at least 500 qualifying adults. Directs the department to reimburse participating providers on a per-member per-month basis for uncovered care coordination activities. Mandates an annual state budget appropriation of $600,000 for the program for fiscal years 2025 through 2027. Allocates a portion of funding to outcome-based reimbursement beginning in fiscal year 2026. Requires the department to report findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by November 1, 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Adults with behavioral health conditions at risk of emergency department utilization or inpatient psychiatric admission, and participating specialty behavioral health care providers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $276,600 in FY 2024 for contractual staff and consultant costs, followed by mandated annual appropriations of $600,000 from FY 2025 through FY 2027, and $59,400 in FY 2028 for closeout contractual staffing. State revenues are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 581 establishes the Behavioral Health Care Coordination Value-Based Purchasing Pilot Program within the Maryland Department of Health (MDH). MDH is responsible for administering the pilot program, selecting providers, applying for federal Medicaid waivers if needed, managing reimbursements, collecting data, and reporting findings to the Governor and General Assembly.

The bill mandates an annual general fund appropriation of $600,000 for fiscal years 2025 through 2027 for the pilot program, directly impacting DBM's preparation and management of the executive budget.

The bill mandates that the Governor include a $600,000 appropriation in the annual budget bill for fiscal years 2025 through 2027, and requires MDH to submit its final report and recommendations to the Governor by November 1, 2027.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the duties and meeting requirements of the Parkinson's Disease Registry Advisory Committee. Requires the Advisory Committee to meet at least quarterly beginning July 1, 2023. Directs the Advisory Committee to consult with specified entities to aid federal efforts creating a national registry. Requires the Maryland Department of Health, collaborating with the State-designated health information exchange, to establish a public website by October 1, 2023. Mandates the downloadable website data include disease incidence and receive annual updates by January 1. Requires the Advisory Committee to report recommendations on establishing a State registry by July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Parkinson's Disease Registry Advisory Committee
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland residents diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease, healthcare providers, Parkinson’s disease researchers, and public health professionals
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $129,700 in FY 2024 to fund two part-time staff positions for committee support and website maintenance, decreasing to $93,100 in FY 2025 when one position reduces hours. Future years reflect ongoing operating costs. Revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Maryland Department of Health with establishing and maintaining a public Parkinson's disease website, supporting and staffing the Parkinson's Disease Registry Advisory Committee, and incurs general fund expenditures for staff analysts and epidemiologists.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the responsibilities, meeting schedule requirements (requiring at least quarterly meetings), consultation mandates, and reporting deadlines of the Parkinson's Disease Registry Advisory Committee.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the earnings threshold for prohibited noncompete and conflict of interest provisions in employment contracts or similar agreements. Voids noncompete or conflict of interest provisions for employees earning equal to or less than 150% of the State minimum wage. Replaces the prior statutory threshold of $15 per hour or $31,200 annually. Applies whether or not the employer and employee entered into the contract or agreement in the State. Excludes agreements regarding the taking or use of client lists or proprietary client-related information.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland employers and employees earning equal to or less than 150% of the State minimum wage rate
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Maryland Labor and Employment Article regarding noncompete and conflict of interest provisions in employment contracts. The Department of Labor is the state agency responsible for enforcing state labor and employment standards.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of State Police to submit an annual report on surplus military equipment acquisitions. Mandates delivery of the report to the Governor and the General Assembly by February 1 each year. Requires the report to cover equipment acquired by law enforcement agencies through federal surplus programs during the preceding year. Directs the Department to place a prominent link on its public website to a Defense Logistics Agency report. Specifies that the linked federal report lists excess property transfers through the Law Enforcement Support Office.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of State Police
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland law enforcement agencies and the Department of State Police
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of State Police can implement the reporting and website requirements using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Department of State Police to compile and submit an annual report on surplus military equipment acquired by law enforcement agencies and to post a link to the federal Defense Logistics Agency report on its public website.
The Governor's Office is designated as a recipient of the annual surplus military equipment acquisition report submitted by the Department of State Police.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires teacher preparation programs to provide training in virtual instruction and online curriculum techniques. Authorizes county boards of education to permit superintendents to use virtual education days during severe weather. Establishes operational standards, enrollment caps, and staffing rules for public virtual schools. Prohibits approving any new elementary grade band virtual school on or before December 1, 2024. Mandates that county boards adopt virtual education plans by June 1, 2024, for prolonged states of emergency.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Maryland State Board of Education; county boards of education
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland public school students and their families, public school teachers and educational support personnel, local school systems and county boards of education, and teacher preparation programs
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $100,000 in FY 2024 and $500,000 in FY 2025 for the Maryland State Department of Education to upgrade computer and internet security infrastructure. Local school systems are anticipated to implement the bill's requirements using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is the primary implementing agency responsible for establishing standards, approving and overseeing virtual schools, developing training standards, expanding cybersecurity infrastructure, and convening the virtual education study group.

The bill mandates an expansion of computer and Internet security infrastructure for virtual education, which the fiscal note indicates requires direct collaboration and an in-depth needs assessment with DoIT.

The bill alters mandatory curriculum components for teacher preparation programs to include teaching effectively in virtual learning environments and includes higher education institutions in the study group.
USM institutions offer public teacher preparation programs that must incorporate the bill's new virtual instruction training requirements into their educator curriculum.
Morgan State University operates teacher education and preparation programs that must update coursework to meet the new requirement for instruction in virtual learning environments.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission to license independent evaluators of sports wagering content by December 31, 2023. Establishes qualification criteria, conflict-of-interest prohibitions, and betting restrictions for licensed independent evaluators and their personnel. Authorizes sports wagering licensees and sports wagering operators advertising in Maryland to contract with licensed independent evaluators. Prohibits evaluators from being compensated by entities utilizing their services solely for marketing materials. Authorizes state gaming commissions to consider certain Class B-2 license location amendments requested by December 31, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission; Sports Wagering Application Review Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Independent evaluators of sports wagering content, sports wagering licensees, sports wagering operators, sports wagering experts, sports wagering influencers, content partners, and Class B-2 sports wagering facility license applicants
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency administrative expenditures may increase beginning in fiscal 2024 to license independent evaluators of sports wagering content, but a precise dollar estimate is currently unavailable. No local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission with licensing independent evaluators of sports wagering content, adopting implementing regulations, and considering location amendment requests for Class B-2 sports wagering facility license applications.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly authorizes the Sports Wagering Application Review Commission (SWARC), an independent statutory commission, to consider requests to amend certain Class B-2 sports wagering facility license applications.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires members of the Health Services Cost Review Commission to be appointed with the advice and consent of the Senate. Maintains the composition of the Commission at seven members appointed by the Governor. Preserves the requirement that four members have no connection with the management or policy of any facility. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor; Senate of Maryland; Health Services Cost Review Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: members and prospective nominees of the Health Services Cost Review Commission
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal effect, as the appointment change is procedural in nature.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the appointment process for members of the Health Services Cost Review Commission by requiring that their appointments by the Governor receive the advice and consent of the Senate.
The Governor is the appointing authority for members of the Health Services Cost Review Commission; this bill subjects those gubernatorial appointments to Senate advice and consent.
The Office of Appointments vets and manages gubernatorial appointments to state boards and commissions, including coordinating nominations through the Senate confirmation process.
The Health Services Cost Review Commission is an independent commission established within the Maryland Department of Health.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the governance, membership composition, and operational duties of the Historic St. Mary's City Commission. Adds a Native American community representative and two legislative-appointed public members to the Commission. Requires the Commission to publish written operational policies and update a comprehensive maintenance plan every three years. Establishes rules for collaborating with affiliated nonprofit organizations, including ethics reviews and mandatory annual audits. Subjects the Historic St. Mary's City Fund to audit by the Office of Legislative Audits. Mandates an audit-progress report to the General Assembly by December 31, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Historic St. Mary's City Commission; Office of the Attorney General; State Ethics Commission; Office of Legislative Audits
qa_results.stakeholders: Historic St. Mary's City Commission members and staff, affiliated nonprofit organizations including the Historic St. Mary's City Foundation, St. Mary's College of Maryland, and Maryland's Native American community
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances and operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly reforms the governance, membership, operating procedures, reporting requirements, and nonprofit collaboration rules of the Historic St. Mary's City Commission.

The Board of Trustees chair (or designee) serves as an ex officio voting member, and the bill establishes specific statutory standards for operating agreements, collaborative programs, and administrative services between the College and the Commission.
