The bill requires the State Ethics Commission to review and approve policies governing conflicts of interest for officials/employees serving on affiliated nonprofits, receive notifications and issue objections regarding dual service, and receive annual implementation reports.

The bill requires the Attorney General to review and approve the Commission's operating agreements with other units or nonprofits, as well as its nonprofit collaboration policies, for form and legal sufficiency.
The bill explicitly establishes that the Historic St. Mary's City Fund is subject to audit by the Office of Legislative Audits pursuant to state law.
The Governor is responsible for appointing 14 voting members of the Commission with Senate advice and consent, and receives annual activity and nonprofit collaboration reports from the Commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes certain City of Bowie Police Department officers to transfer or purchase service credit in the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System. Applies to officers hired between January 1, 2007, and December 31, 2015, who satisfy specified documentation requirements. Requires eligible officers to submit verification by December 31, 2023. Waives statutory one-year transfer deadlines and five-year retirement benefit limitations for eligible transferring members. Permits officers who withdrew prior contributions to purchase service credit through a single payment with regular interest. Terminates all provisions on December 31, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System; City of Bowie Police Department
qa_results.stakeholders: City of Bowie Police Department officers hired between January 1, 2007, and December 31, 2015; participating governmental units in the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Creates a minimal increase in pension liabilities for participating governmental units in the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System, with no discernible effect on employer contribution rates and no effect on local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System, including the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System (LEOPS). The bill directly tasks the system and its Board of Trustees with providing forms, receiving documentation and payments, and processing the service credit transfers and purchases for eligible City of Bowie police officers.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires health care providers and health care facilities to provide a local maternal mortality review team prompt access to certain medical records. Mandates access without undue delay on request of the local team chair. Applies the requirement to all relevant medical records associated with a case under review by the Maternal Mortality Review Program. Exempts disclosures made to a local team from state medical record confidentiality provisions. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Local Maternal Mortality Review Teams
qa_results.stakeholders: Health care providers, health care facilities, and local maternal mortality review teams
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact, as the change is procedural in nature and does not materially affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health oversees the Maternal Mortality Review Program and coordinates with local health departments and local maternal mortality review teams, which are granted direct and prompt access to relevant medical records under the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a nursing home to direct an electronic health network or electronic medical record vendor to release records. Permits release of patient medical records or electronic health care transactions to a business associate with patient consent. Requires networks and vendors to release information timely in an electronic format conforming to specified health information standards. Prohibits networks and vendors from restricting, limiting, or charging a fee for the release of the records. Prohibits fees to exchange-contracted business associates unless approved by the State-designated health information exchange.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Health Care Commission; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: nursing homes, electronic health network vendors, electronic medical record vendors, nursing home patients, and health care business associates
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Health Care Commission (MHCC) is responsible for certifying electronic health networks (EHNs) and overseeing the State-designated health information exchange (CRISP), which the bill directly references regarding record format standards and fee approval for quality-improvement business associates.

The Maryland Department of Health regulates and licenses nursing homes across the state and oversees the statutory provisions governing medical records and health transactions under the Health - General Article.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the State Disaster Recovery Fund to provide disaster recovery assistance to individuals, families, businesses, nonprofits, and local governments. Requires the Maryland Department of Emergency Management to administer the special, nonlapsing fund. Authorizes assistance when a federal disaster declaration is not received or for unmet needs. Permits fund expenditures only if the Governor declares an emergency or a local emergency organization requests aid. Requires the Secretary of Emergency Management to report annually on fund usage by December 31.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Emergency Management; Department of Budget and Management
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals, families, businesses, and nonprofits affected by disasters; local governments and local emergency management organizations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $10.0 million in FY 2024 to capitalize the fund, with special fund revenues increasing correspondingly. Special fund expenditures increase by at least $344,442 in FY 2024 for MDEM administration (3.5 positions), growing to $473,915 by FY 2028. Local revenues and expenditures increase to the extent local governments receive and spend disaster assistance.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDEM is the primary implementing agency tasked with administering the newly created State Disaster Recovery Fund, adopting regulations, determining eligibility criteria, and submitting annual reports.
DBM administers the Catastrophic Event Account, which this bill directly amends to allow local governments to receive funding directly, and oversees state budget and expenditure accounts.

The bill allows the Governor to include appropriations for the fund in the annual budget bill, requires a gubernatorial state of emergency declaration for certain fund uses, and authorizes the Governor to transfer funds via budget amendments.

The State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold the fund separately, invest its money, and ensure interest earnings are credited directly to the fund pursuant to the amendment to Section 6-226 of the State Finance and Procurement Article.
The Comptroller is statutorily designated to account for the State Disaster Recovery Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires a real estate broker or escrow agent to distribute trust money to a residential real estate purchaser after contingency termination. Allows a purchaser who terminates a contract under a contingency clause to request trust money in writing. Requires the seller to provide a copy of a District Court complaint or notarized mediation request within 10 days. Requires the holder to distribute trust money within 30 days if no complaint or mediation request is received. Protects trust money holders from liability for distributing funds under these statutory procedures. Authorizes any aggrieved claimant to file an action in the District Court.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Real Estate Commission; District Court of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: residential real estate purchasers, sellers, licensed real estate brokers, and escrow agents in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor oversees the regulation and licensing of real estate brokers and salespersons through the State Real Estate Commission. The bill directly amends Title 17 of the Business Occupations and Professions Article concerning real estate broker duties and the handling of trust money.

The bill explicitly establishes procedural remedies in the District Court, authorizing sellers to file complaints, holders of trust money to initiate interpleader actions, and aggrieved claimants to file actions in District Court.

The Office of the Attorney General houses the Consumer Protection Division, which monitors residential real estate practices and consumer disputes, and provides legal counsel to state licensing boards within the Department of Labor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Corrects technical errors, omissions, and obsolete references across various articles of the Annotated Code of Maryland. Clarifies statutory language and reorganizes select provisions without intending substantive legal changes. Authorizes the publishers of the Annotated Code to make approved nonsubstantive corrections to codification and style. Requires the publishers to describe any such corrections in editor's notes following affected sections. Takes effect immediately as an emergency measure upon enactment.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Legislative Services
qa_results.stakeholders: users of the Annotated Code of Maryland, legal practitioners, state agencies, and the general public
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact; the bill is technical in nature and does not affect governmental operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Updates statutory references in the Public Safety Article regarding the Maryland Food System Resiliency Council to reflect the agency's cabinet-level status, replacing obsolete references to the 'Director of the Maryland Emergency Management Agency' with 'Secretary of Emergency Management' and 'Maryland Department of Emergency Management'.

Contains numerous technical, grammatical, and typographical corrections to Title 13A of the Public Safety Article (Maryland Code of Military Justice), which governs military justice administration under the Adjutant General.
Technical corrections throughout Title 13A of the Public Safety Article directly pertain to members of the Maryland National Guard and court-martial/nonjudicial punishment procedures.

Enacts various technical, grammatical, and cross-reference corrections across multiple sections of the Education Article governing public school operations, educator pay plans, career ladders, and student health standards.

Includes technical clarifications and obsolete reference updates in the Health - General Article and Health Occupations Article, including terminology regarding the state-designated health information exchange and loan assistance repayment programs.
Makes minor technical and cross-reference corrections to provisions in the Natural Resources Article concerning Program Open Space, regulated shooting grounds, and local water fishing regulations.
Corrects statutory cross-references and minor phrasing in Education Article provisions relating to school construction priority grant awards and maintenance tracking systems.
Corrects technical phrasing and cross-references in the Tax - General and State Government Articles concerning tax filings and the distribution of video lottery terminal proceeds.
Corrects obsolete cross-references in the State Personnel and Pensions Article regarding the reemployment of disability retirees as law enforcement officers.

qa_results.bill_summary: Applies the State sales and use tax to home amenity rentals facilitated by an intermediary or platform. Defines a home amenity as residential property rented by the hour for up to 15 consecutive hours, excluding sleeping quarters. Classifies home amenity rental intermediaries and platforms as vendors required to collect and remit sales and use tax. Authorizes eligible counties to impose a local home amenity rental tax by resolution subject to statutory rate caps. Authorizes municipalities to levy a home amenity rental tax up to 1% if the underlying county imposes one.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: home amenity rental platforms and intermediaries, residential property owners offering home amenity rentals, consumers renting home amenities, and Maryland county and municipal governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund and special fund (Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund) revenues increase by a potentially significant indeterminate amount beginning in fiscal 2025, with potential increases in general fund administrative expenses. County and municipal revenues increase beginning in fiscal 2025 to the extent local home amenity rental taxes are imposed, with potential increases in local administrative costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands the Maryland sales and use tax to include home amenity rentals and home amenity rental intermediaries/platforms. As Maryland's principal tax collector, the Comptroller is responsible for collecting the sales and use tax revenue and will incur administrative costs to implement and enforce the new tax provisions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Department of Natural Resources to exchange certain State-owned real property for adjacent privately owned real property. Limits eligible State-owned real property to parcels not exceeding five acres in size. Requires the private property owner requesting the exchange to pay all related costs, including legal fees and surveying. Requires the Department to notify adjacent property owners, local General Assembly members, and the county governing body in writing. Requires the Department to refer the proposed exchange to the Board of Public Works for final disposition.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources; Board of Public Works
qa_results.stakeholders: Private landowners seeking land exchanges with the Department of Natural Resources; owners of real property adjacent to exchanged private land; county governing bodies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State operations or finances because the bill is authorizing in nature, and the requesting private landowner pays all transaction costs. Local fiscal effect is minimal or none.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR is the primary agency authorized under the bill to exchange up to 5 acres of State-owned real property with adjacent privately owned land under an expedited process and is responsible for providing the required notices.
All proposed real property exchanges under the bill must be referred by DNR to the Board of Public Works for final review and disposition.

Exchanges authorized by the bill bypass the standard excess real property review and disposition study procedures conducted by the Department of Planning under Title 5, Subtitle 3 of the State Finance and Procurement Article.

DGS oversees State real estate transactions and standard property disposition procedures under Title 10, Subtitle 3 of the State Finance and Procurement Article, which are exempted for eligible DNR property exchanges under this bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes members of the State Retirement and Pension System to receive credit for attending a United States service academy. Grants service credit at the rate of four months per full year of attendance, up to 16 months total. Applies to academy attendance that preceded employment or attendance that interrupts public employment. Maintains the existing overall limit of five years on total military service credit. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Retirement Agency
qa_results.stakeholders: Members and former members of the State Retirement and Pension System and members of local retirement systems who attended a United States service academy
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State pension expenditures increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in fiscal 2026; the average state employer cost per member claiming the maximum 16 months of credit ranges from $1,200 to $3,600 depending on the plan. There is no effect on revenues, and no discernible effect on local government pension liabilities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency directly administers the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS). The bill amends state pension law to allow SRPS members to receive retirement service credit for attendance at a U.S. service academy, requiring the agency to process these applications and calculate benefit adjustments.

As the State's central personnel and budget agency, DBM oversees state employee benefits and budgets for employer pension contributions, which will be fiscally impacted by the additional service credit liabilities beginning in FY 2026.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits the Motor Vehicle Administration from charging a fee for a new certificate of title to a surviving spouse. Applies upon the death of a sole vehicle owner when ownership transfers under statutory estate procedures. Eliminates the standard $100 titling fee previously charged to a surviving spouse not listed as a joint owner. Requires vehicle ownership transfer to comply with testamentary disposition or intestate devolution requirements. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Surviving spouses of deceased sole vehicle owners in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund revenues decrease by approximately $375,000 in FY 2024 and by $500,000 annually in subsequent years due to foregone titling fee revenues. Expenditures are not materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly prohibits the Motor Vehicle Administration from charging a $100 fee for issuing a new certificate of title to a surviving spouse of a deceased sole vehicle owner.
As the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration, MDOT's Transportation Trust Fund experiences an estimated revenue decrease of approximately $500,000 annually due to the fee exemption.
The Register of Wills issues certificates of letters testamentary or administration referenced in statutory vehicle transfers upon an owner's death, and was consulted as an information source.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires each deputy State fire marshal to remain in probationary status for two years after appointment. Applies the two-year probationary requirement to individuals appointed for training before regular assignment. Entitles a deputy State fire marshal upon promotion to pay specified for the new rank at their prior step. Restricts promotional pay to the next lower step under specific conditions based on peer service time. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of State Police; Office of the State Fire Marshal
qa_results.stakeholders: Deputy State fire marshals and individuals appointed for training at the Office of the State Fire Marshal
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: None. The bill codifies existing Department of State Police practice.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This was a departmental bill requested by the Maryland State Police. The Office of the State Fire Marshal operates within the department, and the bill directly governs the probationary period and promotional pay structure for deputy State fire marshals.
As the state's central personnel and budget agency, DBM oversees state employee compensation rules, probationary standards, and the approval of departmental pay plans specified in the statute.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to obtain State and national criminal history records checks for youth camp applicants. Applies to individuals seeking to become a youth camp owner, operator, employee, or volunteer with access to a camper. Requires the Department to issue a written hiring determination within three business days after receiving an operator's request. Repeals the authority of youth development organizations and programs to request hiring determinations from the Department. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: youth camp owners, operators, employees, and volunteers; youth camps; youth development organizations and programs
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $172,030 in FY 2024 to hire one full-time administrator, temporary contractual staff, and cover operating expenses, increasing to $207,200 by FY 2028. General fund revenues increase by an indeterminate amount from authorized background check fees. No local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to apply for State and national criminal history records checks for youth camp personnel applicants, review records, issue binding written hiring determinations within three business days, and set fees to cover associated costs, resulting in a direct operational and fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directs the department's Criminal Justice Information System (CJIS) Central Repository to process fingerprint submissions and fees, disseminate criminal history record information to the applicant and MDH, and provide revised records if subsequent criminal information is reported.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the expiration term of a commercial driver's instructional permit from 180 days to one year. Applies this extension to licensed drivers seeking a different class of license. Exempts commercial driver's license renewal applicants from the vision test requirement under specific conditions. Requires renewal applicants to have a current certificate of physical examination on file with the Motor Vehicle Administration. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Commercial driver's license holders and applicants for commercial driver's instructional permits
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund revenues decrease by approximately $263,300 in fiscal 2024 and $351,000 annually thereafter due to fewer permit reissuances. Expenditures are not materially affected, though the Motor Vehicle Administration may realize operational efficiencies.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration is the primary implementing agency directly responsible for issuing commercial driver's instructional permits, administering CDL renewals, verifying federal medical certificates for vision test exemptions, and managing the associated licensing fee collections.

The Maryland Department of Transportation is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration and requested this departmental legislation. MDOT's Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) will experience a special fund revenue decrease of approximately $351,000 annually due to fewer commercial permit reissuances.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date for statutory and regulatory provisions governing the State Board of Architects to July 1, 2028. Continues the board in accordance with the Maryland Program Evaluation Act. Authorizes the board to continue qualifying and licensing architects in the State. Maintains the board's authority to issue permits to businesses practicing architecture. Preserves the board's power to investigate complaints and discipline licensees or unpermitted entities.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Architects; Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed architects, architectural businesses, and applicants for architectural licensure in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Maintains State Board of Architects special fund revenues and expenditures from fiscal 2024 through fiscal 2028. Has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Architects is an occupational licensing and regulatory board housed within the Maryland Department of Labor. The bill directly continues the statutory authority, operations, and special fund revenues and expenditures of the Board through July 1, 2028.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date for the State Board of Certified Interior Designers to July 1, 2034. Continues the board's statutory and regulatory authority under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act. Maintains the board's authority to certify and regulate certified interior designers. Preserves the board's power to investigate complaints and issue disciplinary penalties against certificate holders. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Certified Interior Designers; Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Certified interior designers in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Maintains special fund revenues and expenditures for the State Board of Certified Interior Designers from fiscal 2025 through 2034. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Certified Interior Designers is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor (MD Labor) Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing. This bill extends the statutory termination date of the board by 10 years to July 1, 2034, directly allowing the department to continue its licensing, regulatory, and enforcement functions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date of the State Board of Foresters by 10 years to July 1, 2035. Continues the statutory and regulatory authority of the Board under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act. Maintains the licensing and regulation of foresters within the Maryland Department of Labor. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Foresters; Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: licensed foresters in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Maintains general fund revenues and expenditures for the State Board of Foresters from fiscal 2026 through fiscal 2035. Has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Foresters is an occupational licensing and regulatory board housed within the Maryland Department of Labor. This departmental bill directly extends the Board's statutory authority and termination date from July 1, 2025, to July 1, 2035.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date for the State Board of Examiners of Landscape Architects by 10 years to July 1, 2034. Continues the statutory and regulatory authority governing the practice and licensing of landscape architects. Preserves the board's regulatory operations under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Examiners of Landscape Architects; Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed landscape architects and business entities practicing landscape architecture in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Maintains special fund revenues and expenditures for the board from fiscal 2025 through 2034. Has no local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Examiners of Landscape Architects is an occupational licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Labor. This departmental bill extends the board's termination date under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act to July 1, 2034, allowing the department to continue regulating the practice and maintaining the board's operations, special fund revenues, and expenditures.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the statutory and regulatory termination date for the State Board of Stationary Engineers to July 1, 2034. Continues the board's operations under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act. Maintains licensing standards for individuals who oversee qualifying power plants, plants of machinery, and boilers. Preserves the board's authority to investigate licensing code violations and impose civil penalties up to $5,000.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Stationary Engineers; Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed stationary engineers, license applicants, and operators of qualifying power plants, machinery plants, and boilers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Maintains special fund revenues and expenditures for the State Board of Stationary Engineers from FY 2025 through FY 2034. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Stationary Engineers is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor. This bill directly reauthorizes the Board's regulatory and licensing authority through July 1, 2034, maintaining its special fund revenues and expenditures.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends determination and recordation deadlines for the Voluntary Cleanup Program administered by the Maryland Department of the Environment. Increases the department's deadline to act on program applications from 45 days to 60 days. Expands the department's timeframe to review response action plan completions from 30 days to 60 days. Requires participants to provide written evidence that conditioned determinations were presented for local recordation within 60 days. Mandates participants submit written evidence that conditioned certificates of completion were presented for recordation within 60 days.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: applicants and participants in the Voluntary Cleanup Program, including contaminated property owners, prospective purchasers, and redevelopers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances are not materially affected. The extended deadlines ease administrative burdens for the Maryland Department of the Environment and provide operational flexibility for program applicants.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the statutory deadlines and administrative procedures for the Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP), which is administered by the Maryland Department of the Environment.

The bill alters requirements for presenting determinations and certificates of completion for recordation in local land records, which are maintained by the Clerks of the Circuit Court supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the State Fuel Security Program administered and enforced by the Maryland Energy Administration. Requires the Administration to maintain plans and procedures for use during an energy emergency. Applies the program to motor gasoline, middle distillate, propane, aviation gasoline, and specified residual fuel oil. Authorizes the Administration to collect energy-related data and require fuel suppliers to submit necessary information. Requires coordination with state emergency management and information technology departments to secure and distribute data. Establishes administrative penalties up to $1,000 for first violations and $5,000 for subsequent violations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Energy Administration; Maryland Department of Emergency Management; Department of Information Technology
qa_results.stakeholders: Prime suppliers, suppliers, and wholesale purchaser-resellers of motor gasoline, middle distillate, propane, residual fuel oil, and aviation gasoline
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No direct, material effect on State or local finances. Affected State agencies can implement the program using existing resources, and potential administrative penalty revenues are not anticipated to materially affect State revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MEA is the primary implementing agency tasked with establishing, administering, and enforcing the State Fuel Security Program, collecting energy data, issuing reports, adopting regulations, and assessing administrative penalties.

MEA is required to coordinate with the Department of Emergency Management to create and execute an information distribution plan to disseminate energy-related information during emergencies and routine monitoring to the public and relevant agencies.
MEA is required by the bill to coordinate with DoIT to ensure that sensitive and proprietary energy-related data collected from suppliers is transmitted and securely stored.
The bill authorizes MEA to refer suppliers refusing to comply with program mandates to the Office of the Attorney General for civil enforcement actions and penalty recovery.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date of the Maryland Horse Racing Act to July 1, 2034. Establishes the Maryland Thoroughbred Racetrack Operating Authority to maintain Maryland as a best-in-class thoroughbred racing venue. Creates the special, nonlapsing Maryland Racing Operations Fund to finance capital and operating expenses for thoroughbred racetracks. Authorizes the Maryland Stadium Authority to transfer money from the Racing and Community Development Facilities Fund to the new fund. Extends the deadline for conveying the Bowie Race Course Training Center to the City of Bowie until December 31, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Thoroughbred Racetrack Operating Authority; Maryland Racing Commission; Maryland Stadium Authority
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland thoroughbred racing licensees, horse owners, trainers, breeders, racetrack facility operators, and the City of Bowie
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues for the Maryland Racing Operations Fund increase by at least $15.0 million in fiscal 2023 due to a redirection of capital budget funding. Expenditures from the fund may increase beginning in fiscal 2024 for authority operations, staffing, and a required feasibility study. Maryland Racing Commission special fund revenues and expenditures are maintained from fiscal 2025 through 2034.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill extends the termination date of the Maryland Horse Racing Act and the Maryland Racing Commission—housed within the Department of Labor—by 10 years to July 1, 2034.

The bill authorizes the Maryland Stadium Authority to transfer funds from the Racing and Community Development Facilities Fund to the new Maryland Racing Operations Fund, redirects $5 million of MSA capital funding to the new fund, and places the MSA Chair or Executive Director on the newly established Authority board.
The bill places the MEDCO Chair or Executive Director on the newly created Authority board and authorizes the Authority to coordinate with MEDCO to acquire property and contractual interests.

The Governor appoints multiple voting and nonvoting members to the new Authority and can issue executive orders triggering the Authority's power to assume management of thoroughbred racing operations.
The bill designates the Attorney General as the legal advisor to the new Authority and requires AG approval for the Authority to retain additional legal counsel.
The bill requires the State Treasurer to hold, administer separately, and invest the newly created Maryland Racing Operations Fund.
The bill designates the Comptroller to account for the newly created Maryland Racing Operations Fund and exempts the fund from standard General Fund interest accrual.
The bill amends the FY 2023 capital budget for the Division of Development Finance (within DHCD) to redirect $10 million from Laurel Park backstretch housing to the Maryland Racing Operations Fund.
Bowie State University, a member institution of USM, is statutorily tied to the execution and reporting of a joint use agreement and easement for the Bowie Race Course Training Center property.
The office assists the Governor in vetting and processing appointments to the newly created Maryland Thoroughbred Racetrack Operating Authority.

qa_results.bill_summary: Reestablishes an income tax credit for employers incurring federal security clearance costs from tax year 2023 through 2027. Limits eligibility for the credit to individuals or corporations employing not more than 500 employees. Allows credits up to $200,000 for security clearance administrative expenses incurred for Maryland employees. Authorizes credits up to $200,000 for first-year lease payments for small businesses performing security-based contracting. Limits credits for constructing or renovating a single sensitive compartmented information facility to the lesser of 50% of costs or $200,000. Caps total credits for constructing or renovating multiple facilities at $500,000.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Commerce; Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland individuals and corporations with 500 or fewer employees that incur federal security clearance costs, lease facilities for security-based contracting, or construct or renovate sensitive compartmented information facilities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues decrease by $1.8 million to $1.9 million annually from FY 2025 through FY 2028 across the general fund, Transportation Trust Fund, and Higher Education Investment Fund. General fund expenditures for the Comptroller's Office increase by $50,000 in FY 2024 for one-time tax system modifications. Local highway user revenues decrease by $36,400 to $51,400 annually from FY 2025 through FY 2028, offset minimally by local income tax addbacks.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Commerce is the primary agency administering the Employer Security Clearance Costs Tax Credit program, responsible for reviewing applications and certifying qualified expenses up to the statutory cap.

The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for administering the state income tax system, processing credit claims, and will incur a one-time general fund expenditure of $50,000 in FY 2024 to implement required tax form and system updates.

The Department of Transportation is funded through the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF), which will experience a slight reduction in revenues of $0.2 million to $0.3 million annually from FY 2025 through FY 2028 as a result of the corporate income tax credit.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the mandatory retirement age of 70 years for the Director of the State Department of Assessments and Taxation. Removes the mandatory retirement age of 70 years for county supervisors of assessments. Allows these officials to continue holding office after reaching age 70. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Director of the State Department of Assessments and Taxation and county supervisors of assessments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no effect on State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Director of the State Department of Assessments and Taxation is appointed by the Governor. This bill removes the statutory age restriction of 70 years for holding this gubernatorial appointment.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments, including the Director of Assessments and Taxation, whose statutory age qualifications are modified by this bill.
The bill repeals the mandatory retirement age for certain state and county officials; the agency was consulted regarding potential retirement and pension administration impacts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the $1 per-page fee for electronic copies of documents recorded or filed with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation. Retains the $1 per-page fee specifically for nonelectronic copies of papers recorded or filed with the department. Maintains the $1 fee for duplicate certificates issued at the same time as an original certificate. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals and business entities requesting electronic copies of documents recorded or filed with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by approximately $57,500 in FY 2024 and by $76,700 annually beginning in FY 2025 due to repealing electronic copy fees. State expenditures are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the process for health insurance carriers to provide notice of adverse decisions in nonemergency cases. Authorizes carriers to notify members, their representatives, or providers by text, fax, email, online portal, or other expedited means. Requires affirmative consent from the recipient before a carrier may use these expedited communication methods. Permits carriers to continue providing notice orally by telephone. Maintains the requirement to send detailed written notice within five working days after the decision.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: health insurance carriers, health plan members, members' representatives, and health care providers acting on behalf of members
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact because the change is procedural in nature.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 724 is a departmental bill requested by the Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA). It amends the Insurance Article regarding health insurance carriers' internal grievance processes and notice requirements for adverse coverage decisions, which are regulated and enforced by the MIA.

The required notice for carrier adverse decisions directs members to the Health Advocacy Unit (Health Education and Advocacy Unit), which is housed within the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General to assist consumers in mediating and filing grievances.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to provide free or discounted products or services. Requires these offerings to educate on risk, mitigate risk of loss, or enhance enrollee health or financial wellness. Mandates that carriers make qualifying offerings available to all policyholders who hold the associated policy. Prohibits carriers from increasing premiums or denying claims based on whether a policyholder accepts or uses an offering. Authorizes the Maryland Insurance Commissioner to determine eligible products and services by regulation.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Commissioner; Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Life insurers, health insurers, property and casualty insurers, nonprofit health service plans, health maintenance organizations, insurance producers, and policyholders
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Any administrative impact on the Maryland Insurance Administration can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not materially affected, and local finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 725 is a departmental bill requested by the Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA). It amends the Insurance Article to permit insurers to offer certain products and services alongside policies without violating anti-rebating laws, and authorizes the Insurance Commissioner to adopt regulations and review related contract, form, and rate filings.

qa_results.bill_summary: Continues the State Board of Examiners of Psychologists under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act. Extends the termination date for the Board and its adopted regulations to July 1, 2025. Maintains the Board's statutory authority to license psychologists and register psychology associates. Preserves the Board's power to investigate complaints and enforce professional practice standards.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Examiners of Psychologists; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: licensed psychologists, registered psychology associates, and mental health consumers in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Maintains special fund revenues and expenditures for the State Board of Examiners of Psychologists through fiscal 2025. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Examiners of Psychologists is housed within the Maryland Department of Health, which oversees health professional licensing boards. This departmental bill extends the board's termination date through July 1, 2025, maintaining its regulatory operations, special fund revenues, and expenditures.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date for the State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners by one year to July 1, 2025. Continues the board and its regulatory authority under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act. Maintains the board's oversight of the Physical Therapy Practice Act. Preserves all statutory provisions and regulations governing physical therapists and physical therapist assistants. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed physical therapists, licensed physical therapy assistants, and physical therapy patients in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Maintains existing special fund revenues and expenditures for the State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners through fiscal year 2025. Has no local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners is housed within the Maryland Department of Health. This bill extends the statutory termination date of the Board, allowing it to continue regulating physical therapy practice and maintaining its special fund revenues and expenditures.

qa_results.bill_summary: Continues the State Board of Examiners in Optometry under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act. Extends the termination date for the board and its regulatory authority to July 1, 2025. Preserves the board's authority to license optometrists and regulate optometry practice in Maryland. Maintains the board's power to investigate alleged violations and issue disciplinary actions. Takes effect June 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Examiners in Optometry; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: licensed optometrists and optometry patients in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Maintains special fund revenues and expenditures for the State Board of Examiners in Optometry through fiscal 2025. No local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Examiners in Optometry is a health occupations licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Health. This departmental bill extends the Board's termination date through July 1, 2025, maintaining its regulatory authority and associated special fund revenues and expenditures.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date for the State Board for Certification of Residential Child Care Program Professionals to July 1, 2025. Continues the board under the provisions of the Maryland Program Evaluation Act. Maintains the board's authority to certify residential child care program administrators and child and youth care practitioners. Preserves regulatory requirements and standards for staff in licensed residential child care programs. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board for Certification of Residential Child Care Program Professionals; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: residential child care program administrators, residential child and youth care practitioners, and licensed residential child care programs
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues and expenditures for the board are maintained through fiscal 2025. The bill has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board for Certification of Residential Child Care Program Professionals is housed within the Maryland Department of Health (MDH). MDH sponsored this departmental bill to extend the board's termination date under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act.
The board certifies administrators and practitioners working in residential child care programs licensed by the Department of Human Services, and DHS leadership appoints representatives to the board.

The board certifies administrators and practitioners working in residential programs licensed by the Department of Juvenile Services, and DJS leadership participates in appointing representatives to the board.
The Governor appoints six members of the board with the advice of the Secretary of Health and receives the board's annual reports.

qa_results.bill_summary: Transfers the State Coordinator for Autism Strategy from the Governor's Office of Community Initiatives to the Department of Disabilities. Requires the Department of Disabilities to staff the Advisory Stakeholder Group on Autism-Related Needs. Directs the Governor to transfer two positions and associated general funds to the Department on July 1, 2023. Expands the Maryland Commission on Disabilities by adding an individual with a traumatic brain injury appointed by the Governor. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Disabilities; Governor's Office of Community Initiatives
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals with autism and their families, individuals with traumatic brain injuries, and individuals with disabilities in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No net impact on State expenditures or revenues. In FY 2024, general fund expenditures for the Department of Disabilities increase by at least $131,275 to support the transferred positions, with an equal expenditure decrease for the Governor's Office of Community Initiatives. Local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly transfers the State Coordinator for Autism Strategy and two positions with associated funding to the Department of Disabilities, tasks the department with staffing the Advisory Stakeholder Group on Autism-Related Needs, and expands the membership of the Maryland Commission on Disabilities.

The bill removes the State Coordinator for Autism Strategy and staffing responsibilities for the Advisory Stakeholder Group on Autism-Related Needs from GOCI, transferring two positions and associated general funds away from the agency.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the statutory membership of the Maryland Commission on Disabilities by adding an individual with a traumatic brain injury and modifies the staffing support for the Advisory Stakeholder Group on Autism-Related Needs.

The bill mandates executive action requiring the Governor to transfer two positions and general fund appropriations between executive units, and requires the Governor to appoint an additional member to the Maryland Commission on Disabilities.

The Secretary of Budget and Management (or designee) serves as a statutory member of the Maryland Commission on Disabilities, and the agency coordinates position and budgetary adjustments across executive branch departments.
The agency assists the Governor with recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments, including the new required commission member with a traumatic brain injury.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires vehicle allocation systems operated by a manufacturer, distributor, factory branch, or affiliate to be reasonable and fair. Mandates disclosure of allocation methods to dealers of the same line make upon written request. Places the burden of proving compliance on the manufacturer, distributor, factory branch, or affiliate during disputes. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: vehicle manufacturers, distributors, factory branches, their affiliates, and licensed vehicle dealers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State finances or operations and has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration regulates businesses that manufacture, distribute, and sell motor vehicles in Maryland pursuant to Title 15 of the Transportation Article, which this bill directly amends.
The Maryland Department of Transportation is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration and oversees state transportation statutes and regulations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends through fiscal 2027 a required $14,000,000 annual distribution of abandoned property funds to the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund. Requires the Governor to appropriate $14,000,000 annually from the Fund to the Maryland Legal Services Corporation through fiscal 2027. Repeals the December 31, 2024 termination date enacted under Chapter 40 of 2022. Finances access to legal representation and related outreach for eligible tenants facing eviction proceedings.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland; Maryland Legal Services Corporation; Governor
qa_results.stakeholders: Low-income tenants facing eviction or lease termination proceedings; legal aid organizations; landlords; Maryland Legal Services Corporation
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: General fund revenues decrease by $14.0 million annually in FY 2025 through FY 2027 due to the redirected unclaimed property proceeds. Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund revenues and expenditures increase correspondingly by $14.0 million annually across FY 2025 through FY 2027 to fund legal representation through the Maryland Legal Services Corporation. Local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the State Comptroller distribute $14.0 million annually from net abandoned property proceeds to the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund through fiscal year 2027 and account for the fund.

The bill statutorily requires the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $14.0 million from the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund to the Maryland Legal Services Corporation in the state budget bill for each fiscal year through 2027.

As the agency responsible for state budget preparation and fiscal planning, DBM must implement the $14.0 million annual mandated appropriation and manage the associated impact on General Fund and special fund revenues and expenditures through fiscal year 2027.
Under the provisions of the bill and underlying statute, the State Treasurer holds the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund separately and is responsible for investing the fund's assets.

qa_results.bill_summary: Regulates security guard employers and requires individuals who provide security guard services to an employer to be certified. Mandates completion of initial and continuing security training identified or established by the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission. Prohibits security guards from carrying handguns on duty without employer approval and State Police verification. Requires security guards and employers to report use-of-force incidents within 48 hours. Mandates that security guard agencies and employers maintain specified commercial general liability insurance coverage.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of State Police; Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: security guards, security guard agencies, and security guard employers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $476,900 in FY 2024 for the Department of State Police to hire two administrative specialists and complete technical systems upgrades, with ongoing operating costs in future years. Local finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Police (through the Secretary of State Police) is the primary regulatory and implementing body under the bill, responsible for certifying security guards, regulating security guard employers, tracking handgun authorizations, and collecting use-of-force incident reports. The bill also requires general fund expenditures of over $476,000 for personnel and system upgrades within the department.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission (MPTSC), which operates under DPSCS, identify or establish 12-hour initial and 8-hour continuing training programs for security guard certification. In addition, background checks and fingerprinting run through the department's Criminal Justice Information System Central Repository.

The Department of General Services directly employs security personnel to protect state facilities and Capitol Police property, making it an employer subject to the standards, although fiscal impact on the agency is anticipated to be absorbed within existing operations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Board of Public Works to publish a model liquidated damages policy by January 1, 2024. Requires each unit of State government to adopt a substantially similar written policy by July 1, 2024. Authorizes primary procurement units to adopt policies applicable to procurements within their control authority. Requires a unit to obtain unit head approval when deciding not to include a liquidated damages clause. Requires unit head approval and documentation if not pursuing liquidated damages on contracts valued at $5,000,000 or more.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Public Works; Procurement Improvement Council
qa_results.stakeholders: State procurement units; State contractors and vendors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Board of Public Works and State procuring agencies can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Board of Public Works is the primary implementing agency under the bill, required to publish a model policy regarding the inclusion and use of liquidated damages provisions in State procurement contracts by January 1, 2024, in consultation with the Procurement Improvement Council.

As the State's central procurement authority and a designated primary procurement unit controlling most executive branch procurements, DGS is authorized and required to establish a liquidated damages policy for units within its control and adhere to unit-head approval and documentation requirements.

MDOT is a designated primary procurement unit with independent procurement authority and must adopt and implement a liquidated damages policy substantially similar to BPW's model policy for transportation contracts under its control authority.

The State Treasurer sits on the Board of Public Works, acts as a primary procurement unit for banking and insurance services, and oversees Maryland 529, whose contracts are explicitly brought under the bill's liquidated damages requirements.

USM is a primary procurement unit and the bill explicitly amends § 11-203(e) to subject its procurements to the liquidated damages requirements under § 15-113, despite its general exemption from State procurement law.
Morgan State University is a designated primary procurement unit and is explicitly subjected to § 15-113 liquidated damages policies and documentation rules under § 11-203(e).
St. Mary's College of Maryland is a designated primary procurement unit and is explicitly subjected to § 15-113 liquidated damages requirements under the amended § 11-203(e).
The Maryland Port Administration is a designated primary procurement unit authorized to conduct its own procurements and must adopt a liquidated damages policy governing port-related contracts.
The bill explicitly amends § 11-203(c) to apply the liquidated damages requirements of § 15-113 to the Maryland Stadium Authority, an entity otherwise largely exempt from State procurement law.

The bill amends § 11-203(d) to specifically subject contracts executed for the State Retirement and Pension System (for investment management, asset maintenance, and administration) to § 15-113 liquidated damages rules.
The bill explicitly amends § 11-203(f) to make investment and asset management contracts for the Maryland Prepaid College Trust subject to the liquidated damages provisions in § 15-113.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency administers the Maryland Corps Program, which is explicitly amended in § 11-203(i) to be subject to the liquidated damages requirements of § 15-113.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a State offshore wind energy goal of reaching 8,500 megawatts of capacity by 2031. Requires the Public Service Commission to request transmission system analyses and solicit offshore wind transmission proposals. Directs the Department of General Services to competitively procure up to 5,000,000 megawatt-hours of offshore wind annually. Authorizes offshore wind developers meeting specified labor standards to request exemptions from remitting certain federal tax credits. Mandates that approved offshore wind projects and selected transmission projects enter into binding community benefit agreements.
qa_results.responsible_party: Public Service Commission; Department of General Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Offshore wind developers, electric transmission owners, electricity ratepayers, labor organizations and craft workers, and small, minority, women-owned, and veteran-owned businesses
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: In FY 2024, Public Service Commission special fund expenditures increase by $635,256, offset by public service company assessments. Department of General Services general fund expenditures increase by $213,905 in FY 2024 for procurement personnel. Future state and local electricity costs under resulting power purchase agreements are indeterminate but potentially significant.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: PSC is a primary implementing agency tasked with coordinating with PJM Interconnection to study transmission upgrades, issuing competitive solicitations for offshore wind transmission facilities, selecting proposals, adjudicating federal tax credit remittance exemptions, and submitting annual reports on supplier diversity.

DGS is designated to issue a major competitive sealed procurement and enter into power purchase agreements (PPAs) for up to 5,000,000 megawatt-hours annually of offshore wind energy and associated renewable energy credits, and manage associated labor peace agreement attestations.

MEA is statutorily required to be consulted by the Public Service Commission regarding the transmission system expansion analysis and to coordinate with PSC and stakeholders following the selection of transmission proposals.

DNR's Power Plant Research Program (PPRP) is authorized to propose conditions on transmission project proposals selected by the PSC, and DNR experiences operational impacts associated with environmental and siting evaluations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOSBA is charged with assisting potential offshore wind applicants and minority investors, and collaborating with applicants to establish clear plans for minority business enterprise participation goals and procedures.

OPC advocates for residential utility consumers in proceedings before the PSC, which is directly relevant given the bill's significant provisions regarding ratepayer impacts, transmission cost allocations, and OREC exemptions.

The bill establishes community benefit agreement terms requiring payment of prevailing wage rates set by the Commissioner of Labor and Industry and utilization of registered apprenticeship programs overseen by MD Labor.
OAG is consulted alongside GOSBA to assist applicants and minority investors and to provide legal counsel for the State's complex regulatory and procurement requirements under the Act.

The Governor's Office receives annual reporting on minority business enterprise participation in offshore wind projects, receives statements of determination if transmission proposals are not selected, and is authorized to provide funding appropriations in the state budget for PSC studies.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Secretary of Housing and Community Development to issue multiple final tax credit certificates for phased catalytic revitalization projects. Permits original recipients to transfer initial tax credit certificates under specified written consent requirements. Limits each phased final credit certificate to not more than 20% of eligible project expenses to date. Requires the Smart Growth Subcabinet to study and recommend an implementation plan for preserving and reusing historic complexes. Mandates that the Subcabinet report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by December 31, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development; Smart Growth Subcabinet
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals, nonprofit organizations, and business entities undertaking catalytic revitalization projects or developing historic properties in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential acceleration and extension of the timing of credits claimed against the State income tax, which may significantly affect State general fund revenues in any given year. Corporate income tax impacts may also affect local highway user revenues and the Transportation Trust Fund. The Smart Growth Subcabinet can complete the required study and report with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) administers the Catalytic Revitalization Project Tax Credit. The bill directly alters DHCD's authority by allowing the Secretary to issue multiple final tax credit certificates for phased projects and establishing specific conditions for the transfer of initial tax credit certificates.

The Maryland Department of Planning (MDP) staffs the Smart Growth Subcabinet, which is mandated by the bill to conduct a study and develop recommendations for an implementation plan addressing the preservation and reuse of historic complexes in Maryland.

The Comptroller administers State income tax collections and tax credit claims. The bill's changes to the catalytic revitalization tax credit structure may alter the timing and claiming of income tax credits and refunds.

The Smart Growth Subcabinet operates under the Executive Branch, and the bill requires the Subcabinet to report its findings and recommendations regarding historic complexes directly to the Governor by December 31, 2023.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes individuals to register and terminate domestic partnerships with the local register of wills. Grants surviving registered domestic partners intestate inheritance rights, family allowances, priority of administration, and inheritance tax exemptions. Prohibits a surviving registered domestic partner from claiming an elective share against a decedent's will. Removes statutory references to child legitimacy and clarifies parentage for children of registered domestic partners. Increases the surviving partner or spousal intestate share to $100,000 plus half the residue when non-joint surviving issue exist.
qa_results.responsible_party: Register of Wills
qa_results.stakeholders: couples in domestic partnerships, surviving registered domestic partners, estate heirs, and personal representatives
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: General fund revenues decrease annually by an indeterminate amount due to the new inheritance tax exemption for registered domestic partners, partially offset by filing fees of up to $25. State expenditures and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Register of Wills is the primary agency tasked with implementing the bill, including receiving and recording declarations of domestic partnership and termination, maintaining public records with appropriate address redactions, establishing and maintaining a certified list of reciprocal jurisdictions, and applying domestic partner intestate succession rules and inheritance tax exemptions during estate administration.

The Comptroller oversees state tax revenue collection, including the inheritance tax. The bill expands the inheritance tax exemption for surviving registered domestic partners, which impacts state general fund tax revenues.

The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the Maryland Judiciary, including the Orphans' Courts and Circuit Courts that oversee contested probate, estate administration proceedings, and parentage determinations modified by the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Cyber Maryland Program within the Maryland Technology Development Corporation to expand the State's cybersecurity workforce. Creates the Cyber Maryland Fund to administer grants to elementary and secondary schools, higher education institutions, for-profit corporations, and non-profits. Establishes the Cyber Maryland Board to provide strategic input, stakeholder engagement, and advisory support. Requires the Governor to appropriate sufficient annual budget funds beginning in fiscal year 2025 for program personnel. Requires the Maryland Higher Education Commission to expand the Cyber Warrior Diversity Program to accommodate emerging certification trends. Directs unexpended Cyber Warrior Diversity Program allocations to revert to the Commission for reallocation in the upcoming fiscal year.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Technology Development Corporation; Cyber Maryland Board; Maryland Higher Education Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: cybersecurity employers, information technology workers, elementary and secondary schools, public and private higher education institutions, community colleges, and participating workforce non-profits
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $690,000 in FY 2024, with ongoing mandated and discretionary funding projected between $669,300 and $705,400 annually through FY 2028. Cyber Maryland Fund special fund revenues and expenditures increase correspondingly. Local revenues and expenditures may increase to the extent local school systems and community colleges receive program grants.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: TEDCO is the primary implementing agency tasked with establishing, housing, and administering the Cyber Maryland Program and the Cyber Maryland Fund, appointing the program's executive director, and supporting the Cyber Maryland Board.

MHEC is directly tasked with expanding the Cyber Warrior Diversity Program annually based on industry certification trends identified under the bill, and managing the reallocation of unexpended program funds.
MHEC is directly tasked with expanding the Cyber Warrior Diversity Program annually based on cybersecurity certification trends and administering grant funding and reallocations under the program.

The Cyber Maryland Program is specifically charged with supporting DoIT's efforts to improve the state's cybersecurity posture, and the Secretary of Information Technology serves as an ex officio member of the Cyber Maryland Board.
The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) is a designated member of the Cyber Maryland Board, and the board is mandated to coordinate cybersecurity workforce development efforts with the Department.

The Secretary of Labor serves on the Cyber Maryland Board, the board must coordinate workforce development efforts with MD Labor, and the program considers synergies with MD Labor programs like EARN and Maryland Apprenticeship.
Morgan State University is a statutory participating institution and grant recipient under the Cyber Warrior Diversity Program, which is expanded and restructured by the bill.
Multiple USM institutions (Bowie State University, Coppin State University, UMES, and UMBC Training Centers) participate in and receive funding from the expanded Cyber Warrior Diversity Program.
The Maryland Secretary of Veterans Affairs (now Veterans and Military Families) or their designee is designated as a member of the Cyber Maryland Board.

The Governor is required to include mandated appropriations in the state budget beginning in FY 2025 for program personnel, appoints nine members to the Cyber Maryland Board, and receives annual reports from the program.
DBM is responsible for state budget oversight and must implement the mandated state general fund appropriations required beginning in FY 2025 to fund program staffing.
The State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold and invest the monies of the newly established Cyber Maryland Fund separately from other funds.
The Comptroller is required by statute to account for the newly established Cyber Maryland Fund.
The Cyber Maryland Fund authorizes grants to elementary and secondary schools to operate cybersecurity programs aligned with the statewide strategic plan.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Cyber Maryland Board as a new advisory body to provide strategic guidance, assist with stakeholder outreach, and advise the program.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and appointing the nine required non-ex-officio members of the Cyber Maryland Board.
The board focuses on statewide workforce strategy and oversees Career and Technical Education (CTE) programs in IT and cybersecurity that intersect with the program's talent pipeline goals.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange and the Maryland Department of Health to develop a joint report. Directs the report to compare options offering affordable health care and dental care coverage to undocumented residents. Requires evaluating State costs, impacts on the uninsured, potential benefit designs, and implementation considerations. Mandates analysis across Medicaid, the Maryland Children's Health Program, and qualified Exchange health and dental plans. Requires study of specific groups, including low-income individuals, residents under 21, and adults aged 65 and older. Requires reporting findings and recommendations to designated General Assembly committees by October 31, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Health Benefit Exchange; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: undocumented immigrants in Maryland ineligible for Medicaid, the Maryland Children's Health Program, or Exchange plans due to immigration status
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures and revenues are not affected; the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange and the Maryland Department of Health can develop the report and submit findings with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange, alongside the Maryland Department of Health, to develop and submit a report comparing options, costs, potential benefit designs, and implementation considerations for offering affordable health care and dental care coverage to undocumented immigrants.

The bill explicitly mandates the Maryland Department of Health, in conjunction with the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange, to study and report on options and costs for expanding coverage through Medicaid and the Maryland Children's Health Program (MCHP) to individuals currently ineligible due to immigration status.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of Natural Resources to provide a discount on annual State park passes. Mandates a discount of at least $40 for all first responders and law enforcement officers who are Maryland residents. Defines the pass as allowing unlimited day-use entry to all State parks and State park facilities for one year. Takes effect June 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland residents who are first responders or law enforcement officers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues decrease minimally beginning in fiscal 2023 due to the minimum $40 discount on annual State park passes; expenditures are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Department of Natural Resources provide a discount of at least $40 on annual State park passes for Maryland first responders and law enforcement officers, which directly affects the department's pass administration and results in a minimal decrease in special fund revenues.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of the Environment and the Maryland Department of Health to study local environmental health specialist staffing needs. Mandates that the study examine educational requirements, wage competitiveness, and the feasibility of establishing an apprenticeship program. Requires both departments to report their staffing findings and recommendations by December 1, 2023. Directs the Department of the Environment to study delegating well and septic permitting authority to the health department. Mandates consultation with the Department of Legislative Services and the University of Maryland Agriculture and Food Systems Extension Program. Requires an interim report on permitting authority by December 1, 2023, and a final report by December 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment; Maryland Department of Health; State Board of Environmental Health Specialists; Department of Legislative Services; University of Maryland Agriculture and Food Systems Extension Program
qa_results.stakeholders: environmental health specialists, local health departments, and well and septic systems permit applicants
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected because affected agencies can implement the required studies with existing budgeted resources. Local finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is directly responsible for co-leading the study on staffing needs for environmental health specialists in local health departments and leading the study on the delegation of well and septic systems permitting authority, including submitting interim and final reports to the Governor and General Assembly.
