MDH, in conjunction with the State Board of Environmental Health Specialists (housed within MDH), is tasked with co-conducting the staffing needs study and reporting findings, and is also the focus of the study regarding the delegation of well and septic systems permitting authority.

MDE is required to consult with the University of Maryland Agriculture and Food Systems Extension Program (part of the University of Maryland / USM) in conducting the study on well and septic systems permitting delegation.
The required study findings, interim report, and final report on environmental health specialists and well and septic system permitting must be formally submitted to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Protecting Against Hate Crimes Grant Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund. Provides grants through the Fund to nonprofit organizations, including faith-based organizations, for security enhancements against hate crimes. Requires the Executive Director of the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services to administer the Fund. Requires setting aside at least $1,000,000 each year for faith-based organizations, prioritizing applicants with high hate crime prevalence. Authorizes the Governor to include an annual $5,000,000 appropriation to the Fund beginning in fiscal year 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services; State Treasurer; Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Nonprofit organizations in Maryland, including faith-based organizations and institutions targeted by hate crimes; security technology and enhancement vendors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures increase by $5.0 million annually beginning in fiscal 2025 if authorized discretionary funding is provided to capitalize the fund. Special fund revenues and expenditures increase by $5.0 million in fiscal 2024 and $10.0 million annually thereafter, reflecting existing program funding flowing through the fund in addition to newly authorized grant funding. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly designates the Executive Director of this office (formerly known as the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services) to administer the newly established Protecting Against Hate Crimes Grant Fund, establish distribution procedures, set aside funding for faith-based organizations, and submit annual reports to the General Assembly.
The bill mandates that the State Treasurer hold the new Protecting Against Hate Crimes Grant Fund separately and invest its moneys, with interest credited to the fund.
The bill specifies that the Comptroller of Maryland shall account for the newly established special fund.
The bill authorizes an annual appropriation of up to $5,000,000 in the state budget beginning in fiscal year 2025, which affects state budget development and fiscal planning overseen by DBM.
The bill authorizes the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $5,000,000 to the fund in the annual budget bill starting in fiscal year 2025.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Governor to appropriate $500,000 annually in the State budget bill. Directs the Maryland State Department of Education to grant the funds to local school systems. Funds cover expenses for student field trips to museums of cultural import. Defines eligible museums as those presenting the history and culture of oppressed and historically underrepresented communities. Requires the Department to report annually by October 1 on grant recipients, expenditures, and student participation.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland public school students, local school systems, and museums of cultural import
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $500,000 annually beginning in FY 2025 due to a mandated appropriation. Local school systems receive $500,000 in grant revenue annually statewide beginning in FY 2025, with school system expenditures increasing correspondingly.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is the primary administering agency responsible for distributing the $500,000 in annual grant funds to local school systems for field trips and submitting an annual report to the General Assembly.
DBM oversees the state budget process and will be responsible for incorporating the mandated annual $500,000 general fund appropriation into the executive budget starting in FY 2025.
The bill explicitly mandates that the Governor include an appropriation of $500,000 in the annual state budget bill for the field trip grant program.

The corporation operates the Reginald F. Lewis Museum of Maryland African American History and Culture, which is specifically identified in statute as a qualifying 'museum of cultural import' eligible for student field trip visits funded by the bill's grants.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the circumstances under which specified libraries must permit inspection, use, or disclosure of an individual's circulation record. Applies confidentiality requirements to public, school, college, and university libraries across the State. Prohibits disclosing circulation records that link personal identifiers to patron use of library materials, services, or facilities. Authorizes disclosure only when necessary for the reasonable operation of the library. Permits disclosure upon the written consent of the individual or pursuant to a subpoena or court order.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Library Agency; public, school, college, and university libraries
qa_results.stakeholders: Patrons of public, school, college, and university libraries; public, school, college, and university library staff and administrators
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State government finances or operations or local library system finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly updates privacy and disclosure standards for patron circulation records across public libraries, which fall under the strategic leadership, funding, and coordination of the Maryland State Library Agency.
The bill governs the confidentiality and permitted disclosures of circulation records maintained by public school libraries under the oversight of the Maryland State Department of Education.
The bill applies directly to university libraries, establishing legal standards under which USM institution libraries may disclose or inspect individual patron circulation records.
MHEC coordinates and oversees policies affecting postsecondary institutions in Maryland, whose college and university libraries are subject to the bill's circulation record privacy provisions.
As an independent public university, Morgan State University operates academic libraries governed by the bill's restrictions on the inspection and disclosure of patron circulation records.
As a public college, its library operations are directly governed by the statutory revisions concerning the disclosure and confidentiality of patron circulation records.
As a state-operated public school, its school library facilities and student circulation records are subject to the bill's revised confidentiality and disclosure requirements.
The bill explicitly allows disclosure of library circulation records pursuant to a subpoena or court order issued or processed through the judicial system.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Statewide Rental Assistance Voucher Program in the Department of Housing and Community Development. Directs the Department and public housing agencies to provide vouchers to low-income families on federal waitlists. Limits household payments to not more than 30% of monthly adjusted gross income for rent and utilities. Provides housing assistance payments for up to five years or until a federal voucher becomes available. Mandates annual state budget appropriations of $10,000,000 for fiscal years 2025 through 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Low-income Maryland families on federal housing choice voucher waitlists, local public housing agencies, and residential rental property owners
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $255,400 in FY 2024 for administrative startup and by approximately $10.3 million annually in FY 2025 through FY 2027 to cover the $10.0 million mandated appropriation and ongoing administrative costs. Expenditures increase to approximately $10.6 million in FY 2028. Local public housing agency revenues and expenditures increase to administer vouchers and perform unit inspections, partially offset by a required 6% administrative allocation from program funds.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 848 establishes the Statewide Rental Assistance Voucher Program directly within the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD). DHCD is responsible for administering the program, distributing funds and vouchers, performing inspections in certain subdivisions, adopting implementing regulations, and reporting annually on program performance.

The bill establishes a statutory mandated appropriation of $10 million annually for fiscal years 2025 through 2027, and sufficient ongoing funding beginning in fiscal year 2028, which DBM must incorporate and supervise within the executive budget process.

The bill mandates that the Governor include specific appropriations for the program in the annual state budget bill starting in FY 2025, and requires DHCD to submit an annual report on the program to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Baltimore City to enact an in rem foreclosure process for vacant or nuisance properties with delinquent taxes. Permits the city to file an in rem foreclosure complaint when taxes remain delinquent for at least six months. Requires the city to sell property that has value at public auction or compensate interested parties after appraisal. Allows Baltimore City to retain title without compensating interested parties if the property does not have value. Limits reopening foreclosure judgments to grounds of lack of jurisdiction or fraud within strict timeframes.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore City; Circuit Court for Baltimore City
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners and interested parties of vacant or nuisance properties in Baltimore City, prospective property purchasers, and Baltimore City government
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures may increase beginning in fiscal 2024 for the Circuit Court for Baltimore City clerk's office, and State Annuity Bond Fund revenues may be affected by an indeterminate amount. Baltimore City finances may be impacted by administrative, legal, and maintenance costs, offset by potential property tax revenues and sales proceeds.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a judicial in rem foreclosure process for vacant and nuisance properties in Baltimore City that is conducted through the Circuit Court for Baltimore City. The court is tasked with receiving complaints, conducting hearings, entering foreclosure judgments, and administering the distribution of surplus auction/appraisal funds held in escrow. According to the fiscal note, State general fund expenditures may increase to support additional staff and operating costs for the Baltimore City Circuit Court clerk's office.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands firearm safe storage requirements to prevent access by unsupervised minors and individuals prohibited from possessing firearms. Prohibits storing loaded firearms, or unloaded firearms with ready access to ammunition, where minors or prohibited persons have access. Bars individuals convicted of firearm storage violations from possessing regulated firearms for five years, or longer under aggravating circumstances. Requires the Deputy Secretary for Public Health Services to create a youth suicide prevention and safe storage guide by January 1, 2024. Directs the Maryland Department of Health to distribute the guide and award educational grants to local entities.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Deputy Secretary for Public Health Services
qa_results.stakeholders: firearm owners; minors; individuals prohibited from possessing firearms; local school systems; local health departments; nonprofit agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $50,000 in FY 2024 for the Maryland Department of Health to contract with an outside consultant to develop the guide. Grant-related expenditures and correctional costs cannot be reliably estimated. State and local revenues and local expenditures may increase minimally due to expanded application of existing criminal penalties.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH's Deputy Secretary for Public Health Services is the primary official tasked with developing the Youth Suicide Prevention and Firearm Safe Storage Guide, convening the stakeholder advisory committee, disseminating the guide, administering grant funding, and submitting annual implementation reports to the General Assembly.

MSP regulates firearm possession, enforces statewide firearm laws, and licenses/certifies firearm safety instructors who are specifically mandated to receive electronic copies of the safe storage guide under the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS may experience a minimal fiscal and operational impact from increased incarceration and supervision resulting from the expanded scope of criminal offenses relating to firearm storage and illegal possession of regulated firearms.

The State court system is responsible for adjudicating criminal charges and managing case filings for expanded misdemeanor firearm storage violations and regulated firearm possession disqualifications.
MSDE is explicitly named as a recipient of the guide, and local school systems under its policy umbrella are eligible for grants to educate families on safe firearm storage practices.
DJS is explicitly designated in statute to receive the Youth Suicide Prevention and Firearm Safe Storage Guide to assist in suicide prevention and public safety efforts for justice-involved youth.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a stakeholder advisory committee comprising health practitioners, safe storage experts, affected families, and youth advocates to make recommendations for the state guide.

DNR is referenced regarding the certificate of firearm and hunter safety it issues under the Natural Resources Article, which functions as an exception to the safe storage violation for minors accessing rifles or shotguns.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters requirements for the removal from office of the State Administrator of Elections. Maintains that removal requires the affirmative vote of four duly confirmed members when the State Board of Elections is fully constituted. Repeals the requirement that removal be for incompetence, misconduct, or other good cause. Repeals requirements for the board to provide written charges, notice, and an opportunity to be heard before removal. Repeals the authority of the State Administrator to continue serving until a successor is appointed and confirmed.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Elections
qa_results.stakeholders: State Administrator of Elections and members of the State Board of Elections
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State finances and has no local effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the statutory procedures, grounds, and requirements for the removal of the State Administrator of Elections by the State Board of Elections.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date of the State Board of Social Work Examiners to July 1, 2025. Requires the Board to notify an applicant within 15 business days whether an application or supplemental documentation is complete. Establishes the Workgroup on Social Worker Requirements for Licensure staffed by the Maryland Department of Health. Directs the Workgroup to examine licensing examinations, analyze assessment bias, and identify alternatives. Mandates reports to designated General Assembly committees by September 2023, December 2023, and December 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Social Work Examiners; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: applicants for social worker licensure; licensed social workers; State Board of Social Work Examiners
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $75,000 in FY 2024 and $15,400 in FY 2025 for contractual staff and board operations. Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Board are maintained through FY 2025. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Social Work Examiners is housed within the Department of Health. The bill extends the Board's termination date under the sunset act, imposes application review timelines on the Board, and requires MDH to provide staff and funding for the Workgroup on Social Worker Requirements for Licensure.

The Secretary of Human Services (or designee) is designated as an ex officio member of the Workgroup on Social Worker Requirements for Licensure, which impacts social work practice and workforce pipelines vital to DHS.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Director of the Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing (or designee) is mandated as a member of the Workgroup, which is charged with examining licensing barriers and bias impacting deaf and hard of hearing candidates.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally creates and establishes the Workgroup on Social Worker Requirements for Licensure to study social work examination bias, temporary licensing, and licensure requirements.
The Governor is tasked with appointing eight members to the Workgroup on Social Worker Requirements for Licensure and designating the chair.
Assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointees to the newly established Workgroup.

qa_results.bill_summary: Cures previous Acts of the General Assembly containing potential title defects. Repeals and reenacts without amendments statutory provisions governing the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund. Reenacts prohibitions against fraudulent or dishonest conduct during driver's license and moped operator's permit examinations. Validates the affected 2022 enactments without altering substantive legal requirements. Takes effect immediately as an emergency measure upon enactment.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland General Assembly; Maryland Legal Services Corporation; Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Applicants for driver's licenses and moped operator's permits, low-income tenants eligible for eviction legal representation, and the Maryland Legal Services Corporation.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact, as the bill is technical in nature and validates existing law.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 877 cures a title defect in § 16-301(q) of the Transportation Article, which prohibits fraudulent or dishonest conduct during examinations and tests for driver's licenses and moped permits administered by the MVA.
MDOT is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration and oversees the administration and enforcement of the Maryland Transportation Article.
The bill cures a title defect in Real Property § 8-909, which designates the State Treasurer to hold and invest the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund.
The bill validates and reenacts Real Property § 8-909, which requires the Comptroller to account for the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund.

Real Property § 8-909, reenacted by the bill, provides that settlement funds and judgments obtained by the OAG Division of Consumer Protection under the Consumer Protection Act for rental residential property violations are credited to the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund.

The bill reenacts statutory language in Real Property § 8-909 directing the Governor to include a specific appropriation to MLSC from the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund in the annual budget bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the definition of therapy horse under the Maryland Veterans Service Animal Program. Removes the requirement that a State-licensed stable hold premier accreditation from the Professional Association of Therapeutic Horsemanship, International. Allows any State-licensed stable that is a member center of the association to qualify. Maintains alternate eligibility for stables with certified professionals from the Equine Assisted Growth and Learning Association. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Veterans Affairs
qa_results.stakeholders: eligible Maryland veterans and State-licensed stables providing equine therapy services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the Maryland Veterans Service Animal Program, which is housed within and administered by the Department of Veterans and Military Families (formerly the Department of Veterans Affairs).

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Department of Natural Resources to issue annual license exemptions to governmental entities and nonprofit organizations. Permits clinics for armed forces members, veterans, and individuals participating in physical or mental wellness outdoor events. Includes participants in special needs outdoor events, scientific collection permittees, and underserved State residents. Extends the exemption to primary caregivers or representatives attending to or instructing covered individuals. Requires exempted entities to report event and participant information annually as required by the Department.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Governmental entities and nonprofit organizations providing fishing clinics, individuals serving or who have served in the U.S. Armed Forces, participants in outdoor wellness or special needs events, scientific collection permit holders, underserved State residents, and attending caregivers or instructors.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect in FY 2023. Special fund revenues for the Fisheries Management and Protection Fund and Fisheries Research and Development Fund may increase beginning in FY 2024 if clinic participants subsequently purchase licenses or stamps, though the amount cannot be reliably estimated. State expenditures and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources is the primary implementing agency responsible for issuing the annual fishing license and stamp exemptions, establishing regulations, receiving annual compliance reports, and managing the associated special fund revenues.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the mandated annual appropriation to the Maryland Construction Education and Innovation Fund. Limits the existing $250,000 annual appropriation through fiscal year 2024. Requires the Governor to include an appropriation of $625,000 in the annual budget bill for fiscal years 2025 through 2029. Directs the funding to support operations of the Maryland Center for Construction Education and Innovation. Eliminates all mandated appropriations to the Fund after fiscal year 2029.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor; Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland Center for Construction Education and Innovation; Maryland construction industry employers and trainees
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $375,000 annually from FY 2025 through FY 2029 to meet the increased mandated appropriation, with identical increases in special fund revenues and expenditures. The mandated appropriation terminates beginning in FY 2030. No local effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Construction Education and Innovation Fund is codified under the Labor and Employment Article within the Department of Labor's statutory purview, and the agency is directly involved with workforce development initiatives.
As the agency responsible for formulating and managing the state budget, DBM must implement the statutory mandate requiring an appropriation of $625,000 annually for fiscal years 2025 through 2029.

The bill explicitly mandates the Governor to include a specific appropriation of $625,000 in the annual executive budget bill for the Maryland Center for Construction Education and Innovation from FY 2025 through FY 2029.

The Maryland Center for Construction Education and Innovation (MCCEI), which benefits from the fund's operational support, operates as a public-private partnership located at Towson University, a USM institution.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits the Maryland Insurance Commissioner from removing certain reciprocal jurisdictions from the published reciprocal jurisdictions list. Applies to jurisdictions outside the United States subject to an in-force covered agreement with the United States. Covers member states of the European Union under a covered agreement with the United States. Includes accredited United States jurisdictions meeting National Association of Insurance Commissioners financial standards. Takes effect October 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Commissioner
qa_results.stakeholders: Insurers and assuming reinsurers domiciled in reciprocal jurisdictions, and Maryland ceding insurers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State operations or finances and has no local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 928 directly affects the Maryland Insurance Commissioner and the Maryland Insurance Administration by amending provisions in the Insurance Article regarding the Commissioner's authority to maintain and modify the published list of reciprocal jurisdictions under the Credit for Reinsurance Model Law.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Historical Trust to extinguish or terminate a specified easement on or before July 1, 2023. Covers the June 28, 2010 easement granted by Montgomery County on the parcel known as Warner Manor. Identifies the parcel also as Brainard Warner House and/or Circle Manor in the Town of Kensington. Directs the Trust to complete all necessary recordings and filings to complete the extinguishment or termination. Takes effect June 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Historical Trust
qa_results.stakeholders: Town of Kensington, Montgomery County, owners of Warner Manor (Brainard Warner House and/or Circle Manor), and the Maryland Historical Trust
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact, as the Maryland Historical Trust can implement the bill using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Planning administers and oversees the Maryland Historical Trust (MHT), which is directly mandated by this bill to extinguish or terminate the specified preservation easement on Warner Manor and complete all necessary filings.

qa_results.bill_summary: Abolishes the Maryland 529 Board and transfers administration of the Maryland 529 Program to the State Treasurer. Prohibits the establishment of new prepaid contracts or upgrades to existing contracts under the Prepaid College Trust. Establishes an exclusive administrative process for account holders and qualified beneficiaries to resolve claims against the trust. Requires claimants who accept settlements for disclosure statement disputes to roll their funds into another qualified tuition program. Exempts claim settlement determinations from State and local taxation.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the State Treasurer
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland 529 Prepaid College Trust account holders and beneficiaries, College Investment Plan participants, Maryland ABLE account holders, and transferred Maryland 529 personnel
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $6.7 million in FY 2024 to fund transition costs and eight new positions in the State Treasurer's Office. Ongoing administrative expenditures shift from nonbudgeted funds to special and reimbursable funds. Claim settlements must be paid entirely from existing Prepaid College Trust assets and are exempt from State and local taxes. Local income tax revenues may increase minimally due to foregone deductions on new contracts.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the State Treasurer as the successor to the Maryland 529 Board, transferring full administrative, fiduciary, operational, and financial responsibility for the Maryland 529 Program, its trusts, plans, staff, and claims resolution process to the Office of the State Treasurer.

The bill directly abolishes the Maryland 529 Board and transfers all of its programs, staff, assets, liabilities, and records to the State Treasurer's Office, while phasing out the Maryland Prepaid College Trust.

The bill requires the State Treasurer to work in consultation with the Department of Disabilities to administer, manage, and promote the Maryland ABLE Program, and adds the Secretary of Disabilities to the Financial Education and Capability Commission.

General fund appropriations supporting the Save4College State matching contributions ($11 million) and Maryland ABLE Program administration are budgeted through MHEC and transferred as reimbursable funds to the State Treasurer's Office.

The Comptroller coordinates with the program to verify taxable income eligibility for State matching contributions, and administers the tax provisions governing deductions and tax-exempt claim settlements under the 529 programs.
The bill maintains statutory requirements for the Legislative Auditor to conduct audits of the Prepaid College Trust, the College Investment Plan, and the Maryland ABLE Program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Teachers & State Employees Supplemental Retirement Plans
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the State Treasurer to coordinate marketing plans with the Board of Trustees of the Maryland Teachers and State Employees Supplemental Retirement Plans to increase 529 participation among state employees.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters residency requirements for alcoholic beverages license applicants in Anne Arundel County. Permits State residency to satisfy requirements for partnerships, corporations or clubs, and limited liability companies. Applies this statewide residency standard to all license categories except racetrack or beach and amusement park licenses. Specifies that the license remains valid only while the resident applicant maintains Maryland residency. Takes effect July 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County
qa_results.stakeholders: Applicants and holders of alcoholic beverages licenses on behalf of partnerships, corporations or clubs, and limited liability companies in Anne Arundel County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. Anne Arundel County operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the alcohol industry and sets requirements for alcoholic beverage application forms across the state, though local boards administer county licenses directly.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the definition of captive real estate investment trust for Maryland corporate income tax addition modifications. Excludes entities owned or controlled by qualified foreign entities or certain Australian trust subsidiaries from captive status. Defines a qualified foreign entity based on asset makeup, distributions, ownership limits, and bilateral tax treaties. Relieves qualifying trusts and corporations from adding back their federal dividends paid deduction to taxable income. Takes effect July 1, 2023, and applies to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2022.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Real estate investment trusts, foreign property investment entities, Australian property trusts, and corporate taxpayers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State General Fund, Higher Education Investment Fund, and Transportation Trust Fund revenues may decrease by an indeterminate amount beginning in FY 2024 because fewer entities must add back federal dividends paid deductions. Local highway user revenues and corresponding State expenditures may also experience an indeterminate decrease.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland administers the state's corporate income tax system, enforces tax laws, adopts relevant regulations, and will be directly responsible for implementing the altered definition of captive real estate investment trusts (REITs) and adjusting addition modifications.

A portion of corporate income tax revenues is distributed to the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF), which funds MDOT operations and capital programs; the bill may result in an indeterminate decrease in TTF revenues.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires contractors operating State-owned nursing homes to promptly notify state officials of deficiencies or enforcement actions from monitoring agencies. Directs notifications to the Governor, the overseeing state agency, specified legislative committees, and local legislators. Mandates contractors submit deficiency statements, correction plans, and survey communications within 30 days of receiving a citation or fine. Requires the Maryland Department of Health to report annually on survey activities and enforcement actions at these facilities.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Contractors operating State-owned nursing homes, residents of State-owned nursing homes, and State agencies overseeing State-owned nursing homes
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operational requirements can be handled using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Maryland Department of Health's Office of Health Care Quality as a monitoring agency and mandates that the Department submit an annual report to the Governor and General Assembly on survey activities and enforcement actions at contractor-operated State-owned nursing homes.

The department oversees the Charlotte Hall Veterans Home, the primary State-owned nursing home operated by a contractor in Maryland, making it the supervising State agency that must receive required notices of deficiencies, citations, and plans of correction.

The Governor is a designated recipient of notices of deficiencies, citations, and plans of correction from contractors operating State-owned nursing homes, as well as the annual report submitted by the Maryland Department of Health.
